cards.summary: Use TikTok Shop sales data to find and validate products before committing to ad spend.
cards.use_when: Selecting which product to launch or source for a TikTok Shop store, before building creative or landing pages.
steps: Open the shop tab and filter/sort by items sold to see which brands and products are currently moving volume on TikTok Shop.
Inspect a specific seller to see recent unit sales — the source's example brand sold 384+ items in 30 days (treat as a point-in-time example, not a benchmark).
Shortlist products whose category and price point match your fulfillment and margin constraints.
Take the shortlisted brand into an ad-spy tool to see which ads are driving their sales, so you know the creative format before you commit.
Free plan limits searches per day (source example: 10 searches/day), so plan which products and categories to look up before starting.
caveats: The source finds this more useful for product selection than for ongoing ad inspiration, and doesn't pay for it personally — it's presented as an alternative, not a required tool.
Past 30-day sales don't guarantee future demand; watch for saturated categories before launching.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Three ad production options: DIY, UGC creators, AI
cards.summary: Compare the cost, speed, scalability and conversion trade-offs of in-house, creator and AI-produced TikTok ads.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to resource a new batch of TikTok ad creative when you have limited budget and time.
steps: Option 1 — DIY: cheapest and lets you make real-time edits based on in-account data and swap hooks fast; cons are effort (scripting, filming, editing) and scalability depends on your editing skill. Source recommends CapCut for this path.

Option 2 — hire UGC creators: source says typically best converting because UGC creators convert well, and it is highly scalable; cons are cost. Source recommends marketplaces like Viral Ecom Ads or Fiverr.

Option 3 — AI: fastest and very scalable with a small learning curve; traditionally framed as lowest converting, though the source claims newer AI tools are now among the better converters. Source recommends Creatify and Arc Ads.
Run a small test batch per method and compare against the same product and offer before reallocating budget.
Match method to testing stage: DIY/AI for rapid hook iteration, creators for proven angles you want to scale.
caveats: Conversion ranking (UGC > AI) is the source's stated industry assumption with the caveat that AI is closing the gap; not a universal benchmark.
Cost examples for creator packages vary by vendor — confirm current pricing and deliverables.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Script and shoot a problem-solution ad yourself
cards.summary: Write a UGC-style script and film it in segments on a phone for fast, low-cost ad testing.
cards.use_when: Producing first-party ad creative for a product demo when budget doesn't allow creators.
steps: Follow the eight-step formula from the source's earlier module: hook, problem, failed solution (optional), intro, product, features, benefits, demo, desired result.

Generate or write a script around a specific problem and solution — e.g. provide a prompt like 'Create a UGC-style script for [product] that focuses on the problem-solution. One problem with other [category] is [X]. This one is not.' and let Claude or ChatGPT produce hook, problem, product intro, demo, payoff and CTA sections with visual suggestions.
Film each segment separately on a vertical phone: record the hook, pause, then record problem, then product intro, feature/benefit, and call to action as distinct clips.
Change angle or background roughly every 3 seconds so something new is on screen through the ad (source's stated pacing preference).
Optional hardware: a tripod if you don't want to hold the phone; nothing more is strictly needed.
caveats: The output is a raw demo, not a polished commercial — the source presents it as a realistic starting point.
Hook pacing rules are stated heuristically, not derived from tested platform data.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: CapCut assembly workflow for TikTok ads
cards.summary: Cut dead space, enhance audio, add text, sound effects, music and captions to assemble a vertical ad in CapCut.
cards.use_when: Editing a filmed or AI-generated ad for TikTok to meet platform pacing and accessibility norms.
steps: Import all clips in intended order, then zoom out on the timeline so you can see audio waveforms and dead space between takes.
Cut dead space at the start and between clips so the video begins directly on speech; the source notes TikTok videos shouldn't have leading silence.

Highlight a clip and use CapCut's enhanced-audio options (noise reduction, voice enhance, loudness normalize) — source says these are paid features — to smooth audio peaks and echo from phone recording.
Add a hook text overlay at the start ('Tired of chalky protein?') so viewers scrolling muted understand the video; keep the text up only for the hook segment rather than the whole ad.
Drop a sound effect (e.g. camera click) and a visual sticker (circle/arrow) exactly at the moment a key claim is spoken, so the claim is highlighted visually and audibly.
Add background music from the commercial-use filter only, then lower its volume so it sits just barely behind the voice.
Generate captions, review for false filler-word removals, adjust position so captions don't cover product details, and pick a caption template for readability.
caveats: Some features (audio enhancement, caption generation) require the paid plan — the source notes roughly $20/month; verify current pricing.
Filtering music to commercial sounds is essential for ads; unfiltered music risks copyright issues when the video runs as an ad.
Auto-caption filler detection is imperfect — the source shows 'like' being flagged when it wasn't filler.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Add B-roll to hold attention in short-form ads
cards.summary: Overlay supporting footage on top of talking-head segments to keep viewers watching and illustrate claims.
cards.use_when: Editing a talking-head ad that risks losing viewers during explanation or demo segments.
steps: Place B-roll on the timeline above the main video track so it overlays rather than replaces the speaker (placing it below will take over that segment).
Scale the B-roll clip to fill the frame, and align its timing with the spoken line it illustrates — e.g. footage of someone eating chalk over the line about chalky protein.
Mute the B-roll clip's own audio completely via its audio tab, otherwise it fights the voice track.
Check that captions sit above the B-roll layer so text stays visible; adjust caption placement if the overlay covers them.
Add B-roll at multiple points — the source recommends more rather than fewer cuts to maintain attention.
caveats: The source's 'more B-roll keeps attention' guidance is presented as experience, not a tested threshold.
Track ordering in CapCut controls visibility; verify layer order before exporting.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Hiring UGC creators through marketplaces
cards.summary: Brief and buy creator ad packages that test multiple hooks, using marketplaces with transparent pricing.
cards.use_when: Scaling creative volume after an angle works, or when you don't want to appear on camera yourself.
steps: Use a marketplace like Viral Ecom Ads for quick turnaround, or Fiverr where you can screen individual creators and see pricing up front.

Start with a small multi-hook package rather than a large one — the source recommends beginning with the three-pack (bundle of hook variations) before committing more, e.g. three-pack pricing cited around $180 versus five-pack around $300.

For Fiverr, read each gig's package terms carefully: the source's example creator offered one video with no copyright usage for $50, scaling to around $100 for copyright-provided or premium tiers — confirm usage rights before purchase, especially for paid ad rights.
Decide the level of direction: supply an exact script, or let the creator use their own judgment for a more native feel.
Expect to ship the product to the creator and allow back-and-forth on creative direction before delivery.
Organize delivered videos by hook and angle in your swipe file so you can test them systematically.
caveats: Pricing figures are the source's point-in-time examples and vary by creator and package.
Usage rights and whitelisting permissions differ per gig — verify what you're licensed to run as a paid ad.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Generate AI talking-actor ads with emotion tagging
cards.summary: Create AI spokesperson videos in Arc Ads with script, actor selection, emotion prompts and model choice.
cards.use_when: Producing a high volume of talking-head ad variants fast, when real creators are too slow or expensive.
steps: Create a project inside a named folder organized by video type so outputs stay sortable.
Choose the AI actor option in the project interface; this format suits a script-only talking head where the actor isn't holding or using the product.
Paste your script, then select an actor by filtering all/favorites/my actors and gender, age or background scene.
Select multiple actors at once if you want the same script generated with several faces for A/B testing. The source says you can add three actors and each will generate the script.
Add emotions automatically and review them — the tool detects lines as excited, mischievous, satisfied, etc., which the source says makes delivery less robotic; you can edit individual lines.
Pick the model (source compares Arc Ads 1.0 vs Omni Human 1.5) and whether to use standard text-to-speech or speech-to-speech if you want your own recorded inflection.
Generate and expect roughly 1 credit per video; generation typically takes a few minutes in the source's demo.
caveats: The source warns some features produce sub-par results and can waste credits — test a single video before batch generating.
Model and interface options change; verify current model names and credit costs before spending.
AI talking heads are not shown holding the product in this format — use the product-showcase preset for that.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: AI fashion try-on ads from product photos
cards.summary: Generate realistic model try-on videos from a clothing product image using Arc Ads presets.
cards.use_when: Selling apparel and needing model footage in many styles or scenes without booking shoots.
steps: Open the project's 'see more' menu and choose presets, then select the fashion try-on preset.
Pick a scene preset (e.g. the closet setup the source demonstrates) and click remix to load it.
Upload your own product image of the garment.
Choose the aspect ratio — 9:16 for vertical TikTok output; leave it vertical for ads.
Generate the video and review; the source notes the output looked ultra-realistic with the actor wearing the uploaded product.
Export the try-on clip and combine it with other assets, e.g. a separate talking-actor clip, to build a fuller ad in your editor.
caveats: Each generation consumes credits; the source recommends testing outputs before batch runs.
Output quality depends on the product image you upload; the source's other preset (product showcase) requires clean white-background images.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: AI product-showcase ads with actor holding your SKU
cards.summary: Generate AI actor videos holding or using a physical product from a clean product image plus a written direction.
cards.use_when: Advertising a physical product that isn't apparel and you need demonstration footage without a shoot.
steps: Open 'see more' > presets and choose the product showcase preset rather than fashion try-on.
Select the scene preset closest to your desired setting (e.g. a bedroom) and click remix; note you will get a different actor than the preset shows.
Upload your product photo — the source stresses it should be on a white background with no people in the image for best results.
Set the aspect ratio to 9:16 for vertical ad placements.
Write a description of the action you want: the source's example tells the model to sit as shown while holding the charger and talk about how great it is for charging her phone and other devices.
Generate the video (the source notes roughly one credit and a few minutes waiting) and review whether the actor appears to hold/use the product convincingly.
Export and edit together with talking-head or B-roll clips for a complete ad.
caveats: The resulting actor won't match the preset actor shown in the library.
The source says generation typically takes around two to five minutes, so batch planning matters when testing many angles.
Image cleanliness strongly affects output — crowded or people-containing product photos are explicitly discouraged.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: AI video ad generation: aspect ratio, prompt description, extensions
cards.summary: How to generate a UGC-style talking-head video ad with an AI video tool, including prompt structure and extending a cut-off clip.
cards.use_when: You need a first batch of paid-social ad creatives (TikTok/Meta feed) for a product page or offer and are generating them with an AI avatar tool rather than shooting.
steps: Before generating, set the aspect ratio to match the placement you'll run in (vertical 9:16 for TikTok/in-feed).

Write a description that specifies three things: the model's posture/action, the product prop, and the talking points. Example format from the source: 'have the model sitting like she is while holding the charger and talking about how great it is for charging her phone and other devices.'
Let the tool generate (source notes ~2–5 minutes per render). Budget the tool's credits per render — the base image-to-video generation cost one credit in the source's example.

Review the output for an abrupt cut-off. If the script is truncated, use the tool's Extend button (or find Extend under presets) and describe what the continuation should say, e.g. additional feature walkthrough.
Extend deliberately: the source used extend to go from ~12 seconds to ~19 additional seconds so the avatar could cover more features. Remove the extension if it dilutes the hook.
Download the finished file and upload it as a manual ad creative with your CTA and destination URL.
caveats: Credit costs and render times are tool- and plan-specific and change; verify the current interface and pricing before planning a batch.
Extensions can hurt performance if the extra seconds dilute the opening hook — evaluate the full clip, not just completion.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Swipe competitor hooks and re-voice them for your product
cards.summary: Download a winning competitor or platform hook, upload it to an AI ad tool, and regenerate it with your product inserted to test hook variations cheaply.
cards.use_when: You have product and offer ready but are stuck on ad angles, or you want to test multiple opening hooks for the same PDP/offer without reshooting.
steps: Build a swipe file: use a platform that lets you filter top-performing TikTok (or cross-platform) videos to find proven hooks — the source used Foreplay, which is a paid tool with other options available.
Pick a hook whose format is transferable to your category (e.g. 'My For You page convinced me to buy something again, but this one is actually worth the hype' works for almost any physical product).
Download that video and upload it into your AI video tool as the reference.
Give the tool a short instruction naming your product: the source's example was simply 'Can you talk about my product Premier Supplements?' — the AI preserved the hook and swapped the product.
Generate and review: in the source's run, the output reproduced the hook and inserted the presenter's product, at a lower credit cost (~0.4 credits) than a from-scratch render.
Repeat with multiple hooks against the same product to build a hook-test set for your campaign's creative split test.
Use this as a hook-testing machine, not a final asset: run the variations as separate ads so platform data tells you which hook wins.
caveats: The source demonstrates hook copying on a made-up brand; results are illustrative, not a performance promise.
Reproducing another brand's script verbatim risks IP/brand issues — use the hook structure with your own claims and verify your product claims are compliant.
AI may paraphrase or drop parts of the reference; check the output for accurate product claims.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Choose the right AI video model for your ad by constraint
cards.summary: Model selection for AI ad video: pick based on which constraint matters most — realism, exact length, or resolution.
cards.use_when: You are generating product or UGC-style ad videos and need to decide which generation model to spend credits on for a given spot length or placement.
steps: If realism and 'does this look like a real person using the product' are the priority, the source prefers Sora 2 / Sora 2 Pro and reports using it for most ad outputs, using a product image plus a short description.
If you need an exact duration (every second between ~3s and 15s), use Kling 3.0 — this matters when your spot must hit a defined length for a placement or a multi-scene edit.
If you need high resolution (up to 4K), V0 3.1 offers that, but the source reports its cinematic, artistic style often doesn't match UGC-ad aesthetics and uses it least for ads.
For Sora 2, plan around fixed length options (4, 8, or 12 seconds) and 1080p; if your ad concept requires other lengths, either use Kling or extend the clip.
When prompting, attach a product image so the model renders the actual item, and give a plain-language ad brief (source example prompt: 'make me a UGC ad for a company that sells office chairs').
Allow for post-editing: the source notes Sora 2 sometimes cuts off the video at an odd angle, requiring trimming after generation.
caveats: Model availability, resolution and duration limits change quickly — verify current options in the tool before building a production plan.
Model preference here is the presenter's opinion based on their testing, not a benchmark; run your own A/B between models on the same product.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Motion control and presets to skip
cards.summary: Use motion-transfer to animate a still of a person/product into an existing motion, and avoid the unboxing POV preset because of hand artifacts.
cards.use_when: You want a scroll-stopping format (person reactivating a product, showing a device in motion) without a shoot, or you are deciding which AI presets are worth spending credits on.
steps: For motion transfer, upload (1) a reference video containing the motion you want, and (2) a still image of the person you want performing it. The tool transfers the motion onto your image.
Source example workflow: a clip of a woman dancing was used as the motion reference, and an AI-generated image of a man in an office was the subject; the output made the man perform the same motion.
Adapt the format to commerce: instead of dancing, capture the motion of holding up a product, demonstrating a device, or reacting to unboxing — the motion source can be any clip.
This is a lower-priority format: the source says they rarely use it, so treat it as a novelty format to test, not a core creative.
Avoid the 'unboxing POV' preset for product unboxing ads — the source reports the hands (e.g. crumpling paper) look visibly wrong and it isn't worth the credits.
Instead, prompt Sora 2 to 'make a video of this being unboxed' when you need unboxing content, and treat that output as the testable version.
caveats: Motion transfer adds a step and may produce artifacts on hands and props — inspect closely before setting spend.
Preset quality changes with model updates; the unboxing-POV warning is a snapshot of the presenter's testing, so re-evaluate periodically.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Pick the TikTok ad objective that matches your goal (and why Sales is the default)
cards.summary: TikTok campaign objectives map to funnel stages, but optimizing for Sales is the source's default because it trains delivery toward purchases.
cards.use_when: You are setting up a new TikTok Ads Manager campaign for a product and need to decide what to optimize the account toward before spending budget.
steps: Treat the objective list as a funnel: Awareness/Reach sits at the top (max reach, no optimization toward a page view or sale), Consideration (Traffic, Video Views, Community Interactions) sits in the middle, and Conversion (App Promotion, Lead Generation, Sales) sits at the bottom.
Choose Sales for most ecommerce campaigns, because the goal is a purchase and the algorithm optimizes delivery toward the conversion you've selected.
Only use Reach when the explicit goal is spreading awareness (e.g. a launch) and you accept poor ROAS on that spend.
Consider Community Interactions only for growing a profile's engagement/followers, not for driving a product purchase.
Confirm your TikTok pixel is installed and firing before you optimize toward a purchase — you cannot optimize for a conversion event the pixel isn't reporting.

Inside Sales, you also choose a destination (TikTok Shop vs Website — manual, Smart+, or search). Expect different available options across objectives: the source notes features like creative split testing are not available for every objective, and placements and billing events can differ per objective.
Start with the manual website campaign rather than the recommended Smart+ campaign, and treat Smart+ as a parallel test later: the source reports mixed results between the two in their testing.
caveats: If the pixel isn't set up, the purchase optimization will not function; fix the pixel first.
Objective availability, Smart+ recommendations, and per-objective feature sets are TikTok product specifics that change — verify in the current Ads Manager.
The 'always use Sales' stance is the presenter's opinion for ecommerce; campaigns with pure awareness goals are a legitimate exception.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Manual vs Smart+ campaign and the product catalog setting
cards.summary: Choose manual for control, disable the campaign catalog to avoid showing unintended products under your video, and label campaigns by audience for later reporting.
cards.use_when: You are configuring a new TikTok Sales campaign and deciding whether to use Smart+, whether to show a product catalog under the video, and how to name campaigns.
steps: Start with the manual campaign instead of the TikTok-recommended Smart+; the source reports mixed results between them and prefers manual first, then testing Smart+ alongside it.

Turn the campaign catalog OFF for a first campaign. It pulls images from your product catalog and displays products under the video, which can surface products you didn't intend to promote and add visual clutter. The source keeps it unchecked so only the video and the one product you want are shown.
Name the campaign by audience purpose — the source uses 'Prospecting' to mark cold-audience campaigns — so you can read performance at a glance.
Only check the Special Categories box if you are advertising housing, employment, or credit; otherwise leave it.
Leave Create Split Test unchecked for now unless you have a specific structured test planned.

Decide campaign budget optimization (CBO) here: leaving it off lets you budget at the ad-group level so each audience gets a predictable share (e.g. $25 each across four ad groups), which is what the source recommends for new accounts.
caveats: The source expects mixed manual-vs-Smart+ results, so don't assume one is universally superior.
The catalog setting may be useful for some use cases (e.g. shops with many SKUs); the recommendation to turn it off is specifically for getting-started campaigns.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Campaign budget optimization: off for testing, on for scaling
cards.summary: Leave CBO off when testing audiences so each ad group gets a defined budget, then enable it when scaling to let TikTok allocate toward what already works.
cards.use_when: You are deciding between campaign-level and ad-group-level budget allocation for a TikTok campaign, particularly when comparing broad vs interest audiences.
steps: Understand the mechanism: with CBO on, you set one budget at the campaign level and TikTok distributes it across ad groups however it favors — e.g. $80/$10/$5/$5 out of four groups — with no control from you.
With CBO off, set budget at the ad-group level (the source's term: ad group budget optimization) so each ad group receives an even, predictable amount (e.g. $25 each) and audience tests stay clean.
For new accounts, keep CBO off so you can see which audiences perform and manually move budget toward winners.
Once you've identified winners, switch to CBO for scaling — the source uses it to direct money toward proven ad groups.
If CBO is on, the campaign asks for a daily budget; if off, the daily budget field appears at the ad-group level. Set it there.
Keep the structure shallow: the source generally does not recommend more than four ad groups inside a campaign.
caveats: The >4-ad-group guidance is a practical heuristic from the presenter's experience, not a platform rule.
Switching CBO on re-allocates spend in ways you don't control, so don't use it while you still need clean per-audience comparisons.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Budget recommendations for TikTok: CPA multiples vs TikTok's 10x rule
cards.summary: TikTok recommends 10x CPA daily budget; the source prefers 2x current CPA (or $50 if unknown, $20 minimum) and frames budgets around escaping the learning phase.
cards.use_when: You are deciding how much daily budget to put behind a new TikTok conversion campaign for a product.
steps: Know the platform constraint: TikTok requires a $20/day minimum. Attempting less is rejected in the interface.
Know the platform's recommendation so you can judge it: TikTok suggests 10x your current CPA (e.g. $10 CPA -> $100/day; $40 CPA -> $400/day).

The source does not like the 10x rule for most advertisers. Instead, budget at 2x your current cost per acquisition: a $10 CPA implies a $20/day budget; a $20 CPA on other platforms implies ~$40/day here.
If you don't know your CPA, start around $50/day as a test budget.
If budget forces you to $20/day, proceed but expect a long learning phase.

Understand the learning phase: performance fluctuates while the system finds the best users, and volatility typically settles after 25 campaign results or seven days. Aim to accumulate the 25 results inside the seven-day window if budget allows.

Set the start time, keep campaigns running continuously rather than scheduling short flights, keep day-parting on all day, and leave the optional target CPA and attribution windows untouched on a new account.
caveats: The 25-results/7-day learning phase is TikTok's described mechanism; the source's 2x-CPA budget is their own alternative to TikTok's 10x advice, not a platform rule.
The 10x recommendation makes 2x-CPA budgets hard for high-CPA products — expect slower learning if you underfund.
Leave target CPA blank until you have real data; setting it without data can constrain delivery.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: TikTok cost expectations and the one lever that moves them
cards.summary: Typical TikTok cost ranges (CPM, CPC, CPV) and the factors that shift them, with creative quality named as the dominant driver.
cards.use_when: You are setting CPA and ROAS targets for a TikTok ad plan or diagnosing why your costs are above/below plan.
steps: Use these as rough planning ranges rather than promises: CPM roughly $3–$10 per thousand impressions; CPC roughly $0.17–$1.00; cost per view roughly $0.01–$0.07.
Expect CPA to vary widely depending on product price, category and many other factors — don't apply a single benchmark across categories.

Understand the cost drivers the source lists: creative quality of the ad (good UGC-style ads get cheaper CPMs), audience targeting (broader is cheaper), industry competition (beauty supplements are more expensive), and seasonality (Q4 holiday costs rise).
Treat creative quality as the biggest lever: the source says the better the ad, the cheaper your views, and reports seeing this repeatedly across accounts.
Apply this to decisions: if CPMs are high, test a new hook (see the hook-repurposing workflow) before expanding targeting or raising budget.
Plan seasonal buys ahead of Q4 — raise budget expectations rather than assuming the same CPA holds.
caveats: These ranges are presented as typical, not guaranteed; the source notes having seen both lower and much higher costs, especially on poor ads.
CPM/CPC/CPV bands vary by country, currency and account history — treat them as directional.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Audience targeting: start broad, layer interest testing later
cards.summary: Broad targeting is the source's default because the algorithm finds buyers; add interest/behavior ad groups only when budget allows a clean comparison.
cards.use_when: You are configuring TikTok ad-group targeting (demographics, interests, spending power, devices) for a product campaign.
steps: Start with broad targeting — TikTok itself states broad is best for most advertisers, and the source agrees: with a strong ad, the algorithm finds the right people. The source reports testing this multiple times and finding broad works well.
For a $20/day budget, use one campaign (Prospecting) with one broad ad group containing three ad creatives. Once a winner emerges, move it to a new campaign and scale.

For a larger budget, duplicate the ad group and keep identical settings except the audience: one broad vs one interest/behavior, running the same three ads in each, so you can compare audiences on equal footing.
Keep the same ads in both ad groups: the source duplicated the ad group with its ads so the only variable is targeting.

For interest targeting, search by category keyword (e.g. 'swimsuit') and add 3–5 relevant interests, purchase intentions, video interactions, creator interactions or hashtags. Ignore 'audience narrow' warnings if the reach figure is healthy — the source's example showed ~7 million people while still flagged as narrow.
Leave spending power on 'All' unless you sell luxury. The source tested narrowing to high spenders and found it limits delivery without improving results.

Leave household income on 'All' — the source doubts the platform knows true household income well. Leave devices on all, and leave placements automatic, then check placement data later; TikTok placement is generally the strongest performer.
caveats: Broad vs interest is presented as a budget-dependent test, not a universal rule — the source also admits a personal bias toward granular targeting that the algorithm tends to beat.
Interest targeting significantly narrows reach; only worth it if you have the budget to run proper ($20/day per ad group) comparisons.
Demographic filters like spending power are the presenter's tested opinion, not platform-verified performance data.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Build one ad group, then duplicate it for multiple audiences
cards.summary: Set up one ad group with all creatives first, then duplicate the ad group to create audience variants rather than rebuilding ads each time.
cards.use_when: You are structuring a TikTok campaign that needs separate broad and interest (or demographic) ad groups using the same creative set.
steps: Create one ad group and build all the ads (3–5 creative) inside it first — if you plan to run 3–5 ads, creating them before duplication saves you recreating them in each copy.
Create the ad group with a temporary name, then name it after targeting is set (e.g. 'broad USA' with language, age, gender adjustments as needed).
Publish, then go to the ad-group level in the campaign view and use Duplicate -> duplicate the ad group into the existing campaign.

In the duplicate, change only the audience: add interest/behavior targeting (e.g. swimsuit-related interests), then rename to something like 'interest USA' so broad vs interest is unambiguous in reporting.
Keep all other settings identical between the two ad groups so the audience is the only variable.
To add more creatives later, duplicate the ad inside the ad group and use the update button on the copy to swap in a different video or TikTok post.
Keep at most ~4 ad groups per campaign as a working guideline.
caveats: Duplicating before all creatives are built forces you to update each copy manually — build ads first.
Parallel ad groups each need their own minimum daily budget (~$20/day in the source's examples), so this structure multiplies spend.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Set up TikTok in-feed ad creative: CTA, music, and the ad-library checkbox
cards.summary: Practical creative-level settings for a TikTok ad: use multiple CTAs for testing, decide on music sharing, and uncheck the ad-library box.
cards.use_when: You are in the ad creative step of a TikTok campaign, uploading a video or spark post, and setting the CTA, URL, and visibility options.
steps: In the ad creative section you have two source options: upload a video from your computer, or grab an existing TikTok post from a linked account to run as a spark ad (you need your TikTok account linked to the ads account for this).
Add as many appropriate call-to-action options as possible so TikTok can test which gets the most clicks for that specific video — but make sure each CTA actually makes sense for your product.
Leave music sharing OFF: this option lets others use the sound from your ad, which the source leaves disabled.
Leave product tagging off unless you have TikTok Shop set up and want to tag specific products; the source covers shop product tagging in a later module.
Add your destination URL; TikTok appends UTM parameters for you.
Confirm you have the rights to any music in the ad.
Uncheck the option that places your ad in the TikTok ad library — the source stresses keeping this unchecked so your ads do not appear in the library.
Publish all, then duplicate the ad if you want additional creative variations inside the ad group.
caveats: Ad library visibility, music sharing and CTA list options are platform UI features that change — verify current naming and defaults in Ads Manager.
Running an existing post as a spark ad requires the profile-to-ad-account link; without it, that option won't be available.
This card covers in-feed; search campaigns and TikTok Shop setups differ.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Keyword research for TikTok search ads with the Keyword Planner
cards.summary: Use TikTok's Keyword Planner to build a 20–50 keyword list filtered by competition and volume, then save it as a plan to upload into a search campaign.
cards.use_when: You want to run TikTok search ads (users typing queries inside TikTok) for a product and need a keyword list with realistic CPC and volume expectations.
steps: In TikTok Ads Manager, go to Tools -> Keyword Planner (verify current menu location, as platform UI changes).
Enter your product or category (e.g. 'swimsuits'), set the target area (e.g. United States), and run Discover.
Read the output columns: keyword, average monthly searches, three-month change, year-over-year change, competition level, and estimated low/high CPC.

Filter by low competition first and add any relevant terms — the source finds cheaper average clicks on low-competition terms, though volume is smaller and many results may be irrelevant or in other languages.
Then re-run with all competition levels, sort by monthly search volume, and add the relevant high-volume terms.
Aim for roughly 20–50 keywords. Source example: this produced ~52,000 total monthly search volume, which they judged enough to build a campaign on.
Save the plan with a specific name (e.g. 'swimsuits') — saving is required so you can pull the list into the campaign later.
Use this research to sanity-check whether search ads are worth running for the product at all: if volume is negligible, skip the campaign.
caveats: Keyword Planner data is directional; the source notes some results were irrelevant (other languages, unrelated terms) and had to be filtered manually.
The 20–50 keyword / 52k volume example is the presenter's working heuristic, not a validated threshold.
Tool location and columns can change; check the current interface.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Build a TikTok search campaign and pick match types
cards.summary: Set up a TikTok search campaign from a saved keyword plan, choose phrase match as the middle ground, and disable automated keywords.
cards.use_when: You are launching a TikTok search ad campaign targeting people actively searching for your product terms.
steps: Create a new campaign with the Sales objective and select the search campaign type (instead of manual or Smart+). Reference your saved keyword plan.
Reuse your pixel and conversion settings: website destination, conversion event = purchase. Leave target CPA blank if you don't know it.

Load your keywords from the saved keyword plan. If you skip pre-research, you can search inside the campaign, but the source finds the in-campaign view gives fewer options — do the research beforehand.

Understand the three match types: broad maximizes reach by matching relevant searches; phrase shows ads on searches with the same meaning as your keyword; exact shows ads only for searches containing your exact phrase in order and limits reach most.
The source's default: start with phrase match as the middle ground — you'll appear for related terms like 'modest swimwear' but not wildly unrelated queries.
If you must only appear for specific terms (e.g. black swimsuit or red swimsuit), use exact match and separate ad groups per keyword theme, accepting reduced reach.
Turn automated keywords OFF at launch so you know exactly what your ads show up for; the source treats it as an optional later test.

Set daily budget (minimum $20), start/end times, US + 18+ demographics as appropriate, and note placements are limited to TikTok search results for this campaign type. Allow user comments. Build the ad with a destination URL and a video or spark post, then publish.
caveats: Exact match will meaningfully cut reach; only use when a term is high-volume and highly relevant.
Automated keywords can be tested later, but at launch the source prefers full control over query matching.
Search campaign placement is constrained to search results — this is not a feed placement.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Mine the search term report and add negative keywords
cards.summary: After launching a search campaign, review the search terms your ads actually appeared for and exclude unwanted queries with negative keywords.
cards.use_when: You have a TikTok search campaign running and need to protect spend from irrelevant queries that don't match product intent.
steps: Click into the search campaign, go to the ad group level, and open View Data.
Open the Search tab to see the search term report — the actual queries your ads were shown against.
Review the list closely, as the source recommends doing this after a couple of days of running, to confirm you're showing up for terms that match your brand and product.
Where you see irrelevant queries, use the report's option to add them as negative keywords so your ad no longer appears for them.
Repeat this review periodically — it is described as very important when running search campaigns, because broad/phrase matching will pull in tangents over time.
If you have keyword-specific product angles (e.g. black swimsuit vs red swimsuit), use this data to decide whether to split them into separate ad groups with their own creative.
caveats: Search term reports need volume before they're informative; the source suggests checking after a couple of days, not immediately at launch.
Match type changes (e.g. switching broad to phrase) affect the quality of the terms you'll later need to exclude.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Spark ads: requirements and the organic-first six-step workflow
cards.summary: Run Spark ads by posting creative organically first, waiting 5–7 days to prove it, then amplifying the winners with paid budget.
cards.use_when: You want to amplify organic TikTok content (your own or a creator's) as a paid ad rather than treating paid and organic as separate tracks.
steps: Confirm the prerequisites: a TikTok Ads account (set up in the course), a TikTok profile if the Spark ad runs from your own account, and the profile linked to the ads account. If using influencers, obtain an ad authorization code from them (optional but required for creator posts).
Step 1 — create three or more videos yourself or have influencers create them.
Step 2 — post them to your TikTok account, or have influencers post to theirs.

Step 3 — wait five to seven days for the post to reach its full organic potential; roughly a week is the typical life cycle of a new TikTok post, and you can usually tell within the first two days whether it's starting to get organic traction.
Step 4 onward — do not step in immediately: the source's rationale is that you don't want to spend ad budget amplifying a post that can still earn free organic impressions.
After the organic window, run the winning posts as Spark ads to scale the reach that already proved itself.
Two ways to run them: boost one of your own existing posts, or boost a creator's post using their authorization code.
caveats: The 5–7 day wait is the presenter's tested workflow, not a platform requirement; faster campaigns can still boost earlier.
You must have the profile-to-ad-account link and, for creators, an authorization code — without them the Spark ad can't be created.
This is a lead-in to paid amplification and the source covers the full Spark ad build in a later module; verify current linking and authorization steps in Ads Manager.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Test TikTok creative organically before spending ad budget
cards.summary: Run a six-step Spark Ads loop that posts videos organically first, waits 5-7 days for full organic reach, then amplifies only the proven winners with paid budget.
cards.use_when: You are planning TikTok acquisition creative for a store and deciding which videos deserve paid spend versus which should be left to run free.
steps: Produce three or more videos at a time, either in-house or by briefing influencers, so you always have a batch to compare rather than judging a single creative.
Post them to your own TikTok account, or have the influencers post to theirs, so organic performance data accumulates.

Wait five to seven days before deciding. The presenter's reasoning is that new TikTok posts typically see organic traffic concentrated in the first couple of days and roughly a week-long life cycle — you don't want to pay to reach people who would have seen it free.

After the wait, judge each video on the results it produced: sales attributed to that post, follows, and engagement. The presenter's own example shows three influencer videos at 2.3M, 15K and 8M organic views — pick the clear performer to amplify. In a second example the differentiator was engagement, not raw views.
Run the one or two winners as Spark Ads, then repeat the cycle with a new batch. The loop scales: post 20 videos and take the top 10-30% as ads instead of three.
Expect the creative selection to be the main lever — in the presenter's account, 400+ SKUs and multiple videos existed, but only the organic winners were worth paying to distribute.
caveats: The 5-7 day wait and the 'first two days' signal are the presenter's observations about typical TikTok behavior, not guaranteed benchmarks; verify against your own account's data.
View counts and engagement are proxies — the presenter also references sales and follows as selection criteria, so prefer whichever metric maps to your objective.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Set up a Spark Ad from your own organic post
cards.summary: Inside Ads Manager's ad creative step, select TikTok post to run an existing organic video as a Spark Ad from your own account.
cards.use_when: You have an organic TikTok post from your own profile that performed well and you want to put paid amplification behind it.
steps: Build the campaign as normal through objective and targeting; Spark Ads can be run against essentially any objective, including the sales objective.
At the ad creative step, navigate to the video/creative selection and choose the TikTok post source.
Use the account dropdown to pick the TikTok account you want to pull posts from.
Select the specific organic post from the list. If your posts don't appear, your TikTok ad account is not linked to your TikTok account — fix the linkage before continuing.
Confirm to attach the post as your Spark Ad creative, then finish the remaining campaign setup.
Note the destination URL is editable, so you control where the ad traffic lands even though the ad displays from your own profile.
caveats: The exact interface labels shift over time — verify the current TikTok Ads Manager layout before following these clicks.
The source demonstrates this flow in a specific ad account; account-linking requirements may differ by region.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Run an influencer's video as a Spark Ad using an ad authorization code
cards.summary: Request a TikTok post code from the creator, then add it via 'add post' in the ad creative step to run their video as a paid ad from their profile.
cards.use_when: An influencer posted a video with your product and you want to amplify it with paid spend as a Spark Ad from their handle.
steps: In the ad creative step, open the TikTok post source and use the 'add post' option, which prompts for a TikTok post code.
Instruct the creator: open the video they posted for you, tap the three dots, choose ad settings, and turn on ad authorization.
Tell them to set the authorization duration to 365 days (the presenter's recommendation) so you can run the ad as long as possible.
Once authorized and saved, they generate an ad authorization code, tap manage code and copy it, then send you the code.
Paste the code into the post code field in Ads Manager and continue — the video appears and can be added to your ad library and confirmed as creative.
Set the destination URL so traffic goes to the page you want, even though the ad runs from the influencer's profile.
caveats: Authorization is creator-controlled; the creator can adjust or decline, so agree terms before relying on the footage.
The exact menu names inside the TikTok app change — verify current steps with the creator when you send instructions.
A long authorization period does not guarantee continued performance; the ad still competes on creative merit.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Why Spark Ads engagement accrues to the organic post
cards.summary: Likes, comments and engagement on a Spark Ad also appear on the original organic post, creating one amplified asset rather than a separate ad unit.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to run creator content as a Spark Ad versus a standalone ad creative, and want to understand the compounding effect on the original post.
steps: Recognize that engagement generated by the paid ad — likes and comments — also shows on the organic post, so the ad and the organic asset reinforce each other.
Plan creative selection around posts that already show strong engagement, since paid amplification adds to rather than replaces that interaction profile.
Because the ad runs from the creator's handle, evaluate whether their profile credibility and audience fit the product before committing budget.
Use the editable destination URL to route paid traffic to the page you control, separating 'who it appears from' (creator) from 'where it lands' (your store).
Budget the creator relationship around long authorization windows (the presenter suggests 365 days) so the compounding engagement keeps benefiting a single asset.
Treat Spark Ads as one asset with two distribution layers — organic reach first, paid amplification second — rather than two separate creative lines to manage.
caveats: The presenter's example mixes co-marketing with a partner profile, so results depend on the creator's existing audience and posting cadence. None of the view or engagement figures in the source are benchmarks.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Stand up the TikTok Shop accounts needed before running Shop ads
cards.summary: Running TikTok Shop / GMV Max ads requires a Seller Center, a linked Business Center and Ads Manager, plus GMV Max authorization and admin access to the shop.
cards.use_when: You are preparing an ecommerce store to sell directly inside TikTok and need to know which accounts and permissions must exist before launch.
steps: Create a TikTok Seller Center account (separate from Business Center and Ads Manager) — this is what manages listings, orders, logistics, the storefront, seller-side promotions, affiliate recruitment and shop analytics.
Confirm you have a Business Center account and an Ads Manager account; the Seller Center is the piece specifically for running the shop.
Link the TikTok Shop to the Business Center, and make sure the ad account you'll use has GMV Max authorization for that shop.
Ensure you hold admin access to the shop account, since critical settings live behind it.
Use one consistent email or phone number across your Shopify/WooCommerce account and the Seller Center — the presenter notes this makes account connection smoother.
Check current regional availability before planning GMV Max, since it was limited to specific locations at the time of recording — verify the current list.
caveats: GMV Max availability was region-restricted at the time of the source; the location list may change.
The presenter mentions a signup link with advertised rewards — that is promotional and not required for setup.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Sync your Shopify catalog into TikTok Shop
cards.summary: Install the official TikTok app for Shopify to sync products, stock and pricing into your Seller Center instead of creating listings by hand.
cards.use_when: You are launching a TikTok Shop and want product listings, pricing and stock to flow from your existing ecommerce catalog rather than manual entry.
steps: In Seller Center, open the product listing methods (list a URL, bulk upload, or sync with other platforms such as Amazon, Shopify, eBay).
Choose the sync path, which sends you to an app store; search for the official provider app (in this case 'TikTok for Shopify') and install it, not a third-party clone.
Inside Shopify, click set up on the 'start selling on TikTok' option, then connect to your Seller Center shop account.
Beware the account-connection step asks for verification — email or phone — so use the same contact as your Seller Center signup.
Set shipping: the presenter recommends 'seller shipping' (use your Shopify settings) for most merchants, since fulfilling by TikTok is the alternative.
Map carriers and define warehouse pickup and return addresses in Seller Center; those must exist before you can sell.
After shipping is updated the products sync automatically, but some fail. Open the error view: examples include missing region of origin or other required fields, so complete every red-starred field.
Watch for restricted categories — the demo hits a cookware/dishes restriction that prevents approval on a demo account.
Check listing quality and drive each listing from 'fair' to the highest status, using TikTok's improve-listing-quality checklist for anything below 'good'.
Verify the product is live by searching your store name in TikTok and switching to the Shop tab.
caveats: Restricted product categories can block listing regardless of how complete the data is.
Synced stock and price flow from Shopify, so source-of-truth errors propagate to TikTok.
Interface steps in both Shopify and Seller Center change; verify current flows.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Read the Seller Center dashboard and fix listings below good quality
cards.summary: The Seller Center home, products and marketing tabs surface orders, violations, low stock and listing quality issues you must resolve to sell effectively.
cards.use_when: You are operating a live TikTok Shop and need a routine for catching operational and listing problems before they cost sales.
steps: Check the home tab for recent performance and the to-do list: orders ready to ship, pending returns, violations, low stock, and negative reviews. Treat reviews as a marketplace signal to respond to.
Open the orders view to see current orders, shipped, completed, pending, returns and free shipping obligations.
In products, review active, under review, needs-attention and deactivated listings alongside stock, price and listing quality.
Click into any listing rated below good (e.g. 'fair') and follow the issue list to improve it; use the improve-listing-quality to-do to batch-fix everything below that threshold.
In the marketing tab, open shop design to see how the storefront renders and the current store conversion rate.
Test alternative shop templates if available, then return to the same conversion-rate view to see whether the change actually moved the rate.
Set up the affiliate side (open and target collaborations) so creators can begin producing tagged videos for the catalog.
caveats: The presenter's instruction to optimize every listing to the highest quality score is a recommendation, not a measured guarantee of sales lift.
Conversion rate in this view reflects the store overall, so a design change's effect must be read over time, not from one snapshot.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Structure open and target affiliate collaborations with commission tiers
cards.summary: Offer open collaborations at a fixed commission to anyone who drives a sale, and send target collaborations with custom rates to handpicked creators.
cards.use_when: You want to recruit TikTok creators to post tagged videos for your products without paying upfront for content that doesn't sell.
steps: Set up an open collaboration where the creator earns a commission (the presenter uses 20% as an example) only when they actually drive a sale — you pay nothing extra otherwise.
Decide whether the offer includes free products or a request flow, and whether samples are free or refundable.
Control sample requests: they arrive as requests you approve or reject, so a creator can't simply pull samples.
Set thresholds so only qualified creators can request samples — for example a minimum follower count (the presenter cites 10,000) or a minimum revenue driven (e.g. $100, $1,000, $10,000).
For target collaborations, send a batch invitation with a name, validity dates, contact details, a message, and the specific products.
Assign each handpicked creator a custom commission rate and optionally a flat fee; you can vary rates per creator (e.g. 24% vs 25%).

Add a separate shop ads commission rate that pays the creator when their content is amplified as a paid ad. The presenter recommends setting it lower than the standard rate (he cites around 5%) because you're adding ad spend on top.
caveats: Commission percentages and thresholds in the source are illustrative, not universal rules — set them from your own margin.
When reviewing sample requests, the source shows creators with attributes like post rate and 30-day GMV; those are creator-specific data points, not proof of future performance.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Set up a GMV Max campaign that sells inside TikTok
cards.summary: GMV Max runs a single campaign that tests all tagged product videos, optimizes against a target product ROI, and checks buyers out inside TikTok.
cards.use_when: You have a TikTok Shop with tagged creator videos and want paid distribution that drives direct in-app purchases.
steps: Enter via the campaigns flow: sales objective → TikTok Shop destination → continue to GMV Max, or use the GMV Max tab directly.
Select the shop from the dropdown when creating a campaign. If it doesn't appear, link the Shop to your Business Center first.
Choose promote products or promote live. For a new account, the presenter recommends not promoting all products — start with your top sellers.

Note the constraint: you can only run one GMV Max campaign per product, so a single campaign covering many products limits future flexibility. The presenter's default is to take the top 20% of products (using historical order data to rank) into one campaign. If you have no sales history, you must estimate the top products yourself.

Set product ROI. TikTok suggests a target (the source shows 1.2, which the presenter notes is often below break-even for ecommerce). The presenter takes TikTok's recommendation and adds 1.0 to it (1.2 → 2.2), then watches impressions over the next few days and lowers it if nothing is delivering. Setting ROI too high can stop ads from showing at all.
Set the daily budget at roughly double your target cost per acquisition (the example: $30 target CPA → $60/day). TikTok will always push for more spend than you set.

Adjust special promotion days: left at defaults, TikTok can raise budget by 50% and multiply it up to 10x, which turned a $60 budget into a $360 maximum in the example. The presenter narrows it to 50% with a 1x limit, keeping the setting on for genuine holiday demand.

For ad creative, the presenter recommends leaving auto-select on so TikTok rapidly tests incoming tagged videos, pauses underperformers and amplifies better-ROI ones. You can instead manage specific authorized posts, affiliate posts, custom posts or uploaded videos.
caveats: The 'add 1.0 to TikTok's recommended ROI' and 'double target CPA' rules are the presenter's heuristics, not verified benchmarks.
The one-campaign-per-product limit is a structural constraint that shapes how you group products.
Auto-select means TikTok chooses creative; you trade control for automated testing.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Monitor GMV Max creative performance and boost winning ads
cards.summary: Use GMV Max analytics and the creatives view to see which videos are delivering, and apply a creative boost to push extra daily budget behind winners.
cards.use_when: Your GMV Max campaign is live and you need to see which tagged videos are actually running and where to add incremental spend.
steps: Open the campaign analytics and find the product list with availability, then use view creative to see the videos attached to each product and their statuses.

Interpret statuses: in queue (ready to be tested for conversion potential), learning phase, delivering, and not delivering (tested and no longer producing results, so TikTok pauses it automatically). All of this happens without manual intervention.
When a video is delivering strong return, apply a creative boost by clicking that ad and requesting a daily boost of at least $10/day, with an optional end date.
Account for the boost stacking on top of campaign spend — a $60/day campaign plus a $10 boost becomes a $70/day maximum.

Use the creatives view to see how many creators are producing videos and each creator's gross revenue contribution, so you can identify which creators and individual ads deserve their own dedicated campaign.
Take repeatedly winning videos and run them in their own GMV Max campaign where the one-campaign-per-product rule permits.
caveats: Creative boost minimum is $10/day and is additional to campaign budget — do not treat it as a reallocation.
Statuses and analytics views are interface-dependent; verify current labels in Ads Manager.
The source's $4,000 spend / $12,000 revenue example (~3 ROAS, described by the presenter as 'not awesome') is an individual case, not a performance standard.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Build retargeting audiences from website, engagement and shop activity
cards.summary: Use TikTok's audience manager to build custom audiences from pixel events, video engagement and TikTok Shop activity, then exclude purchasers to avoid wasted spend.
cards.use_when: You want to run TikTok remarketing to store visitors, content engagers or shop visitors and need to define the right audience rules.
steps: Make sure your TikTok pixel is installed and linked to the ad account before building audiences.
In Ads Manager, go to tools → audience manager → create audiences, and choose custom audience.

For website traffic audiences, define the action (page view, add to cart, initiate checkout, purchase) and select the pixel source. You can add a URL-contains rule so only a specific page type qualifies — for example the presenter references targeting pages containing 'product' to reach product-page visitors.
Add an exclusion for purchasers: exclude users who completed a purchase in the last 30 days from a site-visitor audience, so you don't pay to re-reach customers you already converted.
Keep auto-refresh on so the audience is refreshed periodically (the presenter references a 30-day refresh).

Leave off the option to expand the audience with machine-learning-identified users — the presenter prefers knowing he is actually remarketing, arguing that adding lookalike-style expansion defeats the purpose and is no different from broad targeting.
Expect a delay before the audience is usable — initially it shows as unavailable and typically takes around 24 hours to match.

Build lookalike audiences from a strong source, ideally a purchasers-based custom audience, choosing a narrow/balanced/broad option (the presenter usually picks balanced) and setting the target location.
caveats: Auto-refresh interval and the 24-hour match time are the source's observations; platform behavior may vary.
The choice to leave off audience expansion is the presenter's opinion and a trade-off, not a universal best practice — expanding may increase reach.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Run TikTok retargeting campaigns with budget-tiered audience structure
cards.summary: Apply the retargeting audiences in a sales campaign via manual targeting, and scale the number of retargeting and re-engagement campaigns as budget grows.
cards.use_when: You have built TikTok retargeting audiences and want a campaign structure that matches your monthly ad budget.
steps: Create a campaign with the sales objective and website traffic destination continuation, then at the audience step switch to manual targeting.

Under custom audiences, use the include dropdown to add the audiences you built (e.g. website visitors last 30 days, or a lookalike once populated), then continue through the rest of the campaign build as normal.
At budgets around $3,000 or less, the presenter recommends one prospecting campaign testing two audiences and one retargeting campaign for website visitors in the last 30 days.

As budget grows, add narrower retargeting tiers such as website visitors (last 7 days) who did not purchase, and add-to-cart in the last 30 days, potentially with different offers or promotions to bring people back.

At larger budgets (the presenter cites ~$10K+), add a dedicated re-engagement campaign targeting people who engage with your content, and run the GMV Max campaign alongside retargeting so the campaign types work together to scale.
Consider adding a lookalike built from your purchasers audience once the source custom audience has populated.
caveats: The $3,000 and $10K figures are the presenter's budget-tier heuristics for structuring campaigns, not derived benchmarks.
Lookalikes require a populated source audience before they can be created.
The presenter's view that expansion/expansion-based targeting is essentially broad targeting is an opinion; test in your account.
cards.source_name: The BEST TikTok Ads Course For Beginners in 2026.docx

cards.title: Audit Performance Max Spend Distribution Before Replacing It
cards.summary: Break down where PMax actually spends your budget — roughly 60-70% Shopping, 20-30% search text, 5-10% image/video retargeting — to see which components you can rebuild with better control.
cards.use_when: When deciding whether to keep leaning on Performance Max or to build manual campaign structures, and you need evidence of what PMax is doing with the budget.
steps: Before changing anything, pull the spend distribution inside your Performance Max campaign and estimate the split across Shopping, search text ads, and image/video placements. The source's observed pattern across accounts is roughly 60-70% Shopping, 20-30% search, and 5-10% image/video, but verify your own numbers.
Recognize that the image/video portion is reportedly near-100% retargeting rather than cold prospecting, so any ROAS credited to it is largely re-engaging existing visitors, not new customers.
Note that PMax does not expose quality score, ad-group structure, brand vs non-brand splits, or audience/placement-level reporting, which limits your ability to diagnose and optimize.
Use these observations to decide which of the three components to rebuild first — most advertisers start with Standard Shopping because it absorbs the majority of spend.
Set expectations: PMax is described as a reasonable starting point for beginners or low-time operators; the rebuild is aimed at advertisers with capacity to manage more structure.
caveats: The spend percentages are the presenter's typical observation, not a guaranteed split for every account.
Rebuilding campaigns requires ongoing management time; the source explicitly frames this as an advanced-advertiser strategy.
cards.source_name: The Best E-commerce Google Ads Strategy for 2026.docx

cards.title: Performance-Based Shopping Structure by ROAS Tiers
cards.summary: Segment Standard Shopping products into four ROAS/spend tiers when product margins are similar, so budget flows to proven winners, zombies get tested, and inefficient spend is cut.
cards.use_when: Setting up or restructuring Standard Shopping campaigns for a store where product-level profit margins are within about 10% of each other.
steps: Confirm this structure applies: the source recommends it when profit margins are similar across products (within roughly 10% at product level). If margins vary widely, use the gross-profit-margin structure instead.
Tier 1 — high-ROAS products: allocate more budget to scale winners.
Tier 2 — low-ROAS products currently getting spend but converting poorly: reduce bids to improve efficiency.
Tier 3 — low-spend products with insufficient data: give them more opportunity to accumulate data and prove themselves.
Tier 4 — 'zombie' products with zero spend that have never been tested: isolate into their own campaign with a dedicated budget to revive potential hidden gems.
Build these as separate campaigns so each tier has its own budget and bidding control rather than relying on a single algorithm-managed pool.
Feed the tier assignments from your historical ROAS and spend data, and revisit the tiers as new data arrives.
caveats: Tier classification depends on having enough historical spend/conversion data; new products may sit in Tier 3 by default.
The four-tier labels and the ~10% margin-similarity threshold are the source's heuristics, not universal rules.
cards.source_name: The Best E-commerce Google Ads Strategy for 2026.docx

cards.title: Gross Profit Margin Shopping Structure When Margins Vary
cards.summary: When product margins differ widely, build Shopping campaigns around margin tiers and set lower ROAS targets on high-margin items and higher targets on low-margin items to stay profitable at scale.
cards.use_when: Structuring Standard Shopping campaigns for a catalog where product-level margins vary significantly (the source cites roughly 30% to 70% as an example range).
steps: Segment products into margin tiers — the source typically uses three to five tiers depending on catalog size and conversion volume. A simple version uses high, mid, and low margin.
Build a separate campaign per margin tier so you can assign distinct ROAS targets.
For high-margin products, set a lower ROAS target so you can bid more aggressively and capture more volume — even at lower ROAS you remain profitable because the margin is high.
For low-margin products, set a higher ROAS target to stay conservative, since there is less room for error and less profit per sale.
Remember the underlying insight: PMax does not know your product margins and treats every product the same, so this margin-aware structure is something only you can impose.
Review margin tiers periodically as supplier costs or pricing change, since the structure's value depends on accurate margin data.
caveats: The 30-70% margin range is an illustrative example, not a benchmark.
Three-to-five tiers is a starting heuristic; too few products or conversions per tier weakens the approach.
cards.source_name: The Best E-commerce Google Ads Strategy for 2026.docx

cards.title: Shopping Feed Optimization: Titles, Images, Budget Priority
cards.summary: Beyond campaign structure, optimize keyword-rich product titles, high-quality images, and give Shopping the largest share of your Google Ads budget since it is the core ecommerce placement.
cards.use_when: Improving Standard Shopping campaign performance for a store — particularly product feed quality and cross-campaign budget allocation.
steps: Rewrite product titles to be keyword-rich: include the most important search terms shoppers use to find the product directly in the title, so the ad surfaces on more relevant searches and earns more clicks.
Upgrade product images: high-quality images stand out in the Shopping carousel and directly affect click-through rate.

Control budget allocation deliberately: because you are building Shopping yourself, you can prioritize it and give it the lion's share of the overall Google Ads budget — the source calls Shopping the bread and butter for ecommerce on Google Ads.
Hold these feed-level improvements as ongoing tasks rather than one-off fixes, since titles and images affect both impressions and CTR.
Treat budget priority as a deliberate allocation decision you can now make, unlike when PMax auto-splits budget across placements.
caveats: The 'lion's share of budget' guidance is the presenter's recommendation for ecommerce, not a calculated optimum for every account.
Title and image gains are described as affecting impressions and CTR, not a quantified ROAS lift.
cards.source_name: The Best E-commerce Google Ads Strategy for 2026.docx

cards.title: Separate Brand and Non-Brand Search Campaigns
cards.summary: Split branded and non-branded search traffic into distinct campaigns so you can see true incremental performance and set brand ROAS targets much higher than non-brand targets.
cards.use_when: Restructuring Google Search campaigns to reveal true incremental acquisition and avoid PMax's tendency to over-index on branded traffic.
steps: Create separate campaigns for brand queries (searches for your company/brand name) and non-brand queries. PMax does not separate these by default, which the source says leads it to over-rely on branded traffic.

Recognize that brand traffic is less incremental: those searchers already know you and likely first arrived via another channel, so a brand click-to-purchase is often a sale you would have gotten anyway.
Set a much higher ROAS target for the brand campaign because brand converts more easily and is less incremental; set a lower ROAS target for non-brand because those sales are more incremental.
Use the separated reporting to view brand ROAS and non-brand ROAS as distinct numbers, then control the brand vs non-brand budget split — shift budget to non-brand if you are over-indexed on brand.
Build a dedicated strategy to grow non-brand keyword presence, which the source identifies as where real business growth comes from.
Note that the source still sees value in bidding on brand in Google, but with much higher ROAS expectations.
caveats: Brand and non-brand ROAS targets will differ substantially; the source does not provide universal numbers.
The claim that branded sales are usually non-incremental is the presenter's view and may vary by business.
cards.source_name: The Best E-commerce Google Ads Strategy for 2026.docx

cards.title: Use Fewer Headlines and Descriptions to Speed Ad Testing
cards.summary: Limit responsive search ad assets to roughly 8 headlines and 2 descriptions instead of Google's maximum, so each combination accumulates enough impressions to actually be tested.
cards.use_when: Writing or revising responsive search ad copy and wanting interpretable test results rather than an untested combinatorial sprawl.
steps: Reduce asset count: the source typically uses 8 headlines and 2 descriptions in place of Google's recommended maximum of 15 headlines and 4 descriptions.
Understand the rationale: fewer assets produce fewer possible combinations, so each combination is more likely to receive enough impressions to test meaningfully.
Create multiple ads per ad group and rotate/test them so you can learn which copy drives better CTR and conversions.
Feed those learnings back into quality score improvement, since copy relevance affects quality score, CPC, and ad position.
Keep the strongest, most differentiated headlines in rotation rather than padding the count to hit a platform suggestion.
Verify the current asset limits and recommendations in the Google Ads interface, as platform guidance changes.
caveats: The 8-headline/2-description setup is the presenter's preference, not a platform requirement.
Reducing assets trades breadth of automated combinations for cleaner test data — a deliberate choice, not a universal best practice.
cards.source_name: The Best E-commerce Google Ads Strategy for 2026.docx

cards.title: Build Single-Themed Ad Groups from Keyword and PMax Search-Term Research
cards.summary: Mine the PMax search terms report plus Keyword Planner for proven queries, then organize keywords into single-themed ad groups with matching ad copy to raise relevance and quality score.
cards.use_when: Structuring Search campaigns and writing ad copy after deciding to move search traffic out of PMax.
steps: Research your market's keywords using Google Ads Keyword Planner.
Additionally, mine your PMax search terms report for the best-performing queries — the search terms already driving sales inside PMax.
Pull those proven terms out and use them in your dedicated Search campaigns alongside the keywords found in Keyword Planner.
Organize keywords into single-themed ad groups (STAGs), with each ad group focused on one theme.
Write ad copy customized to each ad group's theme, which improves relevance, improves quality score, and reduces costs.
Confirm the exact report names and locations in the current Google Ads interface, since UI labels change.
caveats: PMax search terms reporting can be limited or delayed depending on account settings; verify what's available.
The quality-score-to-cost relationship is directional; the source gives no specific savings figures.
cards.source_name: The Best E-commerce Google Ads Strategy for 2026.docx

cards.title: Use Quality Score Visibility to Cut Search Costs
cards.summary: Monitor per-keyword quality score in manual Search campaigns — something PMax hides — because it affects CPC and ad position and can be improved through relevance work.
cards.use_when: Optimizing existing Search campaigns for efficiency and diagnosing high CPCs.
steps: Open your manual Search campaigns (not PMax, where quality score is not visible) and review quality score at the keyword level.
Identify keywords with weak quality scores and investigate relevance issues — for example, ad copy that does not match the query theme or landing page mismatch.
Apply the fixes available in manual Search that PMax does not allow: split-test ad copy, run campaign experiments, and inspect search terms.
Reallocate or pause keywords where the cost of poor quality score outweighs the value of the traffic.
Re-check scores periodically, since quality score moves with relevance and performance over time.
caveats: Quality score is described as directionally affecting CPC and position; the source offers no quantified relationship.
This optimization only exists if you run manual Search campaigns — it is not available inside PMax.
cards.source_name: The Best E-commerce Google Ads Strategy for 2026.docx

cards.title: Set Up Demand Gen Retargeting with PMax's Winning Creative
cards.summary: Move proven PMax image and video creative into a single Demand Gen retargeting campaign so the algorithm can switch a user seamlessly between image and video ads with consolidated data.
cards.use_when: Building the image/video retargeting component of an ecommerce Google Ads structure to replace PMax's opaque retargeting.
steps: If you have been running PMax, identify the videos and images that have been performing, and reuse that winning creative in the Demand Gen campaign rather than starting from scratch.
Put images and videos into the same Demand Gen campaign for consolidated data, which lets the algorithm track an individual user and switch between image and video retargeting formats.
Set up the campaign as a retargeting campaign using your best creative assets.
Expect better reporting than PMax provides — audience-level and placement/network-level data — which is the basis for the creative optimization steps that follow.
Verify current Demand Gen campaign setup options in Google Ads, as campaign types and interfaces evolve.
caveats: This replaces PMax's image/video retargeting with an equivalent but more controllable setup; it is not a cold-prospecting solution in the source's framing.
Reusing PMax creative assumes you have enough PMax history to identify winners.
cards.source_name: The Best E-commerce Google Ads Strategy for 2026.docx
