cards.summary: Branded query performance is treated as reputation management — you should be the first result for your own brand name.
cards.use_when: Auditing branded search performance, deciding whether to invest in brand-term pages, or comparing your branded click share to a competitor's.
steps: Run searches for your brand name, brand + product, and brand + category (the source's examples: 'Reliance', 'Reliance Phone', 'Nike official website').
Confirm your own site holds the top slot for each, and that the result being served presents accurate information about the brand, offer and price.
Where a third-party page outranks you for your own brand term, treat it as a reputation and brand-SEO problem, not a generic keyword problem.
Use Google Business listing and site links to extend the branded result set with controlled information.

Check branded performance in Search Console impressions and clicks — the source's example shows the brand name receiving 2,416 impressions compared to a product term at 74,000, and notes that a brand term should be a reliable click earner.
Compare against how competitors present in the same branded space; the source describes Google as continually evaluating your branding and prominence when ranking branded queries.
caveats: The source asserts Google gives first-page treatment to highly authorised branded sites such as Amazon, Wikipedia and Flipkart — treat as the presenter's observation.
Brand rankings should not be assumed; verify with real queries in your own market.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Compete on original, current content rather than copied product copy
cards.summary: Original, regularly refreshed content is the source's stated defence against ranking decay, especially in categories where manufacturers supply identical descriptions.
cards.use_when: Writing collection and product copy on a store that carries manufacturer-supplied descriptions, or planning content maintenance.
steps: Assume your competitors use the same product descriptions you do. Write unique product and category copy that adds information not present in the manufacturer's sheet.
Refresh dated content on a schedule. The source's example: content titled for a past year becomes worthless the moment that year ends, so rewrite the title and content for the current season.
Update content when products, configurations or specifications change. The source uses the keypad-to-smartphone shift to show that search demand migrates away from obsolete product generations.

Do not copy the same conversion strategy as competitors (add-to-cart, wishlist, PayPal/card checkout) and stop there — differentiate on the offer, reviews, case studies, feedback and incentives the buyer actually looks for.

Watch competitor originals: the source notes title tags on category pages for skincare retailers being nearly indistinguishable ('shop best skincare products…' vs. 'best skin care products online at best price…'), and shows Amazon and Nykaa holding the top two positions with strong rating signals.
Note the practical ceiling: the source says beating Amazon outright is unrealistic, so aim to outrank the sites below the major platforms by following the same principles better.
caveats: The source's warning that AI-generated copy is detected and devalued is the presenter's assertion; it advises using generative AI for reference or ideas rather than final copy.
The example SERP positions are a single snapshot, not a fixed ranking outcome.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Use eye-tracking and click-tracking principles to shape UX that converts
cards.summary: Users scan rather than read, so design the top band to hold attention and instrument the actions you want them to take.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a storefront, category page or landing page for whether it sustains attention long enough for the visitor to buy or subscribe.
steps: Assume visitors do not read the whole page — the source's F-pattern observation says they read horizontally and in short bands. Put the product name, logo, price and main offer in that first visual band.
Make the visual appearance clear and high quality. The source flags blurred, low-quality images as a reason visitors leave a page they arrived at from Google.
Ensure information availability: the query the visitor typed should be visibly answered within the first scroll band, not several screens down.

Provide enough product visuals for evaluating physical goods — the source's example is a t-shirt where buyers want to see the front, sides, left, right and bottom views, and notes AI try-on/image tools being used.

Instrument the actions: tag add-to-cart, begin-checkout and form submit as GA4 events so click tracking tells you whether people are engaging or leaving. In the source's example these events are visible per page path in the events report.

Read the click-tracking output as your engagement and conversion measure: add-to-cart, checkout initiation and purchase are the ecommerce engagement signals to watch, while a submit button plays that role for non-ecommerce sites.
caveats: The source presents eye-tracking and F-pattern as general design guidance rather than a page-level testing standard.
The source's claim that good UX lifts rankings is indirect: it argues low bounce and continued clicking are read by Google as authority.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Use social media as an adjacent channel that feeds brand search
cards.summary: Social profiles are a visible trust layer on the site and a place to publish current offers; over-marketing without relevance destroys the benefit.
cards.use_when: Planning promotional calendars for a store or deciding whether to invest in profiles and content beyond the site.
steps: Put social follow icons visibly on the site (the source's example shows Facebook, Instagram and YouTube icons on a skincare storefront).
Publish recent, relevant updates on those profiles — offer launches, discounts, seasonal moments such as Christmas and Valentine's Day — so the profiles look active to visitors who check them.

Use the freshness of activity to signal a live business: the source contrasts posts from hours/days ago with an old YouTube video, and notes videos are typically created only when there is a new offer.
Create posts and video yourself with available tools if you own the site, rather than waiting on a client or agency.
For community, use Facebook pages and groups to connect members around the relevant interest, and keep discussions relevant to that topic.
Avoid high-frequency irrelevant promotion — the source explicitly warns over-marketing distracts the audience and wastes effort.
caveats: The source's follower counts and post recency are from one example site, not a benchmark.
The source gives no measurement method for attributing social activity to search or revenue.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Avoid black hat SEO that produces short-lived rankings and penalties
cards.summary: Keyword stuffing, arbitrary pages and other unethical shortcuts are detected within months and downgrade the site.
cards.use_when: Choosing between a fast ranking tactic and a sustainable one, or reviewing an inherited SEO strategy for risky practices.
steps: Recognise the tactics the source names as penalised: keyword stuffing, creating arbitrary pages, and other unethical volume tactics.
Understand the risk profile: the source says Google identifies these tactics within a month or two and penalises the site, lowering rankings and reducing credibility in the search engine's eyes.
Note that even experienced SEO practitioners can violate search engine terms without intending to, because the pressure to rank fast encourages shortcuts.
Anchor content decisions to quality: the source repeats that content is king, and says a technically perfect site with weak content will rank nowhere.
Write so people stay and read rather than bounce — bounce rate is the signal the source ties back to content quality.
Expect continuous algorithm changes each year targeting content quality, spam links and user experience; keep practices aligned with published guidelines rather than chasing loopholes.
caveats: The source's specific detection timeframe is illustrative rather than a documented enforcement window.
The source notes black hat SEO was easier to get away with years ago — an observation about historical conditions, not a current tactic.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Choose the right keywords before worrying about traffic volume
cards.summary: Wrong keyword selection sends you outside the box entirely — keyword, audience and content must be chosen in that order.
cards.use_when: Selecting target terms for a new store's category pages, or re-evaluating why a keyword strategy is not producing conversions.
steps: Start by confirming the keyword reflects real demand for what you actually sell, rather than the term you find easiest to write about.
Account for keyword competition explicitly: the source's example is every iPhone seller targeting the same term, so assume you are bidding for a shared term with Amazon, Flipkart and others.
Decide your realistic ceiling. The source says no one can easily beat Amazon, so target the positions below the major platforms on head terms rather than assuming you can outrank them.
Then check audience fit before content quality. The source states the three are sequential: right keyword, right audience, then content.
Map each chosen keyword to the page type that satisfies its intent (informational, navigational, transactional) rather than sending all traffic to a single landing page.

Treat keyword competition and conversion competition separately: competitors often run identical conversion flows (add-to-cart, wishlist, PayPal/card), so keyword choice is where you can differentiate most cheaply.
caveats: The source does not provide volume, difficulty or ROI thresholds — it argues qualitatively.
The speaker's 'never target the wrong keyword' advice is a heuristic for prioritisation, not a rule that guarantees outcomes.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Teach yourself to read a live SERP before writing a page
cards.summary: Inspecting the actual results for your target query shows what format and what level of detail is already winning.
cards.use_when: Before creating a category page, collection page or product landing page, or when diagnosing why a page is outranked.
steps: Run the target query (e.g., 'skincare products India' or 'iPhone 17 Pro Max') and inspect the composition of the page: which pages are ads, which are organic, and which are marketplaces versus brands versus independent stores.

Note that navigational results appear where the brand is already known — the source's example shows Apple's own page ranked ahead of retailers for its own product, followed by a third-party specification/review site, then Wikipedia.
Look at the title tags competitors are using on collection pages — the source compares near-identical formulations and notes several skincare retailers competing on the same phrasing.
Note which results carry ratings, rich snippets and offers, and which pages show stock status ('sold out' in the source's example), since these visible signals shape which result gets clicked.

Audit the winning competitor page's depth. In the source's example, one competitor page is fast and shows offers, colours and capacity, while another has sparse tech specs — the implication is that the more complete page presents a stronger buying case.
Use what you learn to set the content and feature checklist for your own page before writing, not after.
caveats: SERP composition varies by market, device and time; the source's snapshots are illustrative.
The source says major marketplaces will rank for high-volume terms; your realistic target is the pages beneath them.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Audit Flash and JavaScript bloat as page-experience obstacles
cards.summary: Treat obsolete Flash embeds and unused or glitchy JavaScript as indexing and speed barriers to clean up on an ecommerce storefront.
cards.use_when: Running a technical SEO audit on your storefront's page experience before paid traffic or a redesign push.
steps: Inventory any remaining Flash elements. The source states web crawlers cannot index Flash files and outdated elements reduce visitor interest, so Flash should be limited rather than occupying whole areas of the page.

Note the source's qualification: limited Flash use can actually help ranking, but heavy Flash slows load speed — the same page-speed struggle you find in the page-speed report. Prefer building product visuals in HTML/CSS where possible.
Check the unused-JavaScript section of your page-speed report. Unused scripts occupy space, slow the site, and show in the red zone, which the source says impacts rankings.

Have a developer clean up dead scripts and JavaScript glitches from the back end. The source frames failure to clean code as something Google reads as a poor impression and that blocks the indexing you want.
Recheck page speed for both desktop and mobile, since Google reports the two separately.
Verify current tool interface locations (page-speed report sections, CMS code access) before relying on any specific menu path.
caveats: The source's Flash advice is largely legacy guidance; Flash is dead technology, so treat this as an illustration of the broader rule that unindexable, heavy embeds hurt stores.
The relationship between page speed and rankings is stated loosely; no numeric speed threshold is given.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Confirm your store already has an auto-generated XML sitemap instead of building one
cards.summary: Modern CMS platforms auto-generate XML sitemaps, so verify and submit the existing one rather than generating sitemaps manually.
cards.use_when: Setting up technical SEO for a new store on Shopify, WordPress, or another CMS, especially with hundreds or thousands of product pages.
steps: Check the CMS for a built-in sitemap before reaching for a generator. The source notes WordPress (e.g. RankMath plugin) and Shopify expose sitemap creation as a one-click toggle in the backend, and a site over 500 pages certainly needs one.
Toggle the sitemap setting on and confirm its status. In the source's WordPress example the RankMath sitemap switch was already on.

Verify live visibility by visiting sitemap.xml. The source demonstrates that a WordPress site redirected to sitemap_index.xml instead, listing posts, pages and attachments — expect CMS-specific sitemap URLs.
If a store truly has no sitemap, a free generator such as sitemap-generator.com can produce an HTML or XML file; XML is the format to prefer for search engines.
Submit the sitemap in Google Search Console and reference it in robots.txt so crawlers can find it.
For a store with thousands of SKUs, discuss with your CMS/plugin whether product, collection, image and video sitemaps are generated automatically.
caveats: Sitemap generator tools and CMS sitemap URLs change; verify the current interface before acting.
No fixed page-count rule is supported beyond the source's remark that 500+ pages requires a sitemap.
Sitemaps support discovery; submission does not guarantee crawling, indexing or rankings.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Match sitemap type to audience: XML for crawlers, HTML for shoppers
cards.summary: XML sitemaps feed search bots while HTML sitemaps help human navigation, and each carries a different SEO role.
cards.use_when: Deciding which sitemap to expose when structuring store navigation, a large category tree, or orphaned product pages.
steps: For crawlers, use an XML sitemap. The source states search bots crawl using XML sitemaps and that these are not visible to users. Each URL entry can carry last-modified, modification details and priority — in the demonstration the homepage carried priority 1.0 and other pages lower values like 0.88.

For shoppers, consider an HTML sitemap: a visible list of links guiding visitors to available content. The source says it aids navigation and supplies helpful internal links but has limited SEO value on its own.

Expect different sitemap flavours depending on content type: video sitemaps for /videos, image sitemaps for JPG/PNG/SVG assets, news sitemaps for /article or /news, and product/collection paths on ecommerce sites. WordPress sites surface posts and pages instead.
Once generated, update robots.txt with the sitemap URL and submit via Search Console so crawlers find a store's product and category URLs faster.
If you ever need a text or RSS version, the source notes you can convert between formats, but XML is the most commonly used.
caveats: The source's priority values are illustrative output from a generator, not a prescribed ranking formula.
HTML sitemaps are noted as having limited direct SEO value, so do not treat them as a substitute for clean internal linking.
Sitemaps support discovery; submission does not guarantee crawling, indexing or rankings.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Use Ahrefs keyword difficulty filters to find rankable store keywords
cards.summary: Filter keyword lists by volume and difficulty (KD 0–40) to find terms a new or small store can realistically rank for.
cards.use_when: Choosing which product, category or content keywords to target for a new or low-authority ecommerce store.
steps: Open the keyword research tool's keyword explorer (source uses Ahrefs), enter a seed term and set location to your actual market. The source stresses: if you don't serve Miami, do not target 'Miami SEO agency' style terms.
Read the difficulty band. In the source's example 'SEO' had 247K volume but 'super hard' KD, meaning it is not easy to rank because it is a very general term.
Apply a KD filter of 0–40 for a first phase to surface realistically targetable terms, then scan results for terms you can actually serve.
Exclude terms containing agency names or locations you don't operate in; keep general or service-relevant terms.

Check intent labels: informational, navigational, transactional or commercial. The source shows 'best SEO software' reads as commercial/informational because people want to buy, while 'what is SEO' is informational. Pick keywords whose intent matches your page type.

Inspect the ranking competitors before committing. A term dominated by high-authority sites (domain authority 90+ in the example) is a poor early target — the source warns a very competitive keyword may not appear in the top 100 pages at all.
caveats: Ahrefs KD bands, volumes and filters are tool-specific and change; verify the current interface.
The source's numbers are a demonstration of one keyword, not a benchmark for any other term.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Mine question keywords and filter by KD when planning store content
cards.summary: Question-based informational keywords reveal what shoppers ask, and filtering to low difficulty helps new stores rank for them.
cards.use_when: Planning blog, guide or FAQ content that supports an ecommerce store's SEO and attracts early-stage shoppers.
steps: In the keyword tool, open the 'questions people ask' section for your seed term (e.g. SEO shows 'what is SEO', 'what is SEO audit', 'is SEO dead', 'how long does it take').
Filter question keywords to a realistic difficulty band (the source used KD 0–40) to find terms a small site could target.
Check the intent label for each question. The source shows the intent field telling you whether a query is informational, navigational or transactional.
Discard questions irrelevant to your business context — the source excludes a celebrity/host query as off-topic and says to stick to general, relevant terms.
Sort the remaining list by search volume to prioritise, then shape content around the wording of the questions so those terms can rank and gain visibility.
For each chosen question, inspect which competitors hold the top positions and whether AI overviews, People Also Ask or authoritative blogs dominate the result before committing resource.
caveats: The source's specific volumes and difficulty values belong to its demo term, not your niche.
The presenter distinguishes informational, navigational and transactional queries as loose intent categories, not precise measurement.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Assess competitor authority and SERP features before choosing a keyword
cards.summary: Check who already ranks and whether AI overviews or People Also Ask appear before deciding a keyword is worth pursuing.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether a target product or content keyword is realistically winnable for your store.
steps: Search the candidate keyword and inspect the first-page results. The source's example for 'what is SEO' returned an AI overview, People Also Ask, and a well-known blog.

Identify the domains ranking. In the demonstration they included a high-authority SEO blog (domain authority 91/100), Wikipedia, Reddit, Mailchimp and others — the source notes such sites are not beaten in a day because they have age and qualified writers.
Apply intent filters in the keyword tool (e.g. transactional/commercial) to see whether buying-intent queries even exist for your topic before writing.
If high-authority and community platforms dominate the term, prefer lower-difficulty or less-crowded alternatives rather than fighting for a term where you appear nowhere in the top 100.
For each surviving keyword, note intent so the page you build matches the query type (definition, comparison, or purchase).
caveats: Domain authority and SERP layouts change constantly; the 91/100 figure is one moment in one niche.
Presence of an AI overview may reduce clicks, but the source does not quantify that effect; do not treat it as a hard rule that the keyword is unusable.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Choose a content format matched to the query and buyer stage
cards.summary: Listicles, how-to guides, blogs, video, opinion pieces and infographics each serve different search intents and commercial purposes.
cards.use_when: Deciding what format to publish for a store's content calendar — category education, product guides or brand-building.
steps: Use listicles for scannable roundups (source example: '10 proven SEO techniques to boost your ranking in 2025') where readers want ranked options — useful for category or 'best of' style pages that support product browsing.

Use how-to guides for step-by-step tutorials, requiring clarity and concision, e.g. 'how to submit your website to Google Search Console step-by-step'. Good for setup, care or usage content around physical products.
Use blogs for engagement and trust-building with well-written, relevant discussion pieces; the source notes blogs establish authority, credibility and relationships.
Use video for demonstrations where showing beats telling, but the source insists video must be relevant and systematic — if it doesn't actually answer the query, viewers won't come.
Use opinion pieces to share unique perspectives and position the brand as a thought leader, encouraging discussion.
Use infographics to visualise data, stats or timelines — the source's examples chart algorithm changes or AI adoption year by year.
Match format to intent: transactional shoppers often need comparisons and guides, while informational searchers want definitions and how-tos.
caveats: The source gives no evidence about which format converts better for ecommerce; treat format choice as fit-to-query, not a proven sales lever.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Apply personalization and localization to store content and offers
cards.summary: Personalization uses shopper details to prioritise relevance; localization targets the right message to the right region at the right time.
cards.use_when: Adapting PDP copy, offers or messaging for specific regions, languages or returning customers.
steps: For personalization, capture and use shopper details (first name, last name, address, phone, messages/concerns) as the source demonstrates at the add-to-cart stage, to make marketing prioritise the individual customer.

For localization, define it as sending the right message at the right time to the right customer, then build region-specific offers. The source's coaching example targets local students with a 20–30% discount for board-exam prep — translate that principle into region-specific ecommerce promotions where relevant.
Speak the language of international customers and provide multilingual chat support. The source shows sites where users pick English US/UK/Asia, then country, then state, before chat appears.
Use complete business listings as a localization tactic — full business details help local discovery.
Use AI assistance to personalise and localise content, since the source notes AI understands that there is intent behind a search (buying a washing machine, then searching how to use it).
Validate that the localized offer is legally and logistically serviceable in that region before publishing.
caveats: The discount percentages come from a coaching example; they are not benchmarks for ecommerce.
Personalisation depends on consent and lawful data handling, which the source does not address.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Read engagement, bounce and conversion metrics by page in GA4
cards.summary: Use engagement rate, bounce rate and ecommerce purchase data at page level to find which store pages hold attention and drive purchases.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing which product, blog or landing pages hold shoppers and which lose them, as a basis for content and PDP improvements.
steps: Open the pages report rather than a channel report when you want to know which pages people spend time on — the source explains channel view won't show per-page time.
Sort by engagement rate. The source shows a blog page at 100% engagement with users sticking around, interpreted as useful content, and a correspondingly 0% bounce rate.

Cross-check ecommerce purchases under monetization. In the demonstration, 4,486 items had been purchased and one lotion SKU accounted for 96 items, shown as 2.14% of the total — the source cautions this is not the correct conversion rate.

Get the real transaction conversion rate from a data-studio style report or filtered view, because the default ecommerce table percentage is not the same as transaction conversion. In the source's data studio example the overall conversion rate was shown as 26.8K with a 43% improvement over the comparison period, and a user conversion rate of 99.9% — treat these as report-specific outputs.
For click-through rate, use Google Search Console; for traffic channels and frequency, use GA acquisition reports.
Export the page-level data (the source uses export to Google Sheets) and compute period-over-period differences to find pages with declining traffic to focus on.
caveats: The source's numbers belong to one skincare website and are not benchmarks.
GA4 and data studio interfaces change; verify current report paths and metric definitions before trusting a figure.
Distinguish engagement rate, bounce rate and transaction conversion rate — the source explicitly warns the default ecommerce-table percentage is not the true conversion rate.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Spot declining pages by comparing active users period over period
cards.summary: Export page-level traffic for two periods and subtract to surface pages losing users so you can prioritise their recovery.
cards.use_when: Monthly ecommerce content and SEO review to find PDPs, category pages or blog posts that are losing organic traffic.
steps: In GA4, open acquisition traffic and select your reporting month, comparing with the previous period.
Remove the channel breakdown and add page/screen as the dimension so each row is a page.
Export to Google Sheets. Set current-period and previous-period columns side by side.
Compute the difference (current minus previous) in a new column — pressing equals and clicking the cells auto-fills the reference.
Select the difference column and sort Z to A to see the pages with the biggest drop first. The source describes these as the important pages to focus on next month to recover traffic.
Ignore noise pages like account/login, which the source says people don't target for SEO and which shouldn't distract from commercial pages.
Repeat the process monthly and keep the sheet as a rolling log.
caveats: The source's example comparison windows are arbitrary (e.g. 1 October vs previous 31 days); choose windows that match your seasonality.
A difference column alone doesn't explain cause — pair it with Search Console before acting.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Install GA4 by adding the measurement tag to the site head
cards.summary: Create a GA4 property, place the Google tag in the head, then verify installation in real time.
cards.use_when: Setting up analytics on a new or redesigned storefront so you can see traffic, behaviour and ecommerce revenue.
steps: Sign in to Google Analytics with a Google ID and open Admin (bottom-left gear). Under the account column choose create, name the account, click next.

Enter property details: property name, reporting time zone and currency. The source notes the currency matters for ecommerce and advises setting it up properly now even if you won't use it immediately.

Choose business details and business objectives. The source notes you cannot leave other objectives checked when selecting one — it recommends selecting the relevant ones such as generate leads, drive sales, understand traffic, and engagement/retention.
Accept the terms, select the Web platform, and enter the website URL and stream name to create the data stream.

From the data stream, view tag instructions and choose manual installation to reveal the Google tag snippet. In a Blogger back end the source pastes it under the theme's HTML head section; on other platforms place it immediately after the opening head tag.
The source warns: do not add more than one Google tag per page.

Verify installation: click the test button in the setup flow, then open Reports > Realtime overview and confirm views appear — the source also checks page source (Ctrl+U, then find) to confirm the tag is present.
caveats: Google Analytics and CMS interfaces change frequently; verify the current setup flow and tag format.
Realtime test results are momentary; the source shows 'views 1' from the presenter's own visit, which confirms installation but not production traffic.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Size the SEO opportunity with GA4 channel comparison
cards.summary: Compare organic channel users and sessions across two periods to see whether SEO is growing or slipping.
cards.use_when: Reporting store SEO performance to stakeholders or deciding whether to invest more in organic content.
steps: In the property that has traffic, open Reports > Acquisition > Traffic acquisition and set the date range (the source used one month) with compare to previous period toggled on.

Remove page-level rows so channels are visible, then look at the Organic channel. The source's example showed active users at 8,000 versus 5,000 previously, a 59% improvement, with sessions of roughly 9,000 versus 6,000.
Drill into organic pages to see where the traffic came from, then export to Google Sheets for further comparison of active users by page across periods.
Compare current and previous columns to identify whether organic growth is broad or concentrated in a few pages.
Confirm the data stream is actively collecting (the source shows 'data actively collecting past 48 hours' as a health check).
caveats: The source's channel figures are one account's example, not a benchmark.
Organic session counts do not equal revenue; combine with monetization data before judging SEO ROI.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Create and verify a Google Business Profile for local store discovery
cards.summary: A verified Google Business Profile places your store in maps and local packs, which matters for local and mobile searchers.
cards.use_when: Setting up or improving local SEO so nearby shoppers can find your store or service area.
steps: Start a Google Business Profile, name the business and pick a category that matches how customers search (the source uses a marketing agency example).

Decide whether customers can visit a location. If yes, add the address: street, city, postcode and state. If you're an online-only business, the source demonstrates selecting no for location and no for delivery/visits.
Place and confirm the map pin, add a phone number, and choose whether to verify now or later. The source emphasises that a profile only becomes visible after verification.
Add services or products the store offers (the source lists affiliate marketing, branding, SEO, digital marketing as examples) and set opening hours.
Write a business description and upload images. The source fills these to complete the profile.
Once verified, the listing appears in local packs, Google Maps and mobile search, and supports voice assistant results — the source's client example shows name, address and phone displayed.
caveats: Verification requirements and available fields change; verify the current Google Business Profile flow.
The source's example business address is random and not a real listing.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Use Google Search Console for crawl issues and indexing health
cards.summary: Search Console complements analytics by surfacing crawl errors, 404s and indexing status that GA4 does not show.
cards.use_when: Investigating why store pages are not being indexed or why organic impressions diverge from your expectations.
steps: Sign in to Google Search Console with the same Google ID used for analytics, then review the overview page.
Read the performance graph for queries and clicks, and the indexing report for how many pages are indexed versus not indexed. The source describes these as the two core views.
Install the verification code (the source demonstrates the account setup and code installation step-by-step).
Submit the XML sitemap within Search Console so crawlers can discover store URLs faster.
Check for 404 pages and other crawl errors, which the source identifies as a primary Search Console use case.
Use Search Console, not GA4, for click-through rate analysis at query level.
caveats: Search Console data is sampled and delayed, and the interface changes; verify current report names.
Search Console shows impressions and clicks, not revenue or add-to-cart behaviour — combine with GA4.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Use engagement and conversion metrics to diagnose shopper fit
cards.summary: Click-through rate, time on page and conversion rate are the user-behaviour signals the source highlights for SEO and commercial performance.
cards.use_when: Judging whether a store page is performing and deciding what to improve on a landing page or PDP.
steps: Track click-through rate in Google Search Console. The source's opinion is that a longer (higher) click-through rate correlates with more conversions — treat this as the presenter's claim, not a proven formula.
Track duration on page. The source suggests staying roughly 2–5 minutes signals something useful is there, but presents this as an informal rule of thumb rather than a benchmark.
Track conversion rate and check it in Analytics, using a data-studio style report for the genuine transaction conversion rate rather than the default ecommerce table figure.
Check frequency of visits and navigation channel (organic versus other mediums) to understand how shoppers arrive.

If you're saturated with competition, the source's advice is to improve existing products/services, offer meaningful discounts (e.g. 20–30%) and revisit pricing models rather than assume SEO alone will rescue you.
caveats: The 2–5 minute dwell target is the source's heuristic, not an established benchmark.
The link between CTR and conversion is stated as an opinion; it should be tested rather than assumed.
These store analytics metrics diagnose user experience and commercial outcomes; do not present them as verified direct Google ranking inputs.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Plan visually with mapping tools, but build strategy from competitor analysis
cards.summary: Visual site-mapping tools help structure a store's pages and keywords, but the source insists strategy comes from human analysis of competitors, not tool output alone.
cards.use_when: Planning a store's information architecture, category tree or keyword map before a build or migration.
steps: Use a visual sitemap builder (e.g. WriteMaps) to plan website pages and gather content into a sitemap without drawing every node by hand.

Consider collaborative mapping tools (the source names MindNode) for keyword research and tracking data as inputs to SEO strategy; other tools mentioned include streamingfrog, Slickplan, Dynomapper and RankMath.
Treat tool output as insight only. The source states no tool can create a strategy directly — the strategy is the manual work of analysing human behaviour and competitor activity.
For a large store, rely on CMS automation to cover the structure and navigation rather than mapping thousands of product pages manually.
Cross-check any planned architecture against how your CMS actually generates URLs (Shopify products/collections vs WordPress posts/pages).
caveats: Tool names and features will age; verify current offerings before adopting.
The source does not claim these tools cause ranking improvements — they are planning aids.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Prioritise low-difficulty, high-volume terms over vanity head keywords
cards.summary: The source's core keyword principle: pick terms with good volume and low difficulty so a store can gain visibility rather than chasing unwinnable head terms.
cards.use_when: Deciding which terms to target for a new store or a new category where you currently have no ranking.
steps: Start by sorting candidate keywords by volume in descending order to see the biggest opportunities.
Then apply the difficulty lens. The source warns that directly targeting a very high-competition keyword is very difficult — you may not appear anywhere in the top 100 pages.

For a first phase, filter to lower difficulty terms (the source uses 0–40 KD) and choose those with decent volume. The source's own phrasing is: choose keywords with good volume and low difficulty so it's easier to get visibility.
Reject terms that don't match your service footprint — don't target local terms for cities you don't serve.
Check the intent label for each shortlisted term and make sure the content or page type you'll build matches it.
Re-rank your shortlist by the balance of volume and difficulty rather than volume alone, and revisit the list as your authority grows.
caveats: KD bands are tool-specific; 0–40 is the source's demonstration range, not a universal rule.
The source gives no numeric volume thresholds, so judge volume relative to your market.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Reference the sitemap in robots.txt to control crawling and discovery
cards.summary: robots.txt hides unwanted pages from crawlers and can also point crawlers to your sitemap, combining exclusion and discovery in one file.
cards.use_when: Configuring a store's robots.txt after launch or a site migration so Google crawls product pages but skips non-indexable URLs.
steps: Open the store's robots.txt and check whether the sitemap URL is included. The source finds an example where the sitemap reference is present and explains it lets anyone find the sitemap from that file.
Use robots.txt directives to hide pages you don't want Google to crawl (the source describes this as the file's exclusion purpose).
Keep the sitemap reference as a standard syntax so Google can fetch the sitemap automatically via the file.
Do not block product, category or other indexable pages with robots.txt — exclusion is for pages that should not appear in search at all.
Confirm the final file in a browser and in Search Console's robots report, since the source notes free tools previously took far more time for what is now a single file.
Re-verify the syntax and the sitemap path after any CMS or domain change.
caveats: robots.txt directives differ in effect (disallow vs noindex); blocking crawling is not the same as removing pages from the index.
Sitemap paths are CMS-specific (e.g. sitemap_index.xml), so verify your exact URL.
Sitemaps support discovery; submission does not guarantee crawling, indexing or rankings.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Treat canonical URLs as the single version of each store page
cards.summary: Canonical URLs identify the single preferred version of a page's content, preventing duplicate versions from splitting ranking signals.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a store with filter, pagination or parameter variants that create near-duplicate product URLs.
steps: Understand the source's definition: canonical URLs are the URLs that show a unique page or unique content — the version a page intends to be indexed under.
Check a live page's source code for the canonical tag. The source shows a page whose canonical version points to itself, meaning it isn't treated as duplicated elsewhere.
Expect the XML sitemap to list these canonical versions of your pages, so the sitemap and canonical tags reinforce the same preferred URLs.
Where a store generates variant URLs (filters, tracking parameters, sort orders), plan to consolidate them to the canonical product or category URL.
Verify the implementation after changing it, since incorrect canonical tags can deindex the wrong page.
caveats: The source covers canonicals only briefly; it does not prescribe implementation for complex ecommerce parameter setups.
Canonical tags are hints, not guarantees, and should be paired with consistent internal linking.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Understand where SEO tracking tools fit before wiring them up
cards.summary: GA4, Search Console and Tag Manager are the three core tracking pillars the source recommends for SEO measurement, feeding audits, meta tags and event tracking.
cards.use_when: Planning the tracking stack for a new store or auditing gaps before running SEO and conversion experiments.
steps: Install Google Analytics 4 for traffic and user behaviour.
Install Google Search Console for crawl issues, indexing and query-level performance.
Install Google Tag Manager so you can deploy tags (including rich snippet code and meta tags) without editing site code on every change.
Plan to use Tag Manager to deploy schema/rich snippet code on the store without touching the theme, and to set up ecommerce event tracking such as add-to-cart button tracking.
Run technical and on-page audits (the source uses Ahrefs for its site audit) to identify gaps in on-page and technical SEO.
Use a backlink audit tool and a keyword tool (the source mentions SEMrush) alongside the tracking stack, and build the tracking code into pages at launch rather than retrofitting later.
caveats: This card describes the source's agenda for the session; the specific Tag Manager and rich-snippet processes are covered elsewhere in the course.
Tool capabilities change; verify current Tag Manager tag templates and GA4 event names.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Prepare store content for AI-assisted and voice search
cards.summary: Search is shifting toward AI overviews, People Also Ask and voice, which changes how content should be written and how page speed is assessed.
cards.use_when: Planning content and page experience for a store that wants visibility in AI overviews and voice assistant results.
steps: Write to intent. The source repeats that intent is very important and that AI understands queries such as buying a washing machine and then asking how to use it — so cover both purchase and post-purchase questions.

Structure content so it can be pulled into AI overviews and People Also Ask, using clear question headings and direct answers (the source demonstrates distinguishing informational, transactional and commercial queries).
Optimise page experience for both desktop and mobile separately, because Google reports two page-speed scores — the source attributes this to the shift to smartphone search.
Recognise that AI collects and analyses user behaviour data to improve ranking, so behavioural signals matter alongside content quality.
Voice results depend on a recognisable brand name and relevant terms, so keep brand and offering language consistent across pages and listings.
Verify current AI overview and voice result formats, as they change frequently.
caveats: The source does not provide measured effects of AI overviews on ecommerce clicks; the advice is directional.
AI and voice search behaviour is evolving quickly, so revisit these tactics regularly.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Edit permalinks to keep product and post URLs short and specific
cards.summary: Long title-based URLs are discouraged; custom permalinks let you shorten and specify the URL for a page.
cards.use_when: Publishing a new product, category or blog page where the default URL would be a long version of the title.
steps: When publishing, inspect the auto-generated permalink. The source shows Blogger taking the full title as the URL by default.
If the title is long, open the custom permalink option and replace it with a short, specific slug (the source uses 'brand perception').
Keep the slug meaningful and aligned to the page's topic rather than a full sentence or keyword-stuffed string.
Confirm the final URL before publishing, since changing it after indexing can create broken links or duplicate URLs.
Note the CMS limitation: the source finds Blogger pages do not offer the same URL structure controls as posts, so check your platform's options.
After publishing, verify the live URL and update any internal links that point to the old path.
caveats: Changing permalinks on already-indexed store URLs requires redirects, which the source does not cover.
Blogger-specific limitations are described; other platforms (Shopify, WordPress) have different permalink controls.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Set follow/nofollow deliberately when building internal links
cards.summary: Dofollow links pass ranking opportunity while nofollow links do not; the default is dofollow and should be reserved for pages you want to strengthen.
cards.use_when: Adding internal links between product pages, categories and blog content, or managing outbound links on a store.
steps: When inserting a link in your CMS editor, locate the insert/edit link option, paste the target URL, and choose whether it opens in a new window. The source notes opening in the same window loses the previous page.

Set the rel attribute intentionally: the source states dofollow links are important in SEO because they give a chance of ranking, while nofollow links do not follow SEO guidelines. Every link is dofollow by default.
Keep internal links between your own commercial pages as dofollow so ranking signals flow to product and category pages you care about.
Consider nofollow for untrusted outbound links or links you do not want to endorse.
Follow the source's principle that links should be helpful internal links — link where the target genuinely helps the reader, not everywhere.
Recheck rel attributes after CMS or theme updates, since editors sometimes reset defaults.
caveats: The source describes dofollow/nofollow in simple terms; modern search engines treat nofollow as a hint rather than an absolute rule.
The benefit of dofollow links is stated as the presenter's explanation, without measured evidence.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Set Up Google Search Console for a Store Property
cards.summary: Install and verify Search Console using the exact HTTPS URL-prefix property, and place the verification tag in the site head.
cards.use_when: Onboarding a new store domain or taking over a Shopify/WooCommerce/custom site and you need crawling, indexing and query data before diagnosing traffic.
steps: Log into Google Search Console with the Google account you'll keep managing the store with, open the property dropdown and click Add property.

Choose the URL prefix option rather than the Domain option: the source instructs preferring the exact version with https (and the www/non-www version as it is served) because Search Console is sensitive to URL mismatch, unlike Analytics.
Enter the exact website URL and click continue. If a Google Analytics property already exists for the site, verification may be automatic.
If verification is needed, copy the HTML tag shown under Settings > verification, paste it into the site's homepage head section (before the first body section), save, then return and click Verify.
After verification, the Overview shows the performance graph and Indexing (how many pages are indexed vs not indexed); treat this as the entry point to the audit workflow below.
caveats: The source considers URL-prefix/https the safer choice for Search Console; other guides prefer domain properties. Either way, the property must match the canonical host your store actually serves.
Requires developer or CMS theme-access to edit the head section if the theme does not expose a verification field.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Find High-Impression Low-Click Queries in Search Console
cards.summary: Sort Search Console queries by impressions to surface ranking pages that fail to earn clicks, then diagnose relevance, position and load time.
cards.use_when: Monthly SEO triage for a store: deciding which category, collection or blog pages need new titles, content or speed work.
steps: Open Search Console > Search results and switch between the Queries and Pages tabs; use the Country tab for market-level splits.
Sort by impressions descending to find terms with heavy impression volume but few clicks (the source's example: a clarifying shampoo query with strong impressions but only six clicks).

Work through the source's three explanations: (1) page content is not relevant enough to win the click, (2) the page ranks outside the top 20 so it rarely receives clicks, (3) the page loads slowly, which raises bounce rate and can cause Google to demote it.

For each candidate, check the average position in the table: if the query sits on pages 2-3, prioritize content and internal links; if it sits on page 1 with low CTR, prioritize title/meta and page-speed work.
Track fixes over the following reporting windows rather than judging impact immediately.
caveats: The three causes are the presenter's explanations, not a ranked diagnostic model; several can apply at once.
High impressions with low clicks is not automatically a problem for brand or navigational queries.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Compare Two Periods to Isolate Which Pages Lost Clicks
cards.summary: Use Search Console period comparison plus an exported Google Sheet with a difference formula to rank pages by click and impression decline.
cards.use_when: When store traffic drops after a site change, season shift or algorithm update and you need to name the specific pages that lost the most visibility.
steps: In Search Console > Search results, open the date comparison option and set it to compare, for example, the last 3 months against the previous period; the source also shows comparing a period to the previous year.

Read the headline numbers first: totals for impressions, clicks and average position across both periods (the source's example showed impressions down from 3.39M to 3M, clicks down from 19.2K to 15.4K, but average position improved from 17.8 to 12.7).
Export to Google Sheets. The export contains one tab for queries and another for pages, each with clicks and impressions for both periods.
In the sheet, compute a difference column (the source describes 'A1 minus A2') and sort in decreasing order of decline to surface the biggest losers.
Repeat the pass one metric at a time - clicks first, then impressions, then average CTR - to avoid conflating metrics; the source's example flagged a homepage down 96 clicks while a blog gained 19.
caveats: Improved average position alongside falling clicks means visibility breadth changed, not necessarily ranking quality - interpret the pair together.
The comparison windows are illustrative, not a recommended reporting cadence.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Audit Indexing Coverage and Fix 404s and No-Indexed Pages
cards.summary: Use Search Console Indexing to separate intentionally excluded dynamic URLs from genuine broken product and collection URLs, then repair only the meaningful ones.
cards.use_when: Cleaning up a store's crawl budget and recovering link equity after category, product or URL-structure changes.
steps: Open Search Console > Indexing and review indexed vs not-indexed counts (the source's example: 18.4K not indexed vs 163 indexed).

In the not-indexed reasons, read 'Excluded by noindex tag' and 'Page with redirect' entries: dynamic URLs containing question marks and equals signs are typically irrelevant filter/facet URLs that the source says can be ignored.
Click into the 404 (not found) group and open sample URLs to confirm they genuinely return a not-found page when a shopper would click them.
Export the 404 list and hand it to a developer; redirect each removed URL to the nearest relevant collection or product page, or to the homepage when no relevant page exists.
Re-crawl later to confirm the 404 count falls and the important templates remain indexed.
caveats: Do not blanket-redirect every 404: the source explicitly says to ignore dynamic URLs with query parameters and irrelevant characters.
Redirect execution requires site back-end access or developer support.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Install Google Tag Manager and Deploy Analytics Through It
cards.summary: Set up a GTM web container, fire GA4 through a constant variable so code lives outside the theme, and verify the tag with Preview mode.
cards.use_when: When a store wants to add or change tracking tags (analytics, pixels, schema, event tracking) without editing theme code for every change.
steps: Create the GTM account (account name, country) and a container using the bare domain, selecting Web as the target platform; accept the terms.

Paste the head snippet in the head section and the body snippet immediately after the opening body tag. The source hit a CMS glitch where an ampersand had to be written as '&' - if your platform throws a similar error, fix the escaping.
Create a user-defined variable of type Constant holding the GA4 measurement ID.
Create a GA4/Google tag, set its tag ID to reference that constant, and set its trigger to All Pages - Page View.

Publish the container (the source names each version, e.g. 'Google Analytics firing'), then use Preview to confirm the tag fires on a connected page; also confirm in GA4 realtime that only the GTM-delivered code is present if you removed the direct GA snippet.
Google Search Console is still installed separately with its own HTML tag - GTM does not replace it.
caveats: The source found the Tag Assistant Chrome extension unreliable during the demo; source-code search (view-source and Ctrl+F for the GTM ID) is the fallback verification.
GTM interface labels shift over time - verify current menu names before following step-by-step naming.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Create and Validate Articles/Blog Schema for Rich Snippets
cards.summary: Generate article-type schema from a template tool, fix validation warnings (typically date format), and never deploy unchecked code.
cards.use_when: Preparing blog or buying-guide content for rich results, or planning product-page schema such as star ratings and FAQ blocks.
steps: Use a schema generator template (the source used technicalseo.com) and pick the matching type - Article for a blog post, FAQPage for question blocks; product pages should carry star-rating schema.
Fill fields from the live page: type (Blog), URL, headline, image URL, short description, author type/name (author URL optional), publisher and logo URL, date published and date modified.
Paste the generated code into a rich-results/rich-snippet testing tool and run it; the source's code passed but warned on the date.
Correct warnings using an AI assistant by pasting the code and asking it to fix the flagged field to ISO standard, then re-test until all results are green.
Only then install the code, ideally through Google Tag Manager rather than the theme (see the GTM schema card).
caveats: Validation tools may show an old result after you unpublish a schema tag because the crawl is cached - the source observed a paused tag still appearing in test results.
Schema types and required fields change; check the current validator's requirements rather than copying an old code block verbatim.
Use store FAQs to answer shopper questions. Do not promise Google FAQ rich results or treat FAQ markup as a ranking requirement; verify current search feature support.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Fire Page-Specific Schema from Google Tag Manager
cards.summary: Deploy schema per URL via GTM with a page-path trigger so each blog post or FAQ page carries its own markup without theme edits.
cards.use_when: When content teams cannot touch the CMS templates but need structured data on specific blog, FAQ or product pages.
steps: In GTM, create a variable enabling the needed click/element variables if the configuration is not already set.
Create a new Custom HTML tag and paste the validated schema code.

Create a trigger of type Page View and narrow it with Page Path equals the specific page path (the portion after .com, e.g. the brand-perception post URL) - the source stresses per-page triggers because blog and FAQ pages differ.
Name the tag clearly (e.g. 'schema code for blog'), save, then publish the container with a naming convention you will recognise later.
Verify with GTM Preview that the tag fires on the correct URL, then confirm with a rich-results URL tester against the live page.
caveats: GTM triggers and variable configuration screens change over time - confirm the current labels.
Tag Assistant/preview behaviour can be inconsistent, as the source shows; use both preview and source-code/URL-test confirmation.
Use store FAQs to answer shopper questions. Do not promise Google FAQ rich results or treat FAQ markup as a ranking requirement; verify current search feature support.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Read an Ahrefs-Style Domain Rating and Backlink Profile
cards.summary: Interpret DR, UR, backlinks, referring domains, organic keywords and traffic as a comparative profile rather than a target score.
cards.use_when: Benchmarking a store against competitors before deciding whether link building, content or on-page work deserves the next sprint.
steps: Read the dashboard in the source's order: DR (out of 100, driven by backlink profile), UR for the specific URL, total backlinks, and unique referring domains.
Understand the ratio: 17.7K backlinks from 2.5K referring domains means many domains produce multiple links - the source treats unique referring domains as the more meaningful count.
Combine with organic keywords and estimated organic traffic, and ignore paid keyword counts unless you are also running ads.
Filter organic keywords by position to isolate top-10 rankings, and check the intent labels (informational, commercial, transactional, branded) to see whether the rankings sit on pages that can sell.
Note new tools in the source also report AI visibility metrics (e.g. presence in AI overviews) - treat these as emerging, separately-tracked indicators, not substitutes for organic data.
caveats: The source shows that different tools produce different traffic estimates for the same site (Ahrefs ~4-5K vs Semrush ~9.8K) and different authority scores (44 vs 35) - never compare scores across tools.
DR/UR are third-party relative metrics, not Google positioning signals.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Compare Ranking Position Over Time to Find Lost and Declined Keywords
cards.summary: Export the keyword table, split it into top-3/4-10/11-20 buckets and compare periods to build a fix list of declined and lost terms.
cards.use_when: Quarterly keyword triage: identifying product or category searches the store used to rank for and has slipped away from.
steps: Open the Organic Keywords report for the target country and click the Position column to select top-10 (or top-3) results, then show results to see first-page rankings.
Move the date comparison to the previous month or previous 3 months; the source's example showed a keyword slipping from position 3 to 6.
Apply the lost/improved/declined filters and focus on declined and lost entries - the source states explicitly that these deserve the main effort.
Cross-check period-level totals: the source's example showed a peak around 14,000 keywords in March 2024 versus roughly 3,390 later, with many lost terms visible in the prior-period view.
For each lost or declined keyword, decide between content modification, new supporting content or link building, informed by what competitors now use that you do not.
caveats: Not every lost keyword is worth recovering - the source pairs this with the requirement that keywords must match real services the store provides.
Keyword counts and position history are tool estimates, not Google's internal data.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Attribute Traffic Loss to Specific Pages Using Peak-Period Comparison
cards.summary: Compare today's traffic and top pages against a known good month to name the pages responsible for a decline, including zero-traffic pages that still load.
cards.use_when: When total organic traffic is falling and you need to separate pages that lost rankings from pages that merely lost clicks.
steps: In the traffic report, view six months to a year to locate the peak and the start of the decline (the source's example: October 10,344, November 8,692 and still falling).
Open the Top Pages section and set the comparison date to your best month.
Read the loss column per page: the source's example showed one page falling from 2,261 visits in March to 174 by November.

Flag pages showing traffic in the peak period but zero now, and check whether they still load. The source found a page that opened fine but received no traffic, indicating it is no longer ranking ('N/A' position) rather than broken.
Translate findings into a fix list: lost keywords and their source pages define the content and link priorities.
caveats: A page loading normally with zero traffic points to loss of ranking, not a technical outage - diagnose accordingly.
Peak-month selection is judgemental; traffic seasonality in retail can make a peak month a poor baseline.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Judge Backlink Quality with Referring Domains, DR and Spam Score
cards.summary: Sort backlinks by domain rating, inspect self-created zero-authority and nofollow links, and screen domains for spam before deciding to disavow.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a store's inbound link profile after outreach or a link-building campaign, and cleaning up toxic links.
steps: Sort the backlink report by DR ascending and descending: the source notes zero-DR referring domains contribute nothing, while high-DR links (the example cited DR 78) carry more weight.
For each suspicious domain, check its spam score with a free spam-score checker; the source's threshold is under 5 being fine, above roughly 10 risky, and 10-30 requiring removal or disavowal.
Note the follow/nofollow distinction: the source treats dofollow as the link type that passes ranking value and nofollow as delivering no SEO benefit.
Inspect the anchor-placement style: an example showed a third-party article linking a brand name to an About page, which the source uses as a legitimate quality example.
Compile spam links into a notepad list of domains and upload it to the Google Search Console disavow tool (which requires Search Console to be installed and uses the same Google login).
caveats: The numeric spam-score bands are the source's heuristic, not a Google-published standard.
The source also notes that a relevant but low-authority or new site can be left in place - relevance and age can offset a weak score.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Run an Ahrefs Site Audit and Prioritise Errors by Colour
cards.summary: Crawl the store and work red errors before yellow warnings, fixing 404s, canonical mismatches, orphan pages, http links and oversized images with developer support.
cards.use_when: Setting up a recurring technical audit for a store, particularly before or after a replatform or URL restructure.
steps: From the dashboard use Create Project, either importing from Search Console or adding the domain manually (a manual project continues without analytics verification and updates weekly).
Add target keywords and competitor domains if you have them, then run the crawl and open the health score (the source's example scored 96 - excellent - yet still had errors worth fixing).

Treat red errors as priority: 404 pages (redirect to the nearest relevant page or homepage), canonical pointing to redirect (copy the correct canonical URL into the tag so it matches the page rather than a redirected variant), orphan pages with no internal links (link them from a menu, blog or article), https pages containing http internal links, and oversized image files.
Treat the source's explicit rule for canonical mismatches: first check whether the link works; if not, the redirect explains the gap; if it works, align the canonical tag with the page's own URL.
Hand the exported error list to a developer, since most fixes require back-end access.
caveats: A high health score does not mean the site is clean - the source's example flagged errors at a 96 score.
The source notes developers can resolve most red errors but the auditor cannot change them directly without back-end skills.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Write Meta Titles and Descriptions Inside the CMS Within Length Limits
cards.summary: Fix title and description length warnings by editing the CMS record, targeting roughly 60 characters for titles and 140-160 for descriptions.
cards.use_when: Clearing yellow audit warnings on product, collection and blog pages, and improving click-through from search results.
steps: From the audit warning list, open the URL whose title or description is flagged, and use a browser SEO extension or source view to read the current character counts (the source's example: a 73-character title and a 167-character description).
Determine the page type first (collection, product, blog) because the editing location differs in each CMS.
For a Shopify-style store: admin > Products > Collections to find the collection by its existing title, or Content > Blog posts to find the post by its web page title.

Rewrite within limits: title maximum 60 characters (the source reduced 73 to 54), meta description 140-160 with 160 as the hard maximum (167 reduced to 155-158). Count characters, not words - the source explicitly notes this.
Save, then re-check: the audit tool will drop the warning on its next crawl once the length is compliant.
caveats: The source notes default titles may omit brand terms because the team or agency is unaware - check the title actually reflects the store.
Character limits are guidelines for display truncation, not ranking factors.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Write and Place Alt Text for Store Images
cards.summary: Add concise, descriptive alt text (3-4 words) to product, blog and template images so Google can interpret them, using the CMS or a developer for template-level images.
cards.use_when: Clearing missing/empty alt text warnings on product images, blog imagery and shared footer icons.
steps: Open the flagged page and inspect the missing image to see what it actually shows before writing anything (the source opens the image file directly).
Search the page source for the image tag to confirm whether alt is empty or missing, which tells you whether you can fix it from the page or need a developer.

Write the alt text as the image's subject in 3-4 words maximum; the source's examples are 'fast free shipping' for a shipping badge and 'brand trust 81%' for a data graphic, and rewriting a consumer-needs image around brand trust.
In WordPress-style editors, add images via the editor's image block and use Edit Alt Text (the source found that simply dragging an image into the editor did not expose the alt option).
For images living in shared template areas such as footers and headers, send the alt text to a developer - it applies site-wide rather than to one page.
caveats: Each CMS exposes alt text differently - the source explicitly warns the option location varies.
Do not stuff long keyword phrases into alt text; the source caps it at three to four words.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Use Semrush Keyword Gap to Find Competitor Terms You Are Missing
cards.summary: Compare your ranking keyword set with a competitor's and subtract the common terms to size the untapped opportunity before adding anything.
cards.use_when: Planning content or category expansion and deciding which competitor-driven keywords are safe and relevant to pursue.
steps: In Semrush's domain overview, note that traffic estimates and authority scores differ from other tools (the source saw 9.8K vs Ahrefs' 4-5K, and authority 35 vs DR 44) - assume tool-relative numbers only.

Open organic competitors, pick a rival and read the two figures: common keywords (e.g. 931) and the competitor's total keywords (e.g. 2,953). Subtract the common set - roughly 2,000 terms here - to approximate keywords you do not target.
Drill into specific missing terms (the source's example: a red light therapy mask keyword the competitor ranks for and the client does not) and inspect what the competitor's page does.
Apply the source's hard filter: only pursue keywords that describe services or products you genuinely offer - never target a keyword for something you do not sell.
Compare the keyword distribution buckets (top 3, 4-10, 11-20) across tools to see whether your gap is depth or breadth.
caveats: Keyword gap counts are tool estimates of ranking overlap, not guaranteed traffic.
The source shows Semrush details can require an upgrade - free tiers limit depth if you are not a paying user.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Track Add-to-Cart and Button Click Events Without Back-End Code
cards.summary: Use Google Tag Manager event tracking to count clicks on submit and add-to-cart buttons instead of requesting developer instrumentation.
cards.use_when: Store analytics phase where you need button-level engagement data for PDPs, forms or checkout-adjacent CTAs.
steps: Identify the button to track (the source's example starts with a submit button, then extends to add-to-cart, checkout and transaction clicks) and confirm it is a real interactive element on the live page.
Create a GTM trigger for clicks on that element, using the element variables enabled in configuration (the source shows enabling click elements before writing triggers).
Create a tag that fires on that trigger - a GA4 event tag in modern setups - and give it a name you can trace back to the button.
Publish the container and verify with GTM Preview that the event fires on click in a real session.
Keep GTM as the maintenance layer: when a button changes, update the trigger rather than reopening the theme code.
caveats: The source mentions this can also be done with a developer, so treat GTM as the lower-dependency option rather than the only route.
GTM's click trigger and variable interfaces change; confirm current naming before building.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Set up Add-to-Cart event tracking with Google Tag Manager without touching site code
cards.summary: Use GTM Preview mode to identify a button's click text, then create a GA4 click-trigger tag to log add-to-cart events and build a checkout funnel view.
cards.use_when: You want to measure how many shoppers click Add to Cart (or Checkout/Purchase buttons) on your product pages but don't want to edit the store's backend code.
steps: Install the Google Tag Manager container on the site, then in GTM go to Tags > New and open Preview mode. Verify the GA4 configuration tag (G-XXXX) is already firing on the page you are testing.

Load your product page in the Preview connection. Click the Add to Cart button and watch the event log: a new click entry appears (e.g. click #23). Open that click entry and inspect variables — confirm 'Click Text' shows 'Add to Cart' (or the exact button label). This tells you the correct trigger identifier.
Create a new tag: Tag Configuration > Google Analytics > Google Analytics: GA4 Event. Enter your Measurement ID (the G- code from GA4 Admin > Data Streams). Set the event name, e.g. 'add_to_cart'.
Add a trigger: New > choose 'Click – All Elements' > Some Clicks > set Click Text equals the exact button text (paste 'add to cart' without quotes). Save the trigger and tag.

Submit > Publish the tag. Re-open Preview on the product page and click the button again — confirm the add_to_cart tag fires. It will then appear in GA4 events and can be used in funnel/exploration reports.

Repeat for Checkout and Purchase buttons, using their own click texts (or a different variable such as a CSS class if two buttons share the same text). Do this on a test/staging container first if possible.
caveats: This demo tracks clicks by visible button text — if the button text changes (localization, A/B tests, dynamic labels) the trigger breaks; consider using a unique element ID or CSS selector instead.
Duplicate or repeated tags (e.g. an old add-to-cart tag left active) cause confusing double counting — the presenter deleted the demo tag to avoid confusion.
GTM and GA4 interfaces change frequently; verify the current menu names and event/trigger options before following.
Only clicks are tracked, not whether the cart actually updated server-side — a button click is a proxy, not a confirmed cart add.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Diagnose where shoppers drop off in the add-to-cart-to-purchase flow
cards.summary: Once add-to-cart, checkout and purchase click events are logged in GA4, compare counts across the three steps to locate the biggest funnel leak.
cards.use_when: You suspect shoppers abandon between cart and checkout or between checkout and payment, and want data on which stage loses the most people before deciding where to optimize.
steps: Instrument three click events — add_to_cart, checkout (or begin_checkout) and purchase — using GTM click triggers as described in the tracking card.
Let data accumulate, then in GA4 open an Exploration or Funnel report and compare event counts across the three steps for a chosen date range.
