Read the flow as a drop-off profile. The source's illustrative example: 100 add-to-cart, 60 checkout, 10 purchase — i.e. 40% lost between cart and checkout and roughly 83% lost between checkout and purchase. These are illustration figures from the presenter, not benchmarks.

Direct optimization at the largest gap: heavy cart-to-checkout loss suggests cart UI, shipping-cost surprises or forced account creation; heavy checkout-to-purchase loss suggests payment options, form friction or trust signals.
Re-measure after each change to confirm the drop-off actually narrowed rather than just moving to another step.
caveats: The 100/60/10 figures are illustrative examples the presenter gave for reading the flow, not targets or industry benchmarks.
Click-based events count button clicks, not confirmed completions — some clicks may not represent true funnel progress.
GA4 sampling, bot traffic and ad blockers can distort counts; validate against the platform's own checkout or order reports before acting on large gaps.
cards.source_name: SEO Full Course 2026 _ SEO Tutorial For Beginners _ Search Engine Optimization Course _ Simplilearn.docx

cards.title: Keyword Magic Tool: seed keyword to qualified opportunity list
cards.summary: Use Semrush's Keyword Magic Tool to expand one seed keyword into a filtered list of rankable keywords with intent, volume and difficulty.
cards.use_when: Starting keyword research for a product category or content plan and you need a prioritized list of realistic ranking targets before briefing content or product pages.
steps: Open SEO toolkit > Keyword Magic Tool and enter one broad seed keyword tied to your business (e.g. 'olive oil').
Read the output columns: Volume = monthly searches; KD = Keyword Difficulty percentage (higher = harder to rank); Intent = what the searcher wants.
Classify intent with the four types: Informational (wants to learn), Navigational (seeking a specific site/brand), Commercial (researching before purchase), Transactional (ready to buy/act).
Filter KD with a custom range of 0–49 to strip out the hardest terms.
Add a volume filter (e.g. minimum 5,000 searches/month) so remaining terms have real demand.
Use the topic cluster column on the left to drill into categories and surface more opportunities.
Click the icon next to any keyword to open the mini Keyword Overview: global and per-country volume, KD, SERP features, CPC, trend, related questions and SERP analysis.
Check the SERP preview for an AI Overview appearing above organic results — for those terms you are also competing for the AI answer, not just a ranking.
Add chosen keywords to a named list (e.g. 'Month 1 Focus') via the plus button; aim for 10–15 opportunities per list.
caveats: KD is Semrush's own difficulty metric, not an absolute prediction of ranking success.
Volume and KD figures are estimates that shift over time.
The source advises starting with low-difficulty, decent-volume 'low hanging fruit' rather than the biggest keywords.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: AI Prompt Research: what customers ask ChatGPT and AI search
cards.summary: Use Semrush's Prompt Research to see the questions buyers ask AI tools on your topic, which brands get mentioned, and which sources AI cites.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether your brand appears in AI answers for buying-intent questions, and which prompts to target with content or PDP copy.
steps: Open the AI Visibility toolkit > Prompt Research and enter a high-level topic (e.g. 'olive oil'). Click Analyse.
Read the summary bar: total monthly AI search volume, number of subtopics, prompts, intent types, brands and source domains.
Drill into subtopics (e.g. 'olive oil and its benefits') to see individual prompts, the AI response, brands mentioned, and the sources cited.
Click 'View Full Response' on a prompt to read the actual AI-generated answer — top paragraph, brands named, and buying tips.
Scan whether your brand is mentioned and how prominently versus competitors for commercially relevant prompts like 'best olive oils to buy'.
Decide whether the prompt is worth targeting: if your brand is absent or buried, it is a content or page-copy opportunity.
For prompts you want to own, click Create Content to route into the Content toolkit (an add-on) to generate optimized articles or SEO briefs.
caveats: Prompts are what users ask AI; keywords are what they type into Google — the source treats the intent as the same but the platforms differ.
Content toolkit (AI Article Generator, SEO Brief Generator) is a paid add-on beyond Semrush One with a separate seven-day trial.
AI answers and cited sources change frequently, so re-check prompts periodically.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: Competitor Organic Rankings: read their organic playbook
cards.summary: Use Organic Rankings to see every keyword a competitor ranks for, their SERP features, and how their keyword mix by intent shifts over time.
cards.use_when: Merchandising or content planning when you want to understand which topics and intents a direct competitor is winning and where they are exposed.
steps: Open SEO toolkit > Organic Rankings and enter a competitor domain (e.g. graza.co).
Review their top keywords and which terms they perform best on in organic search.
Check which SERP features they are capturing to see the format of results they win.
Look at the balance of keywords by intent over time — the source example shows a competitor getting most traffic from informational keywords.
Track how their positions and SERP features have changed over time to spot rising or declining topics.
Treat any topic a competitor ranks highly for as a candidate that AI tools may also pull from, so it doubles as an AEO target list.
caveats: The source notes the competitor example was chosen as a real brand with no affiliation.
Rankings and SERP features are snapshots and vary by location and device.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: Keyword Gap: find keywords competitors rank for and you don't
cards.summary: Use Keyword Gap to surface keywords your competitors rank for (Missing) or where you rank far lower (Weak), and convert them into target lists.
cards.use_when: Building a content or category-page roadmap where you want to close specific ranking gaps against named competitors.
steps: Open SEO toolkit > Keyword Gap, enter your domain in the first field.
Use Add Domain to pick Semrush-suggested competitors from the dropdown (add up to three more) or type domains manually. Click Compare.
Open the Missing tab to see keywords competitors rank for where your column shows zero — these are uncontested opportunities.
Open the Weak tab to see keywords you do rank for but far below competitors.

Prioritize Weak-tab keywords that combine a low KD with meaningful volume. In the example, a term where competitors rank #1 and #2 but your site ranks #36 has KD 41 and 1,000+ searches/month — flagged as a strong target.
Add chosen keywords to your keyword list via the plus button.
Select a handful of important terms to actively compete on and push into your content or category plan.
caveats: Position numbers show competitor SERP rank, not their traffic.
Zero in your column can mean no ranking at all, not a low position.
Difficulty and volume are estimates; validate before committing significant production effort.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: Cluster your keyword list into a content calendar
cards.summary: Use Keyword Strategy Builder to consolidate keyword lists and auto-cluster them so each cluster becomes one page or piece of content.
cards.use_when: Turning a scattered keyword list into a concrete monthly content or category-page plan with defined primary intent per page.
steps: Open Keyword Strategy Builder and select your existing list (e.g. 'Month 1 Focus').
Review the quick stats: total keywords, combined monthly search volume, and average KD. The example list has 21 keywords, 136,230 monthly volume and 20.05% average KD.
Sort or filter the list by volume, keyword, difficulty percentage or CPC to organize priorities.

Click 'Cluster This List'. If prompted that the list has too few keywords to create profitable pages, either add more keywords or click 'Cluster List Anyway' — the source notes results improve with more keywords.
After processing (may take minutes), review the clusters: each cluster = one page. Expanding a cluster shows the recommended keywords to target and its primary intent (e.g. commercial).
Note the cluster's average KD and combined potential search volume (example: ~22% KD and 55,900 searches/month).
Send the cluster keywords to Position Tracking to monitor results, to Create Content/Brief for production, or Export as a spreadsheet.
Pick your first five clusters as the content calendar for the next month.
caveats: Clustering on a short list produces weaker results, per the tool's own warning and the source's agreement.
Average KD is a cluster-level average and does not guarantee any individual keyword will rank.
Content toolkit destinations require an add-on subscription.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: Topic Research: headlines and questions that already work
cards.summary: Use Topic Research to find proven headlines and audience questions around a topic so you write from evidence instead of a blank page.
cards.use_when: Planning blog or category-page content when you need headline angles and questions that already resonate before briefing a writer.
steps: Open SEO toolkit > Topic Research, enter a high-level topic (e.g. 'olive oil') and click Get Content Ideas.
Review subtopic ideas (example outputs: Mediterranean Diet, Type 2 Diabetes, Heart Disease, Anti-Inflammatory).
Get more specific by searching longer keywords from your keyword strategy (e.g. 'best olive oil') — outputs become more targeted (Grocery Stores, Cold Pressed, Organic Extra Virgin Olive Oil).
Click into a subtopic to see headline ideas ranked best-to-worst with resonance signals — the source example shows an article with 552 backlinks.
Open the referenced article to study exactly what made it resonate.
Favorite useful headlines and the audience questions surfaced (e.g. 'What is the best olive oil to buy in the USA?').
Collect everything in the Favorite Ideas tab as your content planning board; aim for 10–15 favorited ideas across a few topics.
Use the pattern: mix and match the best parts of the top-performing headlines into your own, then answer the favorited questions inside the article.
caveats: Backlink counts on example articles are illustrative resonance signals, not benchmarks you should expect.
Favorited ideas are a queue to work from, not a guarantee of performance.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: SEO Writing Assistant: score and fix a draft before publishing
cards.summary: Use Semrush's SEO Writing Assistant to score a draft against target keywords and fix readability, title length and originality issues before publication.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a finished or near-finished product description, blog post or landing page copy before it goes live.
steps: Open SEO Writing Assistant and click Analyse My Text.
Import text from an existing URL or paste your draft directly.
Paste your target keywords from the Keyword Strategy Builder cluster into the field provided so the tool scores against them.
Click Get Recommendations and read the overall score (10-point scale) plus the axis chart covering tone of voice, readability, SEO and originality.

Work through the issue list on the left; click any issue to see the proposed fix in the floating bar and accept, reject or retry. Example fixes: a title over 60 characters that may be truncated in search results, and hard-to-read sentences the tool offers to simplify.
Iterate — the source notes new issues can emerge after fixes, and perfect scores are unrealistic. Aim to move the score up (their example improved by 0.3) and reduce the issue count.
Correcting the title also improved readability in the example by removing filler words like 'actually'.
caveats: Readability, tone and SEO scores are heuristics, not ranking guarantees.
The tool does not assess commercial persuasiveness — pair it with your own judgment.
Fixing toward the tool's suggestions can flatten voice if applied uncritically.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: Site Audit: fix errors first, warnings second
cards.summary: Run a Site Audit to find technical errors that block crawling and ranking, then work through issues in priority order rather than chasing a perfect score.
cards.use_when: Before a content or merchandising push, when you need to confirm product and category pages are crawlable and not returning errors.
steps: Open SEO toolkit > Site Audit, select your project (created from the domain entered on the welcome screen).
Read the Site Health indicator — the source example shows 87% versus a 92% top-10% benchmark, a 5% gap.
Check the AI search health score separately (example: 75% with 80% flagged as the competing threshold).
Open the Errors count first — these are the more severe issues. Click an issue type grouped by number of pages (e.g. 'Two pages returned 4XX status code').
Verify broken links by opening the page via the icon; a 404 confirms it goes nowhere real.
Use the 'How to Fix' link for each issue — it explains the cause and remediation steps. Use Share to hand the issue to whoever owns the fix.
Fix red critical errors, then orange warnings, then blue notices. The source says not to panic at a long issue list and not to aim for perfection — just reduce the count.
Treat audits as recurring, not one-off — the source frames this as the foundation step before tracking and content work.
caveats: Health and AI-search-health percentages and the 92%/80% comparison points are Semrush-presented benchmarks in this example, not universal targets.
The AI-health panel may report pages 'Blocked from AI search' and point you to robots.txt; see the llms.txt card for that specific fix.
Google Search does not use llms.txt or require special AI text files. Treat other-engine support as unverified unless documented by that engine.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: robots.txt and llms.txt: crawlability for Google and for AI
cards.summary: Add both robots.txt and llms.txt so traditional crawlers and AI bots can find and prioritize your most important pages.
cards.use_when: When Site Audit reports pages blocked from AI search, or when launching or restructuring a store and want AI tools to surface your key pages.
steps: In Site Audit, check the AI Search Health panel for 'Blocked from AI search' — the source example shows 100 pages crawled and 4 blocked per AI tool.
Click 'How To Unblock Pages' to see the recommended action, typically reviewing the robots.txt file.
Understand the two files: robots.txt tells Google which pages to crawl; llms.txt does the same job for AI tools.
Create llms.txt as a plain text file at yourdomain.com/llms.txt describing which pages on your site are most important and what they are about, so ChatGPT, Perplexity and others can prioritize them.
If the site lacks an llms.txt file, the source says it is worth adding. Use the 'How to Fix' link for issue-specific guidance and resources.
Re-run the audit after adding the files to confirm blocked-page counts drop.
caveats: llms.txt is an emerging convention — AI tools' support for it may vary and change over time.
Verify current file-format and crawler requirements, as AI bot behavior is evolving.
Google Search does not use llms.txt or require special AI text files. Treat other-engine support as unverified unless documented by that engine.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: Backlinks overview: authority, best links and lost links
cards.summary: Use the Backlinks overview to assess referring-domain quality and recover high-value lost links rather than chasing raw link counts.
cards.use_when: When planning link building or diagnosing a drop in domain authority and organic visibility for a store.
steps: Open SEO toolkit > Link Building > Backlinks, enter your domain and click Analyse.
Read the top bar: number of referring sites, total links, and monthly visits driven by those links (example: 2,600 referring sites, 28,000 links, 161,000 monthly visits).

Check the Authority Score — Semrush's metric combining number and quality of backlinks plus overall site authenticity. The source example shows 47, described as 'pretty good', with higher being better.
View the authority score trend over time on the adjacent panel.
Open the Backlinks tab and filter by 'Best' to see links that raise your authority because they come from reputable sites.
Filter by 'Lost and Vital' to find links that used to point to your site and no longer do.

For a high-value, high-page-authority lost link, reach out to the site — it may be broken and need updating, or the site may have deliberately dropped you. Either way, investigate to try to restore it.
Treat backlinks as valuable for both Google trust and AI citation, since the source notes AI tools tend to cite sources other sites also cite.
caveats: You do not need to act on every link in the list — prioritize high-value, high-authority lost links only.
Authority Score is a Semrush metric, not Google's; use it for relative comparison.
The source example does not establish a target authority number.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: Backlink Gap: find sites linking to competitors but not you
cards.summary: Use Backlink Gap to list referring domains that link to multiple competitors but not to you, filtered by authority, as an outreach checklist.
cards.use_when: Planning outreach to earn links and AI-cited authority in your niche, especially when competitor roundups or listicles already exist.
steps: Open SEO toolkit > Competitive Analysis > Backlink Gap.
Confirm your domain sits in the first field labelled 'you', add several competitors, then click Find Prospects.

Read the columns: referring domain, its authority score, the Matches count (how many of the input domains it links to), and links per destination domain. A zero means that domain does not link to that destination.
Filter by Authority Score with a lower threshold (the source uses 50) and Apply.

Scan for patterns — if one site links to several competitors but not you, it is a strong outreach candidate. In the source example, the Food Network links to three competitors but not the target brand.
Weigh relevance and reach: the same example site has a high authority score and 22.5 million monthly visits.
Treat the filtered list as a checklist. Tick the box next to a referring domain and click Start Outreach to open the Backlink Builder tool for managing the campaign.
caveats: The authority threshold of 50 is the source's suggested starting filter, not a universal rule.
The source states a few high-quality backlinks from relevant niche sites beat hundreds from random directories, but does not quantify the difference.
Outreach outcomes depend on editorial fit; a competitor mention does not guarantee coverage.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: Position Tracking: monitor Google rankings and AI summaries together
cards.summary: Set up Position Tracking with your priority keywords so you can watch rank changes and AI-summary appearances over time in one view.
cards.use_when: After publishing new content or making technical fixes, to verify movement and catch visibility changes early.
steps: Open SEO toolkit > Position Tracking and select your SEO project to land on the Landscape tab.
Read the headline metrics: visibility score (example 65.72% with a potential 66.02 over three months), estimated traffic, and average position per keyword.
Review top keywords and open the Rankings Overview for the full keyword list.
Check whether keywords appear in the AI summary — the example shows 'Agave versus honey' ranking first in the AI summary.
Click the magnifier/browser icon on any keyword to view a cached snapshot of the live search result page.
Expand any keyword to see its position change over time; more history accumulates the longer your account runs.
Import keywords from Keyword Strategy Builder: open your list, tick the checkbox, click Send Keywords > Position Tracking > Apply, select the project and confirm.
Accept duplicate warnings (the example sends 19 keywords and skips 2 duplicates) and click Go To Position Tracking.
Filter by a specific keyword in the Overview tab to isolate its trend.
Track your 20–30 most important keywords and check back weekly to see movement in both Google and AI search.
caveats: The visibility score and its projected improvement are Semrush metrics, not traffic guarantees.
You need accumulated history before position-change charts become informative.
Cached SERP snapshots may differ from what a live user sees by location.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: Domain Overview: catch declining traffic and visibility trends
cards.summary: Use Domain Overview to see overall SEO and AI-search visibility in one place and spot negative trends early.
cards.use_when: Doing a periodic health check on your store's organic and AI visibility, or diagnosing a suspected traffic decline.
steps: Open SEO toolkit > Domain Overview, enter your domain and click Search.
Read the high-level standings for both AI search visibility and traditional SEO visibility side by side.
Scroll to the traffic-by-type-over-time chart and toggle between AI search and Google search.
Review distribution by country and cited sources, including branded versus non-branded splits.
Act on early signals — the source example shows a brand with declining traffic and frames catching such a trend early as the goal.
caveats: Domain Overview is a summary view; drill into specific tools to diagnose the cause of a trend.
Visibility scores are Semrush's own composite metrics.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: AI Visibility Overview: which LLMs mention and cite you
cards.summary: Use the AI Visibility Overview to quantify brand mentions across ChatGPT, Google AI, Perplexity and Gemini, and see where to focus AEO effort.
cards.use_when: Deciding which AI platform to prioritize for AEO work, or reporting brand presence in AI answers to stakeholders.
steps: Open the AI Visibility toolkit > Visibility Overview.
Set the region to your primary market (the source example switches from worldwide to the US for a US-focused brand) to get relevant numbers.
Read the AI visibility score out of 100 — the example brand scores 50, described as occasionally mentioned but improvable.
Review monthly mentions (example: ~2,300) and the trend of mentions vs citations vs cited pages over time.
Check mentions by country to see where the brand is actually surfaced — the example shows the US dominating mentions.
Check distribution by LLM: in the example, ChatGPT rarely mentions the brand while Google AI Overview does most of the heavy lifting.
Toggle to see which LLM cites the brand's pages most. Focus effort on the LLMs underperforming — the source suggests prioritizing ChatGPT and Gemini in that example.

Use the 'What's Next' section: 'Uncover Topic Opportunities' lists topics to cover to earn more LLM mentions, and 'Your Performing Topics' shows the topics already driving mentions, with the prompts behind them.
caveats: AI visibility scores are Semrush's composite metrics and the 50/100 example is illustrative, not a benchmark.
LLM behavior and coverage change rapidly, so re-check the region and platform splits periodically.
Worldwide versus single-region settings materially change the numbers.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: Brand Performance: how ChatGPT talks about you and what to fix
cards.summary: Use Brand Performance to see sentiment, share of voice, business drivers and prioritized strategy recommendations for how AI describes your brand.
cards.use_when: Setting AEO and brand-messaging priorities when you need to know how AI assistants position you versus competitors for buying-intent questions.
steps: Open the AI Visibility toolkit > Brand Performance, enter your domain, click Analyse.
Select the target location (e.g. United States) and click Get Started, then allow time for the report to load.

Read the Insights panel for how ChatGPT discusses the brand across conversations — e.g. strong sentiment at 78% but the lowest share of voice, with the recommendation to push high-visibility campaigns to grow volume without losing positivity.

Review overall sentiment in LLM responses and the key business drivers section. Example: the brand ranks second on design-led appeal but lags on freshness, with a suggestion to amplify harvest, origin and testing signals.
Scroll to Strategy Recommendations and read them across timeframes.
Act on the urgent-timeline recommendations first this week, then short, then medium timeframe items.

Use the recommendations as concrete positioning inputs — in the example they include codifying a simple promise (e.g. 'chef-worthy California EVOO for everyday cooking'), and addressing that the brand is seen as a specialty upgrade rather than a default everyday choice.
caveats: The sentiment percentages, rankings and recommendations are generated for the source's example brand and are not transferable benchmarks.
The report can take a while to generate and reflects a point in time; recommendations should be re-read as data refreshes.
Strategy recommendations are AI-generated suggestions, not guaranteed outcomes — pair them with your own category knowledge.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: The four-step search loop: research, organize, fix, track
cards.summary: Follow Semrush's four-step workflow — research Google and AI demand, cluster it into a content plan, fix site and backlink gaps, then track results and repeat.
cards.use_when: Setting up or resetting an ongoing SEO/AEO program for a store and you need an ordered operating sequence rather than ad hoc tasks.
steps: Step 1 — Research: find what people search on Google (Keyword Magic Tool) and what they ask AI (Prompt Research). The source treats keywords and prompts as the same underlying intent on different platforms.
Step 2 — Organize: turn research into topic clusters via Keyword Strategy Builder, then decide what content or pages to create. Pick your first five clusters as the month's calendar.
Step 3 — Fix the foundation: run a Site Audit for errors and AI crawlability (robots.txt, llms.txt), and close backlink gaps with Backlink Gap.
Step 4 — Track: monitor Google rankings and AI visibility side by side in Position Tracking and Domain Overview, then repeat the loop.
Treat this as cyclical, not one-time — the source states SEO and AEO are make-changes-then-watch-what-happens activities, and without tracking you are guessing.
caveats: The source's recommended Semrush One starter plan is $199/month; the source notes it is not cheap.
Several destinations in the workflow (Content toolkit, AI Article Generator, SEO Brief Generator) require add-on subscriptions with separate trials.
Promotional trial and pricing details change — verify current plans and interfaces before purchasing.
Google Search does not use llms.txt or require special AI text files. Treat other-engine support as unverified unless documented by that engine.
cards.source_name: Semrush Tutorial 2026 - Master SEO & AEO with Semrush One.docx

cards.title: Keyword Research Workflow with Google Keyword Planner and Trends
cards.summary: Build a per-page keyword set (one main, two supporting) using Google Keyword Planner volume/CPC data and Google Trends related queries.
cards.use_when: Planning keyword targets before editing a homepage, product page, collection, or blog post's SEO fields.
steps: Open Google Ads and go to Tools > Planning > Keyword Planner (account required to see data). Set language and country to match your target market.
Enter a seed term describing your product category (example: 'homemade soap'); read monthly search volume, competition level, and CPC range to gauge commercial value.

Pick one main keyword and two supporting keywords per page. The source's demo chose 'homemade soap' as main (1,000–10,000 monthly searches, high competition) with lower-volume, more specific terms as support.
Use Google Trends related searches (optionally with the Glimpse Chrome extension) to surface adjacent queries, then paste them back into Keyword Planner to check volume.
Test a query in Google search and harvest autocomplete predictions as candidate keywords, then validate them in Keyword Planner.
Optionally paste a competitor's URL into Keyword Planner's 'start with website' option to see which keywords their pages already rank for, and choose gaps to target.
Assign each page a distinct keyword set based on that page's content; don't reuse the same set across all products.
caveats: Volume/CPC shown are estimates from Google's tools, not guarantees.
Higher-end tools (Ahrefs, Semrush) give richer intent and country data but cost more; Keyword Planner is the free fallback.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Separate Informational vs Transactional Search Intent
cards.summary: Match keywords to intent so product and collection pages target buyers while blog posts absorb informational searches.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether a keyword belongs on a product/collection page, a blog post, or nowhere in your catalog.
steps: Classify each keyword: informational (e.g., 'how to make homemade soap') vs transactional (e.g., 'homemade soap for sale', 'homemade soap near me').
Route transactional keywords to product and collection pages, where the visitor can immediately buy.
Route informational keywords to blog posts and guide pages that link internally to the relevant products.
When using tools with explicit intent labels (e.g., Semrush), use them to confirm intent instead of guessing.
Favor keywords with buying intent when the page's goal is revenue; use informational terms to build topical authority and feed internal links to money pages.
caveats: Intent labels are tool heuristics and can be wrong; spot-check the live SERP if in doubt.
Informational traffic converts far less directly — judge it on assisted discovery, not last-click sales.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Edit Global Store SEO: Homepage Title and Meta Description
cards.summary: Set the site-wide homepage title and meta description so the homepage ranks for your main brand/category keyword.
cards.use_when: Setting or fixing the homepage listing that appears in Google results for brand and category searches.
steps: In Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Preferences and find the Search engine listing section.
Write a title that includes the main keyword; respect the 70-character field limit. The source's demo used 63 characters with the main keyword plus supporting terms.
Write a meta description containing supporting keywords and optionally a call to action; keep it accurate to the brand voice.
Optionally draft candidates with ChatGPT, then edit so they genuinely represent your brand — avoid overly broad keywords that don't match your niche.
Save, then verify by searching the keyword in Google to see how your listing renders.
caveats: The title/description you write here is the homepage listing only; each product, collection, page, and blog post has its own listing fields.
Field character limits may change in Shopify's interface — verify current limits.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Enforce a Single H1 Tag Per Page
cards.summary: Ensure every page has exactly one H1 so Google can identify the page's main topic.
cards.use_when: Auditing a theme or custom section for heading structure on product, collection, homepage, or custom-built pages.
steps: Inspect the page in the browser and check which element carries the H1. On Shopify's Dawn theme, the homepage H1 is typically the logo; on collection pages the collection title is the H1; on product pages the product title is the H1.
Check custom sections a developer or you built — they sometimes introduce an extra H1.
If two H1s exist, demote one to H2 or lower so only the intended main title remains H1.
After fixing, re-inspect to confirm only one H1 remains on every page type.
caveats: Theme behavior differs; the logo-as-H1 behavior is stated for Dawn and may not hold for all themes — verify in your theme.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Write SEO Product Titles from Specs Using Keyword Data
cards.summary: Turn raw product specs into a keyword-rich but readable product title and description.
cards.use_when: Rewriting vague product names (e.g., 'Sweet Honey Bomb') that don't tell Google or shoppers what the product is.
steps: Copy the product's specs/description into ChatGPT and ask for candidate high-volume keywords relevant to those specs.
Validate those keywords in Google Keyword Planner; discard ones with weak volume or poor relevance.
Feed the validated keyword list back into ChatGPT asking for title options; pick the best and include at least the main keyword plus a supporting keyword.
Paste the title into the Shopify product Title field and save.

For the description, ask ChatGPT to write from the specs, instructing it to weave in the researched keywords but keep the text natural (not obviously AI-generated). Aim for at least 100 words; the source says 300–400 words is ideal for product copy.
Format the description — bold key points, add images inside it, and adjust theme title font size in the customizer if the longer title breaks layout.
Edit the result so it matches your brand voice before publishing.
caveats: AI output must be reviewed for accuracy and brand fit; don't publish unedited.
Longer titles may require theme typography adjustments to avoid layout breakage.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Image SEO: Alt Text, File Names, and Formatting
cards.summary: Optimize every product/media image with descriptive alt text and a keyword-based file name.
cards.use_when: Preparing product photos, banners, and gallery media before or after uploading to Shopify.
steps: Write alt text that combines the target keyword, the product name, and a visual descriptor: the source's example is 'summer fragment bath bomb purple frontal' (keyword + product + color + angle).
Reuse the alt text to rename the actual image file so the file name is descriptive rather than a string of numbers/gibberish.
Work through every image in the product's media gallery, then go to Content > Files and fix the alt text and file names for the store's media library.
Optionally verify by inspecting the image on the storefront to confirm the descriptive URL is live.
caveats: Alt text also serves accessibility for visually impaired shoppers — describe the image honestly, don't just stuff keywords.
Compress images before upload (keep files under 2MB) to avoid hurting page speed.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Write Product Meta Descriptions That Earn Clicks
cards.summary: Craft a roughly 160-character product meta description focused on click appeal rather than keyword density.
cards.use_when: Filling the per-product Search engine listing meta description field in Shopify.
steps: Take the product description and ask ChatGPT to produce a ~160-character search engine listing meta description.
Review and edit for accuracy, brand voice, and a compelling reason to click; the source says the meta description is less about keywords and more about enticing the click.
Paste it into the product's Search engine listing meta description field and save.
If you have a large catalog and manual editing isn't feasible, use an SEO app to bulk-generate, and hand-edit top sellers.
Use the listing preview to confirm how the title and description will render in Google results.
caveats: Very large catalogs may not be practical to edit manually — prioritize high-value pages or use bulk tooling.
Excerpts can also be left auto-derived if they already read well.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Clean URL Handles and Enable 301 Redirects
cards.summary: Shorten product/collection URL handles and keep the automatic redirect checked to avoid losing bookmarked traffic.
cards.use_when: Editing a product or collection URL handle in the Search engine listing preview.
steps: In the product/collection Search engine listing section, edit the URL handle to remove filler words and reflect the product/collection name (e.g., use the title with grammar and special characters stripped out).
Before saving, confirm the checkbox that automatically creates a redirect from the old URL to the new one is checked.
Save. Bookmarked old URLs then forward to the new page instead of returning a 404.
Repeat for collections and any page whose handle you change; the handle should contain the keywords from the title so Google understands the page.
caveats: If the redirect box is unchecked, existing bookmarks and external links break with 404 errors and you lose those visits.
Redirect handling in Shopify's UI may vary by version — verify the checkbox location.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Optimize Collection Pages Without Pushing Products Down
cards.summary: Add keyword-rich collection titles and descriptions while keeping the product grid above the fold.
cards.use_when: Improving a collection page (e.g., 'Bath') that currently has no descriptive content.
steps: Do keyword research for the collection and write a descriptive title that names the products it contains (the source's example reframes a vague 'Bath' into a title describing the scent/type of products).
Write a collection description of roughly 100–400 words containing the right keywords so Google can crawl and understand the page.
In the Shopify theme editor, move the collection description below the product grid if you want products visible first — keep the text on the page regardless.
Set the collection's Search engine listing title and meta description, and update the URL handle to remove filler words.
Confirm the automatic redirect checkbox is checked so the old collection URL forwards to the new one.
Repeat for every collection on the store.
caveats: The source notes that many merchants skip collection descriptions because they push products down; moving the block resolves the tension.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Optimize Pages and Blog Posts, Then Interlink Them
cards.summary: Apply the same title/description/handle process to all pages and posts, and build internal links to spread crawl coverage.
cards.use_when: Extending SEO beyond products and collections, and setting up internal linking between blog content and products.
steps: For every Shopify page and blog post, fill in the title (containing the main keyword plus optionally a secondary), the content/description (with keywords and real value), and the Search engine listing meta description and handle.
Publish new content regularly: the source recommends at least two posts a month, ideally one per week, researched through Keyword Planner and relevant to what you sell.
Add internal links wherever there is a natural opportunity — for example, link from a blog post or benefits page directly to the relevant product in the body content.
Link broadly across pages, posts, and products so that crawling one page reveals the next, helping Google discover more pages faster.
caveats: Posting frequency is the source's recommendation, not a documented ranking threshold — treat it as a practical cadence.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Mobile-Friendliness and Page Speed Checks for Ranking
cards.summary: Verify mobile rendering and diagnose load-speed issues Google uses to rank stores.
cards.use_when: Auditing a theme before or after launch for mobile and speed problems that suppress rankings.
steps: In Chrome, right-click > Inspect, toggle device view, and preview as a device (e.g., iPhone 12 Pro); check that nothing overflows the screen, images aren't distorted, and all content is reachable. In Safari, use Develop > Enter Responsive Design mode.
Run Google PageSpeed Insights on your store URL and read the field data — the source notes these graphs reflect the past 28 days, so fixes won't show there immediately.

Compress all images before upload (keep under 2MB; a page should total roughly 2MB, and an uncompressed 1.4MB image is a problem). The source recommends a free compression service; an SEO app can also bulk-optimize.

Do NOT lazy-load above-the-fold images (e.g., a product hero or homepage banner) — these are typically the Largest Contentful Paint element and lazy-loading them worsens LCP. Other off-screen images can use loading=lazy.
Audit installed apps: third-party app code is out of your control and can slow the store; uninstall anything unused (you can reinstall later) and keep only apps that bring real value.
Re-run the speed test and fix the flagged issues you can act on.
caveats: Most modern Shopify themes are mobile-friendly out of the box, so mobile checks often confirm rather than fix.
PageSpeed field data lags ~28 days — don't expect instant improvement in the graphs.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Add Rich Snippets (FAQ and Product Schema)
cards.summary: Enable structured data so search results show FAQs, ratings, prices, and availability.
cards.use_when: Wanting extra visible SERP real estate for product, FAQ, or article content.
steps: Add a lightweight, accessible FAQ answering genuine pre-purchase questions; do not justify it with promised FAQ rich results.
Add the schema either via custom code (the source references a guide) or via an SEO app that generates FAQ and review schema.
For app-generated snippets, toggle the desired type on (e.g., FAQ, product grid, image) and run the app's built-in test to confirm the snippet is correctly injected.
Monitor Search Console for rich result eligibility and errors.
caveats: Structured data markup requirements and Google's supported rich result types change over time — verify current specs before investing in custom code.
Rich snippets make listings larger and more clickable but don't guarantee ranking.
Use store FAQs to answer shopper questions. Do not promise Google FAQ rich results or treat FAQ markup as a ranking requirement; verify current search feature support.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Submit the Shopify XML Sitemap to Search Console
cards.summary: Point Google at your sitemap after setting your primary domain.
cards.use_when: Finalizing technical SEO setup after optimizing pages so Google can crawl and index them.
steps: First confirm the correct domain is primary: Settings > Domains, set your custom (non-myshopify) domain as primary. The source stresses doing this BEFORE submitting the sitemap so Google crawls the right URLs.
View your sitemap at yourstore.com/sitemap.xml and copy the URL.
In Google Search Console, create/link the property for your site, then go to Indexing > Sitemaps and submit the sitemap URL.
Google will begin crawling and indexing the site; if you changed the primary domain afterward, submit a new sitemap.
caveats: Sitemap path and Search Console navigation can change — verify current interface.
Submitting a sitemap requests crawling; it does not guarantee indexing or ranking.
Sitemaps support discovery; submission does not guarantee crawling, indexing or rankings.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Set Brand Information for Search and Sales Channels
cards.summary: Fill in the Shopify brand tab so Google, Facebook, and other channels represent you accurately.
cards.use_when: Setting up or refreshing store branding that feeds external sales channels and search appearances.
steps: Locate the brand settings tab (the source used Shopify Sidekick to find the link); add logos, colors, and brand identity assets.
Ensure the brand data is consistent, since other sales channels like Facebook and Google pull this information to represent you online.
Revisit when adding new channels or products so listings stay consistent.
caveats: The exact location of brand settings may shift in Shopify admin — verify in your account.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Build Backlinks and Recurring Content for Authority
cards.summary: Grow authority through external links and consistent publishing, which the source frames as what Google rewards.
cards.use_when: Planning off-page SEO and content cadence to lift overall ranking potential.
steps: Pursue backlinks from authoritative sites: partner with people who run large websites, or work with influencers who can mention and link to your store in their articles.
Treat authority as transferable — being featured on a high-authority site passes some of that trust to your store.
Publish new content regularly; the source recommends at least 2 posts/month and ideally weekly.
Research each planned post with Keyword Planner and write on topics close to what you sell and that your customers want to learn about.
For each post, set the title with the main (and optionally secondary) keyword, put the keywords in the content, add a click-worthy meta description, and include a keyword-bearing URL handle.
Use an SEO app to track existing backlinks and find broken links to fix.
caveats: The posting-frequency suggestion is the presenter's opinion, not a documented Google requirement.
Backlink effects are slow and depend on the linking site's authority.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Audit Existing Rankings to Fix Wasted Content
cards.summary: Review which keywords you already rank for and correct pages ranking for irrelevant or zero-volume terms.
cards.use_when: Doing a periodic SEO review to redirect content toward terms that actually drive traffic.
steps: Use an SEO app's 'analyze my keywords' feature (the source shows SEOAnt) to list keywords you currently rank for.
Flag pages ranking for keywords with no search volume or no commercial relevance (the source notes blog posts often do this).
Adjust that content or page to target more useful keywords instead.
Optionally monitor competitor sites by entering their URL to track the keywords they rank for and how they change over time, then adapt strategies that fit your budget.
caveats: Competitor-tracking and keyword-analysis features may sit behind paid app tiers.
Prioritize pages with business value; not every irrelevant ranking needs fixing.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Deciding Whether to Automate Shopify SEO with an App
cards.summary: Weigh manual on-page SEO against app-based automation for image compression, scores, snippets, and keyword research.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to execute SEO at scale across a large catalog.
steps: Assess scope: manual editing of every product/collection/page listing is impractical for large catalogs, so prioritize manual work on high-value pages.

Use an SEO app for bulk tasks the source demonstrated: compressing all product/collection images, generating per-page SEO scores with actionable fix pointers, injecting rich snippets without code, and finding/fixing broken links.

Treat app SEO scores as prioritization guides, not goals: the demo raised a product page from bad to 91 by adding a keyword-bearing H2, then to 94 by adding in-description images and a keyword in the meta description without hitting 100.
Use the app's built-in keyword-research and rank-tracking tools as a partial replacement for Keyword Planner/Ahrefs.
Try the free tier for a small store; upgrade only if the workload justifies it.
caveats: The app recommendation is promotional in the source; the presenter discloses a discount code. Evaluate features and pricing yourself and verify the current interface.
Score targets are app-specific heuristics, not Google ranking rules.
Third-party apps add load and can affect page speed.
cards.source_name: Shopify SEO Optimization Guide for Beginners 2026.docx

cards.title: Deciding whether SEO is worth pursuing for a Shopify store
cards.summary: A pre-investment filter for judging if organic search can become a profitable channel or a waste of months.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest budget, time or agency fees into SEO for your store, before writing any content.
steps: Ask the core question first: do people already search for what you sell? SEO only captures existing demand, it does not create it. The source (Dave Fogerty) argues that if you invented a genuinely new product nobody searches for, SEO cannot help.
Check Google search volume and commercial intent for your main category terms. If people rarely Google your category, content will not rank or convert.
Test margin math: SEO favours stores with healthy AOV and margins. If AOV is low or margins are razor thin, the content investment may never pay back.
Recognise the source's binary framing: for most Shopify brands SEO is either the most profitable channel or a huge waste of time, with little middle ground.

Treat this as a channel-diversification play, not a replacement: the source's Calming Blankets example kept selling via SEO when Meta ads broke repeatedly, but that is one brand's case, not a guarantee.
If those tests pass, commit to bottom-funnel, conversion-intent keywords rather than general blog traffic, which the source says is close to worthless in 2025.
caveats: Source's 10M first-year revenue and #1 ranking in 6 months are one brand's anecdote, not a benchmark.
The 'SEO is all or nothing' framing is the presenter's opinion, not a measured rule.
cards.source_name: Steal These Shopify SEO Hacks To Rank #1 Overnight.docx

cards.title: Capturing branded search your paid ads create
cards.summary: Paid awareness generates branded searches that a competitor may capture if you don't rank for your own name.
cards.use_when: Planning paid acquisition or auditing whether competitors outrank you on your own brand and category terms.
steps: Accept that Meta and other paid ads create latent demand: people see the ad, don't click, then Google your brand or product later. The source calls this branded search.
Check whether your site ranks for your own brand name and the generic product term your ads promote.
If you don't rank, a smaller competitor can appear first and take the sale you paid to generate. The source frames this as one brand funding awareness while another captures conversion.
Protect the conversion path by ensuring a product or collection page (not just homepage) ranks for the branded and category search.
Pair this with the source's keyword-structure hack: build collection pages targeting the variations people Google after seeing an ad.
This is a defensive play on existing spend, not a reason to add SEO budget on top of everything else.
caveats: Source gives no data on how much paid spend leaks to competitors; treat the mechanism as a hypothesis to verify in your own Search Console.
Requires that people actually Google your category, which the source says is not universal.
cards.source_name: Steal These Shopify SEO Hacks To Rank #1 Overnight.docx

cards.title: Multiplying collection pages to target keyword variations
cards.summary: Replace one broad collection page with many specific sub-collection pages that reuse the same products.
cards.use_when: Merchandising a product category where you currently have a single broad collection page competing on one high-difficulty term.
steps: Take your bestselling category and list the different ways people search for it: e.g., hoodies splits into men's hoodies, oversized hoodies, zip hoodies, running hoodies, hoodies under $50.
Build a separate collection (or landing) page for each variation. You can include the same products; you're changing presentation, not inventory.
Validate each keyword in Ahrefs or Semrush: set the keyword difficulty filter below 35 and look for commercial intent (check the current interface, these tools change).
Sanity-check by Googling the keyword: if other collection pages rank, you likely can too. If only giants like Nike rank, it's probably too competitive.
Respect one keyword per page and never target the same keyword with both a product page and a collection page. The source calls this keyword cannibalization and says it will tank results.
This converts one unwinnable competitive term into many smaller, easier terms that accumulate traffic.
caveats: Keyword difficulty guidance (<35) is a source-specific heuristic, not a universal threshold.
Requires genuine search variation; splitting a category into terms nobody searches adds no value.
cards.source_name: Steal These Shopify SEO Hacks To Rank #1 Overnight.docx

cards.title: The four blog formats that still drive ecommerce revenue
cards.summary: Replace lifestyle and seasonal blog content with four bottom- and mid-funnel formats built for buyer intent.
cards.use_when: Planning a content calendar or auditing existing blog posts that get traffic but no sales.
steps: Stop producing the formats the source calls dead in ecommerce: seasonal lifestyle posts, generic listicles, trend pieces, and tips that apply to everyone and sell to no one.

Format 1 - You vs competitors: target 'brand A vs brand B' searches by decision-stage buyers. Mentioning a competitor's name can help you rank for their branded search and introduce yourself as the stronger option.
Format 2 - Alternatives to competitors: target 'alternatives to X' and 'best X alternatives' searches, list options and position yourself first to convert people outside your funnel.
Format 3 - Best [product type] for [use case]: target clear buying intent like 'best eye serums for women over 50'; match product to need and target low-difficulty longtail terms.
Format 4 - Buying guides: long-form evergreen content that educates hesitant buyers and naturally earns backlinks that lift domain authority.
Before writing any post, check the SERP: if blogs rank, write the blog; if it's all collection pages, build that page instead.

The source claims 10-15 well-targeted posts can build this system, and cites a client (Simbotanica) ranking #3 for a competitor's brand name within a week of implementing two competitor-focused formats.
caveats: The Simbotanica ranking-in-a-week result is an anecdote, not a benchmark.
Only works for products with existing search demand.
cards.source_name: Steal These Shopify SEO Hacks To Rank #1 Overnight.docx

cards.title: Building an internal linking system that funnels authority to money pages
cards.summary: Use controlled internal links to push SEO value and user flow toward collection and product pages that convert.
cards.use_when: Optimising an existing store with orphaned blog posts and product pages that never get internal links.
steps: Identify your money pages: the collection and product pages where conversion happens.
Write top- and mid-funnel blogs with the linking flow decided upfront, not bolted on later.
Link from each blog to a money page within the first 100-200 words, then add three to five internal links to related blogs later in the article.
Use descriptive anchor text of two to four words that matches the product. Avoid 'click here' and avoid using your brand name as anchor text.
Link collections from general to specific: e.g., from a collagen supplements collection down to a hair loss collagen for women sub-collection.
Start with your top two to three highest-traffic blog posts and add a clean relevant link from each to your bestselling collection or product page.
Repeat until the site is a connected web. The source claims each link takes seconds and can meaningfully shift monthly revenue.
caveats: Internal links transfer value but cannot fix a site with no external authority or no existing traffic.
The $100 vs $1,000 per month difference is a source claim, not a measured outcome.
cards.source_name: Steal These Shopify SEO Hacks To Rank #1 Overnight.docx

cards.title: Getting cited in AI search results (GEO)
cards.summary: Structure product and content pages with high specificity so AI tools quote your store in generated answers.
cards.use_when: Adapting your PDPs, collections and content for AI Overviews, Perplexity or ChatGPT-style answers that bypass the ten blue links.
steps: Accept the shift the source calls GEO: AI tools summarise multiple sources into one answer, so if you're not cited you may as well not exist for that query.
Note the source's cited study of 768,000+ AI citations: over half came from product pages, comparison content and buying guides, not news or homepages.
Split broad collections into specific use-case pages (e.g., mineral sunscreen for sensitive skin, mineral sunscreen for dry skin) reusing the same products but matching exact query language.
Refresh comparison blogs ('brand A vs brand B', 'best collagen supplements for women over 40') so AI tools have citable, question-shaped content.
Test by Googling your product type phrased as a question, e.g., 'What hoodie is best for me?', and study which pages get cited in any AI overview.
Audit each collection: can it be split into individual needs or situations? The source says need-specific pages tend to outperform in both AI and organic search.
Make cited pages skimable, useful and product-focused so both AI tools and humans can extract an answer.
caveats: The 768,000-citation study is reported second-hand; treat the exact split as indicative, not verified.
GEO is an emerging channel with uncertain durability; the source frames it as early-mover arbitrage.
cards.source_name: Steal These Shopify SEO Hacks To Rank #1 Overnight.docx

cards.title: Research conversational and long-tail queries for AI-driven search
cards.summary: Start GEO work by finding the conversational, question-shaped, long-tail queries users actually type into AI engines rather than head keywords.
cards.use_when: Planning product-page copy, category descriptions, or blog topics so the store can surface in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, or Google AI Overviews answers.
steps: List the core topics your store's products sit inside (e.g., organic skincare, gourmet coffee, boutique fitness).
For each, write out the conversational, question-based phrases a shopper would ask an AI, the source's examples: 'best natural moisturizer for dry skin' or 'how to treat acne with organic products'.
Then analyze how the AI platforms structure their responses to those queries — what they include, how they cite, what format wins — and mirror that structure in your content plan.
Map each query to the page that should answer it (PDP, FAQ, comparison or guide) rather than one undifferentiated content calendar.
caveats: The source gives skincare/coffee/fitness examples, not ecommerce performance data; treat the query patterns as a starting method, not a benchmark.
AI engines and their interfaces change frequently — re-verify current response formats.
cards.source_name: 7 Essential Tactics for Mastering Generative Engine Optimization (GEO).docx

cards.title: Write direct, answer-first content instead of keyword-density fluff
cards.summary: GEO content should clearly and contextually answer a specific question rather than stuff keywords into long generic pieces.
cards.use_when: Writing PDP copy, buying guides, or FAQ content intended to be cited by AI engines.
steps: Pick the conversational query the page targets and answer it directly and early.
Keep the writing engaging, informative, and easy to understand — clarity and contextual relevance are what the source says AI engines reward.
Skip long fluff pieces built only to raise keyword density.
Support the page with high-quality supporting media (the source's examples: images, video, infographics) to raise engagement.
For a gourmet coffee store, the source's example of a strong topic is a detailed article on brewing pour-over or the benefits of single-origin beans — apply the same specificity to your own category.
caveats: The source presents this as its view of what AI engines favor, not as a measured ranking factor.
Producing media assets is out of scope here; focus on the copy and answer structure.
cards.source_name: 7 Essential Tactics for Mastering Generative Engine Optimization (GEO).docx

cards.title: Structure and schema-model pages for AI parsing
cards.summary: Well-structured pages with clear headings, lists, and schema markup are easier for AI engines to extract and reuse.
cards.use_when: Formatting PDPs, category pages, or guides, or when adding structured data for schedules, reviews, or pricing.
steps: Break content into clear sections with descriptive headings. The source's fitness-studio example: 'Benefits of Pilates', 'Beginner Pilates exercises', 'Advanced Pilates movements'.
Use bullet points and short, concise paragraphs instead of dense blocks.
Apply structured data and schema markup to surface the facts AI engines need — the source names class schedules, reviews, and pricing as examples.
Translate that for ecommerce: mark up product price, availability, reviews/ratings, FAQs, and specifications so engines can lift clear answers.
caveats: Schema types and platform support change; verify current supported markup before implementing.
Schema improves machine readability but does not substitute for a direct answer in the body content.
cards.source_name: 7 Essential Tactics for Mastering Generative Engine Optimization (GEO).docx

cards.title: Match content to user intent across the funnel
cards.summary: Prioritize what the user actually wants to know, covering informational through transactional intent to widen the chance an AI engine features you.
cards.use_when: Deciding which pages to create or rewrite so both research-stage and buy-stage queries can surface your store.
steps: Identify what the user is looking for and wants to know for each query, then tailor the content to that need.
Cover a spread of intents. The source's eco-friendly home products example maps 'how to reduce plastic waste at home' (informational) and 'top 10 sustainable kitchen products' (more transactional).
For an online store, pair informational guides that answer the how/why with transactional pages that answer the which/where-to-buy, and cross-link them.
Addressing multiple intent levels, per the source, gives more opportunities to be seen in AI-driven engines.
caveats: Intent labeling is a working heuristic; validate against your own search and site behavior.
Do not let informational pages cannibalize the PDP's role — keep the buying path clear.
cards.source_name: 7 Essential Tactics for Mastering Generative Engine Optimization (GEO).docx

cards.title: Use reviews, testimonials and UGC as fresh AI-visible content
cards.summary: Distributing content socially and encouraging customer reviews and UGC adds authenticity and diverse perspectives that AI engines are said to value.
cards.use_when: Building review collection, social distribution, or on-site UGC for a product to improve both trust and AI visibility.
steps: Distribute your content across social platforms rather than letting it live only on the store site.
Actively encourage user-generated content — reviews, testimonials, and social posts.
The source's artisanal chocolate example: invite customers to share reviews and photos on Instagram under a branded hashtag, then showcase that UGC on the website.
Surface the collected reviews and UGC on relevant product pages and category pages so it is machine-readable and reusable.
Treat the richness that comes from customer satisfaction, in the source's framing, as a content asset, not just a rating number.
caveats: The source asserts AI engines value fresh, diverse perspectives but provides no measurement of the effect.
Review solicitation must comply with platform and disclosure rules; do not fabricate reviews.
cards.source_name: 7 Essential Tactics for Mastering Generative Engine Optimization (GEO).docx

cards.title: Build answer authority with citations, experts and statistics
cards.summary: Supporting content with reliable references, expert quotes, and relevant statistics builds trust with both users and AI algorithms.
cards.use_when: Writing category guides, buying advice, or health/specialty product content where credibility affects citation and conversion.
steps: Cite reliable references and link to reputable sources. The source's telehealth example uses links to reputable medical sources.
Include expert quotes. The same example uses quotes from healthcare professionals for topics like telehealth benefits or preparing for a virtual appointment.
Use relevant statistics to substantiate claims rather than asserting them.
Apply this to ecommerce: for supplement, wellness, or technical gear pages, quote qualified practitioners or engineers and cite testing data or standards bodies.
Treat expertise signals as additive — they sit on top of, not instead of, direct answers and clear structure.
caveats: The source asserts this helps with 'AI algorithms' but offers no proof or ranking data.
Regulated categories (health, supplements) require care with claims; cite compliant sources only.
cards.source_name: 7 Essential Tactics for Mastering Generative Engine Optimization (GEO).docx

cards.title: Treat GEO as an ongoing monitoring and adaptation loop
cards.summary: Generative engine optimization is not one-time work; you must watch how AI platforms evolve and keep refining content.
cards.use_when: Setting a recurring workstream for AI search visibility alongside SEO analytics and rank tracking.
steps: Set up recurring monitoring of how AI platforms (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overviews) structure and cite responses to your target queries.
Track visibility and engagement benchmarks across those platforms and review changes over time.
Stay current on AI-driven search trends and refine your strategy rather than locking in a fixed playbook.
Fold this into existing SEO analytics cadence — the source frames GEO as adapting SEO tracking frameworks, not replacing them.
When a platform's answer format or citation behavior shifts, re-check whether your target pages still match it.
caveats: Platform interfaces, features and availability change without notice — verify current tooling before relying on any specific monitoring method.
GEO visibility metrics are newer and less standardized than classic rank tracking.
cards.source_name: 7 Essential Tactics for Mastering Generative Engine Optimization (GEO).docx

cards.title: Keyword vetting with the BID formula
cards.summary: Screen candidate keywords through business potential, SERP intent match and ranking difficulty before committing content budget.
cards.use_when: Product selection and content planning: deciding which keyword clusters to build category, product or comparison pages around for an online store.
steps: Gather candidate keywords from seed terms plus modifiers using a keyword tool's matching-terms report, filtered with include/exclude operators.

Apply B for business potential: ask whether ranking first actually helps the store. A high-volume informational term like 'what is espresso' rarely leads to a purchase, while 'best espresso machine under $500' shows intent and budget.

Apply I for intent: search the keyword and inspect what currently ranks. If the top results are product/category pages and you plan a blog post, the SERP says the searcher wants to buy — match the format or drop the keyword.
Apply D for difficulty: check referring domains and domain rating of the top-ranking pages. Seeing a few low-DR sites in the top 10 is a positive signal per the source.
Only target keywords that pass all three tests.
caveats: BID is the presenter's heuristic, not a scored formula; treat thresholds like 'a few low-DR sites' as qualitative.
AI overviews appear on roughly 21% of keywords overall, and the source cites nearly 58% for question queries, 46% for 7+ word queries, 99.9% informational — verify current figures in your own market.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: AI filter: avoid keywords AI already fully answers
cards.summary: Before targeting a keyword, judge whether an AI overview satisfies the searcher so completely that no click will happen.
cards.use_when: Content prioritisation for a store blog or buying guide where you would otherwise invest in informational posts that never earn clicks.
steps: Take any keyword that passed business-potential and intent checks, then search it and read the AI overview as a shopper would.

Ask whether the AI answer is sufficient or whether the searcher still needs to click for detail, pricing, or options. If the overview nails it, the source says targeting it traditionally may be a trap.
For keywords AI fully answers, do not chase the organic click. Instead re-target them for AEO: aim to have your brand named inside the AI response (see the mention-gap workflow card).

Redirect click-driven effort to action-oriented queries that AI cannot complete — searches containing calculator, checker, generator, tool, template, finder, planner, maker — and to transactional-intent filtered queries, where the source says the organic click is still available.
Verify the current AI overview landscape per keyword in your own market before committing, since coverage changes.
caveats: The claim that AI cannot satisfy interactive tool queries is time-sensitive; re-check as AI interfaces add tool use.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Find competitor mention gaps with branded-query filters
cards.summary: Use AI visibility tooling to isolate prompts where competitors are named but your brand is absent, especially best/top/versus/review/alternative queries.
cards.use_when: Competitive positioning and merchandising decisions about which comparison and best-of content to produce so your store gets named in AI answers.
steps: Enter your domain in an AI visibility tool (the source uses Ahrefs Brand Radar) and open the platform view for the engine you care about.
Use the filter that shows responses mentioning others only — i.e. where competitors appear and you do not.
Layer keyword filters for best, top, versus, review, and alternative to surface the queries where AI recommends brands in your category without you.
Treat the resulting list as your short list of target queries, then plan content and third-party mentions that map to each.
Repeat the report regularly: the source notes over 45% of citations change when AI overviews refresh, roughly every two days.
caveats: Tool menu names may change — verify the current interface before building a workflow.
Brand Radar is the source's commercial product; the underlying method (filtering for competitor-only mentions) is what matters.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Content structure: BLUF, atomic sections, entities, declarative sentences
cards.summary: Four writing rules that let both skimming humans and chunking LLMs extract your key answer from any section of a PDP-supporting article or guide.
cards.use_when: Writing or editing buying guides, category explainers and comparison articles on a store's content hub.
steps: BLUF (bottom line up front): open every section with the answer, not the backstory. Example from the source: 'The most effective way to build backlinks in 2026 is to create original research' instead of several sentences about how the landscape evolved.

Make sections atomic: each H2 should make complete sense if extracted alone, because AI systems chunk pages differently and you cannot control where the split lands. Test by reading an H2 in isolation; rewrite if it depends on earlier context.

Write entity-rich: name brands, products and concepts instead of vague references. 'This tool helps with SEO' becomes 'Ahrefs Keywords Explorer helps you find low-difficulty, high-traffic-potential keywords'. For a store, name the product, the material, the use case.
Keep sentences simple and declarative: one idea per sentence, clear subject-verb-object, and cut anything that takes two reads to parse.
Use this as a clarity checklist for shoppers and extracted excerpts; the source's positional-weight explanation is not a universal model behavior.
caveats: The source explicitly rejects writing a special 'AI format'; the audience remains human readers.
Word count is not a factor — see the length/freshness/format data card.
Google does not require special content chunking. Preserve context and qualifications even in concise answers.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Content length, freshness and format signals for AI citations
cards.summary: Cited pages are not long, are meaningfully fresher than organic results, and skew heavily toward lists and comparisons — so refresh and format beat word count.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to rewrite or expand category and guide pages, and choosing which content formats to invest in for AI visibility.
steps: Do not lengthen articles for citation's sake: across 174,000+ cited pages the source reports a 0.04 correlation between word count and citation, and 53.4% of cited pages are under 1,000 words.
Prioritise freshness: cited content averaged 25.7% fresher than traditional organic results, and for ChatGPT 89.7% of top-cited pages were updated in 2025 with 76% refreshed in the last 30 days.
Make updates substantive, not cosmetic — do not simply change the publish date.

Choose formats AI can lift from: 43.8% of all cited pages are listicles (best X, top X), and data-driven content with original stats and X-versus-Y comparisons also performs because AI cites specific numbers and comparison pages map to how users ask questions.
Apply this to store content by maintaining best-of roundups, head-to-head comparisons and original benchmark or sizing data tied to your catalogue.
caveats: These are Ahrefs study figures presented in the course, not universal benchmarks; re-validate against your own pages over time.
Frequent 30-day refreshes describe ChatGPT's cited set, not a requirement for every page.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Refresh sleeper pages to win citations fastest
cards.summary: Find pages with backlinks but declining traffic and update them, because existing authority plus refreshed content is the quickest route to AI citations.
cards.use_when: Replenishment of an existing content library: choosing which product guides or category pages to update this quarter instead of writing new ones.
steps: Open a site explorer / top-pages report for your domain and sort by traffic change to find pages with significant declines.
Filter for pages that have both a decent number of backlinks (existing authority) and a clear traffic decline (likely stale content).
Verify the decline is a content problem, not a link problem: if the page never had many referring domains, a rewrite probably won't help.
Update the content meaningfully — new data, new products, changed specifications, current-year details — rather than editing the date.
Prioritise these before net-new content when you need fast AI visibility, since freshness is a strong citation signal.
caveats: Requires access to historical traffic and backlink data for the page.
Traffic decline can have causes other than staleness (lost rankings from algorithm changes, seasonality) — check before investing.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Brand the frameworks you invent to resist LLM flattening
cards.summary: Name original concepts after your brand and distribute them widely so AI credits rather than absorbs them as generic knowledge.
cards.use_when: Differentiating your store's expertise — sizing systems, fit guides, material standards or comparison frameworks — in a market where AI summarises everything.
steps: Identify an original concept worth owning, e.g. a scoring matrix or fit methodology.
Name it with your brand prefix rather than a generic label — the source's example contrasts 'content scoring matrix' with '<brand> content scoring matrix'.
Define the concept explicitly on your own site so the definition is citable.
Distribute it widely with the name attached: blog, social channels, podcasts, community platforms such as Reddit.
The rationale: the source notes LLMs tend to flatten unlabelled original concepts into general knowledge without credit; repetition with the name attached makes that harder.
caveats: Branded frameworks are the presenter's recommendation, not a measured causal result.
Requires consistent naming across channels to work.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Tier-one mentions: get listed on editorial listicles and comparison pages
cards.summary: Prioritise mentions in authoritative third-party editorial content, which correlate most strongly with AI overview visibility, and locate the target pages programmatically.
cards.use_when: Acquisition and brand-building for a store trying to be named in AI answers to best-of and versus queries in its product category.
steps: Understand why: the source reports branded web mentions had the strongest correlation with AI overview visibility across 75,000 brands (0.664), and mentions on highly linked pages correlated at 0.7 — higher than general brand mentions, backlinks or domain rating.

Open a cited-domains report for your brand to see which sites AI cites for your topics, plus response counts, page counts and mention frequency. Identify the equivalents of the source's examples (KBB for cars, CNET for tech, niche industry blogs) for your category.

Do not wait for a page to already be cited: use a content search tool with title:best or title:versus plus a minus operator on your brand name to surface listicles and comparison posts where you are absent, then filter for pages with many referring domains.
Pursue those pages for inclusion or review, since 43.8% of ChatGPT citations are listicles and comparisons.
Log which targets convert into mentions for later measurement.
caveats: Correlation, not causation — the source presents these as the strongest observed relationships.
Editorial inclusion usually cannot be bought directly; expect outreach effort.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Tier-two mentions on community and UGC platforms, without spamming
