cards.summary: Reddit, Quora and niche forums are heavily cited and foundational training sources, but the source warns against dropping your brand name into threads.
cards.use_when: Community-led visibility for a store whose buyers research in forums and subreddits before purchasing.
steps: Recognise the value: the source states Reddit is one of the most frequently cited sources by ChatGPT and a foundational training source for LLMs; Reddit also appears among top AI-overview citations.
Identify the specific communities and threads where your category is discussed.
Do not spam threads with brand mentions — the source explicitly says that is not the play.
Contribute genuinely useful answers that establish expertise, so mentions are earned through participation rather than inserted.
Treat this as an ongoing presence channel rather than a one-off campaign, because community citations and training associations compound.
caveats: The source cuts off before detailing the full tier-two method, so this card covers the stated principle only.
Community platforms penalise promotional behaviour; expect slow returns.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Query fan-out and why topical coverage beats single-keyword pages
cards.summary: AI expands one prompt into many synthetic sub-queries, so pages must cover a whole topic rather than one exact match keyword.
cards.use_when: Category page and buying-guide planning for a store that wants to be pulled into AI answers about its product area.
steps: Understand the mechanic: search moved from one-query-one-result to many-to-one, and AI search is one-to-many — a single prompt fans out into sub-queries run in parallel and merged into one answer.

Assume breadth: the source cites research showing an average prompt triggers 9–11 fan-out queries, some as high as 28, and one ChatGPT deep-research example ran 420 searches for a red phone case query.

Audit for topic completeness. The source's example: a page on starting a podcast that covers only the basics but omits equipment, hosting and promotion loses the citation to a page that covers them. For a store, a category page should cover selection criteria, compatibility, sizing, use cases and comparisons.

Do not build a keyword list from fan-out queries: the source says they are synthetic, generated in the moment and inconsistent, and over 95% have zero search volume — use them as a window into what topics AI considers important, not as targets.
If your tooling exposes fan-out queries for prompts (the source uses Ahrefs Brand Radar's AI responses report), review them to sense topic expectations.
caveats: Fan-out counts are research findings, not fixed volumes; the same prompt can produce different fan-outs each time.
Tool support for viewing fan-out queries may change — verify current availability.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: AI visibility is probabilistic, not a ranking position
cards.summary: Citations vary between identical prompts and are shaped by consensus, freshness and authority, so track share of visibility rather than a fixed rank.
cards.use_when: Setting expectations and KPIs for a store's AI search programme before investing in content or mentions.
steps: Stop expecting a fixed position. The source describes AI output as probabilities stacked on probabilities: training patterns, retrieved-page signals and a temperature setting that adds randomness — asking the same question five times might cite you three times.
Track AI visibility as a distribution across repeated prompts and platforms rather than a single rank check.

Influence the probability levers the source identifies: consensus (multiple sources saying the same thing about your brand makes AI more likely to repeat it), freshness (cited content about 25% fresher than traditional SERPs), and authority (pages ranking well in traditional search have a head start).
Use this to justify investing in consistent third-party mentions and ongoing content refresh rather than one-off campaigns.
Report share of voice and impression/mention counts alongside any ranking-style metric.
caveats: The source's '25% fresher' and citation-overlap figures come from Ahrefs' own studies; treat them as source-specific heuristics.
Probabilistic measurement requires repeated sampling — single checks are unreliable.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Two information sources: training data vs real-time retrieval
cards.summary: AI answers come from static training snapshots or live web retrieval (RAG), giving you two distinct levers — broad mentions and crawlable, rankable content.
cards.use_when: Planning how a new product launch or store brand will be discovered in AI assistants within weeks rather than months.
steps: Models can answer from learned patterns, provided context or retrieved information. Training data and update schedules differ by model and are not controlled by publishing a store page.
Recognise real-time retrieval (RAG): when a question is fresh or specific, the assistant searches the web via APIs, pulls pages, reads them and generates an answer from what it found.
Prioritize accurate, retrievable product information and credible brand coverage. Broader mentions do not guarantee inclusion in future model training.
For a product launch, publish current crawlable facts and monitor retrieved answers; treat changes to non-search answers as uncertain observations.
Check that AI crawlers are not blocked — see the robots.txt card.
caveats: Training-data refresh cadence ('maybe every 6 months or so') is the presenter's approximation and varies by model and vendor.
Retrieved pages are scored alongside trained patterns, so retrieval does not guarantee a mention.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Check CDN and robots rules for accidental search-crawler blocking
cards.summary: Verify public product and collection pages are accessible to the intended search crawlers while preserving separate training choices.
cards.use_when: A store wants product pages discoverable in AI search or is diagnosing missing product visibility after CDN or theme changes.
steps: Inspect robots.txt and CDN or firewall rules for representative public product and collection URLs.
For ChatGPT search, check OAI-SearchBot; GPTBot controls training separately. For Google Search AI features, inspect Googlebot access. Do not blanket-enable unrelated crawlers.
Check HTTP responses and actual crawler logs where available; compare initial HTML with rendered product facts to identify rendering dependencies.
Correct unintended blocks for the desired search crawler, preserving deliberate training restrictions and protected checkout or account areas.
Retest after deployment and future CDN or theme changes; access enables retrieval but does not guarantee recommendation.
caveats: Verify current crawler documentation and CDN settings; defaults change. A spoofed user-agent test alone does not verify real crawler access.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Capture AI-driven demand with a post-purchase 'how did you hear about us?' survey
cards.summary: Unlinked AI mentions arrive as 'Direct' traffic, so self-reported attribution is needed to see the brand awareness AI generates.
cards.use_when: Attribution and retention analytics for a store whose AI mentions often come without links.
steps: Unlinked recommendations can lead to later direct visits, branded search or no visit. Referral analytics cannot measure all of this; source-reported link percentages are context, not a universal attribution rule.
Add a 'How did you hear about us?' question to the post-purchase survey so buyers can self-report AI assistants, brand searches or word of mouth.
Provide options that distinguish AI assistants, organic search, social, and a friend or colleague, plus an open text field.
Review responses periodically alongside AI mention data to judge whether AI awareness is translating into purchases.
Combine with platform-level mention and citation monitoring rather than relying on click-through alone.
caveats: Self-reported attribution is imprecise and subject to recall and selection bias.
Requires enough purchase volume for the responses to be meaningful; low-volume stores should treat it directionally.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Diagnose visibility gaps across six dimensions
cards.summary: A six-bucket framework — visibility, narrative, topic, format, web mentions and demand — turns AI visibility data into a prioritised action list.
cards.use_when: Quarterly planning for a store's content and brand programme, deciding whether to fix, build or influence.
steps: Map branded entities first: main brand, sub-brands, product names, proprietary features or metrics, and associated personal brands. Each has its own AI visibility profile and can be analysed separately.
Attach to each entity the topics and attributes it should be associated with, inferred from recurring adjectives and modifiers people use alongside your brand or category.
Run the audit and read four metrics per AI platform: mentions, citations (actual source links), impressions (estimated exposure), and AI share of voice versus competitors.

Classify each finding into the six gaps: visibility (you appear less than competitors), narrative (AI describes you against your intended positioning, e.g. 'budget alternative' when you are premium), topic (topics you should own but do not), format (content types AI cites that you do not produce, such as video), web mentions (external listicles, review sites, forums naming competitors but not you), and demand (branded queries or awareness opportunities you have not captured).

Prioritise by asking how much demand the opportunity could drive, whether it supports credibility, and whether it improves citation chances, then label each fix as fix (optimise existing), build (create new) or influence (offsite mentions).
Start with quick wins: a page that already ranks but needs an update to close a topic gap, or a major listicle your competitors are on that you can win via outreach.
Repeat the same audit for competitors to find topics and gaps you have overlooked.
caveats: The six-gap framework is attributed to an Ahrefs guide and the tooling shown is Ahrefs Brand Radar — the dimensions are transferable, the reports are product-specific.
Most stores will find gaps concentrated in one or two buckets, which the source frames as a signal to build systems around them.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Platform-specific citation preferences: where to allocate AEO effort
cards.summary: AI platforms barely overlap in sources, so match your existing strengths and target sources to the specific engine you prioritise.
cards.use_when: Channel prioritisation: choosing whether to invest in YouTube, editorial PR, community presence or traditional rankings based on which AI engine your category's buyers use.
steps: Accept divergence: across the top 50 cited domains on Google AI overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity, only seven appeared on all three (14% overlap), per the source.
For Google AI overviews: favour authoritative established sites and Google-owned properties; the source states YouTube accounts for about 5.6% of all AI overview citations and Reddit is also strong.

For ChatGPT: favour publishers and media; the source reports the median domain rating of its top cited pages is 90, and that licensing deals with outlets influence sourcing. Being mentioned on high-DR editorial sites, Reddit or niche review sites may matter more than your own pages' Google rank.

For Perplexity: it aligns most closely with traditional Google rankings — the source reports about 28.6% of its citations come from Google top-10 pages, versus roughly 8–10% overlap for ChatGPT — so if you already rank well in Google, Perplexity is likely your fastest AI visibility.

For Google AI mode: do not assume it mirrors AI overviews. The source reports only 13.7% citation overlap despite 86% semantic similarity in answers, YouTube as the top cited domain, and Quora cited 3.5x more than in AI overviews, with heavier Facebook and Instagram sourcing.

Prioritise by market share first (the source says Google AI features and ChatGPT hold most AI search traffic currently, with Perplexity much smaller), then by how much overlap exists with your existing SEO strengths.
Inspect which cited domains differ across platforms for your own brand before committing budget.
caveats: Platform sourcing mixes change frequently; these figures are source-specific snapshots.
The source also reports the AI-overview/top-10 Google connection weakening from 76% to about 38% in a more recent study, and that 14% of cited pages do not rank in Google's top 100 at all.
Do not build separate strategies per platform — the source recommends shared fundamentals with prioritised targeting.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Treat AI visibility as a spectrum: cited, mentioned, or invisible
cards.summary: Three states of AI visibility, each with different business value, so define which state matters for your store before optimising.
cards.use_when: Goal-setting and reporting for an AI search programme, and choosing whether to chase links, mentions or both.
steps: Distinguish the three states: cited and linked (AI links to your page — best case for direct traffic, easiest to measure); mentioned but not linked (AI names you with no clickable link, functioning as word-of-mouth at scale that drives brand search); and fully invisible (you cannot fix what you cannot see).
Weigh reliance on links accordingly: the source reports about 28% of AI mentions include a link on average, with platform variation from 51.6% (Perplexity) to 10.7% (AI overviews).

Note that linked mentions concentrate on higher-traffic prompts: the source reports links appear in about 78% of Perplexity impressions despite 51% of mentions, and 71% of Gemini impressions despite 16.8% of mentions.
Track unlinked mentions as possible brand exposure; a mention is not automatically a training example or proof of a purchase contribution.

Match goal to business type: for product sellers, target being named when buyers ask about your category (e.g. a 'best golf balls' query where shoppers can click through to retailers or manufacturers); for publishers and creators, treat training-data visibility as the long game; for the invisible, start with the gap audit.
Measure the gap between impressions and mentions in your AI visibility tool — that gap is your opportunity.
caveats: Mention-to-link percentages and impression weightings are Ahrefs study figures, not universal constants.
Unlinked mention value is argued through training-association theory and a 0.664 correlation across 75,000 brands — correlation, not proof of causation.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Mining listicles and comparisons where your brand is absent
cards.summary: Find high-authority listicle and comparison pages in your niche that omit your brand, then pursue mentions there because AI pulls from those pages.
cards.use_when: Planning a link/mention acquisition campaign to increase AI citations for your product category.
steps: Identify the authority sites in your niche that AI is likely to cite for your category (industry vertical review sites, mainstream tech/pricing hubs, niche blogs).

Use a content explorer tool: search your product/category title, add operators like title:best or title:versus, and add a minus operator before your brand name to surface listicles and comparison posts that don't currently mention you.
Filter results by number of referring domains to prioritize pages that already attract links and authority.
Don't wait for AI to cite a page first — if a page has strong links and covers your topic, there's a decent chance it will be cited eventually, so target it proactively.
Reach out to the publisher to be added to the list/comparison, positioning your product where it genuinely fits the criteria.
caveats: The source presents this as a judgment call ('good chance') rather than a guaranteed citation outcome.
No conversion benchmarks are given; treat resulting mentions as an awareness/citation play.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Earning mentions in community and UGC platforms
cards.summary: Join and contribute genuinely to Reddit, Quora, and niche forums where your buyers ask questions, because these are heavily cited and used as AI training sources.
cards.use_when: Building brand visibility on community platforms to influence AI recommendations for your product category.
steps: Recognize that Reddit is among the most frequently cited sources by ChatGPT and a foundational training source for LLMs.
Find relevant threads by checking a cited-domains report for your space: if reddit.com appears, drill into which specific threads AI is pulling from.

Alternatively, use Site Explorer on reddit.com, open the organic keywords report, filter for keywords ranking in the top 5, add your niche terms to the include filter — this surfaces Reddit pages already ranking in Google related to your space.
Repeat the same method for niche forums and Q&A sites where your audience discusses problems you solve.
Contribute real, genuinely helpful answers to questions your product or expertise can actually address — not brand-name spam, which backfires quickly.
caveats: Spamming threads with your brand name will backfire fast, per the source.
Community participation has reputational risk if done transactionally.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Using owned content properties as additional AI citation sources
cards.summary: Leverage your own owned channels (secondary domains, YouTube, podcast, social) as topically relevant citation sources that AI can learn from.
cards.use_when: Deciding which owned channels to invest in to increase your brand's presence in AI training and citation data.
steps: Recognize that some brands run multiple authoritative domains (the source cites Ahrefs owning detailed.com and bloggerjet as an example) that can serve as additional citation sources.

If you don't have resources for multiple sites, apply the same principle to your existing properties: your YouTube channel, your podcast, and your LinkedIn content are all indexed and can show up as AI sources.
Ensure all owned properties present your brand in a positive, topically relevant way so AI has more positive training examples to learn from.
Treat owned channels as compounding citation assets rather than one-off campaigns.
caveats: The example of a brand owning multiple domains is illustrative; the source explicitly notes most businesses lack resources for multiple sites.
Value is cumulative and not immediately measurable.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Running a regular brand mention audit
cards.summary: Periodically audit whether your brand mentions and AI sentiment have changed, because pages get updated and your brand can be added or removed without notice.
cards.use_when: Monitoring and maintaining your store's brand reputation in AI-generated answers and cited sources over time.
steps: Use a brand-tracking tool (source: Brand Radar) to track overall mention trends over time and watch for drops in mention volume.
If you find a page that used to mention you but removed your brand during an update, investigate it — it may be worth re-engaging the publisher.
Track sentiment: check whether AI responses about your brand are accurate and positive.
If you spot misinformation, first update your own content to directly contradict it, then reach out to the publisher to request a correction.
Move quickly on inaccurate mentions so AI has less time to learn from the error.
caveats: Fixing misinformation is a two-front effort (your own content + publisher outreach); the source notes speed matters because AI can absorb errors.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Targeting search-hit YouTube topics instead of viral hits
cards.summary: Prioritize YouTube topics with sustained search demand over viral ones because search hits get consistent traffic and are more likely to be cited by AI.
cards.use_when: Planning a YouTube content calendar to drive durable product discovery through both Google and AI answers.
steps: Distinguish search hits (consistent traffic from Google/YouTube search month after month) from viral hits (spike, then dies when the algorithm exhausts interested viewers).
Reason: if Google is already ranking a YouTube video for a keyword, AI overviews will likely cite it too, and search-video titles clearly state what the video covers — which AI prefers.
To find topics: enter www.youtube.com/watch in Site Explorer, open the organic keywords report, filter for rankings in the top 3, and add your niche terms to the include filter.
This yields topics where YouTube videos already rank at the top of Google in your space — target those.
Align these topics with your product's category so the content supports commercial discovery.
caveats: Keyword filters (top 3) are the source's specific method; results depend on your tool's data.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: YouTube video ranking checklist for product discovery
cards.summary: Five on-video elements that make a video rank in Google and get cited by AI, from title keywords to spoken terms and format matching.
cards.use_when: Producing YouTube videos intended to surface in search and AI answers for product-relevant queries.
steps: Put the exact keyword in the title — no clever or clickbaity titles; save creativity for the thumbnail (title handles the keyword, thumbnail sells the click).
Write a real description that summarizes the video and includes the target keyword in the first couple of lines; Google, AI, and viewers all read it.
Add timestamps so they become YouTube chapters; chapters can appear in Google for specific queries, linking directly to a segment (extra visibility for ~2 minutes of work).
Actually say the keyword aloud in the video — Google can understand audio content, so speak the target phrase rather than only putting it in the title.
Match the format already ranking: if tutorials dominate, make a tutorial; if listicles rank, make a listicle — match the searcher's intent.
caveats: The source attributes the audio-understanding claim to Google's VP of Search; this capability could change.
Format-matching assumes the ranking format reflects genuine searcher intent.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Finding YouTube topics AI is already citing for your niche
cards.summary: Use a brand-tracking topics report filtered to youtube.com to find queries where AI pulls YouTube videos, then create content for those topics.
cards.use_when: Deciding which YouTube topics to produce to maximize probability of AI citation.
steps: Open your brand/visibility tool's topics report (source: Brand Radar) for a popular brand or YouTube channel in your space.
Set a filter where the mentioned domain is youtube.com.
Review the queries now surfacing YouTube videos in AI answers.
Create content around those specific topics, applying the ranking checklist: right keyword, thorough and well-optimized, comprehensive without wasting viewers' time.
Keep in mind every video is potential AI training data, so even videos not cited immediately are being absorbed — go for helpful, specific, well-structured content.
caveats: This relies on a specific tool's topics report; the exact interface should be verified as it may change.
Citation is probabilistic, not guaranteed.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Audit search crawler access independently from training permissions
cards.summary: Verify public product and collection pages are accessible to the intended search crawlers while preserving separate training choices.
cards.use_when: A store wants product pages discoverable in AI search or is diagnosing missing product visibility after CDN or theme changes.
steps: Inspect robots.txt and CDN or firewall rules for representative public product and collection URLs.
For ChatGPT search, check OAI-SearchBot; GPTBot controls training separately. For Google Search AI features, inspect Googlebot access. Do not blanket-enable unrelated crawlers.
Check HTTP responses and actual crawler logs where available; compare initial HTML with rendered product facts to identify rendering dependencies.
Correct unintended blocks for the desired search crawler, preserving deliberate training restrictions and protected checkout or account areas.
Retest after deployment and future CDN or theme changes; access enables retrieval but does not guarantee recommendation.
caveats: Verify current crawler documentation and CDN settings; defaults change. A spoofed user-agent test alone does not verify real crawler access.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Handling JavaScript rendering and page speed for AI crawlers
cards.summary: Some AI crawlers can't render JavaScript and drop slow pages during real-time retrieval, so serve server-rendered, fast pages.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why a store's key pages aren't being read or cited by ChatGPT and other AI crawlers.
steps: Rendering support differs by crawler. Compare initial HTML and rendered HTML on product and collection pages instead of assuming a permanent capability for each AI brand.
Where key product facts require unsupported rendering, expose them through the storefront's server-rendered templates or a suitable pre-rendering solution.
Disable JavaScript as a diagnostic, then validate the target crawler's behavior; missing content in this test does not prove invisibility to every engine.
Address page speed: AI systems fetch, parse, and chunk pages in real time, and slow pages can be dropped before scoring — potentially more important for AI retrieval than traditional search.
If you've optimized Core Web Vitals for SEO, you're most of the way there; fast pages with clean HTML benefit both.
caveats: Rendering capabilities of AI crawlers change over time; verify current behavior.
The claim that speed matters more for AI retrieval than for search is the source's assertion.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Structuring HTML for AI parsability
cards.summary: Logical heading hierarchy and self-contained sections make it easier for AI systems to chunk and extract the right content from your pages.
cards.use_when: Building or editing product pages, category pages, or blog posts so AI can cleanly extract and cite their content.
steps: Use proper heading hierarchy: H1 for the title, H2s for main sections, H3s for subsections.
Keep each section able to stand on its own, because AI may chunk your content at any heading boundary.
Write focused paragraphs that each cover one clear idea.
Apply the same content principles used for citable content — clear, atomic, entity-rich writing — but recognize these are also technical parsability decisions, not just style.
This ties into the content-quality principles from earlier lessons; structure and writing quality work together for AI extraction.
caveats: The source presents this as making extraction easier, not guaranteeing citation.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Using and limiting schema markup for AEO
cards.summary: Schema markup is low-risk but unproven for AI citation; add standard types as a good habit without over-investing for AEO alone.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much time to spend on structured data when setting up new store pages.
steps: For ecommerce, inspect accurate Product and Offer data on PDPs, with Organization, BreadcrumbList or Article where appropriate to page purpose.
Recognize that evidence linking schema directly to AI citation is mixed — there's no confirmed data it improves AI citation odds.
Keep accurate schema that supports current search features; correct inaccurate or conflicting markup rather than retaining it blindly.
If setting up a new page, add the appropriate schema types as a good habit that makes content easier for any system to understand.
Avoid spending significant time on schema specifically for AEO; deprioritize it relative to robots.txt, content quality, and rendering.
caveats: The source is explicit that AEO benefit is unconfirmed; this is a 'doesn't hurt' recommendation, not a proven tactic.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Capturing traffic from AI-hallucinated 404 URLs
cards.summary: AI assistants send users to nonexistent pages more often than Google does; catch that traffic by redirecting hallucinated URLs to relevant real pages.
cards.use_when: Recovering lost store traffic that clicks AI-recommended links to pages that don't exist.
steps: Check your analytics for pages receiving traffic from AI referrers that return a 404 status.

Recognize that AI assistants sometimes invent URLs, recommend a nonexistent page, and send users into a 404 (source data: AI assistants send visitors to 404 pages ~2.87x more often than Google Search, with ChatGPT the biggest offender at ~1% of clicked URLs).
If a hallucinated URL gets consistent traffic, set up a redirect to the most relevant real page on your site.
Rather than letting the 404 end the journey, fix or optimize these pages to capture traffic that would otherwise be lost.
caveats: The 2.87x figure is a source-specific data point and may change over time.
This is a catch-up tactic — ideally your site structure prevents key 404s to begin with.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Setting up an AI traffic channel group in GA4
cards.summary: Isolate AI referral traffic in GA4 with a custom channel group so you can see which platforms and pages AI sends visitors to.
cards.use_when: Measuring whether AI assistants are driving measurable referral traffic to your store.
steps: In GA4, go to Admin > Data Display > Channel Groups.
Copy your default channel group and add a new channel named 'AI traffic'.

Match observed referral hostnames, including chatgpt.com and legacy chat.openai.com where present, plus relevant AI services. Escape dots and use hostname boundaries when building a regex; validate against actual source values.
Save, then go to Reports > Acquisition > Traffic Acquisition and select your new channel group.
Review which pages get AI traffic, and how those visitors behave versus other channels.
Some apps and links omit referral data. Test the actual surfaces your shoppers use and treat tracked referrals as a partial view rather than a fixed platform-wide attribution rule.
caveats: Referral reports are likely undercounts due to stripped referrer data; verify current behavior as platform settings change.
GA4 interface details should be verified against your current version.
Use a custom channel group alongside post-purchase survey responses; avoid double-counting the same purchase across attribution views.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Tracking AI bot activity to identify citation candidates
cards.summary: Monitor the AI crawlers visiting your site to find which pages AI is paying attention to and which are underexplored by bots.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing which store pages are strong AI citation candidates and which are hidden from crawlers.
steps: Separate training crawls, search crawls and user-triggered page visits when classifying logs; consult current provider documentation.
Use requests to product and guide pages as evidence of access, not as counts of recommendations or buyers.

Track activity using server logs if you have access, or via a bot-analytics tool; the source notes Ahrefs Bot Analytics has a Cloudflare integration that works on the free Cloudflare plan and shows which AI bots visit, how often, and which pages.
Cross-check repeated crawler visits with sampled citations and referrals before deciding a page is contributing to discovery.
If important pages have no observed visits, check log coverage, internal links and access rules; missing log events alone do not prove a crawl problem.
caveats: Requires server log access or a compatible analytics/Cloudflare integration.
Bot behavior and provider tools evolve; verify current tool capabilities.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Capturing AI impact through self-reported attribution
cards.summary: Survey customers on how they heard about you to capture AI-influenced conversions that appear as direct or branded organic traffic.
cards.use_when: Attributing conversions to AI visibility when analytics can't show the AI touchpoint for your store.
steps: Recognize that AI influence often shows up as direct traffic (user types your brand after seeing AI recommendation) or branded organic search — invisible in standard attribution.
Add a 'How did you hear about us?' question to your sign-up flow, checkout process, or post-purchase survey.
Include options like: AI assistant, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and AI search (e.g., Google AI overviews).

Review responses regularly to connect AI visibility to actual business results (the source notes Ahrefs found ~3% of conversions came from AI based on self-reported data, and AI visitors converted at a much higher rate than organic search visitors).
Use these responses together with referral traffic and bot analytics to build a fuller picture.
caveats: Self-reported attribution relies on accurate customer memory and can be noisy.
Ahrefs' 3% and higher-conversion figures are source-specific examples, not benchmarks to expect.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Combining three tracking pillars for AI visibility
cards.summary: No single AI measurement source is complete; combine referral traffic, bot analytics, and self-reported attribution to see the full picture.
cards.use_when: Setting up an ongoing AEO measurement framework for an online store.
steps: Referral traffic (custom GA4 channel or web analytics with a built-in AI search channel) shows what AI is actively sending to your site.
Bot analytics shows what content AI is paying attention to via crawler visits.
Self-reported attribution shows what's actually driving revenue, including AI touchpoints invisible to analytics.
Use them together since no one source gives the full picture — together they show how AI interacts with your brand and where to focus.
Additionally track brand visibility across platforms in a brand radar tool.
Note practical gaps: some platforms strip referral data, and GA4 lumps unknown traffic with direct traffic while dedicated web-analytics tools may separate them.
caveats: All three sources undercount in different ways; treat combined data as directional.
Tool names and built-in channel support may change.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Prioritizing and evaluating AI traffic volume vs. quality
cards.summary: AI referral traffic is small in volume but high in intent and conversion quality, and its growth trajectory argues for starting early.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether an AEO program is worth investing in for the store, and how to frame its ROI.
steps: Acknowledge the volume reality: source data shows AI referral traffic is ~0.25% of total site traffic on average, and Google sends roughly 210x more traffic than top AI platforms combined.

Weigh the quality signal: the source reports Ahrefs' AI visitors converted at 23x the rate of organic search visitors, Vercel saw 10% conversion rates from AI traffic, and Tally reported AI as its largest acquisition channel helping boost ARR by a million dollars.
Explain the mechanism: when AI recommends you, it has already explained why you're a fit, so traffic arrives pre-qualified and ready to act.
Consider growth trajectory rather than current size — source reports AI traffic grew ~9.7x year over year, with ChatGPT growing 85% since January.
Value unclicked impressions too: brand mentions inside AI conversations can drive later branded search and social engagement even when no click occurs.
caveats: The conversion and growth figures are source-specific company examples, not universal benchmarks.
AEO measurement is imperfect, akin to brand marketing — lack of precise tracking doesn't mean it isn't working, per the source.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Filling information gaps to resist AI misinformation
cards.summary: AI repeats fake or outdated brand info when official, specific content is missing; publish authoritative FAQs and facts to reduce the risk.
cards.use_when: Protecting an online store's brand accuracy in AI answers and reducing the chance AI cites false claims about your products or pricing.
steps: Understand the risk: in a source-reported test, a fake luxury brand was planted with three contradicting sources across a blog, Reddit, and Medium; Gemini and Perplexity repeated the misinformation in 37–39% of answers, while ChatGPT stayed under 7% and cited the brand's official FAQ in 84% of answers.
Fill every information gap about your brand with specific, official content: create an FAQ addressing common questions about your products, pricing, and company.
Use specific numbers, dates, and facts instead of vague claims — the source notes that when AI must choose between vague truth and specific fiction, it tends to pick the specific fiction.
Monitor what AI says about your brand regularly.
If you spot inaccurate info, publish content on your own site directly contradicting it first, then work on correcting the third-party source.
caveats: Platforms differ in misinformation resistance (ChatGPT was more robust than Gemini/Perplexity in this test); results are from a source-run experiment, not guarantees about your brand.
Vague truth can lose to specific fiction — specificity in your own content matters.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Completing a monthly and quarterly brand radar check
cards.summary: Track four AI visibility metrics monthly and do a deeper competitive audit quarterly to know if your AEO efforts are working.
cards.use_when: Reviewing whether content, mention-earning, and video efforts are improving the store's AI visibility.
steps: AI share of voice: check how you've moved relative to competitors; growth means efforts are working, flat-while-competitor-grows means dig into why.
Cited domains: check whether new domains are citing you that weren't before — a signal that mention-earning efforts are paying off.
Topic coverage: check whether you've closed identified gaps and are showing up on topics you weren't before.
Mention sentiment: check whether AI says accurate and positive things about your brand (AI synthesizes from everywhere, not just your site).
Do a quick monthly check on these four items and a deeper competitive audit quarterly.
caveats: Requires a baseline from an initial brand radar setup and gap analysis; without a baseline, trends aren't interpretable.
Metric definitions depend on the chosen tracking tool.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Executing a starter AEO action plan this week
cards.summary: A five-step first week of AEO work: fix crawler access, set up AI analytics, refresh key pages, run a brand gap analysis, and pick top mention targets.
cards.use_when: Kicking off an AEO program for an online store with no prior structured AI visibility work.
steps: Check robots.txt for AI bot access (~5 minutes) — the most common technical blocker; ensure AI can crawl your site.

Set up AI analytics: create the AI traffic channel in GA4 or use a web analytics tool with a built-in AI channel, and add a 'How did you hear about us?' question to sign-up or checkout to measure from day one.

Update your most important pages for freshness — AI content is reported as 25.7% fresher than traditional search results; pick top 5–10 pages and make meaningful updates (new stats, updated examples, current info).
Run a brand gap analysis: set up brand radar and know where you stand before optimizing.
Identify your top 10 mention-earning targets using cited-domains and pages reports to find the pages where a mention would most impact your AI visibility.
Then maintain a monthly brand radar check and a quarterly competitive audit, and repeat.
caveats: The 25.7% freshness figure is a source-specific data point, not a target benchmark.
Ordering reflects the source's recommended sequence; prioritize based on your site's actual blockers.
cards.source_name: AI SEO Course for Beginners_ Complete AEO Tutorial.docx

cards.title: Query fan-out: optimize for the sub-queries AI actually runs
cards.summary: AI assistants expand one user prompt into several background searches, so visibility depends on ranking for those sub-queries, not the original prompt.
cards.use_when: Planning which product, category and landing pages to build or optimize so an AI assistant can surface the store for high-intent shopping prompts.
steps: Understand the mechanism: when someone searches in ChatGPT or Perplexity, the tool 'fans out' the single query into multiple background variations — e.g. 'best running shoes' becomes 'best running shoes 2026'.

Treat this as an SEO problem, not a content-volume problem: AI tools retrieve URLs through search engine APIs (Google, Bing, etc.), so pages that rank in traditional search are the ones eligible for retrieval.

For each commercially important prompt in your catalog (e.g. 'best bathroom vanities', 'best fragrance for men'), list the likely fan-out variations and check whether any page on your site — category page, product page, comparison page — genuinely answers them.
Prioritize building or optimizing the page that serves the fan-out variant with the clearest purchase intent, rather than producing a new article for every variant.
Re-check fan-out behavior periodically, since the assistant's background searches change over time.
caveats: Presented as the source's model of how assistants retrieve pages; the exact search back-end is debated and changes often.
Fan-out behavior is not fully transparent — treat any list of sub-queries as a hypothesis to test, not a fixed map.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Why scaled AI content is a rank-and-tank risk
cards.summary: Mass-producing AI articles to chase fan-out variations creates a short traffic spike followed by a collapse, and the source argues recovery can take years.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to accept a vendor's or in-house plan to scale the store's blog from hundreds to thousands of posts for AI visibility.
steps: Recognize the pattern before committing: the most-promoted GEO method is simply publishing far more content targeting fan-out keyword variations, often via automated content generators.
Anticipate the cycle — the source describes sites going from ~100 to 1,000+ posts in weeks, seeing an initial traffic lift, then declining sharply ('Mount AI' / 'rank and tank').
Weigh the downside as asymmetric: the source states Google already names this 'scaled content abuse' in its guidelines and that sites penalized in an algorithm update can take years to recover.

Check whether the traffic being generated is commercial. The source's critique is that most scaled how-to/what-is/explainer content does not generate revenue — it is top-of-funnel volume for its own sake.
If someone proposes the tactic, ask what happens to the store's core product and category pages in the next algorithm update, not just what the traffic chart looks like today.
caveats: This is the source's strong opinion; recovery timelines cited (2–3 years, 'many case studies') are illustrative, not a guaranteed benchmark.
Brands with strong existing brand search and media mentions may sustain the tactic longer before decline, per the source — that is an observation, not a safe strategy.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Audit a scaled-content case study with keyword difficulty
cards.summary: Aggregate traffic charts can hide a decline in the hard, commercially valuable keywords, so analyze difficulty bands separately.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a GEO agency's or tool's case study before signing, or auditing whether your own scaled content push is actually holding up.
steps: Do not accept the headline traffic chart as proof. The source describes a large finance company whose overall traffic was still above the prior year, appearing to validate the tactic.
Break the case study's keywords into difficulty bands (the source uses Ahrefs difficulty > 30 as the cut) and examine trends separately.

Look for divergence: in the cited example, keywords with difficulty above 30 had begun to decline while easy keywords still propped up the total — meaning the competitive, more useful terms were the first to go.
Ask your own question of any case study: is this traffic producing revenue? If organic or LLM-driven revenue has not increased, the source says it is not a win regardless of the chart.
If you have an SEO tool subscription, verify traffic patterns yourself rather than relying on the vendor's screenshot.
caveats: Difficulty thresholds like 30 are tool-specific heuristics from the source, not universal cut-offs.
A single case example is not evidence the tactic works or fails for every site.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Red flags and yellow flags when vetting a GEO vendor
cards.summary: Screen AI-visibility vendors by whether their platform generates content at scale and by what they actually propose doing off-site.
cards.use_when: Choosing or renewing an agency/tool that promises to improve the store's visibility inside AI assistants.
steps: Biggest red flag: the vendor has a content generator in their platform, or their proposal centers on producing hundreds of blog posts. That is the pattern the source considers the fastest route to a rank-and-tank penalty.
Yellow flag: a Reddit-mentions strategy. Ask specifically how they will post and engage in communities, then verify whether the cited threads are even relevant (see the Reddit verification card).
Demand current performance data on their published case studies: ask the sales rep how the featured client is performing now and how the strategy held up over time.
Ask what they think about off-site SEO (affiliates, third-party listicles) and whether they have a video/YouTube/social strategy, since video appears heavily in Google's AI overviews per the source.
Sanity-test jargon. If they cannot explain their method in plain language you understand, the source treats that as a grifter signal — common across marketing agencies, not just SEO.

Run grifter probes: ask whether they recommend an llms.txt file, a dedicated 'AI info page', or 'chunking' all your content. If they enthusiastically endorse these as necessary, lean toward walking away.
caveats: The llms.txt, AI-info-page and chunking objections are the source's opinion, not established consensus.
An experienced general SEO practitioner may be a better bet than a dedicated GEO vendor, per the source — but verify current tool/format conventions yourself before acting.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: The five questions to ask a GEO vendor before hiring
cards.summary: A concrete question set that surfaces whether an AI-visibility vendor has durable experience or is selling scaled-content tactics.
cards.use_when: Running a sales call or RFP with an agency or platform pitching AI search visibility for your store.
steps: Ask: how do you think GEO is different from SEO? A vague or purely hype-driven answer is a signal.
Ask: how long have you been around, and when did you start in optimization? The source flags companies that appeared only after ChatGPT launched versus those operating in 2015–2017.
Ask: can you share recent case studies — and can you tell me how those clients are performing now and whether the strategy held up?
Ask: what are your thoughts on off-site SEO (affiliate placements, third-party listicles, reviews sites) and on incorporating video and social media into our strategy?
Ask directly: are you going to put up hundreds of blog posts? The source treats a yes as a red flag.
Ask them to explain their approach in plain English; inability to do so is itself disqualifying per the source.
caveats: These are the source's proposed questions; they screen for scaled-content risk, not for every possible vendor weakness.
New vendors are not automatically bad — the source acknowledges newcomers to the industry — but longevity is the screen it recommends.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Correct persistent inaccurate brand facts across public sources
cards.summary: Repeatedly restating a corrected fact on your own site and across distributed channels can shift what a model says even without a web search.
cards.use_when: When an AI assistant keeps repeating an outdated or misleading fact about your store — e.g. shipping times, return policy, product capabilities, implementation or lead times.
steps: Start with your own website: state the corrected fact plainly and explicitly. In the source's example, a company suffering from '9+ months implementation' reputation simply published that implementation can be as fast as 3 weeks. The reasoning: the model repeats information it sees, so your own site is the best place to start.

Distribute the same claim well beyond the website: third-party articles, the founder's social videos addressing the misconception directly, and other channels. The source emphasizes cross-channel repetition, not a single update.

Be realistic about magnitude and lag. LLMs are trained over years, so any single tactic has a minor effect; in the example the model moved from 9+ months to 6 months over roughly two years — an improvement, not the target figure.
Repeat a fixed set of brand questions with browsing controlled where possible; record model, date and cited evidence. Changed answers do not prove retraining.

Treat related off-site profiles as part of the same repair job: G2, Reddit, Trustpilot, local directories and local board-of-trade listings — update them so the stale claim is not being reinforced elsewhere.
caveats: The source says it has seen no true, verifiable case study of a company reliably entering training data through content volume; the demonstrated result here was partial and slow.
Model training cut-offs and behavior change frequently — verify current model behavior rather than assuming a fixed timeline.
The observed SaaS example does not establish control over training data; apply the factual-correction workflow to store policies, specifications and pricing.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Distinguish observed web retrieval from unverified answer provenance
cards.summary: Run the same query in free/incognito and logged-in/paid sessions and inspect citations to see whether the assistant searched the web at all.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in training-data/brand work or web-page optimization for a given set of shopping or brand prompts.
steps: Run an experiment anyone can do: search a prompt in the free version of ChatGPT, then run the same prompt in a separate incognito tab and in a paid/logged-in account, and compare the answers side by side.
Repeat a few times and reword the sentence structure between runs to see how stable the answer is — the source notes answers shift with phrasing.
Check available citations and search or tool traces. Missing citations alone cannot prove that an answer came only from training data.
Prioritize correcting current public product facts and observed cited pages. Label answer provenance unknown when the system does not expose it.
Compare controlled, fresh sessions without supplied brand context where possible; account, memory, model and prompt differences can affect the result.
caveats: Model behavior, paywalls and search triggers change often — re-run the experiment before making decisions.
The source's observations were made at a specific point in time and are not a permanent characterization of any AI product.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Prompt trackers: understand their limits before trusting AI visibility data
cards.summary: Automated AI prompt trackers can report inflated or meaningless visibility when answers vary run-to-run or the model never searched the web.
cards.use_when: Reviewing an AI visibility report from a tool, agency or in-house dashboard to decide whether the store is actually being recommended.
steps: Recognize how these tools work: they capture screenshots of a tracked prompt's answer inside ChatGPT or another assistant and upload them for comparison.
Know the failure mode: if the assistant does not trigger a web search, there are no citations in the answer, so the screen contains no useful evidence of visibility.

Treat citation counts with suspicion. The source argues citations are easy to inflate — one URL can be cited for an infinite number of branded term variations (e.g. 'how to get rid of mold brand name'), so 'we increased citations' does not mean 'we increased visibility'.
Recognize that answers vary dynamically; a single tracked prompt is not a stable measurement.
When reviewing reports, ask which prompts are commercially meaningful to the store, whether web search actually fired, and whether the reported change maps to revenue rather than mention counts.
caveats: The source's view is that the whole citation-measurement system is of questionable value and partly vendor-driven; treat dashboard metrics as directional at best.
Trackers and assistants change interfaces and behavior — verify the current mechanics before relying on any single metric.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Verify claimed Reddit influence before paying for Reddit GEO
cards.summary: Test which Reddit threads actually influence the prompts you care about — often none you can join, and some are locked.
cards.use_when: Being pitched a Reddit-mentions service for your store, or considering building a Reddit presence for AI visibility.
steps: Take the keywords and conversational prompts that matter commercially to the store and run them through an SEO or GEO tool to see the specific Reddit URLs being cited by AI for those prompts.
Identify the subreddits involved and check their rules: the source notes some high-engagement subreddits ban your account the moment a brand name is mentioned, even in a genuinely helpful answer.
Accept dead ends quickly. In the source's example, the only cited Reddit thread for a bathroom-vanity query was eight years old and locked — creating fifty new pages could not break into that answer.

If a vendor claims 'increased Reddit mentions', ask what influence that had on the answers you care about. The source warns that many vendor Reddit posts are autogenerated, add no value, and receive no engagement.
Prefer publishers that already hold AI citations over chasing new Reddit threads that no model currently references.
caveats: Reddit is genuinely cited by AI assistants, per the source, but that does not mean any given Reddit tactic works for any given query.
Subreddit rules and AI citation sources change over time — re-verify which threads are actually referenced.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Get listed in the third-party listicles AI already cites
cards.summary: Find the affiliate review pages and listicles that influence your priority prompts and get your brand placed in those, not in new ones you create.
cards.use_when: Building off-site AI visibility for a store in a category where comparison listicles (supplements, mattresses, credit cards, fragrances, software) drive AI answers.
steps: Use your GEO or SEO tool's 'sources' section to see which third-party URLs influence the AI answers for your priority prompts; these tools typically flag sources where you are not mentioned.
Skip competitor-owned listicles — the source states it will not email a competitor asking to be added, and ignores such requests when received.

Target durable, high-authority publishers in your vertical (the source cites examples like Healthline, WebMD, Sleepopolis for mattresses, large credit-card affiliates) and try to join their affiliate programs, even at a higher cost than you would like.

For smaller or niche blogs that turn out to be influencing many of your prompts, simply email and ask what it would cost to be included — the source describes this as a straightforward paid placement, sometimes very cheap, that can win citations across many prompts.

Run the same analysis on competitors: use link/backlink intersection analysis to see which listicles and guest posts they appear in, then pursue the equivalent for your brand — bigger publications for bigger companies, local or cheaper sites for local players.
Remember the affiliate is often a different team from SEO, so if you run or influence the affiliate program, coordinate with them directly.
caveats: The source notes an unethical variant — companies sponsoring or buying listicles on third-party news sites (it cites a hair-transplant listicle in a Canadian newspaper and law-firm pages) — and explicitly does not recommend or condone it; disclosure requirements vary by industry and jurisdiction.
Affiliate programs sometimes test placement and click-through rate before giving premium positions.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Rank category and product pages for bottom-of-funnel queries without building listicles
cards.summary: Your own category and product pages can capture high-intent queries and get cited by AI, without any third-party placement.
cards.use_when: Deciding what to build next on-site for AI visibility — a new blog post or an optimized commercial page.
steps: Put up product and landing pages that target high-intent terms directly, and cover the use cases and services you offer — the source describes these as being cited heavily in AI answers, and calls the tactic fully ethical.

Use e-commerce category page conventions the source observed: a fragrance site's category page can carry the title and H1 'best fragrances for men' while still presenting the normal product grid — no article required to rank for a bottom-of-funnel query.
Apply the same pattern to service pages: a service page can be optimized for a scenario-driven query rather than written as a blog post.

Use borrowed credibility where it is legitimate: the source describes a law firm that earned a ranking from a legal publication's affiliate program, then published a page citing that recognition, and subsequently appeared for 'best personal injury lawyers in Canada'.

Prioritize commercial pages over explainer content; the source observes many competitive commercial keywords (e.g. 'personal injury law NYC') have surprisingly few sites targeting them properly, despite high cost per click.
caveats: The borrowed-credibility example is a third-party recognition placement; check advertising and endorsement disclosure rules in your industry and market.
SCALE the approach with judgment — the value comes from targeting genuinely searched queries, not from generating pages for their own sake.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Treat GEO as a company-wide function, not a single marketing hire
cards.summary: Because AI answers draw on product quality, reviews, PR, social and support channels, one person cannot fix AI visibility alone.
cards.use_when: Scoping who owns AI search performance at your store and setting cross-team responsibilities.
steps: Map the owners: product quality (bad products generate bad Reddit sentiment regardless of optimization), brand reputation and executive conduct, communications/PR messaging, review profiles (Trustpilot, G2, Glassdoor), affiliate relationships, and web content.

Fix the underlying substance first: if the product or service is genuinely poor, the source is explicit that no amount of Reddit or listicle optimization will overcome what customers say about it publicly.

Align messaging across channels. If the company has been known for one thing for 15 years and wants to be known for something else, a press release alone will not change what AI says — sustained promotion across many channels is required.

Use review profiles as a lever: in the source's example, a law firm improved its Glassdoor rating above four stars by encouraging employee reviews, after which ChatGPT stopped using Glassdoor as its review source. The same logic applies to Trustpilot for consumer brands.
Ensure the affiliate, PR and content owners are coordinate-able, since the cited sources often sit outside SEO's control.
caveats: The Glassdoor example is an anecdote about one firm and one model's source selection at a point in time, not a repeatable guarantee.
Encouraging reviews must comply with platform policies and applicable law; the source mentions incentives without addressing compliance.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Investigate stale brand facts and correct likely public sources
cards.summary: When a model answers about your brand without searching, it is drawing on sources like G2, Reddit or directories — correct those sources directly.
cards.use_when: An AI assistant gives an outdated answer about your store's policies, pricing, product capabilities or review sentiment without performing a web search.
steps: Use matching wording to identify candidate stale sources; wording similarity does not prove training provenance.
Review brand-plus-review and comparison answers; fix inaccurate editable profiles and invite honest customer reviews without screening for positivity.
For local businesses, update directory and local board-of-trade listings — these are the kinds of sources the source names as feeding training data.

Redistribute the corrected claim beyond the profile itself: onto your website, into third-party articles, and into social video from the founder, as in the case study that moved the answer from 9+ months to 6 months.
Retest in controlled fresh sessions with browsing disabled where possible, and record uncertainty about model memory or training effects.
caveats: The source is explicit that it has not seen a truly verifiable case study of a company deliberately entering training data — the demonstrated effect was partial and took roughly two years.
Which sources feed which model is not published and changes over time; treat the G2/Reddit/directory list as the source's working hypothesis.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Test whether an AI answer is naming your brand or only linking your page
cards.summary: A citation is not the same as a mention — being linked while a competitor is named is not a win for the store.
cards.use_when: Reviewing an AI visibility report or checking a Google AI overview for your category to judge whether the visibility claimed is worth anything.
steps: Run your priority queries and read the AI answer carefully. The source describes a case where an AI FP&A software company was cited in Google's AI overview but not named — the answer listed other companies as best and merely linked to their page.
Interpret the two outcomes differently: a mention puts your brand in front of the buyer; a bare link may just position you as a source that recommends rivals.
When a vendor reports growth in 'AI visibility', ask whether it is mentions or citations, and which prompts, before treating it as progress.

Watch for site-scoped searches in the fan-out. The source observed ChatGPT temporarily issuing searches like 'site:G2.com company-name' — evidence that assistants are actively working to improve answer quality and may bypass self-authored listicles.
Use the finding to decide whether to invest in being mentioned inside trusted publishers rather than in publishing your own listicle that names you first.
caveats: The site: operator behavior was observed during a limited window and may have been a test; re-verify current behavior.
Google AI overviews and assistant answers change format often.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Judge AI-visibility tactics by whether they optimize for the user's best answer
cards.summary: The durable test for any GEO tactic is whether it improves the experience of searchers, not whether it produces a spike in tracked mentions.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to adopt a specific AI-visibility tactic — self-authored listicles, scaled comparison pages, paid placements — for your store.
steps: Apply the source's test question to each tactic: does this give a user who lands on the page through Google or an AI search engine the best possible experience?

Use it to reject the spammy version of a legitimate tactic. Comparison pages have existed in legitimate form for years (mattress brand A vs brand B); the GEO version is scaling them to the point of comparing brands nobody searches for.

Apply the same test to self-authored listicles that place your own company first — they may still rank and be cited, but the source frames them as a tactic that assistants are actively working around.
Prefer the version of the tactic that serves real intent: your own product, category and comparison pages that answer genuine buyer questions (see the bottom-of-funnel page card).
Use it as the tiebreaker when a vendor presents a case study: ask whether the pages in question help buyers or simply exist to capture a fan-out variation.
caveats: This is the source's stated ethical/strategic frame, and it explicitly names some effective-but-unethical tactics it does not recommend.
'Best possible experience' is a judgment call — apply it consistently rather than as a rhetorical test.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Bottom-of-funnel pages beat top-of-funnel content for AI citation
cards.summary: Build specific, high-intent scenario and service pages rather than broad informational content that AI already answers itself.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to spend limited content budget on a store's blog versus category/product/scenario pages.
steps: Recognize the source's core claim: top-of-funnel informational content is largely wasted effort now because AI overviews answer 'what is X' questions directly, and most small brands lack the authority to shape a narrative on broad terms.

Instead, build pages for concrete scenarios and services your brand actually offers, because high-intent terms are the least searched and therefore the least competitive, even when their ad cost per click is high.

Apply to ecommerce by making category, product, and scenario pages (e.g. replacing 'what is financial reporting' thinking with 'financial reporting software for brick-and-mortar businesses') rather than broad explainer posts.
Niche down further to reduce competition; the source gives the example that the more specific the term, the fewer sites target it properly.

Note the source's caveat: top-of-funnel content can work for brands with an existing audience and authority who introduce a genuinely new point of view, but for most smaller brands the effort is better directed at bottom-of-funnel pages tied to revenue.
caveats: The 'top-of-funnel is a waste' view is the source's opinion, not a measured benchmark; it acknowledges exceptions for high-authority brands.
Bottom-of-funnel claims should still be tested against your own traffic and revenue data.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Mine query fan-out language to write on-site copy
cards.summary: Inspect the actual searches an LLM runs, then reuse that exact phrasing in page titles, slugs, H1s and first sentences.
cards.use_when: Optimizing a product, category or landing page's on-page text so the store surfaces in AI-run web searches.
steps: First observe query fan-out visibly in Perplexity, which shows the searches it runs. For ChatGPT, the source describes an advanced method: send a prompt, wait for it to search the web, right-click and inspect, open the Network tab, copy the URL string after '/c', paste it into the filter, refresh, find the orange-bracketed matching entry, open its Response tab, and search that response for the word 'queries' to see the literal searches.
Alternatively, run the prompt a few times and note recurring search phrasings. Search Google for current video walkthroughs, because this interface method may change.
Identify the language the LLM uses to gather information, which often differs from the phrasing of your original prompt.
Transfer that language into your page title, URL slug, H1, and the beginning of your first sentence, since the source argues most websites are extremely bad at tightly targeting language.

Because LLMs constantly trigger web searches, matching their phrasing and holding SEO authority (links and shares) increases the chance its search surfaces your page, letting you control what the model parrots back.
caveats: The source admits the ChatGPT network-tab method is more complicated than Perplexity and may change; verify the current interface before relying on it.
This is a research technique, not a guarantee of citation.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Cheap press releases to influence AI answers
cards.summary: Use low-cost newswire distributions with your target phrase repeated in the title, subheading and first sentence to get cited by AI.
cards.use_when: Building brand impressions or correcting/creating an AI-visible narrative about a product, store or founder.
steps: Pick an inexpensive wire service; the source names AB Newswire and cites roughly $80 for a single release, or about $500/year for a package of around 83 releases (about $6 each). Confirm current pricing before budgeting.

Repeat your target phrase in the press release title, subheading, and first sentence. The source cites the example of a 'best-selling SEO book' term placed in all three spots, which later appeared in AI overviews and ChatGPT citations.
Expect the release to syndicate across news sites; the source says AB Newswire distributed into properties like Yahoo News and the Globe and Mail at the time (availability may change).

Use releases for reputation management, company announcements, or local sponsorships (the source gives the example of a local plumbing company sponsoring a little league team) so AI mentions your brand when users ask about it.
The source argues this tactic is durable because real companies rely on press releases, so it is unlikely AI systems stop ingesting them.
caveats: The source describes an experiment that made a fake company appear real; using fake claims risks credibility and legal issues, so apply the tactic only to truthful information.
Distribution networks and pricing change; verify before purchasing.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Publish pricing intent to control AI answers about cost
cards.summary: State your pricing or a starting-from figure on your site so AI doesn't invent a number from G2 or Reddit.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to hide pricing on a B2B or high-ticket product page and what to publish instead.
steps: Accept the source's observation: when you ask ChatGPT about B2B SaaS pricing and the site hides it, the model makes something up or pulls it from G2, Reddit or similar third-party sources.

If you want to hide exact pricing, you can still publish a range, e.g. 'starts from $5,000' or 'starts from $50,000'; the source states ChatGPT will then reference your site and say the company doesn't specify pricing but starts from that figure.
Compare outcomes: your own controlled 'starts from' statement is better than the model linking to a Reddit thread complaining that a quote was too expensive.
Apply this to any product or service with variable or quote-based pricing where a wrong AI-stated figure could deter buyers.
Keep the published figure truthful and consistent with your actual sales process.
caveats: Listing a starting price can anchor or filter out some buyers; weigh that against leaving AI to invent a number.
The source's claims about how ChatGPT handles hidden pricing are anecdotal, not a controlled study.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Optimize reviews across every platform, not just one
cards.summary: Diversify and monitor your review presence everywhere AI looks, because any single platform can drop out of AI results.
cards.use_when: Managing review profiles and reputation for a store that relies on third-party review sites for AI-driven product comparisons.
steps: Recognize that LLMs search review platforms unprompted. The source notes seeing query fan-out that added 'G2 reviews' for the models' own list of companies, sometimes as the initial fan-out and sometimes after an initial search gathered companies to investigate.
Because platforms can suddenly drop from AI answers (the source cites a period when Reddit fell out of OpenAI's results), don't put all review effort into one platform like G2.

Optimize profiles across the platforms your buyers use, e.g. Trustpilot, Trustpilot alternatives, Yelp and Capterra; ensure the rating is good and the profile description matches what you want to be known for.
Set up review monitoring or alerts so a one-star review on an obscure site can be found and addressed.
Accept you can't prevent bad reviews; ensure good reviews are spread across the board, and the source notes the simplest defense is having a good product.
caveats: You can influence but not fully control third-party reviews.
Which platforms AI cites changes over time, so treat the list as examples, not a fixed checklist.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Disclose useful product info on-site so AI doesn't guess
cards.summary: Put pricing, specs and positioning on your own pages so third parties don't define your product in AI answers.
cards.use_when: Deciding what product details to publish versus hide, to control how AI describes your store and products.
steps: The source's framing: GEO comes down to AI parroting whatever you write on your site plus whatever third parties write about your business, so get the parrot to say good things.
Write the accurate product and positioning information you want repeated directly on your own pages.
Encourage mentions on third-party review and affiliate sites that describe your product correctly.
For pricing specifically, publish a range or starting figure even if you keep exact pricing private, so the model cites your site rather than Reddit or G2.
Periodically check what AI says about your products and correct gaps by adding the missing facts to your site.
caveats: This is a principle, not a guarantee AI will cite your page over a popular third-party source.
Inaccurate self-published info that contradicts reality can damage trust once buyers notice.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Recognize when SEO has shifted to old-style purchase pages
cards.summary: Google AI mode increasingly cites homepages, category and product pages over listicles, changing what to optimize.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to keep investing in listicle/blog content versus product, category and homepage pages for AI visibility.
steps: Observe, as the source does, that Google AI mode now more often links directly to a brand's homepage or product page rather than a pile of listicles.

Note that in AI results, brand names are often underlined: a solid blue link goes directly to the company site, while a dotted black line opens a new search for the brand name, making the right-hand citations less relevant.
Adapt your store strategy by strengthening products, categories and homepages rather than making a listicle on your own site that competes with the sites Google already sends users to.
The source still advises one acceptable listicle pattern: if you're a toy store, publish e.g. 'top 10 birthday gifts' and position your own products; lists aren't inherently bad.
Expect long-form blog content to carry less weight and put more effort into being recognized elsewhere (reviews, mentions, videos) so Google lists you as a solution for what you sell.
caveats: The shift the source describes is observational and may change; monitor your own AI-visible queries rather than assuming this is permanent.
Different queries and verticals show different behavior; test your specific terms.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Do GEO research before touching pages
cards.summary: Find where AI sources its answers for your target prompts, then reverse-engineer your way into those sources.
cards.use_when: Starting an AI-visibility campaign for a store and deciding which channels and pages to prioritize.
steps: Run your target prompts through the LLMs your buyers use, and use query fan-out (visible in Perplexity, or via the response-tab method in ChatGPT) to record which sites AI cites.

If fan-out consistently cites a big retailer or review site for a term you want (the source uses 'best running shoes' and REI as an example), get your brand mentioned on the cited site rather than assuming your own page will outrank it.
Ask your SEO team (internal or agency) for the fan-out of your main keywords; note that some prompt-tracking tools now provide fan-out automatically, and it can also be done manually.
Treat the answer to 'where is the AI getting its information?' as the starting point, then build a plan to appear in those sources.
Repeat the analysis periodically, since which platforms AI favors changes over time.
