caveats: Manual fan-out extraction is laborious; the source says sometimes you just have to put in the time.
Fan-out tools and interfaces change; verify current capabilities.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Spend 70-80% of GEO effort on good SEO first
cards.summary: Fix technical SEO and build product/service/location pages before chasing off-site AI tactics.
cards.use_when: Allocating budget and team effort across a store's AI-visibility program.
steps: The source's stated split: 70-80% of GEO is good SEO, with the rest building on top of it.
Ensure the website is technically sound.
Create pages for the products and services you offer, and location pages if the business is location-based.
Build content for what you offer, including acceptable list formats that position your own products.

Once SEO is in place, go beyond the site: check who shows up for your target searches and reach out to affiliates and third-party sites to be mentioned, and decide whether video, TikTok, Instagram or community channels matter for your buyers.
Include reputation management and review monitoring in the off-site portion.
caveats: The 70-80% figure is the source's rough estimate, not a measured formula; adapt to your store's maturity.
Off-site tactics depend on resources the source says may come after the basics are covered.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Screen growth tactics by your time horizon
cards.summary: Ask what a tactic does to your brand in two or three years before scaling it, especially if you plan to be around long term.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to adopt a fast but risky AI-spam content or link tactic for a store with long-term customers.
steps: Before scaling any tactic, ask: what impact will this have on me in two or three years?
If you run a churn-and-burn site built for short-term gains, the source says some aggressive tactics are an acceptable business model.
If you're a real business with real customers and a 10-15 year plan, the source says you cannot afford tactics that risk an algorithm penalty, even for a short-term gain.
Apply this to AI-spam scaling, templated listicles, and any pattern that a platform could penalize at the domain level.
The source's broader warning: companies that scale spam listicles can get hit algorithmically for a couple of years, which creates an opening for competitors to take their rank.
caveats: This is the source's risk judgment, not a measured penalty probability.
Risk tolerance legitimately varies by business model; the source explicitly allows aggressive tactics for short-term sites.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Capture brand impressions from AI answers
cards.summary: Treat logo or link placement beneath AI overviews as paid-ad-equivalent brand exposure, not just lost clicks.
cards.use_when: Evaluating the value of AI overview presence when organic click-through has fallen for a store's queries.
steps: Acknowledge that the traffic top-of-funnel pages got five years ago is gone; AI answers and AI overviews stand between the user and the click.
Look for the residual exposure: AI overviews sometimes include a linked box and your logo, and you can get your brand or site listed right beneath the overview.
Count those impressions as brand exposure, comparable to the impressions companies already pay for on billboards and TV ads.
Use this framing when setting expectations internally or with clients about AI-era traffic, shifting some success measurement from clicks to impressions and branded-search lift.
Combine with on-site conversion work, since the source says listing for a solution or service depends on being recognized for what you do.
caveats: The source frames these impressions as valuable but gives no measurement of their conversion impact; treat the comparison to paid impressions as an analogy, not data.
You may need to track branded search volume and direct traffic to estimate any effect.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Query fan-out: why AI citation needs topical coverage, not one keyword
cards.summary: AI assistants expand a single prompt into many synthetic sub-queries, so you must be relevant across a whole topic rather than one head keyword.
cards.use_when: Planning product-category content or PDP/editorial coverage and deciding which topics to own so your products can be surfaced inside AI answers.
steps: Treat an AI prompt as a research brief, not a lookup: the assistant breaks it into dozens of narrower questions and runs them in parallel, then synthesizes the results. The source cites a reported example of ChatGPT's deep research mode running 420 searches for a prompt about buying a red phone case.

Map the sub-queries a real buyer's prompt implies. Example from the source: 'Plan me a five-day trip to Japan in November' fans out to 'best neighborhoods to stay in Tokyo,' 'November weather in Kyoto,' 'is the Japan Rail Pass worth it.'

For ecommerce, apply this by covering the comparison, fit, use-case and objection questions behind a category (e.g., material durability, sizing, compatibility, vs-alternatives) on category pages, buying guides and PDPs.

Recognize the three retrieval-probability factors the source cites from Ahrefs research: consensus (same brand claims repeated across many places), freshness (AI-cited content averaged ~25.7% fresher than top Google results), and authority (76% of AI overview citations came from pages already in Google's top 10).
Conclude that traditional SEO is the foundation; if you already rank top-10 on Google you start with an advantage.
Prioritize building relevance across the full topic cluster rather than optimizing single keywords.
caveats: The 420-search figure was a reported example, not a guaranteed depth per query.
Freshness/authority percentages are Ahrefs research findings cited by the presenter, not universal guarantees.
cards.source_name: Learn 80% of AEO in 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Brand gap analysis to find missed AI citations
cards.summary: Run a brand gap analysis to surface where your brand is mentioned-but-not-cited, where competitors win, and which topics AI associates with others.
cards.use_when: Auditing AI visibility before choosing which ecommerce content, PDP or mention-building work to do next.
steps: Measure where your brand should appear versus where it actually appears across Google, AI results and the web. The source suggests a tool like Ahrefs Brand Radar: enter your domain, add a couple of competitors, get a comparative overview.
Apply the 'mentioned but not cited' filter: these are AI responses that name your brand without linking your site — your missed citation opportunities.
Apply the competitor-gap filter: queries where a competitor is mentioned and you are not.
Apply the topic-gap view: topics AI associates with a competitor instead of you.
Note all gaps before acting, because you cannot fix everything at once; these gaps feed your prioritization later.

In an ecommerce context, translate gaps into concrete work: competitors recommended in 'best X' AI answers means you need listicle/review/Reddit presence; topics you should own means content or PDP gaps.
Use the ranking of gaps to match the biggest gap to the matched priority before spending on the smaller ones.
caveats: The source specifically names Ahrefs Brand Radar; other tools may work but the workflow shown is tool-specific — verify current interface.
Gap data reflects a snapshot; re-run periodically since AI answers shift.
cards.source_name: Learn 80% of AEO in 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: The AI Filter: deciding when a keyword is a trap vs an unlinked-mention play
cards.summary: Test each target keyword by asking whether an AI overview fully answers it; informational queries that AI 'eats' should be targeted for unlinked brand mentions, not clicks.
cards.use_when: Doing keyword research for a store and deciding where to chase clicks versus where to aim for brand mention inside AI answers.
steps: Generate seed keywords and modifiers using an AI prompt. Source template: 'I'm doing keyword research for my [type of] site which makes money through [revenue model]. My target audience are [these people]. Give me 10 seed keywords that are one to two words max and five plus modifiers that'll help me surface appropriate content formats... The seeds and modifiers should not share the same words.'
Take seeds into a keyword tool's ideas report with modifiers to build a candidate list; vet on business potential, search intent and keyword difficulty.
Run each keyword through the 'AI Filter': Google the query and ask whether an AI overview fully satisfies the searcher. If yes, nobody needs to click and the keyword may be a trap.
Use the source's data to gauge risk: AI overviews appear on ~21% of keywords but ~58% of question queries; 99.9% of keywords triggering AI overviews are informational.
For informational queries AI will 'eat', don't ignore them — change the goal from earning a click to getting your brand mentioned inside the AI response.

Find those queries via the AI-platform 'others only' filter (queries where competitors are mentioned but you aren't), then filter for best, top, versus, review, alternative to build your mention-opportunity short list.
For ecommerce especially, reserve click-earning effort for commercial/product queries and use informational queries to earn unlinked brand mentions.
caveats: The percentage figures are from the source's cited research, not guarantees for your niche.
'Trap' is a heuristic judgment, not a formula; validate against your own conversion data.
cards.source_name: Learn 80% of AEO in 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: BLUF writing for AI and human parsing
cards.summary: Bottom Line Up Front: start every section with the answer, because both people and LLMs weight the beginning and end of a passage more heavily than the middle.
cards.use_when: Writing or rewriting PDP copy, category intros, buying guides or FAQ blocks so AI can extract your answer cleanly.
steps: Put the direct answer in the first line of each paragraph or section; do not lead with backstory or buildup.
Assume the model chunks your content and cannot control where the chunks fall, so a buried key point may be missed by both AI and skim-reading shoppers.
For product pages, this means front-loading the value proposition, key spec, or fit decision (who it's for, what it replaces) rather than a brand-history intro.
For buying guides, state the recommendation or decision rule first, then support it.
Write simply and declaratively: one idea per sentence in clear subject-verb-object structure.
Apply the litmus test the source offers: if a sentence takes two reads to understand, it needs to be simplified.
Combine BLUF with the finding that length doesn't drive citation (see the format card) so you keep sections tight and front-loaded.
caveats: Applies to every section, not just the page intro; the source stresses beginning AND end of passages weigh more than the middle.
cards.source_name: Learn 80% of AEO in 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Atomic content and entity-rich writing for chunk extraction
cards.summary: Make each section understandable out of context and pack it with specific entities and relationships so AI can extract and connect meaning.
cards.use_when: Structuring PDP sections, feature blocks, comparison pages or guides that AI may pull as isolated fragments.
steps: Edit every H2/section so it makes complete sense if extracted alone; AI chunks pages and you cannot control the cut points.
Avoid section openers that depend on preceding context ('as mentioned above', 'this tool'). Name the product or entity explicitly in each section.

Write entity-rich: instead of 'This tool helps with SEO', write 'Ahrefs Keywords Explorer helps you find keywords with low difficulty and high traffic potential' — more specific entities and relationships give AI more to work with.
Translate to ecommerce: instead of 'great battery life', name the exact spec, compatible models, materials and use cases so the fragment carries meaning.
Keep sentences simple and declarative with one idea per sentence, since complex sentences risk being misparsed when chunked.
Reuse the same specific entities across your site, mentions and video so you build the consensus signal AI weighs.
caveats: Atomic structuring trades some narrative flow for extractability; balance against the reading experience for human buyers.
cards.source_name: Learn 80% of AEO in 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Content format and freshness to get cited (length doesn't matter)
cards.summary: AI citations favor lists/comparisons and freshly updated pages, not word count; over half of cited pages are under 1,000 words.
cards.use_when: Deciding the format and update cadence for store buying guides, comparison pages and category content.
steps: Drop the assumption that longer ranks: analysis of 174,000 pages cited in AI overviews showed near-zero correlation between word count and citation, and over half of cited pages were under 1,000 words.

Prioritize formats AI can pull recommendations from: 43.8% of ChatGPT-cited pages were lists — 'best X', 'top X', comparisons and reviews. For ecommerce this maps to 'best [product type]', 'X vs Y', and review/comparison content.
Treat freshness as high-leverage: for ChatGPT, 89.7% of top cited pages were updated in 2025 and 76% were refreshed within the last 30 days.
Set a refresh cadence — the source warns content untouched for six months is already at a disadvantage.
When refreshing, update the visible date, prices, spec and recommendations rather than making cosmetic edits.
Rebuild pages that lost ranking due to becoming outdated first, as the source identifies this as a fast win.
caveats: The percentages are from the source's cited analyses and reflect those datasets, not a guarantee for your category.
Refresh frequency feasible for a large catalog will vary; prioritize high-intent pages.
cards.source_name: Learn 80% of AEO in 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Earn brand mentions in three tiers of pages
cards.summary: Branded web mentions had the strongest correlation with AI overview visibility in a study of 75,000 brands — stronger than backlinks or domain rating — so get named on other people's pages.
cards.use_when: Planning off-site AEO work (PR, lists, community, creator) to increase how often AI recommends your store.
steps: Accept the source's core claim: in a study of 75,000 brands, branded web mentions correlated most strongly with AI overview visibility — stronger than backlinks, domain rating or referring domains.

Tier 1 — third-party editorial: industry publications, review sites (The Wirecutter, TechRadar), and listicles/comparison posts on authoritative blogs. Hardest to earn, most valuable because these are the pages AI loves to cite.

Tier 2 — user-generated content: Reddit, Quora, niche forums. The source says Reddit is one of the most frequently cited sources by ChatGPT and a foundational training source. Find threads where your product or expertise genuinely answers the question and contribute real answers; join communities and contribute regularly rather than gaming.
Tier 3 — owned properties: your YouTube channel, podcast, LinkedIn — all indexable and crawlable.
Remember consensus: the more places your brand appears in a topically relevant way, the more training examples AI has.
For ecommerce, actively pursue inclusion in 'best X' listicles and answer real buyer questions in communities rather than only owning your own pages.
caveats: The correlation figures are from the source's cited study, not causal guarantees.
Community contribution warns against gaming; genuine participation is implied as the ethical requirement.
cards.source_name: Learn 80% of AEO in 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: YouTube AEO: target search hits over viral hits
cards.summary: YouTube is the most cited domain in Google AI overviews and YouTube mentions showed the strongest correlation with ChatGPT visibility in the source's data — build evergreen search-hit videos, not viral spikes.
cards.use_when: Planning video content or creator sponsorships to increase AI visibility for your store.
steps: Prioritize YouTube because the source reports it is the most cited domain in Google's AI overviews, YouTube mentions correlated 0.737 with ChatGPT visibility, and GPT-4 was trained on over a million hours of YouTube transcripts.

Choose 'search hits' not 'viral hits': search hits get consistent Google and YouTube search traffic month after month on evergreen topics, and those are the videos AI is most likely to cite; viral videos spike then die.
Find proven search-hit topics: in Ahrefs Site Explorer, set the YouTube 'watch' subfolder and use the organic keywords report, filter for top-3 rankings, and add niche terms.

Optimize each video: put the keyword in the title and within the first couple lines of the description; add timestamps for YouTube chapters; and actually say the keyword in the video, since Google understands audio and pulls from transcripts.
Retain viewer attention, since retention supports the video ranking across many search queries.
If you don't produce video, get your brand mentioned on YouTube via sponsorships or creator outreach — a mention counts as an AI-relevant signal.
For ecommerce, target evergreen 'how to choose / best X for Y' searches relevant to your products rather than trend-chasing.
caveats: 0.737 correlation and citation claims are the source's reported figures, not promises.
The topic-finding workflow is Ahrefs-specific; verify current interface.
cards.source_name: Learn 80% of AEO in 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Technical AEO: don't accidentally block AI crawlers
cards.summary: Check robots.txt for disallow rules against GPTBot, OAI Search Bot, ClaudeBot and Google Extended, since Cloudflare's AI-bot setting defaults to blocking GPTBot.
cards.use_when: First-step technical audit before any AEO content or mention work on your store's domain.
steps: Go to yourdomain.com/robots.txt and look for any 'Disallow' rules next to GPTBot, OAI Search Bot, ClaudeBot, or Google Extended. If present, you are blocking that AI crawler.
Treat this as the first 30-second check, because if AI can't crawl the site, your content and pages are handicapped from being mentioned.
Check Cloudflare settings specifically: its 'instruct AI bot traffic with robots.txt' feature is enabled by default, so Cloudflare-hosted sites may block AI crawlers without realizing it.
Note the source's context: about 5.9% of 140 million websites were blocking GPTBot — likely mostly inherited from old robots.txt templates.
Override inherited or default rules if you want AI crawlers to access your pages, then re-verify robots.txt.
Do this before investing in content, since blocked crawlers waste that effort.
caveats: Default settings and feature names may change; verify your host/Cloudflare's current controls.
The source frames blocking as usually accidental; deliberately blocking AI crawlers may be a legitimate choice some stores make.
cards.source_name: Learn 80% of AEO in 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Measuring AEO: AI referral traffic, bot activity and self-reported attribution
cards.summary: Track AI referral traffic (as a directional undercount), AI citation-bot activity on your pages, and 'How did you hear about us?' survey attribution to capture otherwise-hidden AI impact.
cards.use_when: Setting up store analytics for AI-driven discovery and deciding which channels actually drive sign-ups or purchases.
steps: Accept that AI search hides much that traditional SEO measures; the source says you're not flying blind and offers three things to track.

Track AI referral traffic: clicks landing on your site from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and others. Recognize the nuance that not all platforms pass referral data properly — ChatGPT source links track but in-content links on paid accounts don't — so any number is almost certainly an undercount. Use it as a relative/directional metric, not precision.

Track AI bot activity instead of (or alongside) human clicks: monitor which citation bots hit which pages, since a bot repeatedly hitting a page suggests that page is used as a source. The source suggests Cloudflare integration, which it says works on Cloudflare's free plan.

Track self-reported attribution: add 'How did you hear about us?' to sign-up flow, checkout or as a post-purchase survey, because someone who sees your brand in ChatGPT then Googles you gets attributed to organic by analytics.

Contextualize with the source's own example: at Ahrefs, AI search traffic was just 0.5% of visits but drove 12.1% of sign-ups — 23x higher conversion rate than organic — which they'd not have known without self-reported attribution.
Set measurement up from day one, then use it to judge whether content/mention/video work is moving AI visibility.
caveats: AI referral traffic is an undercount due to inconsistent referral-data passing; do not treat as exact.
Ahrefs' 0.5%/12.1%/23x figures are a single company example, not a benchmark to expect.
Features and setup (GA4 channel, Cloudflare integration) may change — verify current interfaces.
cards.source_name: Learn 80% of AEO in 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Building a custom AEO strategy by matching gap to priority
cards.summary: Sequence AEO work: technical check first, measurement setup, then fix the biggest brand-gap by matching gap type to the right intervention.
cards.use_when: Turning AI-visibility findings into a prioritized action plan for your store.
steps: Start with the 30-second technical check on robots.txt, because blocked crawlers handicap all other work.

Set up measurement from day one, either via an AI traffic channel in GA4 or a tool with it built in, and implement the 'How did you hear about us?' question — small but highly valuable for capturing hidden AI impact.

Review your biggest brand-gap and match it to a priority: if AI doesn't associate you with topics you should own, that's a content problem — refresh pages that used to rank but lost ranking due to becoming outdated, identified as the fastest win.
If competitors keep getting recommended and you don't, pursue mentions: get included in listicles, reviews and Reddit threads where you're absent.
If AI cites formats you don't produce (e.g. video), get on YouTube — either create your own content or contact creators to amplify your brand.
The source frames AEO as layered on top of SEO: treat SEO as the foundation, then add content, mentions, YouTube and technical setup.

Time-sensitive context from the source: AI traffic grew 9.7x in the past year, ChatGPT sent more traffic than Reddit or LinkedIn, and most businesses hadn't implemented AEO yet — an argument for starting early.
caveats: The source explicitly says this is not one-size-fits-all; prioritization depends on your own gaps.
Growth and traffic-comparison figures are the source's reported context, not forecasts.
cards.source_name: Learn 80% of AEO in 19 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Set up a persistent AI project for SEO and product research
cards.summary: Use a dedicated AI project (not a single chat) to hold your business brief and research files so long ecommerce SEO workflows don't lose context.
cards.use_when: Starting any multi-step keyword, content or AI-visibility project for a store and you plan to paste many research files over several sessions.
steps: Create a new project/workspace in your AI tool (ChatGPT, Claude or similar) rather than running everything in one chat thread. The source's rationale: a single chat has a limited context window, so the AI gradually forgets your earlier business information; a project retains the files you add.
Generate a business brief first: paste a prompt or your store URL and answer the questions about what you sell, who you sell to and where. Save the output as a text file.
Add that brief file as a source inside the project so every later prompt (keyword clustering, category copy, PDP content) inherits the correct catalog and positioning context.
Add each new research artifact to the project as you produce it — keyword clusters, competitor keyword exports, sitemap breakdowns — instead of re-explaining them in chat.
Reuse the same project for content generation and AI-citation work so market, audience and product terminology stay consistent across pages.
caveats: Context limits and project features in AI tools change; verify the current interface.
The source recommends this for service businesses; for ecommerce the brief should capture catalog, categories, target buyer and fulfillment areas, not just services.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Understand GEO and the two new AI-visibility KPIs
cards.summary: Generative Engine Optimization is the practice of getting your brand into AI-generated answers, measured by citations and brand mentions rather than clicks alone.
cards.use_when: Deciding what success looks like for a store's presence in ChatGPT, AI overviews or Perplexity, and choosing metrics to track alongside organic traffic.
steps: Define the category: generative engines (ChatGPT, Google AI overviews, Perplexity) produce an answer instead of sending the user to a blue link, so the goal shifts from ranking-and-clicking to being included in the generated answer.

Track two new KPIs alongside organic traffic and conversion: (1) citations — the AI uses your content to build its answer; (2) mentions — the AI names your brand or business. These are distinct events and both matter.

Map your existing pages against likely AI questions in your niche (e.g. 'best [product category] for X', 'is [product] worth it') and check whether your content is being cited or your brand mentioned.
Keep purchase conversion and revenue as the ultimate commercial outcome; citations and mentions are intermediate visibility metrics, not sales metrics.

Note the source's position that GEO is the only new acronym worth adopting because it is the one appearing in peer-reviewed work; treat other labels (AEO, LLM SEO) as synonyms rather than separate disciplines.
caveats: The source describes GEO as built on top of traditional SEO — it estimates classic SEO still accounts for roughly 80% of the work; this is the presenter's heuristic, not a measured benchmark.
Citation and mention tracking tools and AI engine behavior change frequently.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Discard three common GEO myths before planning store content
cards.summary: Google penalizes thin content not AI-written content, the AI model you use is not a ranking factor, and traditional SEO still underpins AI visibility.
cards.use_when: When a stakeholder or agency argues for or against using AI to produce store product and category content.
steps: Myth 1 — 'Google penalizes AI content.' The source's correction: Google penalizes thin, spammy, no-value content regardless of who or what wrote it. A carefully written AI-assisted product page can rank; a low-effort human-written one will not. Base your quality bar on usefulness, not on authorship.

Myth 2 — 'Picking the right model improves rankings.' The source states the AI model is not and never was a ranking factor, and that current models are more than capable for SEO/SEO-adjacent writing. Use the AI tool you already pay for rather than switching.

Myth 3 — 'AI changed everything; old rules are dead.' The source argues AI search is built on traditional SEO, so solid classic on-page work still delivers most of the GEO benefit. Treat AI-specific techniques as an addition to, not a replacement for, fundamentals.

Practical implication for ecommerce: continue investing in accurate descriptions, specifications, structured data and genuinely helpful buying guidance, and add extractable answer formats on top rather than instead.
caveats: These are the presenter's framings of Google's position; Google's guidance and enforcement evolve, so verify current official statements before making irreversible content decisions.
AI-detector tools are dismissed by the source as unreliable and not a planning input.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Translate customer language into keyword research, not expert terminology
cards.summary: Research the words buyers actually type, which often differ from industry jargon, and split the task into transactional and informational keywords.
cards.use_when: Choosing which search terms a product, category or landing page should target before writing copy or building pages.
steps: List the terms your team uses internally and then list what a first-time buyer would type. The source's example: installers call it 'EVSE installation', customers search 'Tesla charger installation' — the customer phrasing wins because that is the query with demand.

Separate keywords into two buckets the source uses: transactional (buying intent, e.g. 'home EV charger installation' — the shopper wants the product now) and informational (research intent, e.g. 'EV charger installation cost' — the shopper is still deciding).
Start transactional research from your own catalog: enumerate every product, category and service-equivalent page you intend to have, then check search volume and difficulty for each.
Then mine informational queries around the same seed terms — these become blog posts, buying guides and FAQ content that support the commercial pages.
Save every candidate keyword into a planner/spreadsheet and cluster them by seed topic so you can see which page each term belongs to.
Do this per product line or category rather than once for the whole store, so each page gets its own dedicated target.
caveats: The source stresses that third-party SEO tools only give direction — volume and difficulty numbers are estimates, not truth.
Location and language settings materially change results; set the market you actually sell into.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Run transactional keyword research and cluster it by page
cards.summary: Take each core commercial term through an SEO tool's overview and suggestions, save the related terms and cluster them so one page owns each topic.
cards.use_when: Building or restructuring category and product landing pages, and deciding which terms each commercial page should target.
steps: Pick a seed transactional term for a category or product (e.g. 'home EV charger installation') and pull its overview: monthly search volume, difficulty score, and cost-per-click. High CPC suggests commercial value worth targeting.

Save the seed term to a planner, then open the tool's suggestions/related-keywords view to surface adjacent query variants — the source calls these secondary or LSI keywords that search and AI engines expect to see together.

While scanning suggestions, note brand-specific and audience-specific variants (e.g. 'Tesla charger installation', 'BMW EV charger', 'EV charger for businesses'), because these can justify dedicated sub-pages if they show volume.
Watch for modifiers that signal a separate page: costs, rebates, requirements, commercial vs residential. If a variant has its own demand, plan a page rather than cramming it into the main one.
Save every relevant term to the planner, then create a cluster around the seed keyword so the tool groups them and shows total cluster volume.
Export the cluster as CSV and load it into your AI project, then repeat the whole sequence for each of your other categories/services so every commercial page has its own keyword set.
caveats: Cluster volume totals are tool estimates — treat as directional, not as guaranteed traffic.
The presenter's own tool (Datawise) is used in the demo and is disclosed as his paid product; equivalent workflow exists in Ahrefs, Semrush or similar tools.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Mine People-Also-Ask questions for buying-guide content
cards.summary: Pull PAA questions at depth around a core term and turn them into FAQ and guide content that answers real pre-purchase doubts.
cards.use_when: Planning buying guides, FAQ blocks and supporting content that feeds shoppers toward your commercial pages.
steps: Take a core transactional term and run a People-Also-Ask search in your SEO tool with search depth set high (the demo uses depth 3) to surface related questions across the market.
Expand each PAA entry — clicking through reveals subsequent nested questions — to build a fuller list; the demo returned over 140 questions for one term.

Manually review the list rather than trusting the AI blindly; select the questions that genuinely apply to what you sell and that a real buyer would ask (price, suitability, operating cost, whether a standard installer/consumer option works).
Export the selected questions as CSV and add them to your AI project with context, so later content prompts can address them directly.

Use these questions as FAQ blocks on commercial pages (the source suggests keeping commercial-page FAQs short, no more than about five, to preserve the page's transactional focus) and as full buying-guide topics where enough depth exists.
Repeat for each main category so each buying guide is grounded in questions real shoppers ask around that specific product.
caveats: PAA lists are noisy; the source explicitly recommends human review over bulk acceptance.
Question availability varies by market and language.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Answer fan-out queries to win AI citations
cards.summary: Fan-out queries are the internal follow-up questions an AI asks itself when handling a broad prompt; answering them in your content raises citation chances.
cards.use_when: Writing guide, FAQ or PDP content aimed at being cited by ChatGPT, AI overviews or Perplexity for a broad category question.
steps: Understand the mechanic: when a shopper asks an AI a broad question (e.g. 'should I install an EV charger at home?'), the engine decomposes it into sub-questions — costs, permits, local availability — researches each, then synthesizes an answer. Those sub-questions are the fan-out queries.

Find them using a tool that exposes fan-out data (the demo uses a fan-out queries view seeded with a core term; the source notes this data is currently US/English-only, so even non-US sellers can use it preemptively).
Filter hard: the demo returned ~195 queries for one seed and many were irrelevant to the business, so select only the ones your products actually answer.
Fold the selected fan-out questions into your content as headings with direct answers, alongside the People-Also-Ask questions — the source expects heavy overlap between the two lists.
Expect some queries to sit at the informational top of your editorial plan and others to belong on commercial pages as FAQ entries; route each to the appropriate page type.
Treat this as the GEO-specific layer on top of the keyword research you already did, and re-check periodically because fan-out data and coverage change.
caveats: Fan-out query data is described as new and limited to US English at time of recording; coverage may expand.
The source flags that fan-out lists contain irrelevant entries that must be discarded manually.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Do a four-part competitor analysis to plan your page architecture
cards.summary: Study competitors' ranking keywords, winning pages, sitemap structure and backlink profile to decide how much content and how many pages your store needs.
cards.use_when: Planning a category/blog structure for a new store or a new product line, or diagnosing why competitors outrank you.
steps: Pick real competitors: search your main commercial term, exclude sponsored results, and also ask an AI assistant (outside your project) who it recommends for the query to see who is being cited. Choose two to five root domains.
Run a domain comparison in an SEO tool to see total ranking keywords, traffic estimates and keyword value. Identify the competitor with the most ranking keywords and examine them in depth.

Open their ranked keyword list and look at which URLs win. In the source's example, the leader ranked mostly with blog posts plus dedicated location pages — that revealed the page types needed to compete.

Fetch their sitemap (domain/sitemap.xml), paste it into your AI project and ask for it to be categorized into commercial pages, location pages and blog posts as CSV, so you can see the structural scale you must match.

Check their backlinks tab: count backlinks and referring domains, review which links exist (directory/business listings, press, associations) and note the spam score. This tells you whether off-page work will be needed if on-page alone can't close the gap.

Convert findings into your own page count and content plan: match the page types that are working, plan to execute them better, and flag backlinking as a later phase rather than an immediate requirement.
caveats: The source treats this as a flexible, judgment-based process, not a fixed checklist — the right depth changes with the market.
Competitor tools give estimates; a high spam score is described as a good sign (low spam) but you should interpret link quality yourself.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Map distinct product and collection intents to useful store pages
cards.summary: Splitting every offering onto its own page is the single most important structural decision for ranking commercial pages.
cards.use_when: Planning product and collection architecture for an ecommerce catalog.
steps: Adapt the source's separate-offering principle to distinct products and useful collections; do not generate a page for every wording variant.
Use category hubs and product pages where each serves a distinct shopper need, with meaningful content and navigation.
Let the keyword research determine how many pages you need — the number of pages you build should follow demand, not convenience.
Build one page to a checklist you're happy with, then reuse it as a template for the others, changing the content for each target rather than duplicating.
Sequence this work initially in one page type (e.g. your most valuable category) before scaling across the catalog, so the template is proven before replication.
caveats: The source's example is a service business; the structural principle (separate pages per distinct offering and target keyword) is what transfers to ecommerce categories and product lines.
A dedicated page needs enough distinct search demand to justify it — confirm volume per offering first.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Apply the 2-second rule to commercial page first folds
cards.summary: Within two seconds of landing, a visitor must know what you offer, where you offer it, and what to do next.
cards.use_when: Writing or reviewing the above-the-fold area of a product, category, service or payment landing page.
steps: Check three things in the first fold, without scrolling: (1) what you do/sell, (2) where you do/sell it (for local businesses — location/page relevance), (3) the next action you want the visitor to take.

Write a plain, direct headline rather than a tagline. The source contrasts an ambiguous example ('You're spending the money. You just can't see what it's doing...') with a clear one: 'Professional home EV charger installation in Austin. Get a free quote.'

Make the H1 state exactly what the page offers and answer the implicit question 'can you do this for me / is this the thing I want?' The source treats one H1 per page as a technical requirement (see the structured-data card).
Place a primary call to action above the fold — a prominent button matching the outcome the visitor wants (get a quote, add to cart, shop the range).
Save creative taglines and brand flourish for further down the page or other placements; keep the first fold unambiguous because that is where bounce decisions are made.
caveats: The 2-second rule is the presenter's heuristic for commercial pages, not a measured standard.
What 'where' means differs online vs local; for pure ecommerce, location may be replaced by delivery/return terms or product fit rather than geography.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Run a commercial-page checklist: intent, one keyword, schema, design, specifics
cards.summary: Five checks determine whether a product or collection page will perform, starting with search-intent match and including structured data and evidence.
cards.use_when: Finalising a new category, product or collection page before publishing.
steps: Intent match: confirm the page answers the searcher's intent — a transactional query needs a page where the product can be bought or requested, not an article about the topic.
One main keyword per page: assign a single primary target and use secondary/related terms naturally through subheadings and body copy rather than spreading several primaries across one page.

Schema: add appropriate structured data (service/product schema as applicable) so search engines understand exactly what the page contains. The source says you can rank without it but you're giving up an advantage; SEO plugins often insert it, but validate the output rather than assuming.

Conversion-friendly design and evidence: prefer real photos of the actual work/product over stock imagery where possible, be specific about prices, include reviews (ideally reviews mentioning that specific product/service), and add a how-it-works section.

Body structure: use additional H2/H3s for related keywords, and include a short FAQ of the most-asked questions for that specific offering — the source advises keeping commercial-page FAQs to no more than about five so the page stays transactional.

Use the first fold as the priority: pass the 2-second rule (what/where/next action), keep the headline plain, keep H1 exact, and place a primary CTA above the fold. If roughly 90% of these boxes are ticked, the source considers the page in good shape.
caveats: The source deliberately avoids prescribing a word count — length should follow what the page needs, not a target.
Blog/informational content should be kept off commercial pages beyond a short FAQ to avoid diluting transactional focus.
Structured-data support and plugin behavior change; verify with a current validator.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Check descriptive page headings and relevant product structured data
cards.summary: Every page should carry exactly one H1 that states the offering, with H2–H4 for everything else, plus verified structured data.
cards.use_when: Auditing on-page technical setup across a store's templates, especially after theme changes or migrations.
steps: Use a clear main heading and logical heading hierarchy to describe the product or collection; the source's one-H1 rule is an authoring convention, not a guaranteed ranking requirement.

Watch platform defaults: the source notes that on some themes (he cites Shopify's Dawn theme) the homepage H1 is typically the logo, which means the homepage H1 may not be describing your offering. Check and adjust.
Make the H1 state exactly what the page offers so both users and crawlers recognise the page topic quickly.

Inspect the title tag, meta description, heading hierarchy and structured data using a browser extension (the source demonstrates a free Chrome extension for on-page inspection; verify the current tool).
Validate applicable Product, Offer and breadcrumb data for store pages; do not copy Service schema from the source's service-business example.
Re-run the audit after any theme, template or plugin change, since these can alter headings and schema.
caveats: Platform default behaviour (e.g. logo as homepage H1) varies by theme and version — check your own store rather than assuming.
Plugins are described as doing a reasonable job but not a guaranteed-correct one; validation is the control step.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Write content capsules so AI engines can extract clean answers
cards.summary: Place a short, self-contained 20–25 word answer directly under each question heading so AI engines can lift it as a citation.
cards.use_when: Writing buying guides, blog posts and FAQ sections on product or category pages aimed at AI citations.
steps: Structure each section as a question heading (H2) followed immediately by a direct answer. The capsule must make sense on its own, without the surrounding article.
Answer the buyer question immediately. Suggested store application: under a fit question, state verified size and compatibility facts before a longer explanation.
Keep the capsule around 20–25 words. Going over 50 words is acceptable if the answer genuinely requires detail, but brevity is the default.
Target roughly 60–70% of the piece written in capsule form. The remaining 30–40% can be freer prose (process explanations, narrative sections) so the article still reads well to humans.
Do not put links inside the capsule itself — keep it clean for extraction. Put citations in the surrounding text instead.

Cite sources for factual statements, especially any numbers, by linking a contextual keyword to the origin. The source argues that citing sources increases trust and is important for AI engines, and that fear of losing traffic to citations signals a content problem, not a linking problem.

Add first-hand experience wherever possible — the source describes lived experience as the element AI engines can't yet replicate. Experience can be simple ('we tried X and got Y, so do/don't do Z'), not only decades of credentials.
Use the checklist/structure the source provides (structure, sourcing, coverage, on-page, things to avoid) and expect the workflow to become habitual after three or four pieces.
caveats: The 60–70% capsule proportion and 20–25 word target are the source's working heuristics, not measured thresholds.
The technique is described as supported by peer-reviewed study, but results will vary by topic and engine.
These are editorial heuristics, not required AI-search formatting. Keep necessary qualifications and evidence with the answer; Google does not require special chunking.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Prompt an AI to draft capsule-style content from your keyword research
cards.summary: Feed the AI your brief, topic, audience and selected keywords to produce a structured capsule-format draft with sources and first-hand experience slots.
cards.use_when: Drafting buying guides, comparison posts or FAQ-driven blog content that should be extractable by AI engines.
steps: Inside your project, paste a content prompt that instructs the AI to use the content-capsule technique, and supply three inputs: the topic, the audience, and the goal.

Choose the topic from your keyword planner — the source notes you can take a People-Also-Ask or fan-out question as the main topic with related questions as subheadings, and that the tooling offers a content map where one query becomes the post topic and others become sections.
Describe the audience specifically (e.g. 'homeowners in Dallas, Texas who just bought an EV') — the more you know about the audience, the more useful the prompt output.

Let the AI run its research phase: it should surface top-ranking pages for the term and a set of high-quality sources to cite (in the demo these skew toward government sites). Review the sources rather than accepting them blind.
Approve the proposed structure — headings, where capsules go, a table or two, and an FAQ section at the end. Ask for variants (tables, differentiators) to make the content less uniform.
Before requesting the first draft, insert proprietary detail the AI cannot know ('when we did X we found problem Y') so experience and specificity are baked in.
Pull the first draft, then edit — the source treats the AI output as a first draft and warns against trusting it blindly.
caveats: AI models sometimes over-ask clarifying questions; the source suggests capping those if the list gets too long.
Prompts and tool interfaces change, so verify the current prompt template and features.
Do not let cited sources or claims stand unchecked — the source repeatedly advises human review.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Build a content map that routes keywords to the right page type
cards.summary: Use your cluster data to assign each keyword to a commercial page, FAQ, or full article, so supporting content feeds the money pages.
cards.use_when: Planning an editorial calendar or deciding whether a keyword deserves its own page, a section, or an FAQ entry.
steps: Work from the planner/cluster view of your saved keywords, segmented into transactional and informational groups.
Identify which queries deserve an entire article. In the source's tooling, a content map flags one query as the post topic and related queries as the subheadings to answer within it.
Route commercial-intent keywords to money pages — one primary keyword per page — and keep informational content off those pages beyond a short FAQ.
Route informational keyword groups to buying guides or explainer posts written in capsule style, since these are the pages most likely to be cited by AI engines.

Keep the relationship visible: supporting articles should link contextually to the relevant product/category page, because the article's job is to capture research-stage demand and hand it to the commercial page.
Revisit the map as clusters grow, so a section that gains enough demand can be promoted into its own page.
caveats: The source's routing logic is a lightweight two-bucket model (transactional vs informational); more complex intent taxonomies exist and may be needed on large catalogs.
Tool features for content maps change; the principle is separable from any one product.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Use citations and first-hand experience as AI-trust signals
cards.summary: Backing claims with sources and adding lived experience to your content increases trust with readers and citation likelihood with AI engines.
cards.use_when: Writing or reviewing any buying guide, comparison page or product explanation where factual claims and prices are stated.
steps: Whenever you state a number or factual claim, link a relevant contextual word to the origin of that information. The source frames this as at least as important as writing well.

Answer the fear that outbound links leak traffic by improving the content instead — the presenter argues that if a reader leaves because you showed a source, the content wasn't strong enough to hold them.

Add first-hand experience in a form AI can't reproduce: outcomes and specific observations from actually using or selling the product ('we tried X and got Y'). This does not require years of credentials — a single documented result counts.
Give the AI these experience details explicitly in your prompt, because it cannot invent your operational knowledge.
Distinguish this from generic marketing claims: the goal is verifiable specificity that a reader (and an engine) can trust.
caveats: This is the source's argument about trust and citation behaviour, not a measured ranking guarantee.
Citations must be relevant and accurate; a low-quality source undermines the intent.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Iterate to a proven page template before scaling across the catalog
cards.summary: Perfect one commercial page against the checklist, then replicate the structure across other offerings and page types.
cards.use_when: Scaling a store's page production after the first category or service page performs structurally well.
steps: Build one page against the full checklist — intent match, single main keyword, schema, conversion-friendly design, 2-second-rule first fold, short FAQ, real imagery, specific pricing.

Review it critically before replicating: check the first fold, headings, schema validity and keyword placement. The source notes that fresh eyes (a second reviewer) catch what the original builder misses.
Treat that page as a structural template, not a content template — every page keeps the framework but gets its own copy, keywords and evidence.
Apply the same discipline to content pages: once one capsule-style article performs, reuse the prompt structure and section rhythm for other topics.
Track results and revisit structure if performance lags, since the source recommends validating before full rollout and being willing to change the structure by market and competitor landscape.
caveats: The source warns against copy-pasting identical content across pages — only the structure should repeat.
No specific rollout volume or timeline is given; pace depends on catalog size and resources.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Draft and edit long-form content in an editable AI canvas
cards.summary: Use an AI assistant that renders the draft in an editable document so you can refine sections, then paste cleanly into your CMS.
cards.use_when: Producing a long-form blog post or category guide for your store and you want an iterative editing loop rather than copy-pasting from chat.
steps: Feed the AI your outline (headings, quick capsule answers, one or two comparison tables, and an FAQ block at the bottom) before asking for a draft.
Ask for the first draft; then edit directly inside the canvas view and also manually where needed, so you get a back-and-forth collaborative pass instead of a one-shot output.
Inject your own first-hand experience into the sections where it matters (e.g., the friction you hit when applying for a city permit), because that detail is what differentiates the content.
Have it flag internal links to relevant pages; since it can't know a non-real site's links, insert the actual internal link targets yourself.
Check that the draft followed your capsule technique and that it cites high-quality sources with working links (e.g., a city permit guide that actually opens).
Paste the finished piece into WordPress and fix the title duplication and any formatting gaps before publishing.
caveats: The specific AI product name and canvas/edit features change over time; verify the current interface before relying on a particular button.
A first draft is 'probably not' ready to publish — expect an experience-injection and sourcing pass.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Limit AI-generated question lists to keep content focused
cards.summary: If the model proposes too many sub-questions, cap them so the page stays tight and useful rather than bloated.
cards.use_when: Generating FAQ or Q&A sections for a store guide or informational landing page and the model returns an excessive question list.
steps: Let the model propose questions and headings, but judge whether the total is too long.
Trim the list to the questions your shoppers actually ask; keep the structure you're happy with (headings, brief capsule, one or two tables, bottom FAQ).
Once the structure is approved, request the first draft.
Add more of your own non-public information where you have it, since the more unique detail you place in the prompt, the better the output.
caveats: There is no fixed number of questions that is correct; the limit depends on the topic and page type.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Add illustrations to break up text-heavy content (with ecommerce application)
cards.summary: Turn key passages into simple illustrations using a free text-to-visual tool, then convert and place them for impact.
cards.use_when: A product-education section, buying guide, or PDP long-description block reads as a wall of text and you want to make a specific point pop.
steps: Copy just the passage you want to illustrate (e.g., 'how much will an EV charger increase my bill').
In a free text-to-visual tool (the source uses Napkin; a free account has enough capacity), paste the text and generate visuals.
Review the recommended visual, swap it if you don't like it, and pick a styling that fits your site; you can edit elements before exporting.
Export the image and then convert it out of PNG to WEBP (a free PNG-to-WEBP converter works) to keep it light.
Place the WEBP into an image block where it makes sense.
Use this once or twice per post — don't let the page look like nothing but illustrations.
caveats: Don't upload PNGs by default — AI image/visual tools output PNG and heavy images slow the site.
The source did not cover image SEO in detail; treat image-file optimization as the takeaway, not a full image-SEO guide.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Write meta descriptions with an AI assist and length target
cards.summary: Have the AI draft the meta description at under ~150 characters to support click-through, then paste into your SEO plugin.
cards.use_when: Finishing a store blog post or category page and you need the title tag and meta description fields filled before publishing.
steps: Confirm whether the AI already produced the meta description; if not, prompt it: 'give me the meta description for this blog post, less than 150 characters.'
Paste the result into the meta description field of your SEO plugin (e.g., Yoast or similar — installing one is recommended but not strictly necessary).
Check the title tag contains the main target keywords.
Review the description for length; the source notes a slightly-too-long description is a common fix-on-sight issue.
caveats: The source states the meta description 'isn't going to make an enormous difference' but can increase CTR — treat it as a CTR nudge, not a ranking lever.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Map the whole site structure before building the store
cards.summary: Generate a CSV-style page map (URL, name, title tag, page type, focus) from prior research so the site is planned, not improvised.
cards.use_when: Planning a new store build or a major site restructure and you want the URL hierarchy and page list defined before writing pages.
steps: Use the keyword research, competitor analysis, and page list you already produced as inputs.
Run a 'build your site structure' prompt inside the project that holds that research (works in ChatGPT or Claude) to output a structured sheet.
Expect columns like URL, service/parent page, name, title tag, page type, and focus.
Lay out service/parent pages and child service pages following the URL structure (e.g., services/EV-charger-installation, then services/EV-charger-installation/lutz-florida).
Review the output with common sense and change what doesn't fit; don't copy it blindly.
Lock this structure in as the map you follow during the build.
caveats: The source stresses consistency over an 'ideal' order — don't agonize over whether the service or location comes first in the slug; just stay consistent.
The sheet is described as intentionally rough, a page map rather than a finished blueprint.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Deploy the new store and submit it to search consoles
cards.summary: Connect Google Search Console and submit your sitemap so the launched site can actually be found and indexed.
cards.use_when: Just after launching or relaunching an ecommerce site, when you need it discoverable in organic and AI search.
steps: In Google Search Console, go to 'add property', choose the website option, and enter the full new domain; continue and verify ownership.
Locate your sitemap URL (you can check a competitor's the same way to confirm the pattern).
In Search Console's sitemap section, add the new sitemap URL and submit it.
Confirm the status reads success and note the number of discovered pages — a correctly structured site should show many more than a handful.
Work through a launch checklist on a staging site first, then use it as an ongoing on-site SEO checker after launch.
caveats: A site that nobody can find is 'just wasted pixels' — deployment and submission are not optional.
Specific Search Console menus change; verify current navigation.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Audit on-page SEO across five core elements plus speed
cards.summary: Check title tag, meta description, H1, H2s, and schema — plus page speed — using a free browser plugin and Lighthouse.
cards.use_when: Reviewing your own newly launched store or a site you're optimizing, and you want a fast on-page pass without deep technical work.
steps: Install a free on-page SEO browser extension (the source uses SEO Wallet) and confirm it's active (a small blue bar appears at the left of the page).
Check the title tag contains your main keyword; it doesn't have to be perfect.
Check the meta description length and tighten if slightly too long.
Open the headings tab and verify the H1 and H2s/H3s reflect your primary and secondary keyword targets.

Open the structured data view and confirm the schema that matches the page — e.g., course schema for a course, FAQ page, organization schema; schema changes per page type and isn't needed on every page, but is needed on money pages.

For speed, open Chrome DevTools (top-right three-dot menu → More tools → Developer tools), select the Lighthouse tab, and analyze page load; aim to push performance, accessibility, best practices, and SEO as close to 100 as possible.
caveats: On the source's example site, only performance, accessibility, best practices, SEO, and agentic browsing were all reported at 100; getting everything to 100 is not the norm.
How deep you go on on-page SEO depends on the site type; this is a quick pass, not a full technical audit.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Build purposeful internal links into every content page
cards.summary: Internal links improve crawlability, navigation, and pass authority — so link blog content to service/money pages where it makes sense.
cards.use_when: Publishing evergreen store content (buying guides, how-tos, blog posts) and you want it to feed your commercial pages.
steps: Identify your money pages (e.g., the EV charger installation service page) and the related content posts (e.g., cost, permit, level-two posts).
Wherever it genuinely makes sense, add internal links from those posts to the money page — not always, but as often as it fits.
Aim for three purposes: easier crawling for AI and traditional search engines, easier navigation for users, and passing authority to deeper pages.
Remember that the deeper/more inter-linked pages receive less authority, but linking still helps.

Optionally automate with a WordPress plugin like Link Whisper (uses Google Search Console data and adds internal links on new posts) or a content writer tool that handles internal linking when you supply the knowledge base (pages, tone of voice, offer details).
Don't over-complicate — the source keeps internal linking simple and it has worked for them.
caveats: Plugin behavior and integrations change; verify current capability.
Automated tooling still needs your judgment about which links make sense.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Track AI visibility with Search Console and Bing AI performance
cards.summary: Use clicks, impressions, average position, and queries from Search Console, and Bing's AI performance tab for citations.
cards.use_when: Monitoring whether your store is surfacing in AI overviews and chat results, and deciding what to do next month.
steps: In Google Search Console's Performance tab, track total clicks and impressions — impressions typically rise first, then clicks; also watch average position across all ranking keywords.
Expect lower clicks generally as AI search engines absorb some traffic; this is described as the new norm, not automatically an error.
Keep Google Search Console performance separate from dedicated AI citation reporting; verify what each current report actually measures before labeling it AI visibility.
Read total citations, average pages cited, and the queries you're cited for; growth in citations and average cited pages is good.
Optionally use a paid AI-visibility tool for additional coverage: a performance tab (citations by engine), a brand tracker for instant checks, and prompt/keyword tracking.
caveats: The source's visibility-tool data skews to US and English queries; that biases the picture for other markets.
There is no target number for how fast citations should rise; the source says judge month-to-month improvement, not an absolute benchmark.
Do not infer that every impression, click or rank movement in Search Console came from an AI feature.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Track brand mentions and cited queries, not just rankings
cards.summary: Mentions across Google AI overviews, ChatGPT, and Perplexity are tracked as a leading indicator alongside clicks.
cards.use_when: Deciding which AI-visibility signals to watch for your store and whether your brand is being recommended.
steps: Use a brand tracker to see what large language models cite you for (e.g., 'internal linking', 'high-quality links') and pull a total mention count across engines.
Track mentions over time — the source example showed mentions decreasing and flagged it as something to investigate.
Treat brand mentions as important, with the source stating they see more conversions attributable to mentions than other AI metrics.
Optionally track specific prompts and keywords, but avoid over-complicating the dashboard.
caveats: The preference for 'mentions over other metrics' is the presenter's opinion, not an established benchmark.
Visibility-tool data is generally US/English-weighted.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Start with free local citations before any backlink strategy
cards.summary: Build local directory listings with consistent NAP as the first, cheapest authority layer for a local store.
cards.use_when: Launching a local store and you need foundational authority before investing in link campaigns.
steps: Ask an AI for all free online business listing directories in your target location (e.g., 'free online listing directories for businesses in Dallas, Texas'), and supply more detail about your business type to get more results.
Expect directories like Next Door Business, Foursquare, and the Better Business Bureau — the source says always get on the BBB.
Create a free account wherever allowed and enter your info, keeping NAP (name, address, phone number) consistent across all listings.

For more than three sites, delegate this or use a trusted paid citation service (the source uses Bright Local's local citation building; roughly $3.20 per citation, with a '$2 per citation' rate only at bulk).
Avoid cheap Fiverr-style '300 local citations for $5' offers — they should be a red flag.
caveats: NAP inconsistency across listings is the main risk the source flags.
Pricing was quoted at recording time and may differ now.
Local citations don't replace a backlinking strategy for competitive national niches.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Earn expert citations through reporter-request platforms
cards.summary: Answer journalist/publisher questions on a connectivity platform to earn citations and brand mentions with a backlink.
cards.use_when: You or your store's founder have subject-matter authority and want authentic links without buying them.
steps: Create an account on a platform (the source uses 'Connectivity', formerly Featured.com; it used to be HARO/Help a Reporter-style).
After setup and a few questions, you'll see questions publishers are asking; those listing your profile (connected to LinkedIn) are ones the platform predicts you're well-suited for.
Pick the question you can answer best and answer it as thoroughly as you can, then submit.
The answer goes through review, selection, and publication stages; when published you get cited with a link to your site.
Note results vary: the source reports 5 of 12 pitched were published and used the free tier of about three answers per month.
caveats: This 'only really works' for people with some authority or subject-matter expertise in their field.
Publication is not guaranteed; treat the hit rate as variable, not a benchmark.
Platform name and features change — verify the current interface.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: Evaluate sponsored placements by buyer relevance and referral value
cards.summary: If you still can't outrank competitors, buy relevant, high-quality links from vetted agencies — never quantity-focused cheap links.
cards.use_when: After you've built the site correctly, published good content, and gotten indexed — and you still aren't outranking competitors.
steps: Sequence it: do all the free things first (local citations, expert citation platforms) before paying for links.
For paid placements, require sponsored or nofollow link attributes; do not buy unqualified links to manipulate search rankings.
Get on a call with the link provider to verify what they're doing; if they don't know, you'll waste money on poor-quality links.
Assess publisher relevance, actual audience, transparent placement terms and expected referral value rather than copying a vendor endorsement.
Treat backlinks as the last layer, not a launch necessity.
caveats: Google states it doesn't condone purchasing backlinks; the source observes it remains a large industry because it works, but this is presented as an open secret, not a recommendation of policy.
Fiverr backlink sellers are specifically flagged as easy to get burned by.
The source has not tried all backlink services.
cards.source_name: The Complete AI SEO Course 2026.docx

cards.title: AEO mental model: execute like Google, measure like Facebook
cards.summary: Treat answer-engine optimization as SEO-style content work but measure it with ad-style attribution (view-through, self-reported) rather than click-through, because AI referrals are invisible to analytics.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to resource and measure an AEO/generative-search channel for your store, when direct referrer traffic looks flat or falling but you suspect AI assistants are driving discovery.
steps: Execute the channel as you would Google SEO: publish thorough, intent-matched content on your own site and the third-party surfaces LLMs read, targeting the prompts and phrases buyers actually type.
Do NOT judge the channel by Google Analytics click-through referrals alone; analytics cannot see most AI-driven discovery because users never click through.

Add a self-reported attribution survey at signup/checkout ('How did you hear about us?') with AI assistants surfaced as explicit options rather than buried under 'Other'. In the source's experience, moving this question to the front and naming the AI options sharply increased responses.

Track both curves separately: click-through referrals (can fall) and self-reported mentions (can rise simultaneously). Gamma saw ChatGPT-referred traffic grow roughly 8x across channels while click-through later declined.
Accept the measurement is analogous to Facebook view-through attribution: imperfect, but the best available proxy until platform-level reporting exists.
caveats: Source is a growth lead's heuristic account at one large consumer SaaS company, not an audited benchmark; the 8x figure is a case example, not a promise.
Self-reported data is noisy and subject to recall bias.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Platform-by-platform AEO playbooks diverge: don't run one strategy
cards.summary: Reddit's influence is largely isolated to ChatGPT, and the playbooks for ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews differ substantially.
cards.use_when: Allocating limited content and community effort across AI surfaces that send or influence traffic to your store (e.g., deciding whether a Reddit push will help Perplexity visibility).
steps: Sample the same buyer questions on relevant AI surfaces and record the model, date, locale, search mode, recommendations and cited pages.
Identify which retailers, publishers, guides and communities recur for this product category.
Prioritize channels using observed buyer relevance and store conversions, not the source's SaaS platform ranking.
Keep shared SEO and factual product-data fundamentals, then test platform-specific content opportunities.
caveats: Overlap figure is a stated heuristic observation, not a measurement.
Reddit's ChatGPT data deal and platform mechanics may change; verify current behavior.
The source's platform preferences and overlap estimates are hypotheses from a consumer SaaS context, not current ecommerce guarantees.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Prioritize AI discovery surfaces using the store's own buyer evidence
cards.summary: Consumer/prosumer discovery concentrates heavily in ChatGPT, while enterprise-tool research happens in Claude and Copilot, so platform priority should flip by segment.
cards.use_when: Allocating an ecommerce AI-discovery budget across assistants serving retail or wholesale buyers.
steps: Use post-purchase survey responses and observed referrals to identify assistants buyers actually use.
Sample representative category and product questions on these surfaces.
Compare purchases and qualified discovery before allocating effort; separate retail and wholesale customers where relevant.
caveats: Rankings are the source's heuristic bets for a consumer SaaS, presented as educated guesses, not measured benchmarks.
Claude citation-rate comparison is attributed to third-party studies referenced in the conversation, not independently verified here.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Reddit playbook: open-ecosystem wedge posts and competitor-comparison framing
cards.summary: Succeed on Reddit by posting value-oriented content that leverages your tool's interoperability and explicit competitor comparisons, and avoid brand-only self-promotion.
cards.use_when: Planning Reddit participation to earn ChatGPT citations and reach buyers in relevant subreddits without posts being removed.
steps: Find communities where shoppers discuss your product category, use cases and compatible products.
Adapt the source's SaaS interoperability example to verified product compatibility, care or selection questions; disclose brand affiliation and respect community rules.
Contribute useful comparisons based on real specifications and experience rather than promotional claims.
Answer precise buyer needs such as fit for a particular activity or compatible accessory, and monitor whether the contribution remains useful.
caveats: Comments are for sentiment, not discovery lift: the source sees no meaningful impact from commenting on citation direction.
Negative sentiment can get indexed and persist for months, per a referenced case; the claim that LLMs bias toward negative content is a stated theory, not established fact.
Don't over-focus on tiny subreddits at scale — source says these won't move a large company, though they may matter for small startups or niche topics.
This is a suggested ecommerce adaptation, not a demonstrated store result; comments and posts may contribute differently across communities.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Measure citation pickup and persistence before timing a store campaign
cards.summary: New Reddit content takes roughly 30-45 days to be cited by ChatGPT but can be cited by Perplexity as fast as the next day, informing how early to seed content.
cards.use_when: Timing Reddit or community content pushes ahead of a product launch or seasonal campaign when you need citations live by a specific date.
steps: Record publication dates and repeated citation checks. The source observed a 30-45 day ChatGPT lag in one case; do not use that as a launch deadline guarantee.
The source also observed faster Perplexity pickup; measure the current behavior for your own category and content.
For Google AI Overviews, source reports one observed same-day pickup from a niche query — timing is getting faster but varies.
Prioritize participation in other people's subreddits early when starting out; build your own subreddit for the long term (own-community content is cited later).

Plan for citation half-life: the source theorizes citations expire on a cycle and must be refreshed (they manually track citation share in a spreadsheet), so treat Reddit as an always-on engine, not a one-time push.
caveats: Timing figures are observational from one company's experience, not guaranteed SLAs.
Citation lifetime/half-life is explicitly the source's untested hypothesis.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Test question-led product content while preserving shopper usefulness
cards.summary: For AEO-designated initiatives, allocate roughly 80% of effort to agent/crawler consumption and 20% to human readability so content still makes sense if a human finds it.
cards.use_when: Producing YouTube videos, LinkedIn content, or blog posts with the explicit intent of earning AI citations rather than direct human clicks.
steps: Label the initiative as AEO-first and design around agent consumption: choose titles, headings and structure from prompts/phrases people type, not clickbait headlines designed for human clicks.
Keep the whole page useful and accurate for shoppers. The source's 80/20 crawler-to-human split is an unvalidated opinion, not a content quality target.

Decide content angle deliberately: don't just describe the product ('this is a glass of water'); go deeper into comparative/meaningful angles ('why is this steel glass better than plastic') and avoid thin, keyword-stuffed repetition.
Push back on the assumption that AI-written content must be spam: modern models can produce well-researched, thick content, and LLMs are more likely to reward depth.
Treat any citation gains as experimental and recheck performance; avoid sacrificing helpful content for presumed crawler preferences.
caveats: The 80/20 split is the source's rule of thumb, not a measured optimum.
Source acknowledges gaming carries reputational/durability risk and expects platforms to penalize it (e.g., a referenced Google search update penalized low-value content sites).
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Compete in AI citation by niching down the prompt, then expanding
cards.summary: You cannot win broad AI queries like 'best CRM', so start with narrow, defensible prompt phrasings, build topical authority, then attempt broader terms.
cards.use_when: Targeting AI-assistant answers in a crowded product category where broad 'best X' queries are dominated by incumbents.
steps: Map the query landscape from broad to narrow: 'best CRM' → 'best CRM for SMB' → 'best CRM for fintech' → 'best CRM for health tech sales people'.
Enter at the narrow end where competition is lowest and you can plausibly be cited.
