Build topical authority/relevance at that niche level first, then take another shot at broader terms.
On Reddit specifically, use the same strategy: rather than a generic post, target the niche comparison where you can place favorable and get cited.
Expect competitors to follow you into niches — when they do, keep moving to the next under-served angle; the source frames 'keep moving' as what growth is.
Treat this as an always-on engine: continuously produce and refresh content, since you cannot rely on a one-time citation.
caveats: This is the source's stated approach; they explicitly say they lack a proven formula for citation lifetime or selection logic.
No guaranteed ranking — success depends on category and competition.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: AEO channel priority and citation-lifetime tracking
cards.summary: Own-site content is cited fastest and most controllably; track citation share manually to detect when citations expire.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to publish before your own site versus third-party channels, and setting up a lightweight system to monitor AI citation retention.
steps: Prioritize your own website content: source ranks it second-most influential (after Reddit for ChatGPT) because it gets cited faster and you control how your product and competitors are described.
Treat other people's websites (blogs, PR, reviews) as the third cluster — the source constantly switches between second and third, so don't over-invest in one.
Lower priority: YouTube, then LinkedIn (LinkedIn citation behavior is currently thin and unpredictable; both posts and articles have been seen indexed, with no clear engagement pattern).
To track retention, log citations manually in a spreadsheet: record what got cited, from where, and monitor citation share over time to spot declines.
Plan content refresh cycles around observed citation decay — the source suspects a citation 'half-life' but has not measured it.
caveats: No off-the-shelf tool yet tracks citation half-life; source tracks manually.
Ranking positions 2 vs 3 are said to fluctuate.
LinkedIn/YouTube indexing patterns are described as early and patternless.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Test additional publishing surfaces against observed category citations
cards.summary: When Reddit is saturated, extend AEO content into Medium, Quora, and Substack, which are cited but less contested.
cards.use_when: Scaling AEO reach after you've established a Reddit and own-site presence and need additional citable surfaces.
steps: Consider an additional publishing surface only if target shoppers use it or it appears in sampled citations for relevant buying questions.
Consider Substack cautiously: it is indexed, but journalists/authors there tend to gate content, which reduces citation pickup.
Check actual cited sources rather than assuming any social platform is universally included or excluded.
Treat the source's platform-growth predictions as historical speculation, not current channel-selection evidence.
Verify each platform's current indexing behavior before committing budget — this landscape shifts within months.
caveats: All indexing observations are the source's informal tracking, not platform-confirmed.
Instagram/LinkedIn predictions are explicitly speculative bets.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Understand retrieval vs memorization to choose content tactics
cards.summary: LLMs either retrieve fresh web content (~60% of ChatGPT queries per the source) or answer from trained-in knowledge (~40%), and each mode needs different AEO tactics.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in fresh web content or in seeding training-data surfaces, given that the two modes respond to different inputs.
steps: Record whether sampled shopping answers show a live search and which pages they cite.
Do not classify Reddit as training-only or blogs as retrieval-only; source type does not establish how a model used it.
Prioritize current factual product pages and useful public answers; treat any future training effect as uncertain.
Repeat checks in fresh sessions with consistent settings to reduce confounding from account context or memory.
caveats: The 60/40 retrieval/memorization split is a study cited by the source, not verified here.
Memory and retrieval mechanics are described as a black box that may change without notice.
cards.source_name: The Head of Growth at a $100M Company Explains AEO.docx

cards.title: Audit search crawler access independently from training permissions
cards.summary: Verify public product and collection pages are accessible to the intended search crawlers while preserving separate training choices.
cards.use_when: A store wants product pages discoverable in AI search or is diagnosing missing product visibility after CDN or theme changes.
steps: Inspect robots.txt and CDN or firewall rules for representative public product and collection URLs.
For ChatGPT search, check OAI-SearchBot; GPTBot controls training separately. For Google Search AI features, inspect Googlebot access. Do not blanket-enable unrelated crawlers.
Check HTTP responses and actual crawler logs where available; compare initial HTML with rendered product facts to identify rendering dependencies.
Correct unintended blocks for the desired search crawler, preserving deliberate training restrictions and protected checkout or account areas.
Retest after deployment and future CDN or theme changes; access enables retrieval but does not guarantee recommendation.
caveats: Verify current crawler documentation and CDN settings; defaults change. A spoofed user-agent test alone does not verify real crawler access.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Submit sitemaps and confirm indexation as an AI visibility prerequisite
cards.summary: AI engines pull fresh information from Google and Bing, so an unindexed store will not be recommended in AI answers.
cards.use_when: Setting up an ecommerce store for AI visibility, or diagnosing why AI engines describe your brand inaccurately or not at all.
steps: Recognize the dependency: AI search engines like ChatGPT lean on traditional search engines (the presenter notes Microsoft owns roughly 50% of ChatGPT and that Bing feeds it), so pages missing from Bing or Google are effectively missing from AI answers.
In Google Search Console, go to Indexing > Sitemaps, enter your sitemap URL (typically yoursite.com/sitemap.xml), and submit; the presenter's example picked up 94 pages with a successful status.
Repeat the same sitemap submission in Bing Webmaster Tools, which matters disproportionately for ChatGPT-sourced answers.
Spot-check indexation by typing site:yourdomain.com into Google search to see which of your product, category and content pages are actually indexed.
Re-submit or investigate whenever new product or collection pages are not appearing, since unindexed SKU pages cannot be surfaced to AI shoppers.
caveats: Sitemap submission does not guarantee indexation; crawl budget, page quality and technical issues still apply.
Verify the current navigation paths in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools, as interfaces change.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Publish an About/Facts page as structured brand context for AI
cards.summary: A facts page giving what you do, your USPs and how long you've operated gives AI engines the raw material to describe and recommend you correctly.
cards.use_when: Building or refreshing the homepage/about section of an ecommerce store so AI engines can state accurate brand facts in recommendations.
steps: Add an About Us or Facts page to your store if one does not exist; many stores skip this, leaving AI with no authoritative brand description.
List what you sell, your key differentiators/USPs, how long the business has existed, and any relevant credentials in plain, factual language.
Keep the facts consistent with what appears in directories, review platforms and schema so AI does not encounter conflicting claims.
Update the page as the business changes (new categories, certifications, milestones) so AI recommendations stay current.
Treat this page as the canonical fact source you will later point schema and directory listings toward.
caveats: The presenter's claim that adding a facts page will make visibility 'grow' is a directional expectation, not a measured benchmark.
Facts pages do not substitute for product-level crawlability and content quality.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Validate structured product and brand facts alongside visible copy
cards.summary: Structured data spells out your business, products and social profiles in a machine-readable format AI crawlers read reliably.
cards.use_when: Adding or auditing structured data on an ecommerce site to improve how LLMs interpret brand and product information.
steps: Structured data can clarify store facts; it is not a prerequisite for all AI systems and does not prevent hallucination.
Add Organization schema to the homepage including founding date, description, and links to social profiles; this signals that you are a proper, reputable business.
Use a schema generator tool to select a schema type, fill in the relevant fields, and copy the generated code onto the appropriate page.
Apply the other schema types recommended in the source checklist to their matching page types (e.g. product-related types on product pages) rather than dumping all schema on one template.
Link your YouTube channel and social profiles from your website and include them in schema markup alongside the rest of your brand data.
Validate the markup after deployment so errors do not silently defeat the purpose.
caveats: Schema improves interpretability but does not guarantee recommendation; the presenter treats it as one of several inputs.
Exact schema types beyond Organization are in the linked checklist, not enumerated in the video.
Google does not require special AI schema. Validate applicable product search features separately from any citation hypothesis.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Front-load answers on product and category pages with a TL;DR
cards.summary: Put a direct 2-4 sentence answer and a TL;DR at the top of every important page because most AI citations come from the first third of the page.
cards.use_when: Writing or rewriting product pages, category pages, buying guides and landing pages so AI extracts your content as the cited answer.
steps: Open each key page with a direct 2-4 sentence answer to the core question the shopper or AI is asking, rather than a slow marketing build-up.
Follow it with a TL;DR summary block, so both users and AI crawlers get the essential value immediately.
The presenter cites that over 44% of AI citations come from the first third of the page, so move key facts (materials, sizing, use cases, who it's for) above the fold and above decorative sections.
Write in natural language rather than keyword-stuffed phrasing, since AI engines parse natural-language queries and prefer natural-language answers.
Apply the same structure to comparison and informational pages, not just product pages.
Keep updating the top sections as facts change so the first third of the page is always the most accurate.
caveats: The 44% first-third citation figure is the presenter's cited statistic; treat it as a directional heuristic rather than a fixed rule for your site.
Front-loading answers does not excuse poor product information further down the page — shoppers still read details.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Build FAQ sections from 'People Also Ask' to grow topical authority
cards.summary: Harvest the questions Google surfaces for your topic and answer them at the bottom of every important page to demonstrate expertise to AI.
cards.use_when: Adding Q&A coverage to product pages, category pages or buying guides to increase the chance AI engines treat your store as the expert source.
steps: Search your topic (e.g. 'self storage software') in Google and scroll to the 'People Also Asked' section.
Copy those exact questions — Google is literally telling you what people ask about the topic — and draft clear answers.
Add the questions and answers as an FAQ section at the bottom of every important page on the site.
The presenter's stated purpose is boosting topical authority: showing AI engines you are an expert, which in turn lifts visibility.
Repeat per page type so category pages, product pages and guides each answer their own cluster of questions.
Refresh FAQs periodically so answers reflect current pricing, specs and policies.
caveats: The link between FAQ sections and AI recommendation is the presenter's asserted mechanism, not a measured guarantee.
Avoid dumping irrelevant questions; mismatched FAQs can hurt user experience on purchase pages.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Use comparison tables and head-to-head competitor pages to win AI recommendations
cards.summary: Head-to-head comparison pages and tables give AI engines an easy, digestible reason to recommend you over larger competitors it already knows.
cards.use_when: Competing against bigger, better-known brands in your category in AI search, or structuring comparison content on an ecommerce site.
steps: Pick three to four larger competitors than you and write head-to-head pages comparing you versus competitor A, B, C and D.
Break down pros and cons of each option honestly so the page is credible, while clearly explaining why your product is better for the relevant buyer.
The presenter's logic: AI engines already know the big players, so comparing yourself to them supplies the reasoning AI needs to recommend you above them.
For any head-to-head or comparison content, include a comparison table near the top; tables are an easy-to-digest structure for AI engines to lift into answers.
Extend the same approach to comparison tables on your own category and product pages where buyers evaluate alternatives.
Keep the comparison facts accurate — pricing, features, specs — since inaccurate claims undermine credibility with both buyers and AI.
caveats: The presenter frames this as particularly effective for smaller businesses competing with much bigger players; it is not a guarantee of outranking the larger brand.
Legality and platform rules around comparative advertising vary by market; get claims checked where required.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Replace vague claims with hard numbers, expert quotes and original data
cards.summary: High-quality content with specific figures, named expert quotes and at least one piece of original data is more likely to be cited by AI engines.
cards.use_when: Improving the citability of product pages, buying guides, blog posts and category content that currently relies on generic marketing language.
steps: Audit content for vague claims such as 'many users prefer' and replace them with hard numbers and percentages wherever you have evidence (e.g. real customer results, review counts, test findings).
Add direct quotes from named team members who have a credible public presence, such as a strong LinkedIn profile; the presenter says this boosts visibility.

Include at least one piece of original data per important page — a survey, internal benchmark or industry finding AI cannot get elsewhere — since AI engines look for unique data to make answers more credible.
Consider producing an industry report or data roundup with original sourcing to position your brand as the category leader and give AI a citable primary source.
Apply the same rigor to glossary pages and statistics roundups, which the presenter identifies as content types that get cited.
Only publish data and quotes that are real and verifiable; fabricated figures are a reputational and legal risk.
caveats: The presenter asserts high-quality, original data creates a 'massive advantage'; this is expert opinion, not a measured effect size.
Small stores may have limited original data; customer outcome metrics or aggregated review data can serve as a starting point, but must be honest.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Refresh evergreen content and surface a clear last-updated date
cards.summary: Stale content loses to fresh competitors in AI answers, so revisit key pages every couple of months and show the last-updated date.
cards.use_when: Maintaining a content library or buying-guide set on an ecommerce site that has not been refreshed recently and is losing AI citations.
steps: Return to each important article every couple of months to add new statistics, update wording, and reference recent case studies or product changes.
Add a clearly visible last-updated date to every article so AI and Google bots can see freshness without re-reading the whole page.

The presenter claims that even updating only the last-updated date — without changing content — can boost rankings; treat this as the presenter's assertion, and note it will not help if the underlying content is outdated or false.
Recognize that freshness is a ranking factor across search engines, not just AI, so the same maintenance serves traditional SEO.
Prioritize top-performing pages and high-commercial-intent content (category pages, comparison pages, top buying guides) when time is limited.
Avoid deceptive re-dating of unchanged content; the presenter describes this tactic as something to do 'really slightly so your competitors don't notice', which is an admission of manipulation.
caveats: The date-only freshness trick is grey-hat and the presenter frames it as something competitors should not notice; it carries reputational risk and no guarantee of lasting effect.
Real content updates are the durable version of this tactic.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Fix NAP consistency and directory listings to stop AI misdescribing your store
cards.summary: Inconsistent name, address, phone and inconsistent descriptions across directories cause AI engines to produce wrong information about your business.
cards.use_when: Cleaning up brand presence for a store with physical locations, local service areas or notable B2B distribution, so AI shops describe it accurately.
steps: Complete your Google Business Profile with full, accurate details including what you sell, your USPs and how long you have operated.
Create and claim listings in business directories relevant to your category (the presenter names Yelp, Trustpilot, Crunchbase, and industry platforms) and on review platforms.

Ensure your business name, address and phone number are character-for-character consistent everywhere, since inconsistency causes AI to produce wrong information and reduces the chance of recommendation.
Encourage customers to leave reviews on the most relevant platforms, and keep review responses current.
Keep descriptions aligned with the checklist of what AI says it looks for when recommending your type of product (see the 'ask AI what it looks for' card below).
Re-audit listings when you rebrand, move, or add locations, because stale entries will keep feeding AI outdated facts.
caveats: The presenter lists directory platforms generically; which ones matter depends on your category and country.
Paid review-incentive programs must comply with platform rules — Google prohibits incentivized reviews, so check current policies before offering rewards.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Get into 'best of' listicles and roundup articles that AI cites
cards.summary: AI engines frequently draw recommendations from '10 best X' listicles, so securing placement there directly increases the chance your store gets recommended.
cards.use_when: Acquiring recommendations in AI answers for a category where buyer queries surface best-of roundups (e.g. 'best [category] for [use case]').
steps: Search your key category term (e.g. 'best self storage software') in AI Overviews and AI mode and note which sources are used; the presenter's example showed listicles dominating the sources.
Click through to the listicle and identify the people who maintain it; install the Hunter Chrome extension to pull contact details of people at that site.
Reach out via email and LinkedIn with a credible, specific case for why your business belongs on the list — ideally near the top.
Expect that some listings require payment; the presenter says paying for placement can sharply increase AI visibility because listicles are a primary AI source.
Build a simple spreadsheet tracking every site you want to be featured on and work through it step by step rather than ad hoc.
Consider hiring a YouTube creator to produce a best-list video for your industry; video transcripts also get cited by AI engines.
caveats: The presenter states paid placements are sometimes necessary and calls it worth it; disclose paid placements where required and weigh the ethics and platform norms of your industry.
Getting listed does not guarantee a top recommendation, and paying does not override relevance.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Use AI-generated buying criteria as hypotheses for a product-content audit
cards.summary: Prompt AI engines for the criteria they use to recommend your category, then retrofit your website and directory descriptions to match those criteria.
cards.use_when: Setting the target for what your store's descriptions, PDPs and directory listings should contain in order to be recommended in AI answers.
steps: Open an AI engine (the presenter uses Gemini) and ask directly: 'What do you look for when recommending [your product or service category]?'
Treat proposed criteria as research hypotheses, not access to the engine's ranking algorithm.
Compare proposed criteria with customer questions and verified product facts; add only accurate, relevant details to your product copy and editable listings.

Suggested ecommerce application: for waterproof hiking footwear, check whether verified fit, sizing, materials and intended terrain are clear. Do not invent certifications or performance claims to fit an AI checklist.
Repeat the prompt across multiple AI engines and merge the criteria into one master checklist.

Then ask AI: 'Search the internet and tell me what you know about my business', review the cited sources, and update each source's description (or contact the site owner) so it contains the checklist items.
caveats: AI-generated criteria are the model's stated reasoning, which may vary by engine, prompt wording and time; treat it as a research input, not a definitive algorithm.
If you cannot edit a source directly, you must persuade the site owner — an outreach task with uncertain success.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Run an AI brand audit to find and correct the sources AI reads about you
cards.summary: Asking AI to search the internet and report what it knows about your brand reveals the exact sources shaping its view so you can fix them.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why AI engines describe an ecommerce store incorrectly, omit key categories, or recommend competitors instead.
steps: Prompt the AI: 'Search the internet and tell me what you know about [brand]' and read the answer as if you were a prospective buyer.
Open the cited sources listed under the answer — these are the pages the AI used to form its understanding of your business.

For each source you control, edit the description to include the criteria AI says it looks for; for sources you do not control, use contact-finding tools (e.g. Hunter) to reach the site owner and request a correction or an updated description.
Run the same prompt for each main competitor ('Search the internet and tell me what you know about competitor A/B/C/D') to see which sources drive their recommendations.
Aim to win mentions, or better, placement in listicles, on those same competitor-driving sources to capture recommendation share.
Repeat the audit periodically, since AI answers and their sources change over time.
caveats: Cited sources can vary run to run and across engines; treat the list as a starting point rather than a fixed map.
Editing third-party sources depends on cooperation or payment.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Earn third-party mentions, podcasts and video to build AI trust
cards.summary: AI has no personal experience, so it looks for consensus; mentions in trusted publications, podcasts and video transcripts supply that consensus for your brand.
cards.use_when: Building authority signals for an ecommerce brand in a competitive category where reviews and editorial coverage influence AI recommendations.
steps: Secure mentions in at least three industry publications via guest posts, interviews or PR, prioritizing outlets AI cites in your category.

Approach industry accreditation bodies and associations — many allow sponsorship, contributed articles or partner listings; the presenter says paying may be necessary if you are serious about visibility.
Pitch industry podcasts, because transcripts are frequently indexed and cited by AI engines.
Work with influencers to post YouTube videos about the brand; the presenter's example video ranked on page one of Google and its transcript was also used as an AI source.
Structure any long-form external content (LinkedIn articles included) the same way as site content: value in the first 2-4 sentences, a TL;DR, and tables and bullets for easy extraction.
Track target publications and appearances in a spreadsheet so mention-building is systematic rather than opportunistic.
caveats: The presenter's claim that a video 'works like rocket fuel' is anecdotal; treat influencer/video coverage as one contributing signal.
Paid placements and sponsorships should be disclosed where required.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Collect honest product-experience reviews on relevant platforms
cards.summary: Because AI has no first-hand experience, it leans on customer reviews — especially ones that state concrete results — to decide whether to recommend you.
cards.use_when: Designing post-purchase review requests for ecommerce buyers and deciding which review destinations matter for product research.
steps: Choose review destinations shoppers use and that appear in sampled category answers.
Send a neutral post-purchase request asking about actual use, fit, quality and limitations; let customers use their own words.
Use a simple review link or QR code where appropriate for the purchase journey.
Do not script positive outcomes, fabricate numbers or condition requests on satisfaction; review current platform rules before introducing incentives.
Monitor and respond to feedback, separating service fixes from any unproven AI-visibility effect.
caveats: The source's incentive ROI and AI-consensus claims are not ecommerce benchmarks. Honest reviews support buyer decisions; citations are not guaranteed.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Engage Reddit communities with F5Bot monitoring to earn long-term AI citations
cards.summary: Reddit is one of the most-cited sources in AI answers, and cited posts are typically over a year old, so consistent value-first participation compounds.
cards.use_when: Building durable category presence and word-of-mouth for a store where buyers discuss products in Reddit threads and forums.
steps: Identify five to ten subreddits most relevant to your product category.
Participate by providing free value in existing threads first, building account karma before ever mentioning your brand, so you reduce the risk of being banned when you do.
Set up F5Bot alerts for your key category keywords so you get notified whenever they are mentioned on Reddit and can respond while the thread is active.
When relevant, recommend your product naturally within a genuinely helpful answer rather than dropping a link cold.
Expect a long runway: the presenter says the average Reddit post cited by AI is over a year old, so this is a one-to-two-year compounding play, not a quick win.
The presenter reports brands applying this Reddit engagement approach have multiplied visibility several-fold — treat this as an anecdotal case result, not a promise.
caveats: Reddit communities penalize overt promotion; value-first participation is essential and results are slow.
The stated 4-5x visibility uplift is the presenter's claim about unnamed brands and is not independently verifiable.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Publish long-form LinkedIn articles structured for AI extraction
cards.summary: Long-form LinkedIn articles get indexed by Google and can therefore become AI-cited sources, unlike short posts.
cards.use_when: Extending an ecommerce brand's content footprint onto LinkedIn to create additional citable sources about your products and expertise.
steps: Write long-form LinkedIn articles rather than short posts; the presenter notes long-form articles are indexed by Google, which makes them eligible as AI sources.
Structure them like your web content: deliver value in the first two to four sentences, include a TL;DR.
Add tables and bullet points so AI engines can easily extract key information to reuse in recommendations.
Cover core topics in your category and ideally include a natural recommendation of your product or service within the value.
Keep article facts consistent with your website and directory descriptions to reinforce rather than confuse AI's understanding.
Publish on a schedule; each article adds another potential citation surface.
caveats: LinkedIn indexing and discoverability of articles varies over time; verify current behavior rather than assuming permanent indexing.
Attribution of LinkedIn content to AI answers is not directly measurable in most setups.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Use YouTube and video transcripts as a brand and AI citation channel
cards.summary: Video transcripts are indexed and cited by AI engines, so publishing videos about your products adds a durable discoverable source.
cards.use_when: Planning a video/content channel extension for an ecommerce brand to increase AI and Google discoverability.
steps: Create a YouTube channel and an introductory video about your business, even at modest production value; the presenter says this associates the channel with your brand and gives AI a transcript to read.
Pick a specific search term your target customers use across Google, YouTube and AI search engines.
Place that keyword or term in the video title, description, YouTube video filename and thumbnail filename, and say it in the first and last 10 seconds of the video.
Prioritize information value over production quality; the presenter emphasizes value to the target customer.
Produce a companion blog post for every video, and a video for every blog post, to multiply the footprint of each idea.
Link the YouTube channel from your website and include it in schema markup alongside your social profiles.
caveats: The presenter's claim of occupying multiple page-one spots in ChatGPT ads is a personal case, not a guaranteed outcome.
Keyword-in-filename and first/last-10-seconds tactics are the presenter's heuristics; platform ranking behavior changes over time.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Publish transparent original product research through relevant press channels
cards.summary: Framing a listicle as a data-backed industry report and distributing it via a press wire is presented as one of the highest-ROI AI visibility moves.
cards.use_when: A category-level push to become the cited authority in AI answers, especially for a store or brand with data it can package as research.
steps: Title the release as an industry report, e.g. '[Niche] Industry Report: Top Leaders Ranked', rather than a plain 'Top 10' article.
Describe only research actually performed; disclose the method, sample, dates, limitations and brand sponsorship.
Include, where you have it, original data — AI engines look for unique data to cite and trust reports more than promotional posts.
Distribute the release via a press wire such as Newswire; the presenter says submissions cost a few hundred dollars and calls it likely the highest-ROI activity.
Include the store's products only where the comparison criteria justify inclusion, and make commercial interests clear.
Repeat across categories or quarters to build a body of citable reports.
caveats: The presenter's claim that these reports are cited and trusted more than articles is based on personal tests with clients and community members — an anecdotal claim, not a controlled benchmark.
Self-serving industry reports can damage credibility if the underlying 'research' is not real; disclose methodology or expect skepticism.
Do not relabel promotional rankings as independent research; distribution and report formatting do not establish credibility or training inclusion.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Execute a one-week AI visibility quick-win sequence
cards.summary: A prioritized starter list of free and low-cost actions to materially improve AI visibility within a week.
cards.use_when: An ecommerce operator starting AI visibility work and needing an ordered, immediately actionable checklist.
steps: Check robots.txt with a free AI bot access checker; register the site in Bing Webmaster Tools and Google Search Console and submit the sitemap.
Hire a YouTube creator to produce a best-providers list video for your industry and publish it on YouTube.
Add Organization schema linking to LinkedIn, Crunchbase and other reputable mentions of your brand, including social profiles.
Rewrite your business descriptions across all directories and review platforms using the checklist generated from asking AI what it looks for when recommending your offering.
Update your top three blog posts to add a TL;DR at the top and an FAQ section at the bottom.
Ask AI what it knows about you and correct the sources it cites; create new citations and review-platform entries and refresh existing ones.

Publish one long-form LinkedIn article on a core category topic that recommends your product, and start securing placement in 'best X' articles by finding AI-cited sources and outreaching via Hunter and LinkedIn.
caveats: These are the presenter's prioritization, not a validated sequence with measured effect sizes; treat the week as a starting sprint and re-measure.
Some steps (YouTube creation, paid placements) may cost money despite the 'free' framing in the video intro.
cards.source_name: The Ultimate AI Visibility Checklist (AEO_GEO for 2026).docx

cards.title: Build Share of Voice, Not Rank #1
cards.summary: In answer engines the LLM summarizes many citations, so being cited most often beats being the top URL.
cards.use_when: Deciding what to optimize on a PDP, category page or landing page when you want your brand named in ChatGPT or Gemini answers for 'best X' queries.
steps: Accept the structural difference: in Google a #1 blue link 'wins' the click; in an LLM answer the model averages many citations, so the most-mentioned brand is usually named first.
Aim to appear across many citations rather than to rank one URL first.
Ethan Smith's Webflow example: they drove presence via straight SEO, YouTube videos, Reddit and blogs/affiliates — straight SEO first, YouTube second, Reddit third.
For an ecommerce store, layer the same logic: get your brand named in comparison roundups, review sites, YouTube reviews and community threads for your category, not just on your own domain.
Measure mentions across surfaces (a brand name is what gets echoed), not just clicks to your site.
caveats: Source is B2B-leaning; Webflow's specific channel ranking is one company's result, not a universal benchmark.
The named-first result is Smith's observation of behavior, not a published ranking rule.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: On-Site vs Off-Site AEO: Two Workstreams
cards.summary: Split answer-engine work into on-site pages (SEO plus long-tail product Q&A) and off-site citation groups (video, UGC, affiliates, blogs).
cards.use_when: Planning headcount or agency scope for an ecommerce brand's AEO program.
steps: On-site: do traditional SEO landing pages for high-volume keywords like 'best no-code website designer'; per Smith this free-rides into AI answers.
On-site long tail: answer highly specific product questions — use cases, features, integrations, languages, specs — because LLMs scrape detail pages and support docs.

Off-site: pursue citations in distinct groups — video (YouTube/Vimeo), UGC (Reddit, Quora), tier-1 affiliates (Dotdash Meredith titles like Good Housekeeping, Allrecipes, Investopedia), tier-2 affiliates, and blogs.
Write a separate strategy per citation group; they behave differently and need different owners.
Staffing: your SEO team handles the on-site stream; a community/generalist marketer handles video and Reddit, since most SEO people are not strong at those.

Move a help center from subdomain to subdirectory and explicitly answer obscure integration questions (e.g. 'Which meeting transcription tool integrates with Looker?') — LLMs actively scrape support docs.
caveats: Smith's claim that on-site SEO automatically produces AI visibility is an observed pattern, not a guaranteed transfer.
Subdomain-to-subdirectory moves carry their own SEO risk; validate before migrating.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Do AEO Early Even When You Skip SEO
cards.summary: Unlike SEO, answer engines can surface a new brand within days of a citation, so early-stage and low-authority stores should prioritize AEO and skip domain-authority-dependent SEO.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to spend content budget for a new or low-authority ecommerce brand.
steps: Smith's standing advice for early startups: skip SEO, because you lack domain authority and it takes time to build before you can rank.
Apply the opposite logic to AEO: you can earn a citation tomorrow — a Reddit thread, a YouTube video, a blog mention — and start appearing immediately.
Recommended early-stage AEO focus: citation optimization plus long-tail questions only; skip the mid-funnel SEO work.
Cite the example: a brand-new YC company can appear in answers shortly after launch because people are talking about it.
For a new store, prioritize getting named in a handful of review threads, YouTube reviews and niche blog roundups over building a large content library.
caveats: This is Smith's strategic opinion and a change in his historical advice; it assumes you can generate genuine third-party mentions.
Spamming citations is explicitly warned against and gets detected and neutralized.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: The Long Tail Is Bigger in Chat Than in Search
cards.summary: Average chat queries run ~25 words versus ~6 for search, and include follow-ups never searched before — a large, winnable long-tail of specific product questions.
cards.use_when: Choosing which product-detail and FAQ content to write for PDPs, help centers and landing pages.
steps: Note the size difference: Smith cites roughly 25 words per query in chat versus about 6 in Google search.
Treat chat as a conversation: users ask follow-up questions, so map the whole chain of questions a buyer might ask about your product.
Include questions that have never been searched — e.g. 'which AI payment processing API integrates with X' — where competition is minimal.
For ecommerce: build PDP and help-center copy that answers the specific follow-ups around sizing, compatibility, integrations, materials, shipping, returns and use cases.
Winning this long tail is possible early for a new store because the questions are unclaimed.
The old tactic of one auto-generated page per keyword no longer works in search — but the long-tail logic has returned inside chat.
caveats: The 25-vs-6 word figures are attributed by Smith to a third party (possibly Perplexity) and are approximate.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Improve Content With Information Gain and Typicality
cards.summary: Judge content by whether it says something nobody else said (gain) and whether it is so typical it reads as a rewrite (typicality).
cards.use_when: Editing PDP copy, buying guides or blog posts before publishing, so AI engines prefer your page over recycled competitors.
steps: Ask the two questions Smith proposes as the fix for search's rewrite-each-other problem: did you add information gain, and how typical is this page?
Information gain = something another page did not say. Add original research, tests, photography, spec comparisons or first-party data.
Typicality = how closely you mirror the existing top results. Content-scoring tools flag everything competitors already said and push you to match it — which produces the homogenized content problem.
Also demonstrate domain expertise and, where true, credentials inside the content.
Ecommerce application: instead of re-writing a competitor's buying guide, publish actual fit, durability or cost-per-use data you collected yourself.
Alignment logic: these are also what you would want ranking algorithms to reward, so writing this way serves both readers and engines.
caveats: Smith explicitly says he is not seeing Google's E-E-A-T expertise signals produce measurable effects today — treat that as an unrealized possibility, not a ranking guarantee.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Model Collapse: Why 100% AI Content Fails
cards.summary: If AI summarizes AI-written articles, the crowd wisdom collapses and engines are eventually forced to penalize the content.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to mass-produce AI-generated product descriptions, category pages or blogs for an online store.
steps: Understand the loop: AI generates articles, other AI tools summarize them, and the underlying signal degrades because nobody added new information.
Smith's prediction: engines will eventually penalize AI content the same way they penalized scraper sites around 2007 and programmatic auto-generated landing pages after Panda.
He treats the 2007 spam-to-not-spam transition as the biggest change in his 18 years of SEO — larger than the current AEO shift.
Practical rule for a store: use AI for drafting and structure, but require a human-added information gain layer (real specs, real images, real test results).
Do not build a strategy whose durability depends on out-producing the spam filter.
Same dynamic applies inside ChatGPT: spamming the product will be detected by their search-evaluation team and neutralized.
caveats: This is a forward-looking prediction, not an observed penalty schedule; timelines are unspecified.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Authentic Reddit Commenting for Store Visibility
cards.summary: Reddit is heavily cited by LLMs; earn it with identified, genuinely useful answers instead of fake accounts.
cards.use_when: Running community and UGC outreach to get your store named in recommendation threads that LLMs cite.
steps: Do not run the growth-hacker play of hundreds of fake accounts auto-posting and upvoting your product; Smith says it works poorly and those accounts get banned and comments deleted.
Instead: find a thread that is part of a citation you want to appear in, state who you are and where you work, and give one genuinely useful piece of information.
This is what Webflow did — a couple of employees commenting transparently.
You do not need 10,000 comments; Smith says even five good comments can be great, and it scales fine.
Reddit, Quora, Twitter and similar UGC are deliberately ranked by Google's and ChatGPT's search algorithms because the platforms want trusted user-generated content.
Ecommerce version: answer real questions in your category's subreddits about sizing, durability, or which product fits which use case.
caveats: You cannot guarantee a comment stays up — the community can remove it, so it is easy but not controllable.
Requires disclosure of affiliation; undisclosed promotion risks removal and reputational damage.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Research the Questions Buyers Actually Ask
cards.summary: There is no search-volume truth set for chat, so derive target questions from keyword data, competitor paid search, and your own sales/support logs.
cards.use_when: Building an ecommerce buyer-question prompt set for AI visibility measurement and product-page, FAQ or buying-guide content planning.
steps: Start with search data: take your money keywords and your competitors' — for example, look at what a rival bids on in paid search — and convert them into questions.
Paste the keyword list into ChatGPT and ask it to turn them into questions people would ask; Smith says it does a good job.
Mine internal sources for the part of the tail that never appears in search: questions asked in sales calls, customer support tickets, and on Reddit.
Assume question frequency roughly tracks keyword search volume for the overlap terms.
Accept that there is no authoritative volume data for chat questions yet — Smith expects that to change if ad products arrive.
Ecommerce application: standardize the harvested questions into an FAQ schema, PDP Q&A block and help-center articles covering the whole follow-up chain.
caveats: No volume truth set exists for chat, so you cannot weight questions by measured demand; treat it as a coverage exercise.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Pick a Page Type That Already Gets Cited
cards.summary: Study which page formats appear in citations for your target questions and replicate that format rather than inventing one.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether a category page, listicle, comparison page or tool page is the right asset to build for a target query.
steps: For each target question set, look at what is currently cited: is it a listicle, a category page, an article, or a tool page?
Choose the page type that dominates those citations and build your own version of it.
Then make it rank by answering all the follow-up and sub-topic questions in that theme — the more questions the page answers, the more likely it is to be surfaced.
If a competitor answers a sub-question and you do not, you are less likely to appear for it.

Ecommerce application: if roundups dominate for 'best X for Y', build a genuinely comparative buying guide; if category pages dominate, invest in the category template — do not default to a blog post.
Page type is decided by the citation landscape, not by what your team finds easiest to publish.
caveats: Page-type dominance is observed per query set and shifts over time; re-audit rather than locking in one template.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Target Content Where Most Pages Deliver Nothing
cards.summary: One out of 20 landing pages drives about 85% of traffic, so concentrate budget on the few pages that can win instead of mass-producing pages.
cards.use_when: Allocating content budget across a large ecommerce catalog or content calendar.
steps: Apply Smith's analysis: roughly 1 in 20 landing pages drives about 85% of all traffic; 19 of 20 drive little to nothing.
Because most pages fail, the common tactic is spending a small amount on a large number of pages — usually via cheap non-expert rewrites of competitors' articles.
The better approach: identify the few pages that can actually win and put the full budget and best writers behind them.
Identify winners using the target-question list and the citation landscape, not gut feel.
Every dollar not spent on a doomed page is a dollar available for the top page.
Ecommerce application: audit which product or category pages drive traffic and invest in those templates and their copy first.
caveats: The 1-in-20 / 85% split is Graphite's analysis of client landing pages, not a universal law; your ratio may differ.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Match Citation Strategy to Your Business Model
cards.summary: B2B, commerce and marketplace queries pull from different citation sources and require different measurement approaches.
cards.use_when: Choosing which review sites, publications or platforms to target for a B2B, DTC or marketplace store.
steps: Identify the citation set for your model: Smith sees TechRadar appearing heavily for B2B questions; Glamour and Cosmopolitan for commerce; Eater, Yelp and TripAdvisor for marketplaces and local.
Build your target list from the actual citations the engines return for your questions, not from generic top-domain lists.
Measurement differs: many B2B answers have nothing clickable, so last-touch referral traffic undercounts impact — you need answer tracking plus a post-conversion 'how did you hear about us' question.
Commerce does have clickable shoppable cards, so last-touch referral traffic gives a reasonable read of conversions.
For commerce cards, rich snippet schema and the number of reviews matter for appearing in the carousel.
B2B purchase cycles involve roughly dozens of touch points — nobody commits to large software from one search.
caveats: The named publications are Smith's observations of what currently appears, not fixed rules; recheck current citations.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Set Up Answer Tracking as Share of Voice
cards.summary: Answers vary per run, per phrasing and per surface, so track distribution — how often you appear and your average rank — not a single result.
cards.use_when: Measuring ecommerce brand and product recommendations across a fixed buyer-question prompt set, with repeated samples and share-of-voice tracking.
steps: Understand the mechanics: asking the same question produces different answers each time — roughly a weighted random sample from a distribution.
Account for three variance sources: run-to-run variance, question-phrasing variance, and platform variance (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Meta).
Track share of voice: the percentage of time you appear, plus your average rank, across your tracked question set.
Ask each question multiple times and in multiple phrasings to estimate true frequency.
Tooling: answer trackers are essentially keyword trackers — many similar options exist; Smith's advice is to pick the cheapest one that meets your needs.
Prioritize surfaces by traffic rather than tracking all of them; Smith expects roughly three LLM surfaces to matter, not ten.
caveats: Recommendations to track all surfaces are impractical; Smith says you probably only need a few.
Surface popularity is unsettled — he compares it to not knowing in 1999 whether to bet only on AOL search.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Run Controlled AEO Experiments With a Holdout
cards.summary: A before/after read is unreliable because answers drift on their own, so split your question set into test and control groups.
cards.use_when: Designing an ecommerce AI-recommendation experiment: create a buyer-question prompt set, split test and control groups, and measure whether a content or community intervention changes brand visibility.
steps: Take a large question set — Smith's example uses 200 questions — and split it into test and control.
Leave the control group completely untouched.
Intervene on the test group with one channel at a time; consider bucketing several tactics separately (Reddit comments vs. a YouTube/Vimeo video vs. a paid Forbes placement).
Allow a couple of weeks before and after the intervention to compare movement against the control group.
Compare change in the test group with change in the control group, repeat measurements and assess noise before declaring a useful effect.
Reproducibility matters — Smith comes from an academic research background and warns that in SEO it is common to credit the wrong cause and then believe it forever.
Smith's framing: most best practices in SEO and AEO are unverified because people repeat claims nobody ever analyzed.
caveats: Requires enough tracked questions and time to detect a signal; small sets will be noisy.
Paid placements are controllable but expensive; Reddit is cheap but not guaranteed to stay live.
Match question groups on baseline behavior; edits to shared pages or brands may affect both groups, weakening the holdout.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Let AI Index You but Block Training Separately
cards.summary: Opting out of AI indexing forfeits the channel to competitors; you can refuse model training while still allowing retrieval.
cards.use_when: Making robots.txt and bot-access decisions for a store's catalog and content.
steps: Smith's position: it is not optional whether you participate — if you block indexing entirely, you simply cannot appear while competitors do.
Recognize that different bots have different purposes: training crawlers versus retrieval/index crawlers use different user agents.
Configure robots.txt so the training bot is disallowed and the index bot is allowed — Smith says this is the direct way to do it.
Alternatively use a tool or app that blocks training while permitting indexation; verify the current interface of whichever tool you choose.
Decide based on the trade-off: keeping content out of model training versus staying eligible for citation and referral traffic.
Ecommerce application: apply the same setting to catalog, help-center and buying-guide content rather than opting the whole domain out.
caveats: Bot user agents and controls change — verify current names and support before relying on a rule.
Blocking indexing forfeits visibility and is not recommended by the source as a strategy.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Measure whether AI-referred shoppers convert better in your store
cards.summary: Visitors arriving from an LLM conversation have already narrowed their intent through follow-up questions, so they convert at much higher rates.
cards.use_when: Justifying investment in AI-visibility work against other acquisition channels for an ecommerce or SaaS business.
steps: Note the reported gap: Webflow saw a 6x conversion-rate difference between LLM traffic and Google search traffic.
Smith's explanation: the user has built intent through a multi-turn conversation, so they arrive pre-qualified.
Note the scale context: Webflow gets about 8% of signups from LLMs — a substantial channel, but not the largest; paid is likely still number one.
Attribution warning: users often see your brand in an answer, then open a new tab and type your brand or domain directly — your analytics will mislabel that as branded search or direct traffic.
Suggested ecommerce application: compare purchase conversion, revenue per session and order quality across comparable periods, and add a post-purchase discovery question.
Still size the channel honestly: Smith says search remains larger than AEO today, even though AEO is growing.
caveats: Webflow's 6x and 8% figures are one company's results, not benchmarks you should assume.
Under-attribution is expected, so referral reports will understate the channel.
Webflow signups are a SaaS example, not ecommerce purchases; selection effects and small referral samples can explain large differences.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Tool Pricing Is Dislocated From the Work
cards.summary: Smith calls out AI-visibility tooling as unusually expensive for tasks that are essentially commodity keyword tracking.
cards.use_when: Evaluating what to pay for AEO tracking or content tooling for your store.
steps: Apply the sanity test Smith uses: imagine being charged $50,000 for keyword tracking — you would call it absurd because you could write it yourself.
The same commodity work is being sold at high prices in the AEO category because the mechanics feel mysterious and the growth curve looks steep.
Before signing, identify what the tool actually does and whether it is a renamed version of a known commodity task.
Default to the cheapest tool that meets your needs — there is no premium tier of ranking; you either appear or you do not.
Spend the saved budget on the citation work that actually moves visibility: content, video, affiliate placements and community participation.
Verify current pricing and capabilities directly, since the category is changing quickly.
caveats: This is Smith's market opinion; some tools may carry genuine costs (API calls at scale) that justify higher prices.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Google Search Is Not Dying — Reject the Cycle of Panic
cards.summary: New channels add on top of search rather than taking Google's share, so do not reallocate your whole budget on the strength of news headlines.
cards.use_when: Responding to internal pressure to defund organic or search spend because 'AI killed Google.'
steps: Recognize the recurring pattern Smith describes: every couple of years articles claim Google search is dying because of a new thing — previously TikTok search, before that Instagram, Facebook and YouTube.
The pattern is not that these channels are fake; people do search and discover on TikTok, YouTube and Instagram — but those channels add on top rather than subtract from Google.
Smith's framing: Google's slice of the pie stays the same, while the pie gets bigger.
Evidence he cites: Google's VP of search said publisher traffic from Google is not down and is up slightly.
For an ecommerce brand: keep the search channel funded, and add AEO as an additional channel rather than a replacement.
Treat claims that AI has destroyed search traffic as something to verify in your own analytics before acting.
caveats: Smith is an SEO-business owner and argues from within that industry; verify the traffic claims against your own data.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: LLM Mechanics: RAG vs. Model Training
cards.summary: Most controllable AEO work happens in the retrieval layer (search plus summarization), not in model weights.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to invest effort when trying to influence what an AI assistant says about your products.
steps: Understand the two layers: the core model, trained on large web corpora, performs next-word prediction (e.g. the capital of California).
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) performs a live search and then summarizes the results — this is the layer that produces citations.
Almost everything actionable in AEO lives in RAG; influencing the core model is extremely hard and may take a year or more to show.
Importantly, Smith expects a model will probably not name your product if it never appeared in any retrieved results — so RAG presence is the foundation.
Practical implication for a store: prioritize being present in the retrievable set (review sites, comparisons, video, communities, your own indexed pages) over trying to influence training data.
Skip the obscure tactic of mass-producing pages that assert a brand is best for a keyword; Smith says few would want to spend time on it.
caveats: RAG-versus-training behavior is Smith's working model of these systems and may not describe every product's architecture.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Treat AEO as an SEO extension, not a new channel
cards.summary: LLM answer optimization overlaps heavily with SEO; the difference is mostly citation optimization, with different head and tail dynamics.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to allocate content, technical SEO and optimization budget across classic search vs. ChatGPT/LLM answers for your product catalog or content.
steps: Recognize that the source argues SEO and AEO are not fundamentally different channels; the core technology is similar, so existing SEO infrastructure, crawlability and content quality work still apply.
Focus the incremental AEO effort on citation optimization: getting your pages selected as the source an LLM cites, rather than on a separate stack of tactics.
Account for the structural difference the source names: the head (broad, high-volume terms) and the tail (long, obscure queries) behave differently in LLM answers than in classic search rankings.
Be skeptical of vendors selling AEO as a wholly new channel with proprietary tools; the source attributes much of that framing to commercial incentive rather than technical difference.
Keep your classic SEO fundamentals running while adding citation-focused work, rather than replacing one with the other.
caveats: This is the presenter's assessment of overlap, not a measured equivalence; the head/tail divergence is described qualitatively.
AEO tooling and LLM interfaces change frequently — verify current behavior before committing budget.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Track the AEO growth curve shape, not just its size
cards.summary: The AEO channel's adoption curve had an unusual dead period followed by a very steep January inflection, driven by LLM adoption and clickable rich modules.
cards.use_when: Timing when to invest in LLM-answer optimization for your store versus waiting for the channel to mature.
steps: Note the source's observation that the channel's interest curve was atypical: an initial webinar spike, then a flat period from roughly July to January where growth people saw little impact, then a sharp jump in January.
Attribute the inflection to two factors: increased everyday LLM adoption and increased clickability of answers, especially for commerce, local and hotels where rich modules let users click through.
For ecommerce specifically, the source says commerce answers gained clickable rich modules, meaning a citation can now produce traffic rather than just visibility.
Use the steepness of the curve as a signal that the channel moved faster than a typical new channel, so earlier experimentation carries less risk of wasted effort than the flat period suggested.
Re-check current clickability for your category (product, local, travel) before assuming the same click-through behavior applies.
caveats: The timeline and attribution are the presenter's field observations, not a controlled measurement.
Clickability varies by query type and engine; do not assume commerce answers always render clickable modules.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Skip fully automated AI content; use AI-assisted, human-edited content
cards.summary: A large study found only ~10–12% of cited content in Google and ChatGPT is AI-generated while ~90% is not, indicating unassisted AI content does not win citations.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to mass-generate product descriptions, buying guides or category copy with AI for your store.
steps: Interpret 'AI-generated content' as automated content with no human in the loop; that is the specific thing the study tested and found ineffective.
The source's study pulled thousands of searches and questions, collected the Google results and ChatGPT citations, and ran an AI detector (Surfer SEO's) across them.

They validated the detector by generating thousands of AI articles and sampling 100,000 Common Crawl URLs from before ChatGPT launched, finding roughly an 8% false positive rate — supporting detector accuracy.
Result: about 10–12% of content ranking or cited was AI-generated, roughly 90% was not, and a correlation analysis showed the same pattern.

Apply this by treating AI as a drafting and editing aid: use it to accelerate research, outlines and first drafts, then have a human edit for accuracy, specificity and usefulness before publishing product or guide content.
Do not publish bulk unedited AI product copy or landing pages expecting it to rank or get cited.
caveats: The study measured correlation between AI-detected content and ranking/citation, not causation.
AI detectors are imperfect; the source reports an ~8% false positive rate, so some flagged content may be human-written.
This is one firm's study; results may shift as engines and detectors change — re-verify before basing a full content strategy on it.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Expect AI-generated content to collapse citation diversity (model collapse risk)
cards.summary: If purely AI-generated content dominated, the source argues it would degrade into a self-summarizing loop and converge answers to a single opinion, like 'vanilla is the only flavor'.
cards.use_when: Evaluating the long-term risk of an AI-content-heavy content strategy for your store's category pages and buying guides.
steps: Understand the two places derivatives enter a system: the core model training and the retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) layer that supplies citations.
A published paper on 'model collapse' showed that training a core model on its own derivatives quickly breaks it — producing hallucinations and failures.
The source ran a RAG-side study: generate 10 derivative articles, put them into rankings, summarize, then generate 10 more and summarize the summaries in an infinite loop.
The result: answers converge on a single opinion. The wisdom-of-the-crowd effect (averaging many diverse opinions beats the best single individual) shrinks to one answer.

The analogous incentive argument: if scraped or generated content worked, everyone would do it, and engines would eventually have to suppress derivatives — as Google did to shopping comparison sites in 2007.

For an ecommerce operator, the practical takeaway is to keep original, first-hand content (real product testing, real customer questions, real usage photos/data) that cannot be produced by re-summarizing others.
caveats: This is a reasoned scenario the source describes, supported by a model-collapse paper and an internal RAG study, not a prediction with a date.
The 'vanilla' ice cream example is an illustration, not a measured outcome.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Optimize the help center as an AEO asset
cards.summary: Help center content frequently answers the 'can you do X / do you support Y' follow-up questions people ask LLMs, making it an underused AEO surface.
cards.use_when: Auditing your store's support and FAQ content to capture LLM-answer citations for feature, integration and use-case questions.
steps: Recognize that in chat, users ask follow-up questions about tools, features, use cases and integrations — questions typically answered in a help center, not a marketing page.
Move the help center from a subdomain to a subdirectory; the source says subdomains do not work well for this and subdirectories perform better.
Fix internal linking: help center pages are usually poorly internally linked. Add cross-links between related help center pages so the cluster is crawlable and connected.
Fill in the tail: you likely have help center articles for head terms but none for narrow, obscure use cases. Use sales call questions and customer support tickets to find those tails.

Example the source gives: no meeting-transcription tool integrates directly with Looker, but a workaround via Otter's Zapier integration into BigQuery could be documented — a non-zero-demand question with no existing article.
Open a community Q&A so users can surface tail questions you would never have anticipated, and answer them on your own site.
Note that common helpdesk tools (Zendesk, Intercom, etc.) should support these two changes; verify current subdirectory and internal-linking capabilities in your tool.
caveats: The subdirectory-vs-subdomain recommendation is the presenter's stated observation, not a published benchmark.
Tail questions may have very low volume; the value is being the only citation, not high traffic.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Mine sales calls and support tickets for tail questions to answer
cards.summary: Tail questions are asked in chat and sales contexts but rarely covered; sourcing them from calls and support lets you become the sole citation.
cards.use_when: Building FAQ, help center or comparison content that answers low-volume but high-intent questions about your store's products or integrations.
steps: Collect questions that appear in sales calls and support interactions — these reveal the real use cases buyers ask about.

Identify questions where no competitor has published anything, such as the source's example of needing a meeting-transcription tool that integrates with Looker (solved via Otter plus Zapier plus BigQuery).
Write a plain, useful answer for each such question even if search volume looks near zero, because being the only source lets you win the citation.
Pair this with an open community Q&A where users can ask anything, so the tail keeps expanding without you having to guess all the questions in advance.
Cross-link these answers into your existing help center cluster so they are discoverable and connected.
caveats: Tail content is a long-tail bet; expect low individual traffic and value the citation position rather than volume.
The Looker example is illustrative of method, not a template solution for every integration question.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Apply persuasion and behavioral-economics frameworks to growth tests
cards.summary: The source recommends drawing on psychology research — persuasion, emotional intelligence, dual-process thinking — as the basis for growth hypotheses instead of guessing.
cards.use_when: Designing A/B tests for product pages, offers, pricing, checkout or signup flows where you need a reason to believe a variant will outperform.
steps: Use frameworks from persuasion psychology (the source names Cialdini) to generate hypotheses about why a visitor would sign up or buy — scarcity, social proof, consistency, reciprocity, authority, liking.
Use emotional-intelligence research to understand how people feel when making a purchase decision, informing tone, reassurance and objection handling on product and checkout pages.
Apply dual-process thinking (fast vs. slow thinking) when designing pages: decide whether the buyer is in fast, intuitive mode or slow, deliberative mode and design accordingly.
Turn each framework into a testable hypothesis rather than treating it as a universal rule, and test it on your own store.
Read the source material behind these frameworks rather than only the popular summaries, since the source emphasizes that the frameworks are grounded in actual psychology research.
caveats: These are the source's reading recommendations and reasoning; no ecommerce conversion benchmarks are provided.
Persuasion tactics can backfire if applied manipulatively or without testing on your specific audience.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Measure things that seem unmeasurable by finding proxies
cards.summary: The source recommends 'How to Measure Anything', which shows how to measure indirect concepts through observable proxies — like judging a conductor by standing ovations.
cards.use_when: Setting measurement for AEO, brand, content quality or other store outcomes where you lack a direct metric.
steps: Identify the concept you want to measure that lacks a clean metric (e.g., AEO impact, content usefulness, brand strength).
Find an observable proxy that correlates with it — the source's example: instead of surveying audiences, count standing ovations to judge an orchestra conductor.
Use the proxy consistently over time so you can detect direction of change, even if the absolute number is imperfect.
For an ecommerce AEO application, proxies could include citation appearances in LLM answers, click-throughs from answer modules, or branded search lift — measure whichever is observable to you.
Treat the proxy as a decision aid, not a precise measurement, and keep watching for a better proxy.
caveats: Proxies can be misleading if the correlation is weak; validate the proxy before relying on it for major decisions.
This is the source's reading recommendation, applied here by analogy to ecommerce AEO; the source did not give an ecommerce measurement example.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Recognize LLM and search are converging into one experience
cards.summary: The source predicts search and LLMs will merge — Google adding AI overviews, LLMs adding maps and shopping carousels — into a single experience.
cards.use_when: Setting content and channel strategy for your store on a multi-year horizon rather than optimizing separately for classic search and LLMs.
steps: Observe the convergence in both directions: Google Search is adding LLM AI overviews, and LLMs are adding maps and shopping carousels.
Plan for a single optimized experience rather than two separate playbooks, since the surfaces are merging.

Identify the perverse incentives in this merged world (such as AI-generated content and scraping) and avoid building a strategy that depends on them, the way the source advises thinking about what a bad actor would do.
Invest in the things LLMs can be uniquely good at — memory of your past interactions, personalization, and eventually autonomous agents that make decisions without intervention.
For ecommerce, this points toward making product and feature data structured and answerable so it can be surfaced and acted on inside a converged assistant experience.
caveats: This is the source's forecast, not a measured fact; timing and exact form are uncertain.
Autonomous-agent commerce is presented as something that will eventually come, not something available for planning concrete campaigns today.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Prepare product data for autonomous-agent purchasing
cards.summary: The source describes a future where LLMs, with full context on your preferences and reasoning, make purchase decisions without user intervention — like an executive assistant booking a trip.
cards.use_when: Planning accurate machine-readable product facts for a future or currently supported shopping integration.
steps: Understand the source's model: an assistant that deeply understands the buyer's preferences (ocean view, restaurant with music in the example), remembers everything, has context and reasoning, then makes decisions without intervention.
Anticipate that in this scenario the assistant, not the shopper, compares your product — so machine-readable attributes, availability, pricing and compatibility matter more than persuasion copy.
Make sure your product data clearly answers 'does this fit the use case' questions in structured, unambiguous form.
Ensure integration and compatibility facts (does it work with X) are documented, since assistant-driven decisions hinge on fit rather than brand persuasion.
Keep this as a forward-looking bet and continue optimizing current surfaces; the source presents autonomous agents as eventual, not immediate.
caveats: The transcript is forward-looking; verify current channel support and merchant requirements before implementing any transaction integration.
No ecommerce data point or benchmark is given for agent-driven purchasing.
cards.source_name: The ultimate guide to AEO_ How to get ChatGPT to recommend your product _ Ethan Smith.docx

cards.title: Adapt Search Analytics for Zero-Click and AI-Surfaced Demand
cards.summary: Shift ecommerce search measurement from SERP rank and click-through volume to zero-click behavior, brand mentions and citations inside AI answers.
cards.use_when: When reviewing your store's organic search reporting and deciding what to track now that AI Overviews and assistants answer questions directly, so you know whether non-clicking discovery is growing.
steps: Recognize the baseline problem: the source cites that 60% of Google searches now end without a click, and surfaces many product and how-to questions are answered inside AI Overviews, Perplexity and ChatGPT rather than on a results page. Treat click-through-only dashboards as a partial view.
Keep your existing SEO analytics (rank tracking, organic sessions, keyword performance, technical site health, backlink profile) as one layer, because GEO complements SEO rather than replacing it.

Add an exposure layer: manually or via tooling, record where your brand, product names or URLs are mentioned or cited inside AI-generated answers for the queries that matter to your catalogue (category queries, 'best X for Y', comparison and spec questions).

Track indirect traffic signs: branded search volume, direct traffic lifts, and mentions in AI answers that later correlate with sessions or conversions, rather than expecting a click on every impression.
Track competitor appearances in the same AI answers so you can see which sources the engines prefer for your category.
Report both layers side by side in a recurring review so you can attribute growth in visibility without over-crediting clicks.
caveats: The 60% zero-click figure comes from the source and is a cited heuristic, not a measurement you can verify from your own analytics.
Indirect, exposure-driven traffic is hard to attribute causally; do not present correlation as proven incremental revenue.
AI platform interfaces and answer formats change often, so verify current tooling before building a fixed report.
