steps: Treat the sample as a demonstration of what is possible, not a guarantee of what bulk will be: the source's seller loved his sample, then received bulk units of inconsistent quality because he did not verify the run.
Hire an independent quality-control agent to inspect the bulk goods before they ship — the source states you can hire someone in China for around $100 to check product quality.
Budget QC as a standard line item on every production run, especially after any change of manufacturer.

Track return rate and review sentiment as your measurement of QC: in the source case, bad quality produced returns and bad reviews, and the presenter frames reviews as currency on Amazon — poor reviews suppress the listing's ability to convert and rank.
caveats: The ~$100 inspection price is the presenter's stated figure and will vary by supplier, city and inspection scope.
No QC method removes all defect risk; inspection reduces, not eliminates, the chance of a bad batch.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Title and bullet keyword construction for Amazon search
cards.summary: How to research search phrases and build an Amazon title where the exact primary search phrase appears first.
cards.use_when: Writing or rewriting an Amazon product title, bullet points and description for a new or underperforming listing.
steps: Identify the exact phrase a buyer would type to find your specific product and put it as the first words of the title. In the source example, the assistant initially wrote "berberine supreme herbal tea", and the presenter changed it to "berberine tea" first because ~1,200 people per month search that exact phrase and no product on Amazon matched it.
Use a keyword tool such as Helium 10 (Magnet or Cerebro) to get real search volumes and related phrases; verify the current tool interface and free/paid feature split before relying on it.

Filter the tool's suggestions into three buckets: (a) exact-match core phrases you must rank for, (b) specific supporting phrases that describe real attributes of your product (e.g. immune support, glucose, antioxidant, caffeine-free, organic), and (c) generic terms (health, wellness, energy, cardiovascular, metabolism) that are too broad to rank for and waste title space.

Mine competitor listings for phrases you may have missed — the source found "glucose support", "high strength" and "HCL" by reading berberine supplement listings, even though those products are not tea.
Put the primary phrase in the title, repeat supporting keywords naturally in the bullets and description, and understand that Amazon treats your listing text as the only way it knows what you sell.
Remember the click decision is made from title, main image, price and review count — so the title must both contain the keyword and be readable enough to earn the click.
caveats: Generic high-volume terms were rejected by the presenter because a small new listing cannot rank for them; this is his judgment, not a rule.
Keyword volumes and tool pricing change — re-verify data before committing to title terms.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Amazon listing setup mechanics: existing listing vs. new listing
cards.summary: Step-by-step path through Seller Central for adding a product to an existing ASIN versus creating a brand-new listing.
cards.use_when: Setting up a new product in Amazon Seller Central, or choosing between piggybacking on an existing ASIN and building your own.
steps: Register at sell.amazon.com, then log into Seller Central; open the menu, go to Catalog, then Add Products (verify the current menu labels, which change).

If the product already exists on Amazon, search by name or product ID (UPC/EAN/ISBN/ASIN), pick the matching listing, select condition, click Sell this product, then enter an optional SKU, quantity, price and fulfillment channel.

If the product does not exist on Amazon, choose the blank-form/start-new-listing option and fill in item name (title), product type/category, item type keyword, variation status, brand name and external product ID.

Choose a category by looking at where similar products are actually listed — scroll to the bottom of a competitor's detail page to see their category, then match it. The presenter also mentions the advanced tactic of listing in a slightly-off subcategory where you can become the number one product, but treats it as advanced rather than default.
Decide variations up front: if you sell one flavor, size or color, answer No; if you will sell multiple flavors or sizes, answer Yes and structure them as variations.

Sourcing details to have ready: a legitimate GS1 barcode (gs1.org; the presenter notes a single barcode is about $30 versus the older ~$250 ten-pack), your brand name, and a trademark case number if you intend to use Brand Registry.
caveats: Menu paths, field names and the private-seller/condition options in Seller Central change over time — verify the current interface.
The source says to avoid unofficial barcode resellers because cheap codes can cause problems later; this is his recommendation.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Compare FBA and merchant fulfillment for the actual product
cards.summary: Evaluate delivery eligibility, total costs and operational capacity rather than assuming FBA guarantees higher sales.
cards.use_when: Deciding the fulfillment channel for a new Amazon listing, or comparing the cost of FBA fees against the sales benefit of Prime eligibility.
steps: Compare current FBA fees, storage and inbound costs with the merchant's own shipping and service costs.
Assess delivery promises, stock availability, returns and operating capacity for the product.
FBA can provide Prime eligibility; qualifying merchants may also use Seller Fulfilled Prime where available.
Test conversion and contribution where practical rather than assuming a fixed sales multiplier or direct ranking boost.
Choose FBA, merchant fulfillment or a mix using actual economics and service requirements.
caveats: Source sales uplifts are individual cases; check current program requirements in the selling marketplace.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Using Amazon ads and promo-clear listings to relaunch a stalled product
cards.summary: How the case-study seller used PPC, A+ content and a competitor's removal to jump from a stockout toward a record month.
cards.use_when: Planning a relaunch or ranking push after a stockout, or deciding how much ad spend to reinvest into an existing Amazon listing.
steps: Reinvest profit into PPC (pay-per-click) rather than treating ad spend as pure cost: the source seller spent roughly $2,000–$3,000 on PPC in the month he grew revenue from a depleted position to about $23,000.
Improve conversion assets at the same time as buying traffic — the seller also invested in A+ content on the listing in that same month, so traffic and conversion were worked together.

Watch the competitive set for structural openings: the seller's main competitor's listing was taken down, and he took advantage of the freed demand. The source does not explain why the competitor was removed and no cause should be assumed.
Expect the ad spike to interact with inventory: that $23,000 month was followed by a stockout-driven fall to $9,000 and then ~$3,000, so a relaunch push only pays if supply supports it.
caveats: The source does not attribute the $23,000 month solely to PPC — a competitor's removal was a co-factor.
Ad budgets, campaign types and A+ eligibility rules on Amazon change; verify current requirements.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Launch speed and review momentum as copycat defense
cards.summary: Why a fast, review-generating launch is presented as protection against manufacturers copying your product.
cards.use_when: Planning the launch timeline and early review-generation push for a new private-label product, or deciding whether to delay a launch.
steps: Treat speed as a defense: the source describes a student pair whose product was copied by manufacturers a few months after a quiet launch, and says a big launch with a strong review base would have made the copy less damaging because they would have been far ahead.
Execute a large social media and launch push at launch rather than trickling in, so the listing accumulates reviews and ranking early.
Use the accumulated review advantage as the barrier — on Amazon, the source frames reviews as currency and early momentum as the thing a later copycat cannot easily match.
Pair this with formal protection (trademark/brand registry) rather than relying on launch speed alone.
caveats: This is the presenter's interpretation of what would have happened in one student's case; no measured comparison is provided.
Amazon's review-solicitation rules restrict how reviews can be requested — launch tactics must comply with current policy.
Launch velocity is a source hypothesis, not a guaranteed ranking mechanism. Use genuine demand; do not arrange reimbursed purchases, incentivized reviews or search-rank manipulation.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Prepare an entity-structure brief for the ecommerce business
cards.summary: Gather the operational facts needed to select a suitable entity and tax setup rather than copying a course example.
cards.use_when: Forming the legal entity for a new Amazon or ecommerce store, or deciding whether a new product line needs its own entity.
steps: List ownership, operating jurisdictions, planned products, liability exposure and banking needs.
Clarify whether a proposed name registration, entity formation or tax election serves the actual requirement.
Compare setup and ongoing administration using current qualified advice.
Confirm eligibility and required filings before selecting a tax treatment; do not assume an S-corporation election is a generic formation checkbox.
Keep store accounts, contracts and financial records consistent with the chosen structure.
caveats: The source's US entity preference and historical fees do not apply universally.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: EIN, seller's permit and separating business banking
cards.summary: The free federal and state registrations an online seller needs, plus why commingling business and personal money is risky.
cards.use_when: Setting up back-office paperwork before launching an Amazon store, or fixing banking hygiene after mixing personal and business spending.
steps: Get an EIN directly from irs.gov: the source says it is free, takes roughly 10–15 minutes, and returns a PDF — do not pay third parties for this.

Get a seller's permit from your state, found by searching your state name plus "seller's permit" and using the official .gov site. The presenter says it is free and that anyone charging for it is running a scam.
Use the seller's permit for two things it enables: buying goods tax-free for resale (ingredients and packaging in the source's example), and filing state sales tax.

Understand the sales-tax scope the presenter describes: for online sales you collect state sales tax only from buyers in the state where you or the business resides, and larger businesses with physical locations collect in each of those states. He explicitly notes he is not a lawyer and the reality is more complicated.
Open a business bank account with the entity, EIN and permit paperwork; the presenter does this online now rather than in branch, and mentions Payoneer or WorldFirst for sellers outside the US.

Keep personal and business spending strictly separate: the presenter says commingling is an IRS red flag, can let a litigant pierce the LLC and reach personal assets, and makes it impossible to see your true profit.
caveats: The tax-scope explanation is the presenter's non-lawyer understanding; consult a professional for nexus and sales-tax obligations, especially as you add states or marketplaces.
Fee statements and agency options reflect the source's date and location.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Keep Amazon launch expenses traceable and separate from personal spending
cards.summary: Record inventory, freight, advertising and software spend consistently during a launch.
cards.use_when: Choosing how to pay for a product business's build-out costs (inventory, ads, samples, tooling) to maximize rewards.
steps: Use the business's appropriate payment account and retain invoices for each launch expense.
Classify inventory, freight, ad spend, software and other costs so the launch budget can be reconciled.
Match transactions to invoices and supplier deposits rather than treating the card balance as the expense total.
Plan payment dates in the cash forecast; rewards do not offset an unaffordable borrowing cost.
caveats: The source's card offers and travel-redemption examples are excluded as time-sensitive personal-finance tangents.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Map the product and brand assets that need IP review
cards.summary: Identify brand identifiers, appearance and technical features before deciding what protection to investigate.
cards.use_when: Deciding what intellectual property to file before applying for Amazon Brand Registry, or protecting a product design from copycats.
steps: Inventory the brand name and logo, distinctive product appearance and any technical innovation.
Record who developed each asset and what rights the manufacturing and design agreements provide.
Seek appropriate advice about protection options and timing in the markets where the brand operates.
Check Amazon enrollment requirements separately; Brand Registry is not a substitute for broader IP assessment.
Use current filing requirements and quotes, not historical patent or trademark prices from the course.
caveats: No filing guarantees registration, enforceability or exclusion of every competing product.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Choosing an Amazon category and item type for your listing
cards.summary: How to pick the category and item-type keyword that determines where your product can rank.
cards.use_when: Filling in the category and item type fields while creating a new Amazon listing, or reconsidering the category of an existing listing.
steps: Let Amazon's auto-suggestion start you off, then override it if it is not specific enough: in the source, Amazon auto-selected "herbal supplement" for a tea, and the presenter changed it to the herbal tea subcategory he judged the best fit.
Validate your choice against competitors: open similar products on Amazon, scroll to the bottom of the detail page, see which category they are listed in, and match it.

Consider the advanced tactic the presenter mentions: listing in a subcategory that is not a perfect match when you believe you can become the number one product there. He flags this as an advanced decision, not a default.
Set the item type keyword that Amazon derives from the category chain, and confirm the variation setting — one flavor or size means No variations; multiple flavors, sizes or colors means Yes.

Recognize the stakes: the presenter states the number one search result takes most sales, with second through fourth well behind, and that a product off page one gets essentially no sales — so category and keyword placement decide whether you can appear at all.
caveats: Category best-fit and ranking effects vary by product and change with Amazon's browse node structure.
Category-drift tactics can restrict certain features or invite a category correction by Amazon; the source does not cover those enforcement risks.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Reading keyword lists critically: choose specific buyer language over generic buzzwords
cards.summary: A filtering method for turning a raw keyword list into title and bullet terms that can actually rank.
cards.use_when: Editing a keyword list before writing Amazon title, bullets or description copy.
steps: Take the raw export from your keyword tool and mark each term against three questions: does it describe my exact product, is it specific enough that a small listing could rank, and is it something a buyer with purchase intent would type?

Reject broad terms per the source's example: metabolism, energy, cardiovascular, cholesterol, health, wellness and detox were set aside as too generic to rank for; herbal tea was judged good but very competitive, so a more specific variant is preferable.

Keep terms that are both searched and true of the product — in the source, immune support (~9,700 searches/month claimed), antioxidant, organic, caffeine-free, glucose/glucose support, and the product's own name.

Add terms your product actually supports even if you may not rank for them, because they still help buyers recognize the product's fit — the presenter kept "caffeine free" in the title knowing he would not rank first for it.
Combine the surviving phrases into a readable title with the primary exact phrase first, then carry the rest into bullet points and the description.
Do the same filtering on competitor listings: extract the phrases they emphasize ("high strength", "HCL", "glucose support") and check whether each applies to your product before borrowing it.
caveats: Search volumes and which terms are 'too generic' are the presenter's judgments and shift by niche and time.
Borrowing competitor keywords does not mean copying their claims — only apply terms that are accurate for your product.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Bullet points: lead with product name + benefits, not features
cards.summary: Structure Amazon bullet points so the primary keyword appears first and each bullet translates a feature into a concrete customer outcome.
cards.use_when: Writing or rewriting the five bullet points on an Amazon listing (PDP copy) for a consumable or any private-label product.
steps: Make the exact primary keyword (e.g. 'Berberine Tea') the first two words of bullet one so Amazon reinforces what the product is.
Put the strongest quantified/emotional hook early — the source likes a number like '100% natural and organic' because specifics feel credible.

Convert every feature into the benefit the buyer actually experiences. Instead of 'supports healthy blood sugar levels,' describe outcomes like steady energy, easier weight maintenance, or eating sweets without a blood-sugar spike.
Note the trade-off: 'blood sugar support' can still be a valid keyword because many shoppers search it, so keep searchable phrasing where demand exists even if the literal benefit is more abstract.
Drop generic phrases no one searches (e.g. 'antioxidant-rich blend') and replace them with keywords people actually type.
Add sourcing specifics only if verifiable (e.g. 'sourced from the Himalayas') — verify before claiming.
Make the final bullet a 100% money-back guarantee. The source notes every Amazon product already carries this, but stating it explicitly reassures buyers.
Enter each bullet one at a time via 'add more' in Seller Central; the source's formula is copyable but keywords should be tailored to your product.
caveats: The bullet formula is the presenter's opinion, not a platform rule.
Keyword choice should follow actual search demand for your niche, verified with a keyword tool.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Make the main image differentiate on the search results grid
cards.summary: Winning the click depends on packaging and main-image choices that stand out against competitors' thumbnails on Amazon search.
cards.use_when: Designing product packaging and the main listing image before launch so the product is clickable in search results.
steps: Search your main keyword and screenshot the results grid to study what competitors' thumbnails look like (common palettes: whites, pale pinks, yellows).
Choose packaging colours that contrast with Amazon's white background — the source cites black packaging with red lettering for a high-caffeine tea to pop against boring competitor images.
Print the exact search term in large letters on the front of the packaging (e.g. 'High Caffeine Tea' / 'Berberine Tea') so shoppers instantly recognize a match.
Use a clean main image showing just the front of the packaging, and upload it via the listing's upload button.
Treat the main image as the highest-leverage listing asset: the source argues a weak image can kill a product before launch.
Verify current Amazon main-image requirements (pure white background, no text overlays on the photo itself) since the packaging text is printed, not overlaid.
caveats: The presenter's claim that the standout image is also the bestseller is an observation of one niche, not proof of causation.
Amazon main-image rules change; confirm current requirements in Seller Central.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Use all eight side images to sell what buyers can't touch
cards.summary: Supplementary images substitute for the physical product experience and should include a comparison chart against competitors.
cards.use_when: Building the image gallery and A+ assets for an Amazon product page before or after launch.
steps: Upload as many of the eight available side images as possible — buyers can't hold the product, so images do the selling.
Include at least one graph or comparison chart showing how your product beats competitors.
Show lifestyle/usage, dimensions, ingredients or specs, and any guarantee details across the gallery.
Avoid low-quality photos: the source cites a seller (Mina) whose poor launch images cost over $10,000 in lost potential customers — treat as an illustrative example, not a benchmark.
Consider supplementing the gallery with A+ content (richer modules Amazon may suggest under Growth), since the source reports Amazon flagging potential sales lift from improved A+ content.
caveats: A+ content requires Brand Registry and may not be available to every seller.
The $10,000 figure is a single anecdote.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Fill product details thoroughly and consistently
cards.summary: Completing Amazon's product-detail attributes accurately (manufacturer, unit count, ingredients, expiration) prevents listing errors and improves discoverability.
cards.use_when: Creating a new Amazon listing and filling out the product-details section for a consumable or physical good.
steps: Manufacturer: you can enter your brand name or yourself even if a different factory makes the product.
Number of items = identical units per sale (one 30-teabag pouch = 1), not the count of tea bags inside.
Special ingredients: add distinctive actives (e.g. 'berberine') even if they're not in Amazon's dropdown.
Heat sensitivity and temperature rating: set for your product (frozen/chocolate goods are heat sensitive; tea is ambient room temperature).
Ingredients/caffeine/form factor/unit form: describe accurately (form factor = physical size/shape; unit form = teabags).
Unit count: enter how Amazon should measure value (e.g. 30 tea bags, or ounces for liquids) — this feeds value comparisons.

Expireable: yes for consumables (legally requires a date), no for shelf-stable paper/cardboard goods like the source's 'cocktail cards'. Set shelf life in days (365 for ~1 year; the source's tea may run 700+).
SKU is an internal code only you see — use something descriptive like 'berberine-tea-30count' rather than a bare name.
Quantity and condition matter mainly for FBM/used goods; new FBA sellers set condition = new.
caveats: Amazon's prompted questions vary by product category and change over time — verify the current fields.
The source notes its own first SKU choice was suboptimal, so pick descriptive SKUs from the start.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Price at 3x cost and position premium, not cheapest
cards.summary: The source recommends a minimum 3x markup over unit cost and pricing above competitors to signal quality and protect margin.
cards.use_when: Setting the launch price for a private-label Amazon product after calculating FBA fees.
steps: Use a floor of 3x your per-unit manufacturing cost (a $10 unit cost → list at $30 minimum) because Amazon fees typically consume about a third of the sale price.
Note the fee share isn't always a third: for a light $100 item it may be closer to 20–25%, so recalculate for your size/weight.
Factor in the 15% referral fee plus FBA pick-and-pack when checking margin.
Look at comparable products' price points and consider pricing slightly above competitors rather than undercutting — the source argues many shoppers want the best product, not the cheapest.
Position as a premium 'passion product' where the category supports it; the source set $28.99 for the example tea.
Set list price separately as the reference/retail price.
caveats: This is the presenter's stated preference, not a rule; price-sensitive categories and commodity products may behave differently.
Some buyers always chase the lowest price, so premium pricing depends on category and differentiation.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Use hidden listing attributes and a future offer start date for launch
cards.summary: Filling all attributes and setting a future offer start date lets you control launch timing and capture back-end discoverability fields.
cards.use_when: Finishing a new Amazon listing before hitting 'save and finish' and planning the launch day.
steps: Click 'all attributes' to reveal hidden fields most new sellers miss; fill the ones relevant to your product for extra discoverability.
Set the offer start date to a specific future day so the listing doesn't go live the moment it's approved.
Coordinate a truthful launch announcement to interested customers once stock and the listing are ready; do not organize purchases to manipulate rank or reviews.
Measure actual conversion and contribution; launch sales do not guarantee an organic ranking increase.
Complete back-end keyword fields — the source calls this section 'gold' because it tells Amazon which searches to show you for.
caveats: The velocity-to-ranking 'snowball' is the presenter's model, not a guaranteed algorithm behaviour.
Requesting incentivized/friend purchases may conflict with Amazon's review and manipulation policies — check current rules before acting.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Read Seller Central's home and inventory signals for restock timing
cards.summary: Daily Seller Central metrics (restock days-left, recommended quantity, buy box, open orders) drive replenishment decisions.
cards.use_when: Managing day-to-day operations and deciding when to reorder and ship replenishment inventory.
steps: Check the Restock Inventory widget for days of supply remaining and Amazon's recommended send quantity; the source treats very low days-left as urgent.
Confirm your Buy Box win rate hovers near 100% for a unique private-label product (dips are an advanced issue).
Monitor open orders, today's sales, and buyer messages; unanswered buyer messages can cost you points, so respond promptly.
Under Manage FBA Inventory, distinguish available vs inbound vs unfulfillable (damaged) vs reserved units. 'Reserved' typically means sold-but-not-yet-shipped or being transferred between warehouses.
Use this to trigger replenishment before stockouts, since the source warns running out is a common costly mistake.
caveats: Widget layout and field names in Seller Central change — verify the current interface.
Buy Box dynamics apply mainly to shared listings; unique private-label products rarely lose it.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Diagnose performance with Business Reports: sales, page views, conversion
cards.summary: Use Business Reports (sales & traffic) to separate traffic changes from conversion changes over time.
cards.use_when: Reviewing weekly or monthly store performance to decide whether to work on traffic or on conversion.
steps: Open Business Reports → Sales and Traffic; view by week or month for stable trends rather than noisy daily numbers.
Track total sales alongside total page views: the source's example saw page views roughly double (≈2,000 → ≈4,000 in a week) while conversion dipped slightly.
Read Unit Session Percentage as your listing conversion rate — the share of visitors who purchase.
Compare current month to last month and to same month last year (the report plots prior periods as overlays).
When traffic rises but conversion falls and total sales still grow, you may have a traffic win with a conversion nuance to investigate rather than a failure.
Use the findings to decide where to intervene: creative/ads for traffic, PDP/price/reviews for conversion.
caveats: Convert conversion metrics only for purchase conversion — this is listing conversion, not close rate or lead conversion.
Report periods and metric names change; verify current Seller Central labels.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Protect account health and address negative reviews
cards.summary: Monitor account-health issues separately from product reviews and resolve customer problems through permitted channels.
cards.use_when: Routine account maintenance and when a negative review or defect claim appears.
steps: Review current Account Health metrics, notices and required actions.
Investigate seller feedback, claims and chargebacks using the order evidence.
Use permitted support tools to resolve legitimate customer issues; do not seek reviewer identity outside approved tools or ask for a review change.
Treat product reviews as product-feedback data, not as interchangeable with seller feedback or account-health metrics.
Correct recurring listing, fulfillment or product problems and document the response.
caveats: Use current marketplace thresholds and communication rules.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Activate Brand Referral Bonus to offset fees on off-Amazon traffic
cards.summary: Brand Registry sellers earn back roughly 10% of sales driven from external traffic to their Amazon listing.
cards.use_when: Running off-Amazon ads, influencer posts, or email campaigns that send buyers to your Amazon listing.
steps: Enroll in Brand Referral Bonus under the Brands dashboard (requires Brand Registry).
Point off-Amazon traffic to your Amazon listing using the tracked links so Amazon attributes the sale.
Treat the bonus as partial fee offset: the source cites an average ≈10% back, e.g. $5 on a $50 item, which helps cover FBA fees.
Cross-check against your ad spend — the bonus alone is small, so use it to improve ROI on external campaigns, not as a standalone profit source.
caveats: Requires Brand Registry and enrollment; bonus rates and terms can change — verify current programme details.
Only qualifying externally-referred sales count.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Create a case-pack template with correct box dimensions and weight
cards.summary: Before shipping to FBA, define a reusable case-pack template meeting Amazon's size/weight limits.
cards.use_when: Preparing the first FBA shipment or changing how you pack units into cases.
steps: From Manage Inventory, use 'Send/Replenish Inventory' on the product; if the option is missing, switch the item from FBM to FBA first.
Create a new case-pack template — a case is a container holding multiple units (e.g. ~40–45 tubs per box).
Ensure no side of the case exceeds 25 inches and the packed case weighs no more than 50 lbs (the source's box was 11x18x10 in at 37.35 lbs; the 45-unit example was 37.35 lbs).
Enter units per box and box dimensions; set prep category if your product needs special prep (adult, baby, fragile glass, liquids).
Save the template so repeat shipments reuse the same dimensions and unit count.
If you need boxes, buy locally or from a discounter like Uline.
caveats: Amazon's size/weight limits and prep requirements can change — verify current FBA shipping requirements.
Entering wrong dimensions causes fees and shipment problems.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Label units with FNSKU yourself or via manufacturer, not Amazon
cards.summary: Apply FNSKU labels before shipping; having Amazon label costs about $0.50/unit and is avoidable.
cards.use_when: Preparing units for an FBA shipment, especially private-label or wholesale/arbitrage products.
steps: Understand the difference: a UPC identifies the product for retail scanning, while an FNSKU identifies *your* specific inventory so Amazon can track which units are yours.
For private-label products, print the FNSKU directly on the packaging at the manufacturer — this avoids sticker costs and labor.
For retail arbitrage/wholesale, print FNSKU labels (via Seller Central 'print FNSKU labels') and stick them over the UPC barcode.
Buy sticker paper or ask your manufacturer to print and apply the labels for a small fee.
Avoid Amazon's labelling service (about $0.50/unit) whenever possible.
caveats: Regulations and label requirements vary by product/category — verify current Amazon FBA labelling rules.
Mislabeling causes receiving delays and lost inventory.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Choose small parcel vs less-than-truckload by shipment size
cards.summary: Match the FBA shipping method to volume — small parcel for boxes, LTL/pallet for large shipments — to cut freight cost.
cards.use_when: Selecting a shipping method and carrier when creating an FBA shipment.
steps: For small volumes, choose small parcel delivery and ship via UPS, either dropping off or scheduling a pickup (the source shipped 9 cases, 336 lbs, for about $266).
For large volumes, switch to less-than-truckload and send full pallets — the source says this can roughly halve shipping cost versus repeated small-parcel sends.
If using LTL, confirm your manufacturer will accept a truck, can palletize, and wrap the load properly; you can also schedule a liftgate pickup from your home.
Use Amazon's discounted UPS rates where possible; choosing another carrier (DHL, FedEx, USPS) usually costs more.
Choose the correct marketplace destination and set the fulfillment capability appropriately (standard FBA vs multi-channel/blank-box if you also ship for your own website).
caveats: LTL requires a local trucking company, not UPS, and different paperwork (BOL).
Rates, pickup rules, and interfaces change — verify current options in Seller Central.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Double-check box labels: weight, dimensions, and addresses
cards.summary: Errors on shipment labels cause lost inventory, fees, and carrier surcharges — verify before dispatch.
cards.use_when: After generating FBA box labels and before handing packages to the carrier.
steps: Attach both labels to each box: the UPS/carrier label (for tracking) and the Amazon FBA box-ID label (which Amazon scans to track inventory at every move).
Keep the Amazon box-ID barcode untaped/uncovered — covering it can cause scan failures, lost inventory, or rejection.
Verify weight and dimensions for each case match what's declared; incorrect info can trigger UPS surcharges.
Confirm ship-from and ship-to addresses are correct, and that the ship-to on both labels matches — Amazon may route boxes to different fulfilment centres across the network.
Match the number of printed label pages to the number of boxes (e.g. 9 pages = 9 cases).
Print on sticker paper, or on plain paper and tape on carefully.
caveats: Addresses and routing can change per shipment; re-verify every time.
Label requirements and surcharge rules change — confirm current limits.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Track FBA shipments and reclaim lost inventory with documentation
cards.summary: Monitor shipment statuses and keep all paperwork to recover the value of lost or mis-received units.
cards.use_when: After sending inventory, while it's in transit and being received, and if quantities don't match.
steps: In Inventory → Manage FBA Shipments, monitor each shipment's status: in transit → delivered → receiving → closed. 'Delivered' only means the carrier dropped it off — no one has checked it in yet.
Expect Amazon to check-in within days to weeks after delivery; the source saw a shipment received Jan 28 but not cleared until Feb 25.
Under the Contents/Problems tabs, compare units shipped vs units received; a discrepancy (e.g. 405 sent, 400 received) is where you must prove what you sent.
Keep every receipt and document: BOL (bill of lading) for LTL pickups, truck pickup receipts, and case-pack records. Without proof, Amazon may not pay for missing units.
If evidence is sufficient, Amazon can pay you as though missing units were sold. The source lost a pallet's receipt and risked $10,000 until Amazon found the pallet months later.
To reduce risk, consider splitting a large send into two shipments a few days apart so a loss only affects half.
caveats: Amazon is not obligated to pay without adequate proof; recovery can take months.
Check-in, receiving, and claim timelines and interfaces change — verify current procedures.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Ship inventory 3–6 weeks ahead and avoid stockouts
cards.summary: FBA check-in can lag weeks, so plan replenishment with a buffer and never assume urgency speeds it up.
cards.use_when: Planning replenishment timing and launch timing for FBA products.
steps: Ship inventory at least 3 weeks before you expect it checked in; allow up to about 6 weeks, and expect longer during holidays.
Don't wait until you have only a week or two of stock — Amazon won't prioritize your shipment just because you'll soon be out of stock.
Use the Restock Inventory widget's days-left and recommended send quantity as an early trigger.
Separate receiving time from available-to-sell time: a shipment may sit 'delivered' but not 'receiving' for weeks.
For launch, schedule products to arrive and be checked in before your planned offer-start launch date.
caveats: The 3–6 week window is the presenter's rule-of-thumb, not a platform SLA.
Delays vary by season and warehouse load; verify current expectations.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Keep shipment paperwork and the carrier receipt for FBA pallets
cards.summary: Retain the bill of lading and the driver's pickup receipt for every FBA pallet so you can prove shipment if Amazon reports inventory missing.
cards.use_when: Fulfillment: preparing or dispatching an FBA pallet shipment and setting up your record-keeping for inbound inventory.
steps: Print the BOL (bill of lading) from the individual shipment summary in Seller Central; the driver needs it at pickup to verify they are taking the correct pallet. Missing required paperwork can trigger a fee.
File every receipt and paper connected to the shipment, however unimportant it seems, in one consistent place.
When the driver collects the pallet, get the pickup receipt and store it with the BOL. This is your proof the full pallet left your premises.

If Amazon later claims it never received the shipment, retrieve the receipt to open a reconciliation case. The source recounts a pallet that was reported missing for months and would have cost over $10,000; it was eventually found and re-added, but only after a long delay.
Verify current BOL and reconciliation requirements inside Seller Central before each shipment, since Amazon's inbound workflow changes.
caveats: The $10,000 figure is the presenter's own loss experience, not a typical loss rate.
Without the carrier receipt, a lost-shipment claim is much harder to win.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Call the carrier and pickup location the day before an FBA pallet pickup
cards.summary: Confirm truck type, liftgate or forklift needs, dock access and arrival window the day before pickup to avoid failed collections.
cards.use_when: Fulfillment: scheduling a pallet pickup from a home, warehouse or manufacturer for FBA inbound.
steps: Read the BOL to identify which trucking company is collecting the pallet, then phone them the day before pickup.
If pickup is at a residential address, tell them so they dispatch a smaller truck; an oversized truck at a house causes problems.
If you have no forklift at the pickup site, request a truck with a liftgate so the pallet can be lowered and loaded.
If pickup is at a warehouse or manufacturer, call ahead and ask whether they have a loading dock or forklift, and request a liftgate truck if not.
Confirm the arrival time and make sure someone can be present: you at home, or a manufacturer employee if the goods ship from the factory.
Re-verify the carrier's current booking and appointment process, as interface and requirements may change.
caveats: Applies to pallet/LTL freight rather than small-parcel FBA shipments.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Send roughly three to six months of FBA inventory and reorder at two to three months
cards.summary: Keep FBA stock between about three and six months of cover so you avoid both monthly storage and long-term storage fees and out-of-stock rank damage.
cards.use_when: Replenishment: deciding how many units to ship into FBA on each inbound and when to trigger the next production order.
steps: Estimate your monthly unit sales, then ship approximately three to six months of cover in each inbound shipment rather than a full year.
Avoid over-shipping: excess units sit in the warehouse and incur monthly storage fees, and the source states long-term storage fees kick in beyond six months of aged inventory.

Avoid under-shipping in competitive categories: running out of stock can lower your product's ranking or, in the presenter's experience, leave sellers unable to recover, and Amazon may blacklist the account.
Start the next replenishment order when remaining stock approaches the two-to-three-month mark so new units arrive before stockout while aged inventory stays under the long-term fee threshold.
Confirm current Amazon storage-fee tiers and long-term aged-inventory thresholds in Seller Central before committing, since fee structures change.
caveats: Three-to-six months is the presenter's recommendation, not a published Amazon rule.
Seasonal demand, lead time and cash flow may justify different cover; treat this as a heuristic to adjust.
The source's months-of-stock range is a scenario, not a default order size. Use demand uncertainty, lead time, cash, capacity and current storage costs.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Optimize the search-result click drivers: main image, title keywords, price and review count
cards.summary: Amazon ranks on click-through and conversion, so tune the only elements shoppers see in search results and put your target keywords into the title.
cards.use_when: Product listing/SEO: creating or refreshing an Amazon listing title and main image before and during launch.
steps: Recognize that in Amazon search results a shopper sees only your main image, title, price and number of reviews; these drive the click.

Write the title to contain the exact keyword phrase you want to rank for, so Amazon reads the listing as relevant to that query (the source example uses 'cocktail flashcards' where both words appear in the title).
Optimize the main image for the same target shopper's query, since a stronger image raises click-through.
Support conversion after the click with review volume and rating, because Amazon infers a review-rich product is more likely to satisfy buyers.
Treat click-through and conversion as the mechanism: products Amazon expects to be purchased rank higher, so improve both rather than chasing a single ranking trick.
caveats: The source treats keyword-in-title as a ranking input; Amazon's exact ranking weights are not disclosed and change over time.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Build launch-day sales velocity because Amazon rewards early sales spikes
cards.summary: Concentrate sales into launch day and the first weeks to signal demand and trigger a ranking snowball, since the top search positions take most sales.
cards.use_when: Acquisition: planning a new Amazon product launch and setting launch-day sales targets.
steps: Aim to generate as many sales as possible on day one rather than spreading them thinly, because a sudden sales-velocity spike signals to Amazon that the product is in demand.
Stack multiple traffic sources into the launch window (social audience, email list, giveaway buyers, influencers, early PPC) so the velocity signal is concentrated.
Expect a feedback loop: higher rank brings more impressions, more sales and further rank gains, which the presenter describes as a snowball and as the core of the launch.
Accept that lower search positions receive progressively fewer sales, so the launch objective is ranking, not just the first day's revenue.
Note the presenter's own example launched one product with over $11,000 in sales on day one; treat this as an anecdote, not a benchmark.
caveats: The presenter's $11,000 day-one figure is a personal case, not an expected outcome.
Velocity tactics must still comply with Amazon's terms; incentivized-review methods carry account risk.
Launch velocity is a source hypothesis, not a guaranteed ranking mechanism. Use genuine demand; do not arrange reimbursed purchases, incentivized reviews or search-rank manipulation.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Warm an audience before launch with social content plus an email waitlist
cards.summary: Post niche content on TikTok/Instagram/Facebook/YouTube, funnel viewers to an email waitlist, and email the list on launch day.
cards.use_when: Acquisition: building pre-launch demand and a launch-day traffic source for a new Amazon product.
steps: Pick the platforms you will actually maintain; the presenter rates TikTok as the easiest for reach and suggests repurposing the same short videos to Instagram Reels and Facebook, or choosing YouTube or a podcast if preferred.
Put a link in each bio or video description directing viewers to join a waitlist rather than straight to the not-yet-live Amazon listing.
Start engaging the list one to three months before launch, emailing updates and building anticipation like a film marketing campaign.
Offer a sweepstakes entry for a free unit to give people a concrete reason to join the list, using a tool such as Rebate to host the giveaway entry form.
On launch day, email the list with a direct link to the Amazon listing so purchase takes one click.
The source cites a student using TikTok for a cocktail-cards product reaching over $140,000 in sales in the first three months; treat as an example only.
caveats: The $140,000 result is a single case, not a forecast.
Sweepstakes rules vary by platform and jurisdiction; confirm compliance.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Run a pre-launch Facebook group to get product feedback and build commitment
cards.summary: A Facebook group beats a pure email list because members interact, give product feedback, and feel committed to buying at launch.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/merchandising: gathering buyer input on a product before finalizing it and creating a launch-day audience.
steps: Create a Facebook group for people interested in the product category before launch, instead of relying only on an email list.
Post questions in the group such as what members think of the current product or packaging, and harvest the comments to improve the product and listing.
Let members interact with each other so they see other excited buyers, which the presenter treats as stronger than a one-way email list.
Advantage of groups over pages: posts in groups are more likely to be shown to members than page posts.
When the product goes live, post in the group that it is available and link to the Amazon listing.
Use consistency: members who have participated and engaged are more likely to follow through and purchase at launch.
caveats: The source frames the group as producing a community effect; no measured conversion figures are given.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Recruit small influencers with free product and use a podcast to build relationships
cards.summary: Find 5,000–10,000-follower creators in your niche, offer free product for a post, and interview influencers on your podcast so they reciprocate with promotion.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/creative strategy: sourcing creator content and launch-day traffic for an Amazon product without a paid ad budget.
steps: Search Instagram, YouTube and TikTok for your niche and message creators directly asking whether they would post a photo or video in exchange for a free product.
Target the roughly 5,000–10,000 follower range for unpaid collaborations: the source says these creators are new enough not to charge and have a small, dedicated audience.
Budget to pay larger-audience creators when their reach justifies it; the source says this can be worthwhile, not that free always wins.
Use 'spotlight marketing': start a podcast and invite these creators as guests, building a relationship that makes them more likely to promote your product for free.
Ship product to confirmed creators ahead of launch so posts land in the launch window.
The presenter sent 85 boxes to influencers for one launch and credits it with a strong launch-day effect; treat as one case.
caveats: Niche and performance vary; the 5,000–10,000 range is the presenter's free-work sweet spot, not a rule.
Verify each platform's current disclosure and gifting rules before running creator campaigns.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Use Amazon Live and one-click shoppable video to convert viewers directly
cards.summary: Amazon Live puts an influencer talking about your product next to a buy link, so viewers purchase in one click while watching.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/creative strategy: adding a live or video shopping channel to a launch plan or ongoing traffic mix.
steps: Identify creators who host Amazon Live streams and are relevant to your category, using influencer discovery tools such as Rebate to shortlist them.
Offer free product and, where appropriate, payment for a mention so the host features your listing in a live stream.
Prefer Amazon Live over off-Amazon live platforms when purchase friction matters: viewers watch on Amazon and can buy with one click from the stream.
Cross-apply the same creators to YouTube, Instagram and other platforms where they will talk about the product if a live slot is not available.
Treat live shopping as an early-stage, less-crowded channel in the source's framing, so test it with a small number of creators before scaling.
caveats: The source calls this untapped; that is a point-in-time opinion and availability, requirements and fees can change.
Gift-and-review or paid-mention arrangements must follow Amazon's and the platform's disclosure rules.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Collect authentic Amazon reviews without incentives or review gating
cards.summary: Use permitted feedback channels while keeping compensation, relationships and review sentiment out of solicitation.
cards.use_when: Launch/retention strategy: deciding whether to pursue review velocity through incentivized purchases and outdoor recruiting.
steps: Use Amazon's permitted review-request workflow for eligible orders without selecting only satisfied buyers.
Never reimburse purchases or offer money, discounts or gifts in exchange for reviews, changes or removals.
Do not recruit friends, family or business associates to review your product.
Consider Amazon Vine only under its current eligibility and program terms; ratings and review counts are not guaranteed.
Use customer feedback to improve the product and listing, and keep support remedies independent of review behavior.
caveats: Replaces the source's prohibited purchase-review tactics; using different accounts or networks does not make them acceptable.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Start with an automatic Amazon PPC campaign, then move to manual targeting
cards.summary: Automatic campaigns let Amazon pick relevant keywords while you learn what converts, then manual keyword campaigns become more profitable.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/paid search: launching Amazon advertising for a new or newly launched product.
steps: In Seller Central open the advertising menu and campaign manager, choose Sponsored Products and create a campaign and ad group.
Name the ad group by intent (the source names one 'close match'), select the product to advertise, and let Amazon auto-target keywords relevant to your listing.
Run the automatic campaign first when you do not yet know which search phrases drive purchases; use its search-term data to discover converting queries.
Use the data to build manual keyword-targeted campaigns for the phrases that actually produced sales, which the source says is more profitable long term.
Add product targeting campaigns so your ads appear on competitor listings, and add negative keywords to stop paying for irrelevant clicks.
Note the source's claim that well-run Amazon PPC can return four to five dollars per dollar spent; that is a presenter aspiration, not a guarantee.
Verify the current campaign manager interface before setting up, as ad console layouts change.
caveats: Pay-per-click means you pay on every click whether or not it converts, so irrelevant targeting burns budget.
The 4–5x ROAS figure is presented as an upside example, not a benchmark.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Use negative keywords and relevance to avoid paying for junk clicks
cards.summary: Negative keywords block searches where your ad would spend money without selling, and only relevant search phrases should receive your bids.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/paid search: managing an Amazon PPC campaign's spend and search-term report after launch.
steps: Only let your product appear on searches relevant to what you sell; the source notes people click random results, so irrelevant impressions drain budget without sales.
Set up negative keywords to explicitly tell Amazon which searches your ad must not appear on; the presenter calls this one of the most important and most neglected PPC steps.
Build the negative list from the automatic campaign's search-term data, excluding queries that generated clicks but no orders.
Pair this with product-targeting campaigns on competitor detail pages, where the audience is already shopping the category.
Review the search-term report regularly and move spend from junk queries to converting ones rather than letting auto-targeting run unchecked.
caveats: Blocking too aggressively can suppress discovery in the early learning phase; review before adding negatives.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Enroll in Brand Registry for A+ content, video and conversion lift
cards.summary: Brand Registry unlocks A+ content pages, product videos and other modules that raise listing conversion, which in turn supports ranking.
cards.use_when: Product page/merchandising: building or upgrading an Amazon detail page and deciding which Brand-Registry-only modules to use.
steps: Enroll in Brand Registry before selling seriously, then open A+ Content Manager and replace the plain text description with image and infographic modules.
Add video to the listing: A+ content and video modules let shoppers see the product in use, which the source says increases purchase likelihood.
Why it matters for ranking: the source argues higher conversion per click leads Amazon to place the listing higher in search.
Use subscribe and save for consumable or repeat-use products, offering a discount for recurring deliveries on a schedule the customer chooses (monthly, bi-monthly, quarterly).
Use customer engagement tools to send targeted email campaigns to past buyers to raise retention.
Confirm current module availability and eligibility in Seller Central, as Brand Registry features change.
caveats: The claim that A+ content improves ranking follows from conversion, not from a published Amazon ranking factor.
Subscribe and save suits replenishable products; the source names food and drink as the clear fits.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Apply for Brand Registry with a trademark and a product listing in place
cards.summary: You need a pending or registered trademark, ownership verification and an active seller account, plus an existing ASIN and a branded product image.
cards.use_when: Brand setup: preparing a Brand Registry application before or shortly after launching an Amazon product.
steps: Get a trademark first: a text-based (word) mark or an image-based (logo) mark; the source says logo marks are generally easier to obtain when the product name is generic or crowded (e.g. 'performance nut butter' versus a distinctive logo).

File yourself at uspto.gov for around $275 by choosing your product category, uploading the image and entering the text on it; or hire a lawyer for typically a few hundred to a couple thousand dollars more.
Before applying, create the product listing so you have an ASIN: the application asks for your top-selling ASINs per category, and the source says the listing does not need to be perfect.

Go to the Brand Registry signup flow, sign in, choose 'enroll a new brand', enter the brand name exactly as it appears on the trademark, select the trademark office and enter the registration or serial number.

Upload a photo clearly showing the brand on the actual product packaging. The source's shortcut: print stickers of your branding onto competitor packaging with similar dimensions to create a convincing mockup when the product is not yet produced.
Verify ownership via the emailed code, answer the distribution questions (do you sell to distributors, where are products distributed, do you license your trademark), and submit.
Approval can take a couple of weeks and you may need to reapply; enrollment requirements and the interface should be verified at brandservices.amazon.com before starting.
caveats: The sticker-on-competitor-packaging mockup is a workaround the presenter used; the image must still convincingly show your branding on packaging.
You cannot complete the application without an existing listing/ASIN.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Use Brand Registry protections and programs to stop hijackers and cut fees
cards.summary: Evaluate brand protection and marketing programs individually, using current eligibility and charges.
cards.use_when: Retention/risk management: ongoing account and listing protection once a branded product is selling on Amazon.
steps: Use available violation-reporting tools for documented infringement; enrollment is not proof every competing offer is counterfeit.
Evaluate Transparency for the relevant products and supply chain with actual program requirements and costs.
Check Vine eligibility, enrollment fees and product readiness without assuming free access or positive reviews.
Model Brand Referral Bonus as a conditional credit on qualifying sales, not a universal lower fee.
Use eligible brand content, Store and advertising tools according to current requirements.
caveats: Historical free-code, review-count and promotional credit examples are not guaranteed entitlements.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Read Brand Analytics and Attribution to see who buys and where traffic comes from
cards.summary: Brand Registry unlocks search-term, demographic and cross-purchase reports plus Amazon Attribution for off-Amazon campaigns.
cards.use_when: Measurement: diagnosing which queries, audiences and off-Amazon channels produce Amazon sales.
steps: Open Brand Analytics to see what shoppers search for before buying your products, then feed the highest-intent terms back into titles, A+ copy and manual PPC keywords.
Use the demographics view to understand who buys, which informs imagery, tone and audience targeting in ads and creative.

Review the item comparison, alternate purchase and market basket reports to see what customers compare you against and what they buy alongside: use this for bundle ideas, positioning and competitive gaps.

Use Amazon Attribution when running off-Amazon paid traffic (Google ads, Facebook ads, social) to measure how many visitors from each channel reach the listing and actually purchase, rather than guessing at channel value.
Use these reports as the feedback loop for the keyword and creative decisions made elsewhere in the launch plan.
Confirm which reports your brand currently qualifies for, since availability varies by category and account.
caveats: Report availability and definitions can change; verify inside Seller Central.
Attribution measures a channel's contribution to Amazon sales; it does not prove causality on its own.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Apply Cialdini's six principles of influence to Amazon launch assets
cards.summary: Reciprocity, scarcity, authority, consistency, liking and consensus can each be mapped to a concrete pre-launch and listing tactic.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/offer design: assembling launch messaging, promotions and PDP elements for a new Amazon product.
steps: Reciprocity: give something small first, such as free product to influencers or a free podcast interview slot, so they feel inclined to promote you in return.
Scarcity: cap a launch incentive, for example only 200 units at a discounted price, and tell the email list and social followers the price returns to normal when they sell out.
Authority: use recognized creators or experts to recommend the product, since shoppers follow authority figures' recommendations.
Consistency: get people to join the Facebook group and participate before launch; earlier engagement commitments make them more likely to buy.
Liking: introduce yourself and your brand to the audience through social content, an about-us video, and about-us content on the Amazon page.
Consensus/social proof: get influencers talking about the product, surface group and list members saying positive things, and share real customer stories.
The presenter's 80/20 for a launch: some social or influencer presence, an engaged email list, and a scarcity element on the offer.
caveats: The presenter advises using these principles from a healthy, honest place because they can be used manipulatively.
Scarcity claims must be genuine to avoid misleading customers and platform issues.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Set Up an Automatic Sponsored Products Campaign Inside Out (Split by Targeting Group)
cards.summary: Launch one auto campaign and split close match, loose match, substitutes and compliments into separate ad groups so each match type gets its own bid and its own performance data.
cards.use_when: You are launching Amazon PPC for a new or existing ASIN and want a beginner-safe automatic campaign you can later read and optimize.
steps: In Seller Central open the menu, go to Advertising > Campaign Manager and choose Sponsored Products (source calls this the easiest, most beginner-friendly ad type; Sponsored Brands needs three SKUs and Sponsored Display is covered separately — verify current interface).
Create a campaign, add the product you want to advertise, and select Automatic targeting.
Instead of clicking the single 'set default bid' option, choose to set bids by targeting group so the four automatic groups can be priced separately.

Create one ad group per targeting group rather than running them all together: name the first 'close match' and turn off loose match, substitutes and compliments. Then repeat creating further ad groups named 'loose match', 'substitutes' and 'compliments', each with only its own group enabled.

Use Amazon's suggested bids as a starting point. In the source's example the suggestions were close match $0.92, loose match $0.72, substitutes $0.13, compliments $0.71 — treat these as example values for a sample product, not benchmarks; read your own suggested bids.

Choose a bidding strategy. The source says fixed bids cap you at your max bid and suit tighter cash, while dynamic bids up-and-down can raise your bid up to +100% when Amazon expects a sale and lower it otherwise; dynamic down-only is a middle option. Source used dynamic up-and-down here.

Set the campaign name and start date, and set daily budget to an amount you are willing to lose while the campaign learns — source suggests starting around the recommended daily budget (e.g. $14 in the example) or as low as $5.
Launch the campaign, then return to Campaign Manager to confirm the campaign appears with its ad groups nested underneath.
caveats: Bid suggestion values and available targeting-group options change over time and by product; verify in the current UI before applying.
The source explicitly calls this the very beginner version and defers negative keyword/product targeting and placement bid adjustments to later lessons.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: What Each Amazon Automatic Targeting Group Actually Matches
cards.summary: Understand close match, loose match, substitutes and compliments so you can decide which automatic groups deserve budget and which to switch off.
cards.use_when: You are deciding which automatic targeting groups to enable or how much to bid on each when launching or cleaning up an Amazon auto campaign.
steps: Close match: Amazon shows your ad to shoppers using search terms closely related to your product. Example from the source: for a 400-count cotton sheets product, close match triggers on searches like 'cotton sheets' and '400 count sheets'. This is the group the source says deserves the most spend.

Loose match: shows your ad on search terms loosely related to your product. Same example, loose match could trigger on 'bed sheets' but also 'bath sheets' or 'bath towels' — the source argues this is often irrelevant and not worth heavy budget.
Substitutes: shows your ad on detail pages of products that compete with or substitute for yours (example: your cotton sheets ad on 300-count cotton sheets and queen 400-count sheet listings).
Compliments: shows your ad on detail pages of products that pair with yours (example: queen comforter and feather pillows).

Use the logic rather than the numbers: bid highest on close match, keep substitutes running at the suggested bid as a starting point, and be skeptical of spending heavily on loose match because the intent gap is wide.
After running, judge each group by whether its traffic converts for your product rather than assuming all four are worth keeping.
caveats: The example and bid figures come from one product and one point in time; match definitions are Amazon's and can change, so verify in the current campaign UI.
This is the source's opinion on which group deserves the most money, not a universal rule.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Build Keyword Lists With Magnet: Filtering Rules for Low-Competition Terms
cards.summary: Use the Magnet keyword tool to harvest hundreds of buyer search terms, then filter out head terms and irrelevant queries to build a targetable keyword list.
cards.use_when: You are building the keyword list for a manual Amazon Sponsored Products campaign or deciding which search terms your listing title and bullets should cover.
steps: Seed Magnet with the phrase you believe buyers use (source example: 'carnivore electrolytes'). The tool reports monthly search volume for the seed and generates hundreds or thousands of related terms.
Save results into a named folder (e.g. the product name) so the list carries over to campaign setup.
Sort by the Magnet IQ score to surface the more relevant terms first.

Apply filters to remove terms that are too hard to win: source excluded phrases with more than 5,000 monthly searches and set a minimum word count of 2 so single generic words like 'electrolytes' are dropped as too competitive.

Filter for demand and winnability rather than volume alone: source set competing products max 100 to find low-hanging fruit, and set keyword sales minimum 2 to require at least minimal sales actually flowing through the term.
Hand-pick the survivors for relevance to your exact product before exporting; the source reviewed the filtered list and kept only terms a buyer of that product would plausibly type.
caveats: Thresholds (5,000 searches, 100 competitors, 2 sales, minimum 2 words) are the presenter's heuristics for one product, not validated benchmarks.
Search volume and sales estimates are tool estimates, not Amazon's actual figures.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Manual Keyword Targeting: Broad, Phrase and Exact Match Explained With Ads Implications
cards.summary: Set up a manual keyword campaign and choose broad, phrase or exact match knowing exactly what searches each will trigger and when negative keywords become mandatory.
cards.use_when: You are creating a manual Sponsored Products keyword campaign or diagnosing why a keyword campaign is burning spend on irrelevant search terms.
steps: In Campaign Manager create a new Sponsored Products campaign, name the ad group 'manual keyword targeting', add your product, then choose Manual targeting > Keyword targeting.
Understand the match types before bidding — using the source's example term 'electrolyte powder':
Broad match bids on any search containing 'electrolyte' and 'powder' with other words anywhere in the query, e.g. 'watermelon electrolyte drink powder'.

Phrase match requires the words to stay together with nothing inserted between them, so 'watermelon electrolyte powder' and 'watermelon electrolyte powder drink mix' trigger it but 'watermelon electrolyte drink powder' does not.
Exact match shows only for the query 'electrolyte powder' and nothing more or less; the source calls exact the most powerful match type.

Note the source's observation that exact match was cheaper than phrase or broad for its example product, the reverse of what is usually true — check the suggested bids on your own terms rather than assuming.

Add Amazon's suggested keywords if relevant, or use 'enter list' to paste your filtered keyword list at once; keywords with no suggested bid were assigned $0.92 in the source's example and flagged for later review since no suggestion likely means low search interest.
The source recommends running all three match types but insists that broad and phrase require negative keywords to control waste.
caveats: Match-type behaviour is defined by Amazon and the interface changes; verify current definitions and bid suggestions.
Exact match being cheaper than broad/phrase was an observation on one product, not a rule.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Split Keyword Campaigns Into Themed Ad Groups to See What Makes Money
cards.summary: Organise manual keyword campaigns into topic-based ad groups so you can attribute profit to themes rather than reading one blended number.
cards.use_when: You are structuring manual Amazon PPC campaigns for a product with several distinct buyer intents or sub-audiences.
steps: Group keywords by the buyer intent they represent, not by alphabetical or volume order. Source example: one ad group for the carnivore diet containing all carnivore-related terms, a separate group for flavorless electrolytes (flavorless electrolytes, flavorless electrolyte powder, no flavor electrolyte powder), and a third for meat-based diet because that intent differs from carnivore.
The source notes you can technically run everything in a single ad group to start, but recommends multiple themed ad groups for control.
The practical benefit stated is attribution: separate ad groups let you see which topic actually creates profit so you can shift budget toward it and cut or rework the losers.
Apply the same logic to automatic campaigns by keeping match types in separate ad groups, and to product targeting by keeping competitors in separate ad groups.
Set each campaign's daily budget independently so one theme cannot consume the budget of another.
caveats: More ad groups means more management overhead; the source presents the single ad group as a simpler starting option.
The examples describe one seller's product; group boundaries should follow your own product's intents.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Product Targeting Ads: Run on Competitor Detail Pages (and Group by Competitor to Read Profitability)
cards.summary: Create manual product-targeting Sponsored Products campaigns that place your ad on chosen competitor listings, and split ad groups by brand so you learn which competitor placements pay.
cards.use_when: You want to intercept demand on competitor PDPs or refine a broad category-targeting campaign.
steps: In Campaign Manager create a new Sponsored Products campaign, name the ad group 'product targeting', select the product to advertise, and choose Manual targeting > Product targeting.

Choose between targeting the whole category (e.g. the sports nutrition/endurance/energy powders category) or individual products. The source says category-wide targeting is probably not advisable, though it can be refined.

For individual products, review the suggested product list and deliberately choose the listings most similar to yours — the source says to take time deciding where you want your product to appear rather than adding everything.
Expect these bids to be expensive in some niches; the source notes they were high for its example product.

Group by competitor brand: rather than one ad group with everything, create an ad group containing all products from one brand, and separate ad groups for other brands (source examples: one for Element, one for Liquid IV).
Use the split to compare results — the source's stated goal is to see that advertising on one brand's listings makes money while another brand's placements do not, then act on that.
Optionally use negative product targeting, especially when targeting an entire category, to exclude specific products you don't want to appear beside.
Set daily budget and launch.
caveats: On-page placement beside a competitor does not guarantee conversion; the source frames this as a powerful ad type, not a guaranteed winner.
Bid levels vary by category and time; verify current interface options and suggested bids.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Negative Keywords in Amazon PPC: Exclude Mismatched Formats Before You Spend
cards.summary: Add negative keywords to every campaign so ads don't show for search intent your product cannot satisfy — starting with format and variant mismatches.
cards.use_when: You are launching or optimising any Amazon Sponsored Products campaign and want to reduce wasted clicks on non-buyers.
steps: For each campaign (automatic, manual keyword, product targeting) add negative keywords that tell Amazon not to show your ad when those phrases are searched.

Start by reasoning through your own product: list everything a shopper might search that is related but incompatible. Source example: the electrolytes product ships in a tub, not individual packets, so 'packets' was added as a negative keyword.
Reinforce with data: open Helium 10's Magnet tool, scan the generated search-term list for phrases that would attract the wrong buyer, and add those as negatives.
Apply negatives especially to broad and phrase match campaigns, which the source says require negatives as a condition of running them.
Revisit negatives as you review search-term reports, since new mismatched queries appear over time.
caveats: The source treats negatives as essential for broad/phrase but defers a full negative-targeting lesson; expect a more complete method elsewhere.
Over-blocking can cut legitimate traffic, so review what you exclude rather than blocking loosely related terms blindly.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Target Amazon Keywords by Reverse-Engineering Competitor ASINs (Cerebro / Reverse ASIN)
cards.summary: Pull a competitor's ASIN into a reverse-ASIN tool to see the exact search terms that lead shoppers to find and buy that listing, then build your own target list.
cards.use_when: You are choosing keywords for a new listing, validating product demand, or benchmarking your keyword coverage against a competitor's.
steps: Find the ASIN on the Amazon product page — the source reminds that every Amazon product has an Amazon Standard Identification Number.
Paste the ASIN into Helium 10's Cerebro reverse-ASIN tool.
Read the resulting list of keywords shoppers used to find and purchase that product. Source example: cocktail card searches surfaced terms like 'recipe card deck' and 'recipe cards'.
Use that output in place of guessing: the source says reverse-ASIN is how it actually does product research and claims most sellers are not using it.
Adapt the same method to your own listing by checking which competitor terms you do and don't index for, then adding missing terms to your campaign and listing copy.
Combine with Magnet keyword results so you cover both competitor-proven terms and terms the competitor may not target.
