caveats: The source says reverse-ASIN is how it identifies product opportunities — that is a claim based on personal experience, not a guarantee of finding a viable product.
Tool data is estimated from Amazon's data and can be incomplete for low-volume ASINs.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Validate Demand Before You Buy Inventory: Sales Estimator, BSR and Fee Calculator
cards.summary: Estimate a product's monthly revenue and profit before committing inventory by converting BSR with a sales estimator and running the numbers through a fee calculator.
cards.use_when: You are evaluating a product opportunity and need to check whether units sold, price and Amazon's cut leave real profit.
steps: On the product page scroll down and copy the Best Sellers Rank number.
Paste it into the free Jungle Scout sales estimator tool, choose your marketplace and the product's category, and read the estimated units per month.

Multiply estimated units by the product's price to approximate monthly revenue. Source example: this method produced a $60,000/month revenue estimate for one product and a $40,000/month estimate for another.
Do not stop at revenue. Run the same product through an Amazon FBA fee calculator to see actual profit after costs.
Account for at least the referral fee — the source gives an example of a $27.99 product paying a $4.20 referral fee per unit — plus the FBA pick-and-pack fee per unit and other costs.
Alternatively use Helium 10's free extension on the product page to see estimated monthly sales without manual BSR work.
caveats: The source stresses that revenue is not profit; a high-revenue product can be unprofitable after fees.
Estimates are approximations derived from BSR, not actual seller data; treat as directional only.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Find Product Opportunities by Filtering Revenue, Review Count and Category (Blackbox)
cards.summary: Use a product database tool with explicit filters for monthly revenue, review ceiling and category to generate a candidate list instead of browsing randomly.
cards.use_when: You are searching for a product to launch and want a shortlist that matches your revenue target and competitiveness tolerance.
steps: Open a product research database tool (source used Helium 10's Blackbox).
Set a minimum monthly revenue target — source example: at least $10,000 per month.
Set a competition ceiling. The source example used under 400 reviews to find less-contested listings.
Restrict to a category you are willing to operate in; the source used baby as an example of a hot category.
Run the search and work through the returned products, screening for relevance and whether you can realistically source and differentiate.
Supplement with trend tools (source mentions Trendster) to check whether demand in the niche is rising or fading.
caveats: Low reviews can mean the niche is unproven as easily as it can mean it is winnable; the source does not resolve this ambiguity.
Database figures are estimates and category dynamics change; re-run filters periodically.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Pre-Launch Validation With Crowdfunding and Pre-Sales
cards.summary: Reduce the risk of ordering inventory for an unproven product by selling it before manufacturing it, using crowdfunding or similar pre-sale validation.
cards.use_when: You are about to place a first production order for a new product and want evidence people will buy before you commit capital.
steps: Identify the product concept you intend to sell on Amazon.
Run a Kickstarter or Indiegogo campaign for it before buying bulk inventory, so real buyers must commit money.

Use the result as demand evidence: the source raised about $15,000 on its first product this way, and a partner raised over $100,000 with cocktail cards before selling on Amazon, which the source says let them know the products would do well.
Apply the same principle more cheaply if crowdfunding is impractical by creating a pre-order or waitlist offer and measuring real sign-ups.
Only scale into Amazon FBA inventory once pre-sales demonstrate paying demand; treat the raised amounts as case examples, not expected outcomes.
caveats: Crowdfunding campaigns require their own marketing effort and a compelling concept; success is not automatic.
The dollar figures cited are single case results from the source's own products and should not be read as typical.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Compare FBA and merchant fulfillment for the actual product
cards.summary: Evaluate delivery eligibility, total costs and operational capacity rather than assuming FBA guarantees higher sales.
cards.use_when: You are deciding how to fulfil a product or considering switching an FBM listing to FBA to lift sales.
steps: Compare current FBA fees, storage and inbound costs with the merchant's own shipping and service costs.
Assess delivery promises, stock availability, returns and operating capacity for the product.
FBA can provide Prime eligibility; qualifying merchants may also use Seller Fulfilled Prime where available.
Test conversion and contribution where practical rather than assuming a fixed sales multiplier or direct ranking boost.
Choose FBA, merchant fulfillment or a mix using actual economics and service requirements.
caveats: Source sales uplifts are individual cases; check current program requirements in the selling marketplace.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Invest in Branding and Packaging Quality Instead of $5 Designs
cards.summary: Cheap logos and packaging suppress conversion on Amazon because shoppers judge the product's credibility from the visual assets before reading copy.
cards.use_when: You are budgeting for product design, logo, packaging or listing imagery before launch or relaunch.
steps: Do not source your logo, branding or packaging from the lowest-price freelance tier. The source describes beginners paying around $5 for these assets and the result looking 'absolutely terrible' with nobody buying.
Treat design spend as conversion infrastructure rather than an avoidable cost — the source frames the cheap option as false economy that costs more in lost sales than it saves.
Apply the same standard to packaging, since it is part of the perceived product quality in Amazon imagery and on arrival.
Judge the spend against expected units sold, not against the cheapest available quote.
caveats: This is the presenter's opinion based on observing student outcomes; it does not set a spending threshold or guarantee returns.
Premium design does not compensate for a product nobody wants — pair with demand validation.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Launch Velocity: Why Early Sales Volume Shapes Amazon Search Placement
cards.summary: Aim to generate concentrated sales in the launch window because Amazon's ranking rewards early sales with higher search placement, and higher placement compounds into more clicks.
cards.use_when: You are planning a product launch window or deciding how much PPC and promotion budget to front-load on a new ASIN.
steps: Accept the ordering logic the source describes: products ranking first get the most clicks, then second, third and fourth, and the drop-off is described as exponential rather than linear.
Therefore treat the first days as the priority spend window: drive as many sales as possible from day one so Amazon reads the listing as relevant and pushes it up in results.

Fund this with a deliberate PPC budget plus any pre-launch demand you built (crowdfunding/pre-sales), and accept that short-run PPC profit may be negative — the source explicitly says you probably will not make much money in the short run with Amazon PPC.
Set the daily budget at an amount you are willing to lose during this learning period rather than at a level that throttles the campaign.
Monitor whether ranking improves; if it does not, the launch tactics or the listing are the problem, not just the budget.
caveats: The source's ranking mechanism description is its own explanation of Amazon's algorithm, not documented Amazon policy.
Spending to rank is a loss-leader strategy that can fail if the product or listing does not convert.
Launch velocity is a source hypothesis, not a guaranteed ranking mechanism. Use genuine demand; do not arrange reimbursed purchases, incentivized reviews or search-rank manipulation.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Choosing Between Helium 10 and Jungle Scout: A Function-by-Function Comparison
cards.summary: Pick your Amazon tool stack by which specific capabilities you need — Helium 10 for breadth of research, listing and PPC automation, Jungle Scout for its supplier database.
cards.use_when: You are choosing which paid Amazon research tool to subscribe to, or deciding whether a second tool is justified.
steps: Map your gaps first. Source notes Helium 10 organises tools into product research, keyword research, marketing, listing optimisation, analytics and operations; Jungle Scout groups into product research, suppliers, keywords, marketing, sales analytics and advertising.

If keyword depth matters, note the source's comparison: on the same seed term, Jungle Scout's keyword tool showed roughly 11 filters versus 14 in Helium 10 and returned 49 keyword ideas versus over 1,400, with fewer data columns.

If supplier identification matters, Jungle Scout's supplier database is the standout — the source says you can enter a competitor or similar product and learn who manufactures it, and knows people who keep Helium 10 for research while subscribing to Jungle Scout just for this tool.

Consider pricing structure: the source cites Helium 10 having a free plan plus a 7-day money-back period, and Jungle Scout having no free plan, with a cited offer of three months for $149 (about $49/month) which is more expensive upfront but cheaper monthly and comparable to a Helium 10 tier priced around $79/month.

If PPC automation matters, note Helium 10's Adtomic has no Jungle Scout equivalent (it tiers this to platinum and above), and Helium 10's Refund Genie recovers money Amazon owes you while Jungle Scout has no equivalent.

Compare user experience: source flags Helium 10 as harder for beginners to navigate due to many similarly named tools and a weak mobile experience; Jungle Scout as easier but less capable in data depth and listing-launch support.
Both tools were described as having a 7-day money-back period, so the source suggests trialling one, then the other, and choosing.
caveats: Pricing, plan tiers and feature availability change frequently — verify current plans and any trial or guarantee terms before subscribing.
The stated winner (Helium 10) is the presenter's opinion, and the presenter states an affiliate relationship with both tools.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Using a Listing Analyser and Index Checker to Diagnose Conversion and Rank Gaps
cards.summary: Score your listing against competitors and check which keywords you actually index for, so you can fix the specific weakness instead of rewriting blindly.
cards.use_when: An Amazon listing is getting impressions but weak conversion, or you want to confirm you rank for the keywords you are bidding on.
steps: Run your own product through a listing analyser and read the listing quality score. Source example: a listing scored 7.5, which the source read as leaving room for improvement.

Run the same analysis on competitors to see what they do differently, and use the analyser's recent sales figures (the example reported last-7-days sales) plus historical data as context for how the listing performs.
Use an index checker to confirm whether you actually show up in Amazon search for each keyword you care about, rather than assuming that adding a term to the backend means you rank for it.
Use keyword processing tools (source mentions Frankenstein) to organise and de-duplicate the keyword set before putting terms into title, bullets and backend fields.
Cross-reference with a keyword rank tracker that records position over time so you can confirm whether changes moved you.
Fix the weakest measured area first — copy, imagery or indexing — and re-measure rather than making wholesale changes and losing attribution.
caveats: Quality scores and analysis outputs are tool-generated heuristics; a 7.5 is the source's illustration, not a defined pass/fail threshold.
Some listed tools are tier-gated and the available feature set changes; verify in your current plan.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Recover Amazon's Own Errors and Protect Inventory With Operations Tools
cards.summary: Run scheduled checks that claw back money Amazon owes you and guard against listing hijackers and stockouts, since both quietly destroy Amazon margin.
cards.use_when: You are operating an existing Amazon listing and want to reduce leakage in fees, reimbursements and inventory continuity.
steps: Use a refund/reimbursement tool (source: Helium 10's Refund Genie) to systematically identify money Amazon owes you. The source states plainly that Amazon does not always send what it owes and makes mistakes that cost sellers money.

Use inventory alerts and monitoring so you do not run out of stock. The source warns that running out of inventory risks Amazon treating you as an unreliable or unprofessional seller, which can be far more damaging than the lost sales.
Use alerting that flags hijackers on your listing so unauthorised sellers can be removed before they damage the listing's performance.

Automate post-purchase follow-up emails to prompt reviews — the source lists an automated follow-up tool as part of the standard operations stack; keep within Amazon's messaging rules as they currently stand.
Run these checks on a recurring schedule rather than once, since reimbursements, stock levels and hijack activity all change over time.
caveats: The source's statements about Amazon blacklisting sellers for stockouts are its own characterisation, not a documented policy; verify current Amazon policy and messaging rules.
Automated follow-up and review requests must comply with Amazon's current Terms of Service and messaging rules.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Commit Budget to Tools Early Rather Than Trialling Everything Manually
cards.summary: The source argues that refusing to spend on tooling early is itself the expensive choice, because manual guesswork leads to larger downstream mistakes.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to pay for Amazon research, listing or PPC tooling on a tight starting budget.
steps: Recognise the source's position: as a beginner it avoided spending on the belief that spending money equals losing money, and now considers that the wrong calculation.

Use the source's analogy to size the decision: you can build a doghouse with a rock instead of a hammer, but building a mansion justifies buying the tool — invest in proportion to the size of the business you intend to build.

Test cheaply first: several of the recommended tools have free tiers or free versions, and the source says a student found a $100,000/month product using Helium 10's free plan. Helium 10 was also described as having a 7-day money-back period, and Jungle Scout a 7-day guarantee.
If you do pay, start on monthly rather than annual billing if you are only doing a short product-research sprint, and switch to annual only once you know you will keep the tool.

Note the source's stated losses from under-investing and other mistakes: thousands on manufacturing issues, tens of thousands on expiring excess inventory, and over $100,000 attributed to the other mistakes discussed — treat these as the presenter's own figures, not typical outcomes.
Weigh tool cost against the cost of the mistake it prevents (buying wrong inventory, unprofitable PPC, penalties).
caveats: The dollar figures are the presenter's personal losses and are not benchmarks.
The presenter has affiliate relationships with the tools recommended, which is a conflict to account for.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Amazon Referral Fees and Unit Economics: Start With the 15% Cut
cards.summary: Before locking a price, model the referral fee as a percentage of sale price plus per-unit fulfilment cost so a healthy-looking price still leaves profit.
cards.use_when: You are setting or revising a product price, or checking whether a sourced product can be profitable at the price the market supports.
steps: Count the three major FBA cost blocks the source identifies: the Amazon referral fee, the FBA pick-and-pack (fulfilment) fee, and other costs.

Understand the referral fee as a flat percentage charged for selling on Amazon, which the source says depends on the product's price. Source example: a product priced at $27.99 pays a referral fee of $4.20 per unit sold, which is roughly 15% — the source separately states sellers pay 15% for the Amazon selling fee.
Apply the fee per unit, not per order or per month, when calculating contribution margin.
Add the pick-and-pack fee per unit on top of the referral fee, since the referral fee alone does not include fulfilment.
Enter price and dimensions into an Amazon FBA fee calculator to get the net profit figure rather than estimating by hand.
Re-check fees after any price change or product/packaging change, since the referral fee scales with price while fulfilment fees depend on size and weight.
caveats: The 15% figure and the $27.99 / $4.20 example are illustrative; referral fee percentages vary by category and Amazon's fee schedules change, so verify current rates.
Some product categories have minimum referral fees that matter more on low-priced items.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Cheap Ways to Get Amazon Data Without Paying: Free Tools and Scorecards
cards.summary: Run initial product screening with free tools and structured criteria before paying for any subscription, so budget goes only where it changes a decision.
cards.use_when: You are starting Amazon product research with no budget and need a practical workflow that still produces a real decision.
steps: Use the Amazon FBA fee calculator to check profit on candidate products — the source lists this as a free tool.
Use the free Jungle Scout sales estimator for unit estimates by pasting the BSR; note that the free version caps how many times you can use it per day, and the paid version removes that cap.
Use the free Helium 10 extension on any product page to see estimated monthly sales without manually looking up BSR.
Use Helium 10's free plan for keyword and product research with some restrictions — the source says it personally knows a student who found a $100,000/month product using the free plan.

Build a scorecard before spending: for each candidate record estimated units, price, estimated revenue, fee-adjusted profit, review count and category, then compare candidates against each other rather than one at a time.
Only upgrade to a paid tool when a specific research task is blocked, not pre-emptively.
caveats: Free tier caps and available features change; verify what your current free plan includes.
Free estimates are approximations and should not be the sole basis for a large inventory commitment.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Avoid the Big Beginner Amazon Mistakes: Wrong Product, FBM by Default, Cheap Assets
cards.summary: Three recurring beginner errors — unvalidated product choice, defaulting to merchant fulfilment, and underinvesting in branding — account for most of the money the source sees lost.
cards.use_when: You are in the early planning stage of an Amazon launch and want to sequence your decisions to avoid expensive rework.
steps: Do not buy inventory on thin research. The source describes beginners doing a little research, ordering 1,000 units, and discovering nobody wants the product. Validate demand first with keyword search volume data and, preferably, pre-sales or crowdfunding before placing a bulk order.

Do not default to FBM just because fees look lower. The source argues Prime eligibility drives materially more purchases and gives the example of its own dance-clothing brand where converting best sellers from FBM to FBA caused sales to 'skyrocket'.
Do not buy $5 logos, branding and packaging from budget freelancers; the source says the result looks terrible and nobody buys, framing it as false economy.
Sequence accordingly: prove demand, then design the brand assets, then fulfil via FBA for the products you most want to sell.

Treat every figure in the source's own loss history — thousands on manufacturing, tens of thousands on expiring inventory, over $100,000 on other mistakes — as the presenter's experience, useful as a warning about cost categories rather than a prediction for your business.
caveats: The sales multiplier from FBA and the loss figures are personal observations, not measured benchmarks.
The source says these mistakes are avoidable based on observing over a thousand students, which is a claim of pattern, not proof of causation.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Launch Product Demand Research From a Theme Tool and a Seed Phrase
cards.summary: Use a keyword tool's related-term output as a product-idea generator, not just as a campaign keyword list, because it reveals adjacent buyer needs you could sell into.
cards.use_when: You have a product category or audience in mind and want to identify a specific product to launch, rather than a keyword list for an existing one.
steps: Enter a seed phrase describing what buyers type — the source used 'cocktail cards' and found over a thousand monthly searches, which was how the cocktail cards product was originally identified.

Read the adjacent terms the tool returns as product ideas, not just bid terms. Source example: 'easy cocktail recipe book' at over 200 searches per month, and a much larger unrelated term like 'card shuffler' at over 26,000 searches per month which is a signal about the broader gift/card category rather than a term to bid on.
Sort by search volume to see the shape of the niche, then look for a cluster where volume exists and competition is beatable rather than chasing the single biggest term.
Cross-check any candidate against a reverse-ASIN lookup on the closest existing product to see the full set of terms buyers use to find and buy it.
Use misspelling tools to capture common misspellings in backend keywords as an additional free source of impressions.
caveats: High-volume adjacent terms can be irrelevant to your product; the source treats them as category signal, not automatic targets.
Search volumes are tool estimates and shift seasonally.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Model Amazon FBA unit economics with the three-big-fees framework
cards.summary: Split every candidate product's selling price into product cost, Amazon fees and profit using a thirds rule before committing to inventory.
cards.use_when: Pricing and product selection: deciding whether a product can survive Amazon's fee stack, or setting a target retail price.
steps: List the three big fees: the referral fee (a flat percentage to sell on Amazon; the source uses 15%), the FBA pick-and-pack fee (per unit, based on size and weight), and the monthly storage fee (charged per cubic foot of warehouse space).
Sanity-check the split the source uses as a planning rule of thumb: roughly 33% of margin to product cost, 33% to Amazon FBA fees, 33% profit. Treat it as a heuristic, not a calculation.

Plug a real comparable product's price, dimensions and weight into Amazon's free FBA calculator to get referral fee, pick-and-pack fee and monthly storage cost per unit. Verify the current calculator's interface and current fee tables before relying on output.
Compare the resulting per-unit contribution against your target profit, and reject products where fee load pushes you below target before you spend on design, samples or inventory.
Re-check numbers for the apparel category (roughly $0.30-$0.40 more per shipped item per the source) and for dangerous goods, which bill at different tiers.
caveats: The 33/33/33 split is the presenter's rule of thumb, not a derived formula; actual results vary widely by price point and size.
Fee amounts and thresholds change; the numbers cited are examples from the source's experience and date, so confirm current Amazon fee schedules.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Choose small-standard packaging deliberately to cut pick-and-pack fees
cards.summary: Design product dimensions and weight to land in the cheapest FBA size tier, since pick-and-pack pricing moves sharply by tier and weight band.
cards.use_when: Product and packaging design or sourcing: specifying box dimensions, jar size, or bundle configuration before ordering inventory.
steps: Apply the source's stated tier boundaries: small standard means longest side up to 15 in, median side up to 12 in, shortest side up to 0.75 in, and weight under 1 lb. Large standard means up to 18 in longest, 14 in median, 8 in shortest, and under 20 lb. Verify the current Amazon definitions, which do change.

Within a tier, weight bands drive the fee: the source cites different fees for under 6 oz, 6-12 oz, and 12-16 oz for small standard. Shaving a product just under a band boundary can reduce cost per unit.

Give the manufacturer a target spec rather than accepting their default. The source's example: instead of a 16 oz jar, he produced a smaller jar under 10 oz specifically to lower FBA pick-and-pack fees.

For low-price, lightweight products, check whether the product qualifies for Amazon's Small and Light program; the source cites an example of $2.16 per unit instead of $2.70, a $0.54 per-unit saving, and reports that a colleague saved hundreds to thousands of dollars.

After your first shipments, verify Amazon recorded the correct dimensions and weight; the source says Amazon sometimes places products in a higher tier and will sometimes reimburse overcharges if you catch it and contact them.
caveats: Tier dimensions, weight bands, and program fees are set by Amazon and change; re-verify before tooling packaging.
Making the product smaller can reduce perceived value or change the use case, so weigh fee savings against customer expectations.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Estimate monthly storage cost and avoid long-term storage fees
cards.summary: Calculate per-unit storage cost from cubic volume and plan inventory turnover so units don't sit in Amazon warehouses past 365 days.
cards.use_when: Replenishment and inventory planning: deciding how many units to send to FBA and when to pull slow stock.
steps: Measure product height, width and depth to get cubic inches. Divide by 1,728 (cubic inches in a cubic foot) and multiply by the per-cubic-foot rate. The source's example: a 3x4x5 in product is 60 cubic in, giving about $0.026 per unit per month at $0.75/cubic foot.

Account for the seasonal rate: the source cites roughly $0.70 per cubic foot January-September and $2.40 per cubic foot October-December, because Amazon raises fees to discourage Q4 overstocking. Confirm current rates.
Estimate total storage by multiplying per-unit monthly cost by the months you expect the unit to remain in the warehouse, and fold that into your unit economics.
Avoid the long-term storage fee: if inventory stays past 365 days, the source says Amazon charges $6.90 per cubic foot or $0.15 per item, whichever is greater.
Monitor sell-through. If a SKU is slow, request removal before the one-year mark, even if you intend to re-ship it back in, or let it sell down and reset the clock with fresh inventory.

Size shipments so you don't end up with residual units sitting past a year: the source contrasts 100 units selling 50/month (clock resets continually) with 100 units selling 10/month (20 units remain after 12 months and start accruing long-term fees).
caveats: Rates are cited from the source's experience and change; verify current Amazon storage fee schedules.
Removal and re-shipment costs can rival the long-term storage fee for very cheap, very small items.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Compare FBA and merchant fulfillment for the actual product
cards.summary: Evaluate delivery eligibility, total costs and operational capacity rather than assuming FBA guarantees higher sales.
cards.use_when: Fulfillment model choice for a new listing, or deciding whether to migrate seller-fulfilled SKUs into FBA.
steps: Compare current FBA fees, storage and inbound costs with the merchant's own shipping and service costs.
Assess delivery promises, stock availability, returns and operating capacity for the product.
FBA can provide Prime eligibility; qualifying merchants may also use Seller Fulfilled Prime where available.
Test conversion and contribution where practical rather than assuming a fixed sales multiplier or direct ranking boost.
Choose FBA, merchant fulfillment or a mix using actual economics and service requirements.
caveats: Source sales uplifts are individual cases; check current program requirements in the selling marketplace.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Pick the right Amazon selling plan instead of paying monthly from day one
cards.summary: Match the individual vs professional selling plan to actual monthly order volume to avoid paying $39.99/month before you're selling.
cards.use_when: Pre-launch account setup and cost control while sourcing a product or running low-volume arbitrage.
steps: Use the individual selling plan while you're not yet live or selling few units: the source describes it as free to hold, with a $0.99 fee per item sold, and recommends it below roughly 40 items per month.

Upgrade to the professional plan at $39.99/month when volume crosses that band or when you're ready to send inventory to FBA, since the source says FBA requires the professional plan and gives access to promotions and reports.
Avoid the common mistake the source flags: paying $39.99/month for months while still only thinking about starting, before any inventory is sent in.
Treat the ~40 items/month crossover as the source's heuristic and recalculate with your own average selling price and per-item fee.
caveats: The break-even item count depends on per-item fee and current plan pricing; verify current Amazon selling plan terms.
Feature availability on each plan can change.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Model Brand Referral Bonus as a credit on qualifying external sales
cards.summary: Compare external traffic contribution after actual advertising costs and eligible referral-fee credits.
cards.use_when: Acquisition and off-Amazon marketing: running ads, influencer or social traffic to your own Amazon listing.
steps: Check marketplace availability, enrollment and eligibility for Brand Referral Bonus.
Use the required Amazon Attribution links or current tracking method on external campaigns.
Forecast the actual applicable bonus and referral fee separately; do not assume every 15% fee becomes 5%.
Reconcile qualifying sales and credited amounts, allowing for exclusions and timing.
Compare net contribution and customer value against sending traffic to the brand's own store.
caveats: Bonus rates and qualification vary; Amazon's conversion advantage must be tested for the actual offer.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Cut avoidable FBA prep, return and disposal fees
cards.summary: Handle labeling and prep yourself or through your manufacturer to avoid per-unit Amazon service charges, and plan for returns and disposal costs.
cards.use_when: Sourcing, packaging and post-sale operations: negotiating labeling with your manufacturer and setting up returns handling.
steps: Ensure every unit carries an FNSKU barcode sticker before it reaches Amazon. Have your manufacturer apply stickers cheaply or print the barcode directly on the box, rather than paying Amazon the source's cited $0.30 per unit labeling fee.

Handle any other prep (poly bagging, etc.) yourself or at the factory; the source says Amazon charges about $0.50-$2.00 per unit for these services. Read the prep requirements for your specific category.
Budget for return fees: the source says each customer return within 30 days triggers another size/weight-based fee covering return shipping and processing.
Choose what happens to returned units: have Amazon return good-condition units to your sellable inventory so the next order ships that same unit, or have them disposed of at roughly $0.50 per unit.
Optionally review undeliverable inventory and remove it rather than letting it accrue fees.
caveats: Prep service and disposal fees, and category prep requirements, change; confirm current rates and rules.
The source describes return and disposal fees as relatively small and uncommon, but they matter more for high-return categories like apparel.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Budget a private-label launch from a component checklist
cards.summary: Build a line-item startup budget covering plan fee, design, samples, inventory, photos, business registration, UPCs and cushion before committing.
cards.use_when: Launch budgeting for a private-label or wholesale product, or deciding whether you have enough capital to start.
steps: Include the recurring professional selling plan ($39.99/month per the source) and confirm whether you need it for your fulfillment model.

Budget design: the source recommends hiring a legitimate designer and cites about $150 for a private-label logo and label, advising against relying on the cheapest Fiverr option for brand-critical work.
Budget samples: the source cites about $50 shipping per sample round and recommends at least one sample, ideally two, to catch defects before mass production.

Budget first inventory around 400 units at roughly $6/unit (about $2,400) as his default illustration, and check whether your unit cost drops at higher volumes (the source cites ~$5.50 at 1,000 units and ~$5 at 2,000 units).
Budget photography: the source says the main image drives clicks and purchases and recommends $50-$100 for a computer rendering, treating the other listing images as doable in-house.

Add business registration ($150 DBA via LegalZoom, or ~$350 LLC setup plus recurring state fees such as California's $800/year), GS1 UPC codes (~$250 for 10), and about $100 of miscellaneous costs (sticker paper, ink, gas).
Add a marketing reserve: the source suggests at least $1,000 for Amazon PPC and argues that under about $5,000 total, he would advise against starting at all.
caveats: All figures are the presenter's planning estimates from his own launches, not vendor quotes or guarantees.
He explicitly says the $3,500 minimum assumes everything goes perfectly and no marketing is needed, which he calls unrealistic; the $5,000 figure is his recommended realistic floor.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Order 3-6 months of inventory, not the cheapest per-unit quantity
cards.summary: Size your first production run for 3-6 months of expected sales rather than chase volume discounts that lock up cash in unproven product.
cards.use_when: Replenishment and first production order: choosing quantity with a manufacturer before you have sales data.
steps: Estimate expected monthly unit sales and order enough for 3-6 months, favoring the higher end because manufacturer lead times mean you can't restock quickly if sales spike.

Weigh the volume discount against the risk. The source's case study: ordering 2,000 units at ~$5/unit cost $11,000, versus 400 units at ~$7/unit costing about $2,800; he calls the large order a mistake because it took far longer to sell than expected and locked in early product defects.
Avoid running out: the source warns that stockouts can cause Amazon to penalize the listing and make it hard to regain sales velocity, which is his reason for leaning toward the 6-month end.
Order a small test batch first when the product is new or has known issues, fix defects, then scale quantity.
Account for landed cost beyond unit price: the source mentions import duties (he recalls 10%, possibly 20%) that vary by product, so check current rates rather than assuming.
caveats: The lead-time and stockout penalty arguments are the presenter's experience and may not apply to easily restockable domestic suppliers.
Shelf-stable products can justify larger runs than perishables or trend-sensitive goods.
The source's months-of-stock range is a scenario, not a default order size. Use demand uncertainty, lead time, cash, capacity and current storage costs.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Choose brand protection based on the asset, not promised filing shortcuts
cards.summary: Separate the brand's protection needs from Amazon enrollment and content-tool access.
cards.use_when: Brand protection and listing presentation for a private-label product that needs richer PDP content and defense against hijackers.
steps: Identify the brand name, logo and other assets for which protection is needed.
Check current relevant trademark and Brand Registry requirements before investing in packaging.
Do not assume a logo filing is always easier, that a generic name becomes protectable, or that a mark stops all reselling.
Obtain appropriate filing guidance for the jurisdiction and budget using current quotes.
Treat content tools and protection as distinct benefits rather than guaranteed outcomes.
caveats: The source's filing prices and logo-versus-word-mark preference are personal examples, not universal guidance.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Set an advertising budget from per-click cost, conversion rate and margin
cards.summary: Translate click costs and conversion into acquisition cost, then cap spend against contribution.
cards.use_when: Product launch and acquisition planning: deciding how much to spend on Amazon PPC and how to interpret early ad spend.
steps: CPA = CPC / purchase conversion rate expressed as a decimal. $1 CPC / 20% conversion = $5 per order.
Compare CPA with pre-ad contribution after product, Amazon fees, fulfillment and expected returns; $10 pre-ad contribution less $5 CPA leaves $5 before remaining overhead.
Set an affordable launch testing budget and stop conditions; the source's $1,000 starting amount is not a requirement.
Measure search-term relevance, conversion and contribution as data accumulates.
Keep advertising and review collection separate; do not reimburse friends for purchase reviews.
caveats: Illustrative conversion and CPC figures are not benchmarks; allow for reporting and attribution lag.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Treat private label and wholesale as saturated, and differentiate instead
cards.summary: Evaluate private label/wholesale against structural headwinds and consider a novel own product to avoid price wars and Amazon's own copycats.
cards.use_when: Business model and product selection: choosing what to sell on Amazon before committing capital.
steps: Weigh four risks the source raises against private label and wholesale: Chinese manufacturers selling direct to Amazon and cutting out the middleman; similar disintermediation in wholesale; oversaturation (the source cites 5 million sellers and ~4,000 new sellers daily, driving price wars and margin erosion); and Amazon copying winning products with its own basics line that outranks you.

Note his observation that the consistently successful private-label and wholesale sellers tend to be long-established operators with more capital, tolerance for thin margins, and better manufacturer relationships than a newcomer.

Consider creating a product that doesn't yet exist as the alternative. The source's example is a set of wine flashcards — not revolutionary, but with no direct competitors, which he argues raises the odds customers buy.
Design for something you're genuinely interested in, since the source argues passion makes the long launch grind more survivable.
Consider crowdfunding to fund the first production run: the source raised about $15,000 on Kickstarter and cites a friend raising about $5,000, which can cover most or all startup costs.
caveats: These are the presenter's opinions and cited market observations, not measured research; private label and wholesale still work for some sellers, as he acknowledges.
Crowdfunding results vary enormously and require their own marketing effort.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Fund a launch without capital: sell assets, arbitrage and skill-building work
cards.summary: Raise initial capital by liquidating unused items, flipping discounted goods, cutting personal costs, and taking work that teaches Amazon skills.
cards.use_when: Launch funding and pre-launch skill building when you don't have savings to cover inventory and fees.
steps: Sell unused possessions you own but don't use (the source's examples: a surfboard and a hammock, about $100 each) to generate seed cash.

Run retail or online arbitrage: buy a product at a deep discount and resell on Amazon. The source's example is a $300 coffee machine bought for $150, netting roughly $100 after Amazon fees — useful for building cash and learning listing mechanics, though arbitrage margins are thin.
Reduce personal costs temporarily (cheaper housing, less premium food) and redirect the difference into inventory, as the source describes doing when starting out.

Take a second job that builds Amazon-relevant skills rather than unrelated work: the source suggests approaching local shops that sell unique products but aren't on Amazon and offering to list and sell for them for a fee or a profit share, which pays you while you learn.

Alternatively, find an investor for your product: the source's example is funding a friend's wine-flashcard business, recouping his money, and sharing in roughly $15-$20 profit per unit on 50-100 units sold monthly.
caveats: Arbitrage margins are thin and depend on finding genuine discounts; the source's example is illustrative.
The profit-share and investor examples are one-off case studies, not typical returns.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Pick a research tool: Helium 10 vs Jungle Scout
cards.summary: Choose a research tool based on filtering depth and data accuracy, with the source favoring Helium 10 for beginners.
cards.use_when: Product research and keyword/competitor analysis tooling decisions for an Amazon listing.
steps: Consider Helium 10 first if you want more tools, deeper filtering and, per the source, more accurate data — he recommends it for beginners and says it has way more tools than Jungle Scout.

Consider Jungle Scout as a valid alternative; the source explicitly says there's nothing wrong with it and calls it a great tool, so choose based on the specific filters and reports you'll actually use.
Check for discount links or affiliate offers associated with whichever tool you pick, since the source mentions providing a discounted rate.
Verify current pricing, tool set and data coverage directly with the vendor before subscribing, since both products change frequently.
caveats: This is the presenter's tool preference and may be influenced by affiliate relationships; validate with your own trials on products you know.
Tool feature sets and data accuracy change over time.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Funding a first production run with crowdfunding instead of savings
cards.summary: Use a Kickstarter or Indiegogo campaign to raise the cash for your first inventory order before you ever list on Amazon.
cards.use_when: You have a product idea for your Amazon store but little capital and need to fund the first production run while simultaneously testing demand.
steps: Design the product and build marketing/buzz before paying for any inventory; the campaign itself is the spend, since backers pay first and you produce after.
Launch the crowdfunding campaign and collect the pledged money; the source raised $15,000 this way, which covered most of an initial production run.
Use the raised funds to produce the inventory, then ship the product to the backers who funded it.
Treat the campaign as a market test: pledges are evidence people want the product, which is especially useful when the item is too unique to estimate sales from existing Amazon listings.
After fulfillment, transition to Amazon with an existing buyer base and reviews to seed the launch.

If crowdfunding is not viable, the source also describes asking a friend or investor for startup cash (he gave one seller a few thousand dollars, was repaid, and shared in the upside) or, as a last resort he does not usually recommend, taking a loan.
caveats: Backers are giving you money for a promised future product; failing to deliver damages your reputation and may breach platform terms.
The $15,000 and $5,000 figures are the source's own and his students' campaign results, not typical or guaranteed outcomes.
The source says getting a loan is not recommended in most situations.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Don't let analysis paralysis delay launch
cards.summary: Weigh the profit from launching a month sooner against the cost of the mistake you're trying to avoid, and start.
cards.use_when: You're stuck comparing manufacturers, designs or keywords and keep pushing back the date you place your first inventory order.
steps: Estimate your product's likely monthly profit; the source's example product made about $10,000/month profit, meaning each month of delay cost roughly $10,000.

Compare the delay cost to the mistake you're avoiding. Example from the source: spending a month choosing between two manufacturers to avoid a $5,000 error loses $10,000 in profit, so the 'wrong' fast choice still nets $5,000 ahead.
Accept that early mistakes are survivable if the product is good; the source lost about $5-6k of leaky jars on one run yet still made roughly $67,000 profit on the sellable first thousand units.
Pick one income method and commit to it for 3-6 months rather than dabbling across several models.
Start, then solve problems as they appear instead of trying to know everything in advance.
caveats: The $10,000/month figure is the source's own product, not a benchmark for your niche.
Speed does not excuse skipping basic product-quality checks that cause refunds and account problems.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Screening criteria for a viable Amazon product
cards.summary: Filter candidate products for price band, shippability, defensibility and personal knowledge before committing.
cards.use_when: You're choosing which product to private-label or source for your Amazon store.
steps: Set a price floor of about $15 (source's minimum); below that, Amazon fees and shipping make profitability very hard.
Ideally price under $20, because FBA fees and shipping rise sharply above that.
Reject fragile or leak-prone items: the source threw away 1,000 leaking glass jars from a 2,000-unit run; avoid glass, weak seals or anything that breaks in transit.
Avoid products Chinese manufacturers can copy exactly and undercut; the source names oversaturation, China and Amazon Basics as reasons old-style Alibaba private labeling is largely dead.
Aim to sell the best/premium version in the category so you can charge the most and earn more per unit.
Prioritize a product you're genuinely passionate about, because you'll understand and market it better through the down phases.
Validate demand before ordering: run social media or a crowdfunding campaign; the source used Kickstarter because his unique product couldn't be sized with sales-estimator tools.
caveats: The $15 minimum and under-$20 target are the source's heuristics, not universal rules; some categories support different bands.
The source acknowledges some private-label opportunity remains if you add a strong brand or other differentiator.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Using Helium 10 to find an underserved product
cards.summary: Treat Amazon as a search engine and mine search demand for phrases no one has built a product for.
cards.use_when: You need a product idea for your Amazon store and want demand data rather than guesswork.
steps: Enter a broad interest term (the source used 'cocktails') into Helium 10 and review the related product and keyword ideas it returns.
Look for specific phrases with real monthly search volume; the example found 'cocktail recipe cards' and 'bartender flashcards' had thousands of searches per month.
Check whether a product already exists for that exact phrase; the source found cocktail recipe books but no cocktflashcard product, which became the opportunity.
Build the product to match the phrase people actually type, so your listing can rank for that term.
Sign up for the free tier or use a discount link if available; verify the current Helium 10 interface and pricing before relying on any specific feature.
Combine this with a product you're passionate about so marketing is easier.
caveats: Search volume alone is not proof of profitability; check competition, price band and shippability too.
The AJ case (over $500,000 in first-year sales) is a single example, not a typical result.
Tool features and free-tier limits change; confirm current terms.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Title, main image and review count drive listing clicks
cards.summary: Optimize the three elements the source calls decisive for click-through and conversion on an Amazon listing.
cards.use_when: You're writing or revising a product title and main image, or diagnosing why a live listing gets no sales.
steps: Put the main target keyword at the very front of the title; Amazon weighs early words more and shoppers instantly confirm relevance. Don't lead with your brand unless you're an established brand like Nike, which still leads with the product.
Write the title so a shopper immediately recognizes the match; the source's principle is 'don't make users think.'
Use a clean, clear main image that fills the frame with minimal white space, since the image sits on a white background and must pop.
Show the product itself, not your box or logo; a small logo is fine but the product must dominate.
Treat review count as a purchase prerequisite; the source argues a listing with only three to five reviews won't sell and you should not believe in a product you can't get reviewed.

Build a genuine interested audience for launch demand. Request reviews only through permitted neutral workflows; the source's first-week review count is not a repeatable target or justification for a purchase-review group.
caveats: The source states his review-solicitation methods are against Amazon's terms of service and says to proceed at your own risk; Amazon can remove reviews and crack down.
Amazon has title-format rules that the source says the platform often doesn't enforce strictly, but that is his experience, not a guarantee.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Writing bullet points and secondary images that convert
cards.summary: Lead with benefits and show ownership scenarios to make an online shopper mentally experience the product.
cards.use_when: You're building the bullet points and image stack on your Amazon product page.
steps: Write bullets for the customer, not the algorithm, though you can weave keywords in naturally.
Translate features into benefits: instead of '19g of fat,' say the product gives sustained, long-lasting energy.
Describe only the actual applicable returns or guarantee terms, where allowed in the listing. Do not invent a blanket money-back guarantee or assume every product has identical return eligibility.
Use the secondary images to show what owning the product is like: real people using it, it in real settings, and answers to common questions (for his food product, ways to eat it and recipes).
Put modest effort into the text description; the source estimates 99% of buyers decide from the main image, reviews, title, bullets and other images.
Audit your own buying behavior on Amazon to see which of these elements actually drove your last purchase.
caveats: Bullet and image content cannot fix a bad product or a duplicate, undifferentiated offer.
The guarantee-bullet tactic is a persuasion device, not a new policy; returns still cost you.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Choosing an FBA manufacturer and avoiding manufacturing losses
cards.summary: Screen manufacturers for simple per-unit pricing, short lead times and clear contracts before you commit.
cards.use_when: You're selecting a supplier to produce your Amazon inventory and want to avoid costly production-run surprises.
steps: Insist on simple per-unit pricing; the source rejected a manufacturer that billed per production day after quoting an estimate, which then stretched to five days.
Check how fast they can produce and reorder, because long lead times cause stockouts; the source lost about $5,000 in sales waiting on a slow manufacturer.
Get the contract terms, including any buried fees, reviewed before signing; the source was effectively out $10,000 from fees buried in a long contract that even his lawyer missed.
Sit with a printed spec for every component: no tear notch on pouches cost $2,000 to fix by hand, and leaky pouches forced him to discard and clean units.
Keep every document — bill of lading, receipts, contracts — safe; he lost a pallet claim because the bill of lading couldn't be located.
Consider US manufacturers found through sourcing directories if you want to reduce copying risk.
caveats: The source notes outright manufacturer scams are not that common, and the one that hit him was US-based.
A lawyer review did not catch the buried fees in his case, so review contract economics yourself as well.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Compare FBA and merchant fulfillment for the actual product
cards.summary: Evaluate delivery eligibility, total costs and operational capacity rather than assuming FBA guarantees higher sales.
cards.use_when: You're deciding how to ship orders for your Amazon store: from your own warehouse (FBM) or through Amazon FBA.
steps: Compare current FBA fees, storage and inbound costs with the merchant's own shipping and service costs.
Assess delivery promises, stock availability, returns and operating capacity for the product.
FBA can provide Prime eligibility; qualifying merchants may also use Seller Fulfilled Prime where available.
Test conversion and contribution where practical rather than assuming a fixed sales multiplier or direct ranking boost.
Choose FBA, merchant fulfillment or a mix using actual economics and service requirements.
caveats: Source sales uplifts are individual cases; check current program requirements in the selling marketplace.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Ordering the right amount of inventory to avoid fees and stockouts
cards.summary: Balance Amazon storage costs against lost sales by ordering roughly six months of inventory and cycling aged units.
cards.use_when: You're planning a replenishment order or see units sitting long in Amazon's warehouse.
steps: Order roughly six months of inventory so that if the product sells faster than expected you still have time to reorder from your manufacturer.
Watch stock levels closely; a one-week stockout on his first product cost at least $3,000 in lost sales.
Monitor aged inventory in Seller Central, and if units approach the one-year mark, request Amazon return them to you and ship them back so the clock resets.
Do that return-and-resend whenever the round-trip shipping is cheaper than the long-term storage fee, which the source says is usually the case.
Avoid over-ordering perishable or expiring goods; he discarded a few hundred units of an expiring product but still made about $10,000 profit on that run.
caveats: The ~$0.75 per cubic foot per month storage and ~$6 per cubic foot long-term figures are from the source and from the period he describes; verify current Amazon fee schedules.
Amazon penalizes chronic stockouts with lower search placement, and the source says it can even blacklist you.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Auditing Amazon fee overcharges
cards.summary: Monitor your seller account for incorrect fees and reimburse claims before the window closes.
cards.use_when: You're running a live Amazon store and want to recover money lost to overbilling or missing inventory.
steps: Review FBA fees, storage fees and other charges regularly rather than assuming they're correct; the source says he lost over $3,000 to overcharges.
When you find an error, open a case by email with Amazon promptly; the source says they usually fix it if you catch it early.
If you wait too long, expect Amazon to refuse reimbursement for the overcharge.
Consider third-party reimbursement software that scans your account for overcharges and money Amazon owes you; the source wishes he'd used one earlier.
Treat any Amazon-carried shipment as evidence you must document: keep the bill of lading and every receipt so you can dispute a claim that a pallet never arrived.
caveats: Reimbursement tool names, features and fees change; verify the current tool and interface before buying.
The source lost a missing-pallet claim because the bill of lading wasn't kept, so retain all shipping paperwork.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Differentiating against oversaturation and copycats
cards.summary: Sell a differentiated 'passion product' and expect competitors to grow the category rather than steal your share.
cards.use_when: You're evaluating whether a niche is too crowded or deciding how unique your product needs to be.
steps: Diagnose the problem as specific saturated categories, not Amazon as a whole; the source notes Amazon has over 9 million sellers but only about 1 million active, and cites that 43%+ of sellers have made at least $100,000.
When everyone is selling the same category, zag: look for a product no one else offers rather than another Alibaba item with your sticker on it.
Build a 'passion product' that is genuinely better than the competition, supported by strong branding.

Expect first-mover advantage to hold: the source's first keto nut butter saw competitors enter in year two and sales rose from about $300,000 to about $400,000 as the category's customer pool expanded.

Identify design, brand and invention assets early and seek appropriate protection guidance. A provisional application is not an issued patent or a year of enforceable protection; avoid relying on historical filing prices.
Compete on branding and social media, which the source argues is where he can beat overseas copiers.
caveats: The source rates China-related copying risk as 10 out of 10 for concern before mitigation, and notes NDAs don't work in China the way an NN agreement can.
Sales-growth-through-competition is his own product's example, not a rule that applies to every niche.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Rating recession and inflation risk for an Amazon launch
cards.summary: Assess macro fears by category and adjust pricing and product choice instead of delaying.
cards.use_when: You're deciding whether to launch or which category to enter given recession or inflation concerns.
steps: Note that the source cites 50% of Fortune 500 companies being started during recessions, and that Amazon sales have risen every year regardless of the stock market.
Rate outright recession fear around 5 out of 10; certain categories drop, but groceries, baby items, pet items and small indulgences like candy tend to hold up.
Choose a category whose demand is recession-resistant if you expect a downturn, or position your product as an affordable pleasure.
Handle inflation by raising your prices as your input and shipping costs rise; as an owner you can adjust, unlike a salaried worker.
Don't let macro predictions become analysis paralysis; the source warns that worst-case focus keeps people from ever starting.
caveats: Specific statistics (50% of Fortune 500, 23% shipping-cost increase, 43% of sellers earning $100k+) are the source's claims; verify before using them in your own planning.
The source himself says no one actually knows where the economy is going.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Recession-Proof Product Selection for Amazon
cards.summary: Pick Amazon product categories whose demand holds up in downturns instead of freezing on recession fear.
cards.use_when: Deciding which product categories to source or launch when you're worried about a recession or soft consumer spending.
steps: Accept the source's view that a recession is a 5-out-of-10 concern: some categories drop in sales, but others stay resilient.
Weight categories the source names as recession-resistant: groceries, baby items, pet products and small-pleasure items like candy.
Treat this as directional, not a rule: verify current demand with keyword/search-volume tools before committing capital.
Do not let uncertainty become analysis paralysis — the source says every year people predict collapse and most never start.
Size your first order so a soft launch doesn't sink you rather than betting the farm on a macro call.
caveats: The presenter rates recession risk 5/10 and admits nobody actually knows; category lists are his opinion, not researched benchmarks.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Financing an Amazon Launch With Pre-Sales
cards.summary: Raise production funds from pre-sales instead of paying startup costs out of pocket.
cards.use_when: You want to start an Amazon FBA business but don't have capital for inventory.
steps: Validate interest in your product before producing anything, e.g. by collecting demand signals on social media or via a crowdfunding page.
Collect payment or committed orders up front and use that cash to fund the first production run — the source says AJ started with zero dollars this way.
Treat startup capital as variable, not fixed: audience-reported bands range from under $500 (11% of sellers) to over $10,000 (22%), so pick a scale you can fund.
Invite interested campaign supporters to learn about the launch; do not tie crowdfunding perks or other benefits to Amazon reviews.
caveats: Pre-sale cash flow only works if you can actually deliver; delays (see the source's 4→8-week manufacturer slips) can turn pre-sales into refunds or angry backers.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Modeling Amazon Fees and FBA Fulfillment
cards.summary: Understand the 15% referral fee, monthly plan choice and per-unit FBA cost before pricing your product.
cards.use_when: Building unit economics or deciding between FBA and self-fulfillment for a new Amazon product.
steps: Account for the 15% Amazon referral fee on every sale; the source frames it as marketing cost versus the billions Amazon spends acquiring customers.
Choose plan: individual seller is free but adds $0.99 per item, so professional at $39.99/month makes sense above roughly 40 units/month.
Use FBA so your items are Prime-eligible — the source claims Prime products sell about 5x more than non-Prime (his own FBM→FBA switch).
Budget FBA pick-and-pack per unit by size: ~$4/unit for the source's electrolyte product; heavier items cost more.
Compare FBA fee to your own shipping + labor instead of treating it as pure loss; the source says it was equivalent to his own shipping cost without the work.
caveats: Fee percentages and FBA rates change — verify current Amazon fee schedules in Seller Central. The 5x sales lift is one seller's anecdote, not a benchmark.
Brand referral program was cited as reducing the fee from 15% to 5%; confirm current eligibility before relying on it.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Estimate Monthly Product Revenue From BSR
cards.summary: Convert a competitor's Amazon best-seller rank into estimated monthly units and revenue before entering a niche.
cards.use_when: Sizing demand and revenue potential for a product idea or category before sourcing.
steps: Open Amazon Best Sellers in your target category to find top-ranked products.
Record the product's Best Sellers Rank (BSR) number and its price.
Enter marketplace, category and BSR into a free sales estimator (the source uses Jungle Scout's) to get estimated monthly units.
Multiply estimated units by price to approximate monthly revenue — the source's examples: pimple patch ~170k units ≈ $1.9M/month; sports-nutrition #1 ~145k units ≈ $3M/month.
Cross-check at the category level: the source notes 4 of the top 8 bestselling supplements were electrolyte powders, several doing $1–3M/month.
caveats: BSR-to-sales estimates are third-party approximations and drift by category and season; treat as a screening range, not a forecast.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Keyword Mining for Product Gaps With Helium 10 Magnet
cards.summary: Find underserved search terms with real volume and no exact-match product, then build your product around them.
cards.use_when: Choosing a specific product to launch, or validating that a niche has a keyword gap you can own.
steps: Enter an interest or niche (e.g. 'carnivore diet', 'caffeinated gum') into Helium 10's Magnet tool and pull keyword data.
Sort by the Magnet IQ/opportunity score and scan the list; the source spent ~30 minutes reviewing candidates.
For each promising keyword, search it on Amazon and check whether any product exactly matches the search.

Target keywords with meaningful monthly search volume but no perfect-match listing (source example: 'carnivore electrolytes' ~2,000 searches/month with only sugar-laden or flavored electrolytes ranking).
Also look for smaller long-tail terms with lower competition (e.g. 'gym gum', 'workout gum') to center your title and listing around.
caveats: Search volumes are tool estimates and shift over time (the source saw 'caffeinated gum' spike from ~2,000 to ~15,000/month later). Verify current demand in Seller Central/tools before ordering inventory.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Search-First Product Framing: Amazon Is a Search Engine
cards.summary: Design your product and title around an exact search phrase buyers already type, not around what you want to make.
cards.use_when: Naming a product, writing a listing title, or deciding whether a product idea can win on Amazon.
steps: Treat Amazon as a search engine: buyers type a query and see image results, so your job is to match an existing query with a distinct product.
Name your product the exact search phrase when it's descriptive (the source named his product 'Carnivore Electrolytes' so searchers immediately recognize fit).
Build the title around your validated core keyword(s) so Amazon associates your listing with that query.
Confirm the query has unsatisfied demand — the source's test was 'is anyone selling a product that perfectly matches this search?' If not, that's your opening.
caveats: Exact-match naming may hurt trademark distinctiveness; the source later emphasizes trademark/brand registry needs, so balance SEO naming against brandability.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Packaging Design for Category Contrast
cards.summary: Choose packaging colors that visually contrast the dominant colors on the search results page so your thumbnail gets clicked.
cards.use_when: Designing your product's packaging or main image to stand out against named competitors in Amazon search results.
steps: Search your target keyword on Amazon and screenshot the results grid to see the dominant colors.
Identify the emotional signal of those colors — the source says blues/whites/greens read as calming (insurance-like), red reads as high-energy (car/fast-food-like).
Deliberately invert: the source chose black packaging with red lettering for a supplement in a sea of blue, white and green competitors.
Apply contrast at thumbnail size — the decision happens in a grid of images, not on the product page.
Extend the palette consistently to logo, packaging and listing images so the click-through is reinforced at the PDP.
caveats: Color psychology is the source's heuristic, not a tested result; validate with your own search-results screenshot and category norms.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Sourcing Design Help at Four Price Tiers
cards.summary: Pick the right design vendor tier for logo and packaging based on budget and risk tolerance.
cards.use_when: Commissioning a logo, brand identity or Amazon packaging design for a new product.
steps: DIY free: Canva if you have design skill and no budget.
Cheapest: Fiverr, from ~$5, but 'you get what you pay for' — the source shows a $5 logo example.
Mid-tier: Upwork freelancers, ~$50 for a logo in the source's experience.
Crowdsourced: 99designs, ~$300, gets hundreds of submissions and lets you poll friends/family/pre-launch supporters before choosing.
Amazon-specific: the source recommends FBA Creatives (logos, brand, packaging built for Amazon) and used it for all his products.
caveats: A 99designs winner was flagged for brand infringement in the source's own story and 99designs offered no help — always run a basic trademark check on any chosen logo.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Opening an Amazon Seller Account
cards.summary: Set up the correct seller plan and gather the documents Amazon requires before you start the signup flow.
cards.use_when: Registering a new Amazon selling account and choosing between individual and professional plans.
steps: Go to sell.amazon.com and find the individual-seller signup option (the source notes it's hidden at the bottom of the page).
Choose individual (free) if you'll sell fewer than ~40 units/month; it adds $0.99 per item.
Choose professional ($39.99/month) if you expect more than 40 units/month — the source's own plan.
Have ready before starting: valid ID or passport, recent bank/credit-card statement, a credit card for the monthly fee, and a mobile phone number.
Provide business details and the bank account where Amazon will deposit your payouts.
caveats: Amazon's signup flow and UI change frequently — verify current steps and fees in Seller Central; $39.99/month is the source's figure at recording time.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Finding a Manufacturer for an Amazon Product
cards.summary: Choose among four sourcing channels based on whether your product is consumable and how fast you need a partner.
cards.use_when: Sourcing a manufacturer or private-label supplier for a new Amazon product.
steps: Alibaba.com — largest directory of overseas manufacturers (Asia/Europe/India).
ThomasNet.com — US-based manufacturers, useful when you want domestic production.
Google search 'your product + manufacturer' or '+ private labeler' — the source found his own manufacturer this way and notes many US manufacturers require large quantities.
Ask another seller who already makes a similar product who their manufacturer is — fastest route, and the route used in the 7-day challenge.
Match channel to product: for a consumable/ingestible, the source avoided China and used Google/ThomasNet and referrals for domestic production.
caveats: Referral-only sourcing depends on access to a seller network; without one, expect longer lead times. Verify certification/ingredient claims before ordering.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: First Production Run Sizing and Lead-Time Reality
cards.summary: Order a test-sized run against expected daily sales, and plan around multi-week manufacturing plus inbound lead times.
cards.use_when: Deciding how many units to order on your first production run and when to place reorders.
steps: Get tiered quotes: the source's manufacturer quoted $8/unit at 500 units and $7/unit at 2,000 — cheaper per unit at higher volume.
Estimate realistic daily sales, then size the order as roughly 3 months of that rate (the source guessed 3–4 units/day and ordered 500).
Ask for the production lead time up front and pad it: in the source's case it slipped from 4–6 weeks to 6–8 weeks, plus a couple more weeks for Amazon to receive and check in.
Time the launch to your category's peak season (the source targeted January for supplements because of New Year's resolutions).
Place reorders based on observed sell-through, not your original pessimism — repeated stockouts in the source's case came from underestimating demand.
caveats: Lead times vary widely by product and factory; the source's specific weeks are an example, and his own plans slipped repeatedly.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Building a Pre-Launch Audience and Launch-Day Velocity
cards.summary: Grow a small brand following before launch, then convert it into concentrated day-one sales and early reviews.
cards.use_when: Preparing to launch a new Amazon listing and needing early sales velocity to rank in search.
steps: Before launch, create Instagram and TikTok accounts for the brand and post content to accumulate followers.
For speed, the source spliced his product into existing viral niche videos (e.g. a 'what I eat on the carnivore diet' clip) rather than filming original content.
Collect emails from interested followers and email them leading up to and on launch day.
Offer a launch-week discount to convert that audience immediately: the source dropped his planned $24.99 price to $16.99 for week one.
Ask buyers for reviews (Amazon prohibits asking specifically for 5-star reviews) to build early social proof, which supports ranking.
caveats: Amazon prohibits incentivized or 5-star-solicited reviews; only ask neutrally. The presenter's own network promoting his product is not replicable for most sellers.
Launch velocity is a source hypothesis, not a guaranteed ranking mechanism. Use genuine demand; do not arrange reimbursed purchases, incentivized reviews or search-rank manipulation.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Creating and Publishing an Amazon Listing
cards.summary: Publish a listing with imagery, title, bullets and description before inventory arrives so the launch isn't delayed.
cards.use_when: Setting up a new product detail page in Seller Central, or preparing listing content in advance of inventory.
steps: In Seller Central, use the menu → 'Add a Product' → 'I'm adding a product not sold on Amazon' and pick your category.
Fill in title (with your validated core keyword), brand name, bullets and description.
Upload your prepared images and set price and other required attributes.
Do this while manufacturing finishes — the source completed his listing weeks before the product was ready, so launch only needed inventory.
Check Amazon's category-gating rules early: the source's 'carnivore diet'-related product was flagged and required a Certificate of Analysis (COA) from the manufacturer before approval.
caveats: Amazon UI labels and gating/COA requirements vary by category and change — verify current requirements in Seller Central before listing.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Inbound Shipping and Amazon Check-In Workflow
cards.summary: Send inventory to an Amazon fulfillment center in a way that gets checked in before you run out of stock.
cards.use_when: Shipping a production run to Amazon's warehouse and timing the handoff to your live listing.
steps: In Seller Central, open the product and choose Send/Replenish Inventory.
Enter box dimensions and the total number of units per box.
Print box labels, attach them to each carton, and drop the shipment with a carrier (the source used UPS).
Allow a couple of weeks for Amazon to receive and process the shipment before it's sellable.
Coordinate the check-in with your current stock run-out date — the source twice had inventory check in the day before running out.
caveats: Amazon's inbound workflow and label requirements change; verify current shipping requirements. Amazon may split or reject shipments, so build buffer time.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Launch-Week Discounting to Drive Rank
cards.summary: Discount aggressively in the first week to concentrate sales, then raise price once rank and reviews are established.
cards.use_when: Pricing a new Amazon product during its launch window.
steps: Set a launch-week discount below your intended long-term price (source: $16.99 launch vs. planned $24.99).
Tell your pre-launch audience the discount is time-limited to convert them early.
Expect thin margins during launch — the source made $75 profit on $500 of day-one revenue at the discounted price.
After the first week, raise to your target price; the source found sales held even as he moved $24.99 → $29.99 → $34.99.
Use the resulting reviews and rank as support for the higher price.
